full_output.paper_title: MglA/SspA complex interactions are modulated by inorganic polyphosphate.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies inorganic polyphosphate (polyP) as a critical molecule that stabilizes the interaction between the MglA and SspA proteins in Francisella tularensis, which is essential for the regulation of pathogenicity genes.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized bacterial two-hybrid systems, chromatin immunoprecipitation, and biochemical assays to investigate the role of polyP in stabilizing the MglA/SspA complex.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that gene-silencing antisense oligomers, specifically PPMOs targeting the acpP gene, inhibit the growth of Acinetobacter lwoffii and Acinetobacter baumannii both in vitro and in vivo.
full_output.methodology: The study used minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) and viability assays in vitro, and a murine pulmonary infection model in vivo to evaluate the effectiveness of PPMOs.

full_output.paper_title: Novel staphylococcal glycosyltransferases SdgA and SdgB mediate immunogenicity and protection of virulence-associated cell wall proteins.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies two novel glycosyltransferases, SdgA and SdgB, which modify serine-aspartate repeat (SDR) proteins in Staphylococcus aureus and S. epidermidis. These modifications protect SDR proteins from proteolysis and create an immunodominant epitope recognized by human antibodies.
full_output.methodology: The study uses immunoblotting, mass spectrometry, and genetic manipulation to characterize the role of SdgA and SdgB in SDR protein glycosylation.

full_output.paper_title: A structure-guided mutation in the major capsid protein retargets BK polyomavirus.

mutations_found.validated_by: STD NMR spectroscopy and carbohydrate microarray analyses
STD NMR, carbohydrate microarray analyses, flow cytometry

VP1.notes: Mutations in VP1 affect receptor binding and viral infectivity

full_output.key_findings: A single point mutation (K68S) in the BKPyV VP1 protein enables the virus to switch its receptor specificity from b-series gangliosides to GM1, a receptor typically used by SV40.
full_output.methodology: Structural analysis, STD NMR, carbohydrate microarray analyses, flow cytometry, and mutagenesis experiments.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the structure and function of the large progenitor toxin complex (L-PTC) of botulinum neurotoxin A (BoNT/A), highlighting the role of the HA complex in facilitating BoNT absorption through interactions with carbohydrate receptors.
full_output.methodology: Structural biology techniques including X-ray crystallography, electron microscopy, and functional studies were employed to elucidate the molecular architecture and mechanisms of the L-PTC/A.

full_output.paper_title: MicroRNA-155 promotes autophagy to eliminate intracellular mycobacteria by targeting Rheb.
full_output.key_findings: miR-155 promotes autophagy and eliminates intracellular mycobacteria by targeting Rheb, a negative regulator of autophagy.
full_output.methodology: Real-time PCR, Western-blot, luciferase reporter assay, CFU assay, confocal microscopy, and siRNA knockdown.

full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the impact of Apa mannosylation on T cell antigenicity and immune responses, showing that both nApa and rApa induce comparable T cell responses and protection against Mtb challenge, indicating that mannosylation is not essential for protective immunity.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized ELISPOT assays, flow cytometry, and T cell hybridoma generation to analyze T cell responses and antigen recognition.

full_output.paper_title: Heme-Iron Restriction Influences Morphology, Biofilm Architecture, and Persistence of Non-Typeable Haemophilus influenzae
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that transient heme-iron restriction in NTHI leads to changes in biofilm architecture, increased survival in the middle ear, and reduced disease severity. It identifies SulA as a key factor in filamentation and biofilm formation under heme-iron restriction.
full_output.methodology: The study used culture-based systems, fluorescent reporter strains, and animal models to investigate the effects of heme-iron restriction on NTHI biofilm architecture and pathogenesis.

full_output.paper_title: Dominant role of nucleotide substitution in the diversification of serotype 3 pneumococci over decades and during a single infection.

patAB.validation_method: expression profiling and phenotype microarray testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the patAB efflux pump as a key determinant of fluoroquinolone, acriflavine, and tetracycline resistance in Streptococcus pneumoniae. A putative upstream sequence (PUS) regulates the expression of patAB, contributing to altered resistance profiles.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, phenotype microarray analysis, susceptibility testing, and transformation experiments were used to characterize resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Susceptibility to tulathromycin in Mannheimia haemolytica isolated from feedlot cattle over a 3-year period.

blaROB-1.mechanism: confers resistance to ampicillin and penicillin
blaROB-1.validation_method: PCR detection of antimicrobial resistance genes

aphA-1.validation_method: PCR detection of antimicrobial resistance genes

tet(H).validation_method: PCR detection of antimicrobial resistance genes

full_output.key_findings: The study found that tulathromycin resistance in Mannheimia haemolytica from feedlot cattle in western Canada was very low, with only five isolates showing resistance. These isolates were also resistant to other antibiotics such as neomycin, oxytetracycline, tilmicosin, and ampicillin/penicillin. The resistance mechanisms involved the genes bla ROB-1, aphA-1, and tet(H).
full_output.methodology: The study involved isolating M. haemolytica from feedlot cattle, testing their susceptibility to various antibiotics, and detecting resistance genes via PCR.

full_output.paper_title: Targeting fungal genes by diced siRNAs: a rapid tool to decipher gene function in Aspergillus nidulans.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the effectiveness of d-siRNAs in silencing the endogenous genes An rasA and An rasB in Aspergillus nidulans, leading to altered growth and development. The d-siRNA approach was found to be more potent than chemically synthesized siRNAs.
full_output.methodology: Gene silencing using d-siRNAs, qRT-PCR, and phenotypic analysis.

full_output.paper_title: The ComP-ComA quorum system is essential for "Trojan horse" like pathogenesis in Bacillus nematocida.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the ComP-ComA quorum sensing system as essential for the pathogenesis of Bacillus nematocida B16, particularly in the synthesis of attractants and the regulation of virulence proteases.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation, nematocidal activity assays, protease assays, RT-qPCR, and EMSA were used to analyze the role of the ComP-ComA system in pathogenesis.

full_output.paper_title: Marine sediment-derived Streptomyces bacteria from British Columbia, Canada are a promising microbiota resource for the discovery of antimicrobial natural products.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified four new novobiocin analogues from marine-derived Streptomyces isolates, highlighting the structural features critical for anti-MRSA activity.
full_output.methodology: Chemical analysis and structure-activity relationship studies of bioactive compounds from Streptomyces isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that the presence of Listeria monocytogenes in a dual-species biofilm with Pseudomonas putida significantly increases the resistance of P. putida to benzalkonium chloride (BC).
full_output.methodology: The study used mixed-culture biofilm formation on stainless steel coupons, exposure to BC, and PFGE analysis to assess resistance and microbial composition.

full_output.key_findings: Mutations in TbAT1 and TbAQP2 are associated with decreased susceptibility to melarsoprol and pentamidine in Trypanosoma brucei ssp. field isolates.
full_output.methodology: Genotyping and drug sensitivity assays were conducted on 16 T. brucei ssp. field isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Gene Expression Analysis of Macrophage Responses to Leptospira Infection
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies differences in gene expression between murine and human macrophages infected with Leptospira interrogans, highlighting variations in immune response pathways.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptomic analysis and cytokine array experiments were conducted to compare gene expression in macrophages infected with Leptospira interrogans.

full_output.paper_title: An investigation of resistance to β-lactam antimicrobials among staphylococci isolated from pigs with exudative epidermitis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the mecA gene as a major determinant of β-lactam resistance in various staphylococcal species isolated from pigs with exudative epidermitis, including Staphylococcus hyicus, Staphylococcus aureus, and others. The majority of methicillin-resistant isolates carried SCC mec type V.
full_output.methodology: PCR, latex agglutination test, and disk diffusion susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize β-lactam resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Genome analysis of Pseudoalteromonas flavipulchra JG1 reveals various survival advantages in marine environment.

blaC.validation_method: gene cloning and enzyme activity assay

full_output.key_findings: P. flavipulchra JG1 possesses genes encoding beta-lactamases, aminoglycoside modifying enzymes, and efflux pumps that confer resistance to penicillin, kanamycin, tetracycline, and chloramphenicol.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, gene cloning, enzyme activity assays, and MIC testing.

full_output.paper_title: Horizontal gene transfer converts non-toxigenic Clostridium difficile strains into toxin producers.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that the pathogenicity locus (PaLoc) of Clostridium difficile can be transferred from toxigenic to non-toxigenic strains through horizontal gene transfer, converting non-toxigenic strains into toxin producers.
full_output.methodology: PCR, DNA sequencing, cytotoxicity assays, and genomic sequencing were used to analyze gene transfer and toxin production.

full_output.paper_title: Distribution of genes encoding tetracycline resistance and aminoglycoside modifying enzymes in Staphylococcus aureus strains isolated from a burn center.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various tetracycline resistance genes (tetM, tetK) and aminoglycoside modifying enzymes (aac(6')-Ie-aph(2'')-I, aph(3')-IIIa, ant(4')-Ia) in Staphylococcus aureus isolates from burn patients.
full_output.methodology: PCR and multiplex-PCR were used to detect the presence of tetracycline resistance and aminoglycoside modifying enzyme genes.

full_output.paper_title: Aetiological agents of ventilator-associated pneumonia and its resistance pattern - a threat for treatment.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Escherichia coli as common aetiological agents of ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) and highlights the presence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) pathogens, including ESBL and MBL producers.
full_output.methodology: Prospective study involving bacteriological methods, Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion, ESBL, and MBL testing.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance and molecular epidemiology of Staphylococcus aureus from Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mecA and PVL genes in Staphylococcus aureus isolates from Mongolia, indicating methicillin resistance and virulence potential. The prevalence of MRSA was 8.8%, and 28% of isolates were multidrug resistant.
full_output.methodology: PCR for gene detection, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and molecular typing techniques.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of a novel zinc transporter ZnuA acquired by Vibrio parahaemolyticus through horizontal gene transfer.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel zinc transporter gene, vpa1307, in Vibrio parahaemolyticus, which is part of the ZnuA family and contributes to the bacterium's growth under zinc limitation and its pathogenicity.
full_output.methodology: Gene deletion and complementation assays, RT-PCR, and growth assays were used to validate the role of vpa1307.

full_output.paper_title: Drug resistance profile and biofilm forming potential of Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolated from contact lenses in Karachi-Pakistan.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that most Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from contact lenses in Karachi, Pakistan, were resistant to multiple antibiotics, with high resistance rates to erythromycin and ampicillin. Additionally, the isolates exhibited strong biofilm-forming potential, which was significantly higher in multi-drug resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: The study used the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method to assess antibiotic resistance and various qualitative and quantitative methods to evaluate biofilm formation.

full_output.paper_title: Potential for inhibition of bacterial efflux pumps in multidrug-resistant Vibrio cholera.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies EmrD-3, a new multi-drug efflux pump in V. cholerae, which confers resistance to multiple antibiotics including linezolid, rifampin, ethidium bromide, minocycline, erythromycin, trimethoprim, chloramphenicol, and rhodamine 6G.
full_output.methodology: Experimental validation of the efflux pump's resistance phenotype in V. cholerae.

full_output.paper_title: Elicitation of induced resistance against Pectobacterium carotovorum and Pseudomonas syringae by specific individual compounds derived from native Korean plant species.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies capsaicin, fisetin hydrate, jaceosidin, and farnesiferol A as compounds that elicit induced resistance against Pectobacterium carotovorum and Pseudomonas syringae in plants. These compounds activate salicylic acid (SA) and jasmonic acid (JA) signaling pathways, leading to the upregulation of defense-related genes such as PR2 and PDF1.2.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized an X-plate system to screen plant compounds for their ability to induce resistance. It included genetic analysis of Arabidopsis mutants and transgenic lines to determine the signaling pathways involved.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular architecture of Streptococcus pneumoniae surface thioredoxin-fold lipoproteins crucial for extracellular oxidative stress resistance and maintenance of virulence.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Etrx1 and Etrx2 as surface-exposed thioredoxin-like lipoproteins that act as redox partners for Sp MsrAB2, playing a critical role in extracellular oxidative stress resistance and pneumococcal virulence.
full_output.methodology: Immunoblot analysis, flow cytometry, oxidative stress resistance assays, and growth experiments with MetSO were used to validate the function of Etrx1, Etrx2, and Sp MsrAB2.

full_output.paper_title: A deletion polymorphism in the Caenorhabditis elegans RIG-I homolog disables viral RNA dicing and antiviral immunity.
full_output.key_findings: A 159 base-pair deletion in the drh-1 gene (niDf250) is a major determinant of viral sensitivity in C. elegans. The wild-type drh-1 gene is required for the initiation of an antiviral RNAi pathway and the generation of virus-derived siRNAs (viRNAs).

full_output.paper_title: A novel type of N-acetylglutamate synthase is involved in the first step of arginine biosynthesis in Corynebacterium glutamicum.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies cg3035 as a novel N-acetylglutamate synthase involved in the first step of arginine biosynthesis in Corynebacterium glutamicum, demonstrating its functionality through various experimental validations.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic diversity and adaptation of Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium from analysis of six genomes of different phage types.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the genomic diversity of six Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium strains with different phage types, identifying variations primarily due to SNPs, insertions/deletions, and gene inactivations. It highlighted the presence of prophages and plasmids, and noted the absence of the pSLT plasmid in some strains.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing using Illumina technology, SNP identification via BWA and SOAPdenovo, and phylogenetic analysis with PAUP.

The structural and functional analysis reveals the mechanism of drug extrusion and the role of specific amino acids in substrate binding and protonation.

full_output.paper_title: Coagulase-negative staphylococci strains resistant to oxacillin isolated from neonatal blood cultures.

The mecA gene was detected in 69 out of 100 CoNS strains, with varying prevalence among different species.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of crucial amino acids of bacterial Peptide deformylases affecting enzymatic activity in response to oxidative stress.

mPDF.notes: Mutations in noncatalytic residues of mPDF affect oxidative stress sensitivity.

full_output.paper_title: Multiresistance of Staphylococcus xylosus and Staphylococcus equorum from Slovak Bryndza cheese.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of Mur34 as the novel negative regulator responsible for the biosynthesis of muraymycin in Streptomyces sp. NRRL30471.
full_output.key_findings: Mur34 was identified as a novel negative regulator involved in muraymycin biosynthesis, and its disruption significantly enhances muraymycin production.
full_output.methodology: Mutagenesis, gene expression analysis, EMSA, and DNase I footprinting were used to characterize Mur34's role in regulating muraymycin biosynthesis.

full_output.paper_title: NADPH oxidase deficient mice develop colitis and bacteremia upon infection with normally avirulent, TTSS-1- and TTSS-2-deficient Salmonella Typhimurium.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that NADPH oxidase deficiency in mice leads to increased susceptibility to infection with a normally avirulent Salmonella Typhimurium mutant, highlighting the critical role of NADPH oxidase in mucosal defense against bacterial infections.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized mouse models, bacterial strains, and molecular techniques to investigate the role of NADPH oxidase in defending against Salmonella Typhimurium infections.

full_output.paper_title: Analysis of integrons and associated gene cassettes in clinical isolates of multidrug resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa from Southwest Nigeria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies aadA6-orfD and aadA13 gene cassettes within class 1 integrons in multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from Southwest Nigeria, conferring resistance to streptomycin and spectinomycin.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification, sequencing, and conjugation assays were used to analyze integrons and gene cassettes in P. aeruginosa isolates.

full_output.paper_title: The establishment of a duplex real-time PCR assay for rapid and simultaneous detection of blaNDM and blaKPC genes in bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: A duplex real-time PCR assay was developed for the rapid and simultaneous detection of blaNDM and blaKPC genes in bacteria, showing 100% concordance with conventional PCR.
full_output.methodology: Duplex real-time PCR assay with specific primers and probes for blaNDM and blaKPC genes.

full_output.paper_title: Bovine salmonellosis in northeast of Iran: frequency, genetic fingerprinting and antimicrobial resistance patterns of Salmonella spp.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that 18 out of 19 Salmonella isolates were resistant to oxytetracycline, and five isolates showed multi-drug resistance. Salmonella Typhimurium was the most frequently isolated serovar and exhibited resistance to multiple antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study used ERIC PCR for genetic fingerprinting and disc diffusion method for antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Clonal diversity of Acinetobacter baumannii clinical isolates revealed by a snapshot study.

blaOXA-23.validation_method: detection in isolates with carbapenem resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaOXA-23 as the primary carbapenemase gene in Acinetobacter baumannii isolates, with 40 isolates carrying this gene, including five carbapenem-susceptible ones. Other carbapenemase genes such as blaOXA-51, blaOXA-24, blaOXA-58, and blaOXA-143 were also detected.
full_output.methodology: PCR screening and sequencing of carbapenemase-encoding genes, along with pulsed-field gel electrophoresis (PFGE) and multilocus sequence typing (MLST) for strain characterization.

full_output.paper_title: Methodological comparisons for antimicrobial resistance surveillance in feedlot cattle.
full_output.key_findings: The study compared different methodological approaches for antimicrobial resistance (AMR) surveillance in feedlot cattle, focusing on susceptibility testing methods, target bacteria, and sampling strategies. It found that the choice of susceptibility test significantly affected resistance detection, with broth microdilution and disk diffusion yielding different results. The study also highlighted the importance of selecting appropriate bacterial targets and sampling methods for accurate AMR estimation.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth microdilution and disk diffusion susceptibility testing to assess AMR in non-type-specific E. coli (NTSEC) and Mannheimia haemolytica isolates. It compared resistance prevalence across different testing methods, bacterial organisms, and sampling strategies.
full_output.sample_size: 3362 NTSEC isolates and 1574 M. haemolytica isolates

full_output.paper_title: Burkholderia pseudomallei Isolates from Sarawak, Malaysian Borneo, Are Predominantly Susceptible to Aminoglycosides and Macrolides.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel nonsynonymous mutation in the amrB gene of Burkholderia pseudomallei isolates from Sarawak, Malaysian Borneo, which confers susceptibility to aminoglycosides and macrolides.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, allele-specific PCR, and reversion assays were used to characterize the mutation in amrB and its impact on antibiotic susceptibility.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that combination therapy with vancomycin (VAN) and a β-lactam (BL) significantly improved microbiological eradication of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) bacteremia compared to VAN alone.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective cohort study analyzing patients with MRSA bacteremia treated with VAN alone or in combination with a β-lactam.

full_output.paper_title: Deletion of the β-Acetoacetyl Synthase FabY in Pseudomonas aeruginosa Induces Hypoacylation of Lipopolysaccharide and Increases Antimicrobial Susceptibility.

full_output.key_findings: Deletion of the β-acetoacetyl synthase FabY in Pseudomonas aeruginosa leads to hypoacylation of lipopolysaccharide and increased antimicrobial susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: ARG-ANNOT, a new bioinformatic tool to discover antibiotic resistance genes in bacterial genomes.

rmtF.validation_method: BLAST analysis with short sequences (17 to 40 bp) found in other genes of the rmt family

full_output.key_findings: The paper introduces ARG-ANNOT, a bioinformatic tool designed to identify antibiotic resistance (AR) genes in bacterial genomes. It highlights the ability of ARG-ANNOT to detect a higher number of AR genes compared to existing tools like Resfinder, particularly in Acinetobacter baumannii and Staphylococcus aureus genomes. The tool was validated through various tests, including BLAST analysis of the rmtF gene, demonstrating its effectiveness in identifying AR genes even with partial sequences.
full_output.methodology: ARG-ANNOT was developed using a local BLAST database created with BioEdit. The tool was validated through BLAST analysis of different AR gene sequences and compared with existing databases like Resfinder.

full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and pulsed-field gel electrophoresis were used to characterize carbapenemase genes and genotypes of the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Activities of fosfomycin and rifampin on planktonic and adherent Enterococcus faecalis strains in an experimental foreign-body infection model.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the activities of fosfomycin and rifampin against planktonic and adherent Enterococcus faecalis strains, demonstrating fosfomycin's effectiveness against both forms of the bacteria, particularly in combination with gentamicin.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro and in vivo experiments, including antimicrobial susceptibility testing, time-kill studies, microcalorimetry, and an animal model to evaluate the effects of fosfomycin and rifampin on Enterococcus faecalis.

full_output.paper_title: Low-molecular-mass penicillin binding protein 6b (DacD) is required for efficient GOB-18 metallo-β-lactamase biogenesis in Salmonella enterica and Escherichia coli.

blaDHA-1.evidence_note: blaDHA-1 was identified in 5 K. pneumoniae strains and shown to confer resistance to cefoxitin and carbapenems.

OmpK35.notes: Mutation in OmpK35 gene leads to altered porin structure

OmpK36.notes: Base deletions in OmpK36 gene lead to loss of porin

full_output.paper_title: Extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing enterobacteriaceae in community-acquired urinary tract infections in São Luís, Brazil.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaTEM and blaCTX-M genes as the primary mechanisms of extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL) production in Enterobacteriaceae causing community-acquired urinary tract infections in São Luís, Brazil. These genes conferred resistance to several β-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic analysis using disk diffusion and Vitek 2, along with triplex PCR for detection of blaTEM and blaCTX-M genes.

full_output.paper_title: Frequency of plasmid-mediated AmpC in Enterobacteriaceae isolated in a Brazilian Teaching Hospital.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of the blaCMY-2 gene in a single Klebsiella pneumoniae isolate, indicating plasmid-mediated AmpC beta-lactamase production.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Plasmid-mediated quinolone resistance (PMQR) and mutations in the topoisomerase genes of Salmonella enterica strains from Brazil.

qnrA1.mechanism: protects DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV from quinolone activity

qnrB19.mechanism: protects DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV from quinolone activity

full_output.key_findings: The study identified qnrA1 and qnrB19 genes as plasmid-mediated quinolone resistance determinants in Salmonella enterica strains from Brazil, along with various mutations in the gyrA gene that contribute to ciprofloxacin resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification, sequencing, and analysis of quinolone resistance determinants and topoisomerase gene mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Tivozanib reverses multidrug resistance mediated by ABCB1 (P-glycoprotein) and ABCG2 (BCRP).

ABCB1.validation_method: drug efflux assays, intracellular accumulation assays, ATPase assays

ABCG2.validation_method: drug efflux assays, intracellular accumulation assays

full_output.key_findings: Tivozanib reverses multidrug resistance mediated by ABCB1 and ABCG2 by inhibiting their efflux function without altering protein expression.
full_output.methodology: Drug efflux assays, intracellular accumulation assays, ATPase assays, and western blot analysis were used to evaluate the effects of tivozanib on ABCB1 and ABCG2.

full_output.paper_title: Oxacillin alters the toxin expression profile of community-associated methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: Oxacillin increases the expression of mecA, leading to reduced toxicity in CA-MRSA by repressing the Agr quorum sensing system. However, it also increases the secretion of alpha-toxin and PVL.
full_output.methodology: Experimental validation through qRT-PCR, Western blot, and toxin secretion assays.

full_output.key_findings: The study explores the use of Raman spectroscopy for phenotypic profiling of antibiotic responses in E. coli, demonstrating its capability to distinguish between different antibiotic classes and identify unknown antibiotics based on their phenotypic effects.
full_output.methodology: Raman spectroscopy combined with chemometric analysis was used to analyze the phenotypic responses of E. coli to various antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro and in vivo antibacterial activities of omadacycline, a novel aminomethylcycline.
full_output.key_findings: Omadacycline showed potent in vitro and in vivo activity against a wide range of Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, including those with resistance mechanisms such as ribosomal protection and tetracycline efflux. It was effective against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus (VRE), and other multidrug-resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: In vitro susceptibility testing and in vivo efficacy studies in a murine infection model were conducted.

full_output.paper_title: Response to metronidazole and oxidative stress is mediated through homeostatic regulator HsrA (HP1043) in Helicobacter pylori.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies HsrA (HP1043) as a homeostatic regulator in Helicobacter pylori that mediates the response to metronidazole and oxidative stress. HsrA regulates the expression of genes involved in metabolism and oxidative defense, and its levels are significantly reduced upon exposure to metronidazole and oxidative stress agents.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized protein purification, electrophoretic mobility shift assays (EMSAs), and mutagenesis to identify and characterize HsrA as a transcriptional regulator involved in the response to metronidazole and oxidative stress in H. pylori.

full_output.paper_title: Nafcillin enhances innate immune-mediated killing of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: Nafcillin enhances the killing of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) by cationic host defense peptides (HDPs) such as LL-37, hNP-1, and RP-1. This effect is observed in vitro and ex vivo, and translates to reduced MRSA virulence in a murine infection model.
full_output.methodology: Ex vivo and in vivo studies examining the effect of nafcillin on MRSA susceptibility to HDPs and innate immune cells.

full_output.paper_title: Reduced vancomycin susceptibility in porcine ST9 MRSA isolates.

mutations_found.nucleotide_change: four successive mutations at base numbers 672−5
insertion of a codon coding for isoleucine

full_output.paper_title: Investigation of Biofilm Formation and its Association with the Molecular and Clinical Characteristics of Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the fnbB gene as being significantly more prevalent in biofilm-forming MRSA strains compared to non-biofilm-forming strains, indicating a potential link between the presence of this gene and biofilm formation capabilities.
full_output.methodology: PCR, biofilm formation assay, and statistical analysis were used to evaluate the molecular and clinical characteristics of MRSA isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that the majority of Staphylococcus aureus infections in New Zealand were caused by methicillin-susceptible S. aureus (MSSA), with a significant increase in community-associated non-invasive MSSA infections. Methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) infections remained stable, leading to a decrease in their contribution to the overall burden of S. aureus disease.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed S. aureus infections in patients admitted to Auckland District Health Board over an 11-year period, using laboratory databases and hospital administrative records to determine incidence, trends, and demographic factors.

full_output.paper_title: De novo design and synthesis of ultra-short peptidomimetic antibiotics having dual antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory activities.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the design and synthesis of ultra-short peptidomimetic antibiotics (HDAMPs) with dual antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory activities. HDAMPs showed potent antimicrobial activity against various bacterial strains, including MRSA, and exhibited anti-inflammatory effects by inhibiting NO and TNF-α production. They also demonstrated proteolytic resistance, making them promising candidates for future antimicrobial therapies.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the design, synthesis, and evaluation of HDAMPs for antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory activities through various assays including MIC determination, hemolysis testing, LPS neutralization, and proteolytic stability assessments.

full_output.paper_title: Transformation of sexually transmitted infection-causing serovars of chlamydia trachomatis using Blasticidin for selection.

bsd.validation_method: transformation and detection of GFP-BSD fusion protein
bsd.evidence_note: The BSD gene was cloned from the vector pLenti6.3_V5-TOPO and fused to the downstream of the GFP gene in pGFPBSD/Z::SW2.

full_output.key_findings: The study describes the construction of a novel shuttle vector, pGFPBSD/Z::SW2, which incorporates the bsd gene for blasticidin resistance and the shble gene for zeocin resistance, enabling the transformation of plasmid-free C. trachomatis serovar D.
full_output.methodology: Vector construction, transformation, and detection of GFP-BSD fusion protein.

full_output.paper_title: Changes in the expression of miR-381 and miR-495 are inversely associated with the expression of the MDR1 gene and development of multi-drug resistance.

MDR1.mechanism: miR-381 and miR-495 target the 3'-UTR of MDR1, reducing its expression and P-gp levels
MDR1.validation_method: stem-loop real-time PCR, FACS analysis, EGFP reporter assay

full_output.key_findings: miR-381 and miR-495 are down-regulated in MDR leukemia cells and negatively correlate with MDR1/P-gp expression, suggesting their role in modulating drug resistance.
full_output.methodology: Next-generation sequencing, stem-loop real-time PCR, FACS analysis, EGFP reporter assay, and miR transfection experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Nasal carriage of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus among pediatricians in Taiwan.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that 6.8% of pediatricians in Taiwan were colonized with community-associated methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (CA-MRSA). All 12 MRSA isolates were susceptible to vancomycin, teicoplanin, linezolid, fusidic acid, trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole, and doxycyclin, and resistant to penicillin.
full_output.methodology: Nasal swabs were collected and analyzed using PCR, culture, PFGE, MLST, SCC mec typing, and PVL gene detection. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the disk-diffusion method.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies D-alanine-D-alanine ligase (Ddl) as the primary lethal target of D-cycloserine (DCS) in mycobacteria, demonstrating that DCS inhibits Ddl, leading to the accumulation of D-alanyl-D-alanine and disruption of peptidoglycan synthesis.
full_output.methodology: Metabolomics analysis using NMR spectroscopy and bioinformatics to determine the mechanism of action of DCS in mycobacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Low Helicobacter pylori primary resistance to clarithromycin in gastric biopsy specimens from dyspeptic patients of a city in the interior of São Paulo, Brazil.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified low primary resistance of Helicobacter pylori to clarithromycin in gastric biopsy specimens from dyspeptic patients in Marilia, Brazil, with A2142G and A2143G mutations in the 23S rRNA gene being the main causes of resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR/RFLP assay and sequencing were used to detect A2142G and A2143G mutations in the 23S rRNA gene of H. pylori.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies three mosaic penA alleles (XXXIV, XXXVIII, and LA-A) in Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates with reduced susceptibility to extended-spectrum cephalosporins, with the mosaic XXXIV allele showing the strongest association with elevated MICs.
full_output.methodology: Molecular detection of mosaic penA alleles via real-time PCR and DNA sequencing, along with antimicrobial susceptibility testing using Etest.

full_output.paper_title: MDR1 synonymous polymorphisms alter transporter specificity and protein stability in a stable epithelial monolayer.
full_output.key_findings: Synonymous polymorphisms in the MDR1 gene alter P-gp conformation and stability, leading to differences in drug efflux and resistance to mitoxantrone.
full_output.methodology: Drug efflux assays, cytotoxicity assays, and protein stability experiments were conducted in stable cell lines expressing wild-type and variant forms of P-gp.

full_output.paper_title: Fitness cost associated with resistance to fluoroquinolones is diverse across clones of Klebsiella pneumoniae and may select for CTX-M-15 type extended-spectrum β-lactamase.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies blaCTX-M-15 as a gene conferring resistance to ceftazidime and cefotaxime in Klebsiella pneumoniae. Mutations in gyrA (Ser83Leu) and parC (Ser80Ile) were found to contribute to fluoroquinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing of QRDRs, MIC testing, and plasmid analysis were used to identify AMR genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of NDM-producing non-baumannii Acinetobacter spp. isolated from China.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the emergence of NDM-1-producing non-baumannii Acinetobacter spp., including A. nosocomialis and A. pittii, in China. It identifies novel bla ADC genes (bla ADC-69, bla ADC-70, and bla ADC-71) and confirms the presence of bla NDM-1 on a plasmid.
full_output.methodology: PCR, DNA sequencing, conjugation experiments, PFGE, MLST, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Analysis of quinolone-resistance in commensal and diarrheagenic Escherichia coli isolates from infants in Lima, Peru.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the aac(6')-Ib-cr and qnrB genes as important contributors to quinolone resistance in commensal and diarrheagenic E. coli isolates from infants in Lima, Peru.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze quinolone resistance mechanisms.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the pharmacological properties of 7-(4-(piperazin-1-yl)) ciprofloxacin derivatives, focusing on their antibacterial activity, cellular accumulation, susceptibility to efflux transporters, and intracellular activity. It highlights that N-benzyl-ciprofloxacin (4) shows high cellular accumulation in macrophages and is not significantly affected by efflux transporters like Mrp4, but it does not exhibit higher potency against intracellular bacteria compared to ciprofloxacin.
full_output.methodology: The study synthesized and characterized ciprofloxacin derivatives, determined their minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs), assessed cellular accumulation, and evaluated their intracellular activity against bacterial strains.

full_output.paper_title: Bacterial profile and antimicrobial susceptibility pattern of isolates among burn patients at Yekatit 12 Hospital Burn Center, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bacterial isolates including Coagulase negative Staphylococci, Staphylococcus aureus, Bacillus spp., Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, with high rates of antimicrobial resistance to Ampicillin, Doxycycline, Nalidixic acid, Penicillin G, and Tetracycline.
full_output.methodology: Cross-sectional study involving blood and wound swab cultures, with antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the disc diffusion method.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the mecA gene as a key determinant of methicillin resistance in coagulase-negative Staphylococcus (CoNS) isolates from neonates in a Brazilian NICU, with a significant increase in resistance at discharge compared to admission.
full_output.methodology: PCR for mecA detection, antimicrobial susceptibility testing via disk diffusion, and SCCmec typing.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the genetic diversity and drug resistance patterns of Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates in Iran, highlighting the dominance of Ural, CAS, and T families. It found that Beijing strains were strongly associated with multidrug resistance (MDR), while Ural family isolates showed minimal MDR. The study also noted the geographical distribution of these strains.
full_output.methodology: The study used spoligotyping and drug susceptibility testing to characterize M. tuberculosis isolates from five provinces in Iran.

full_output.paper_title: Structural and Functional Analysis of T6SS Family 4 Endopeptidase Effectors and Their Immunity Proteins
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the peptidoglycan endopeptidases Ssp1 and Ssp2 from Serratia marcescens and their corresponding immunity proteins Rap1a and Rap2a, revealing their structural and functional properties in the context of the type VI secretion system.
full_output.methodology: Structural and biochemical analyses, including crystallography, mutagenesis, and peptidoglycan cleavage assays.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies DsbP, a novel domain-swapped dimeric protein-disulfide isomerase encoded by multidrug resistance IncA/C plasmids, which plays a role in conjugative plasmid transfer and exhibits unique structural and functional properties.
full_output.methodology: Structural analysis and functional assays of DsbP, including crystallography, redox potential measurement, and disulfide isomerase activity tests.

full_output.paper_title: Meleagrin, a new FabI inhibitor from Penicillium chryosogenum with at least one additional mode of action.
full_output.key_findings: Meleagrin was identified as a new FabI inhibitor with potential for treating multidrug-resistant bacteria. It exhibits selectivity for FabI over FabK and inhibits fatty acid synthesis, suggesting additional targets beyond FabI.
full_output.methodology: Screening of microbial extracts, purification of meleagrin, biochemical assays, and evaluation of antibacterial activity.

full_output.paper_title: Proteomic and genomic analyses of antimony resistant Leishmania infantum mutant.

MRPA.validation_method: transfection of its gene conferred antimony resistance in wild-type cells

LinJ.33.1810.notes: The mutation was confirmed by conventional PCR and DNA resequencing.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the ABC transporter MRPA as a key contributor to antimony resistance in Leishmania infantum through proteomic and genomic analyses. Additionally, a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) in the protein kinase gene LinJ.33.1810 was found to be associated with antimony resistance.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative proteomics using SILAC and whole genome sequencing were employed to identify differentially expressed proteins and genetic alterations in the antimony-resistant mutant.

full_output.paper_title: Substitutions in penicillin-binding protein 1 in amoxicillin-resistant Helicobacter pylori strains isolated from Korean patients.

mutations_found.validated_by: natural transformation of pbp1 gene into amoxicillin-susceptible strains

pbp1.notes: Only mutations in the N-terminal region of pbp1 were associated with amoxicillin resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple amino acid substitutions in the penicillin-binding protein 1 (PBP1) of amoxicillin-resistant Helicobacter pylori strains, with specific mutations in the N-terminal region contributing to amoxicillin resistance.
full_output.methodology: DNA sequencing and natural transformation of pbp1 gene into amoxicillin-susceptible strains.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of antibiotic resistance in enterococci isolated from urinary tract infections, with E. faecium showing greater resistance compared to E. faecalis. Several virulence genes including gelE, asa1, cpd, ace, and esp were prevalent among the isolates.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing via disk diffusion and agar dilution, along with multiplex PCR for virulence gene detection.

full_output.paper_title: First identification of coexistence of blaNDM-1 and blaCMY-42 among Escherichia coli ST167 clinical isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first identification of coexistence of blaNDM-1 and blaCMY-42 in Escherichia coli ST167 clinical isolates, highlighting the spread of these resistance genes in Enterobacteriaceae.
full_output.methodology: PCR, DNA sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and plasmid transfer experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis of 3-(3-aryl-pyrrolidin-1-yl)-5-aryl-1,2,4-triazines that have antibacterial activity and also inhibit inorganic pyrophosphatase.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis of 3-(3-aryl-pyrrolidin-1-yl)-5-aryl-1,2,4-triazine derivatives that show antibacterial activity against drug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, Mycobacterium tuberculosis, and Bacillus anthracis. Compound 22h exhibited potent antibiotic activity against a wide range of drug-resistant S. aureus strains without cytotoxicity to mammalian cells.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis of triazine derivatives and evaluation of their antibacterial activity against various pathogens, along with assessment of their ability to inhibit inorganic pyrophosphatase.

full_output.paper_title: Exposure of Escherichia coli ATCC 12806 to sublethal concentrations of food-grade biocides influences its ability to form biofilm, resistance to antimicrobials, and ultrastructure.
full_output.key_findings: Exposure of E. coli ATCC 12806 to sublethal concentrations of food-grade biocides led to increased resistance to antibiotics, particularly aminoglycosides, cephalosporins, and quinolones. Adaptation to sodium nitrite (SNI) and sodium hypochlorite (SHY) enhanced biofilm formation and resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed the effects of biocides on E. coli's biofilm formation, antibiotic resistance, and ultrastructure using microscopic and susceptibility testing methods.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis, antimycobacterial activity and in vitro cytotoxicity of 5-chloro-N-phenylpyrazine-2-carboxamides.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimycobacterial activity of 30 5-chloro-N-phenylpyrazine-2-carboxamide derivatives against Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv, M. kansasii, and M. avium strains. Several compounds exhibited potent activity with MIC values ranging from 1.56 to 6.25 µg/mL. Compounds with hydroxyl substitutions showed reduced cytotoxicity. Compound 30 displayed non-toxic properties in in vitro models.
full_output.methodology: Chemical synthesis, in vitro antimycobacterial activity testing, and cytotoxicity assessment in HepG2, CHO-K1, and ACHN cell lines.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of genes involved in low aminoglycoside-induced SOS response in Vibrio cholerae: a role for transcription stalling and Mfd helicase.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies genes involved in the SOS response induced by sub-MIC aminoglycosides in Vibrio cholerae, highlighting the role of helicases and repair enzymes in managing DNA damage.
full_output.methodology: Genetic screening, deletion mutants, and over-expression analyses were used to identify genes involved in the SOS response.

full_output.paper_title: Modulation of cell wall synthesis and susceptibility to vancomycin by the two-component system AirSR in Staphylococcus aureus NCTC8325.

mutations_found.position_in_molecule: upstream and downstream regions of airSR

airSR.notes: Inactivation of airSR leads to reduced viability in vancomycin.

full_output.key_findings: The airSR mutant exhibited reduced autolysis and down-regulation in many cell wall metabolism-related genes in S. aureus NCTC8325. AirR can directly bind to the promoter region of some of these cell wall metabolism genes, demonstrating that AirSR is a positive regulator in cell wall biosynthesis and turnover. The airSR mutant showed reduced viability in the presence of vancomycin.
full_output.methodology: Microarray analysis, real-time RT PCR, gel shift assays, and construction of mutant and complementary strains.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial effects of the tellurium compound OTD on E. coli isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The tellurium compound OTD exhibits potent antibacterial activity against E. coli isolates, including those resistant to β-lactam antibiotics. OTD effectively inhibits bacterial growth, biofilm formation, and causes cellular damage.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antibacterial effects of OTD using MIC/MBC assays, agar diffusion tests, growth curve analyses, biofilm inhibition assays, and microscopic techniques (SEM, TEM, XRMA).

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of Escherichia coli sequence type 131 isolates producing KPC-2 carbapenemase in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the emergence of KPC-2-producing Escherichia coli sequence type 131 isolates in China, highlighting the spread of carbapenem resistance through the blaKPC-2 gene.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification, sequencing, and molecular typing techniques were used to identify and characterize the blaKPC-2 gene and its genetic environment.

full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the clinical significance of inducible clindamycin resistance in beta-hemolytic streptococci, demonstrating that clindamycin fails to eradicate infections in an animal model and in human cases.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a neutropenic mouse thigh infection model and analyzed clinical cases of patients with beta-hemolytic streptococcal infections treated with clindamycin.

full_output.paper_title: Diarrheagenic enteroaggregative Escherichia coli causing urinary tract infection and bacteremia leading to sepsis.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports on a case of enteroaggregative Escherichia coli (EAEC) causing urinary tract infection and bacteremia leading to sepsis, highlighting the potential of EAEC to cause severe extraintestinal infections.
full_output.methodology: The study characterizes the EAEC isolate through adherence patterns, PFGE, virulence gene analysis, serotyping, MLST, and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the challenges of treating multi-resistant bacteria in leukemic and hematopoietic stem cell transplant recipients, emphasizing the use of colistin, tigecycline, fosfomycin, and other non-conventional antibiotics. It highlights the need for targeted therapy based on in vitro susceptibility data and the limitations of existing antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews published literature and expert opinions to provide guidelines for the treatment of infections caused by multi-resistant bacteria in immunocompromised patients.

full_output.paper_title: Evolution and genetic diversity of the Spain23F-ST81 clone causing adult invasive pneumococcal disease in Barcelona (1990-2012).

pbp2x.mechanism: chromosomal mutation leading to penicillin resistance

pbp2b.mechanism: chromosomal mutation leading to penicillin resistance

erm(B).mechanism: chromosomal mutation leading to macrolide resistance

tet(M).mechanism: chromosomal mutation leading to tetracycline resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study characterized chromosomal mutations in pbp2x and pbp2b contributing to penicillin resistance, and identified erm(B) and tet(M) genes associated with macrolide and tetracycline resistance in the PMEN1 clone.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification, sequencing, and analysis of resistance genes and mutations in pneumococcal isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Suppression of type 1 pilus assembly in uropathogenic Escherichia coli by chemical inhibition of subunit polymerization.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes a small molecule inhibitor, AL1, that suppresses type 1 pilus assembly in uropathogenic Escherichia coli by targeting the subunit polymerization step in the chaperone-usher pathway.
full_output.methodology: The study uses in silico screening, in vitro DSE inhibition assays, biofilm formation assays, ELISA, electron microscopy, and yeast agglutination assays to validate the inhibitory effects of AL1 on type 1 pilus biogenesis.

full_output.paper_title: Lincomycin biosynthesis involves a tyrosine hydroxylating heme protein of an unusual enzyme family.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies LmbB2 as a heme protein involved in the biosynthesis of lincomycin, catalyzing the hydroxylation of tyrosine to 3,4-dihydroxyphenylalanine (DOPA).
full_output.methodology: Expression, purification, and biochemical characterization of the LmbB2 protein in E. coli, along with spectrometric and enzymatic assays.

full_output.paper_title: Both group 4 capsule and lipopolysaccharide O-antigen contribute to enteropathogenic Escherichia coli resistance to human α-defensin 5.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies gfcA and waaL as contributing to resistance against human α-defensin 5 (HD-5) in EPEC, highlighting the role of group 4 capsule and lipopolysaccharide O-antigen in AMP resistance.
full_output.methodology: qPCR, mutant construction, susceptibility assays, and polysaccharide purification.

full_output.paper_title: Whole genome sequencing reveals complex evolution patterns of multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis Beijing strains in patients.

fabG1/inhA.evidence_note: The paper mentions that the mutation inhA (-15C>T) confers resistance to ethionamide.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified various mutations in genes associated with drug resistance in multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis Beijing strains, including mutations in gyrA, rpoB, rpsL, rrs, katG, pncA, eis, thyA, thyX, alr, embB, ethA, and Rv0565c, which confer resistance to fluoroquinolones, rifampicin, streptomycin, kanamycin, capreomycin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, para-aminosalicylic acid, cycloserine, ethambutol, prothionamide, and ethionamide.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing (WGS) and Sanger sequencing were used to identify and validate mutations in drug resistance genes in Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates from patients undergoing MDR-TB treatment.
full_output.sample_size: Three patients (A, B, C) with multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

full_output.paper_title: In silico assigned resistance genes confer Bifidobacterium with partial resistance to aminoglycosides but not to β-lactams.

Bbr_0651.validation_method: insertional inactivation and disc diffusion assay

Bbr_1586.validation_method: insertional inactivation and disc diffusion assay

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Bbr_0651 and Bbr_1586 as contributing to aminoglycoside resistance in B. breve UCC2003, while putative β-lactamase genes do not confer resistance to β-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: In silico analysis, insertional inactivation, disc diffusion assays, and MIC tests.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic use and resistance in emerging economies: a situation analysis for Viet Nam.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies various AMR genes and mutations associated with resistance to multiple antibiotic classes in Vietnam, highlighting the widespread prevalence of multidrug-resistant pathogens such as Enterobacteriaceae, Staphylococcus aureus, and Streptococcus pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzes data from hospital and community-based studies, along with surveillance reports, to evaluate patterns of antibiotic use and resistance in Vietnam.

full_output.paper_title: Vancomycin and daptomycin minimum inhibitory concentration distribution and occurrence of heteroresistance among methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus blood isolates in Turkey.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that 13.7% of MRSA blood isolates in Turkey were heteroresistant to vancomycin (hVISA), with higher prevalence among isolates having vancomycin MICs >1 μg/ml. No vancomycin or daptomycin resistance was detected, and daptomycin remained effective against hVISA isolates.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing using broth microdilution (BMD) and Etest methods, along with screening for hVISA using macro Etest (MET) and population analysis profile-area under the curve (PAP-AUC) methods.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic resistance, virulence determinants and production of biogenic amines among enterococci from ovine, feline, canine, porcine and human milk.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that enterococci isolated from milk of various mammals showed a wide genetic diversity and harbored various virulence determinants. However, none of the strains were resistant to vancomycin, and all were susceptible to tigecycline, linezolid, and vancomycin.
full_output.methodology: The study used molecular typing techniques, including MLST, and antibiotic susceptibility testing via E-test to analyze the enterococcal isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization of multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolated from south-central in China.

rpoB.mechanism: mutation in the RIF resistance-determining region (RRDR)

katG.mechanism: mutation at codon 315

rpoB.notes: mutations in the rpoB gene are associated with rifampicin resistance

katG.notes: mutations in the katG gene are associated with isoniazid resistance

inhA.notes: mutations in the inhA gene are associated with isoniazid resistance
