full_output.paper_title: High antimicrobial effectiveness with low hemolytic and cytotoxic activity for PEG/quaternary copolyoxetanes.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial effectiveness of various PEG/quaternary copolyoxetanes, identifying C8-50 as the most effective against E. coli, S. aureus, and P. aeruginosa with low hemolytic and cytotoxic activity.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial testing, MIC assays, and cytotoxicity evaluations were conducted using bacterial strains and human cells.

full_output.paper_title: Multi-centre evaluation of real-time multiplex PCR for detection of carbapenemase genes OXA-48, VIM, IMP, NDM and KPC.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a real-time multiplex PCR assay for detecting the most prevalent carbapenemase genes, including blaOXA-48, blaVIM, blaIMP, blaNDM, and blaKPC, demonstrating high sensitivity and specificity.
full_output.methodology: Real-time multiplex PCR assay for detection of carbapenemase genes in various bacterial isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Prevention of Clostridium difficile spore formation by sub-inhibitory concentrations of tigecycline and piperacillin/tazobactam.
full_output.key_findings: Sub-inhibitory concentrations of tigecycline and piperacillin/tazobactam significantly reduced spore formation in most Clostridium difficile isolates, whereas vancomycin and metronidazole had minimal effects. Ciprofloxacin inhibited sporulation in ribotype 027 isolates.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing, sporulation assays, and microscopic evaluation of spore formation in C. difficile isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance and characterisation of staphylococci isolated from healthy Labrador retrievers in the United Kingdom.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the mecA gene as a key determinant of methicillin resistance in various coagulase-negative staphylococci (CoNS) species isolated from healthy Labrador retrievers. Methicillin-resistant CoNS were prevalent, with mecA-positive isolates detected in multiple species, highlighting the importance of this gene in antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, MIC testing, and MALDI-TOF-MS were used to identify and characterize antimicrobial resistance genes and staphylococcal species.

full_output.paper_title: Genotypic characterization of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus strains isolated from the anterior nares and catheter of ambulatory hemodialysis patients in Mexico.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterized methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) strains from the anterior nares and catheters of ambulatory hemodialysis patients in Mexico, identifying various adhesion genes and virulence markers associated with MRSA strains.
full_output.methodology: The study used pulsed-field gel electrophoresis (PFGE), PCR detection of adhesion genes, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing to characterize MRSA isolates.

full_output.paper_title: PCR-Based Detection of Extended-Spectrum β-Lactamases (bla CTX-M-1 and bla TEM ) in Escherichia coli, Salmonella spp. and Klebsiella pneumoniae Isolated from Pigs in North Eastern India (Mizoram).
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of blaCTX-M-1 and blaTEM genes in Escherichia coli isolates from pigs in Mizoram, India, indicating the occurrence of extended-spectrum beta-lactamases (ESBLs) in livestock.
full_output.methodology: PCR and phenotypic confirmation using double disc synergy test.

full_output.paper_title: Efflux pumps of Gram-negative bacteria: what they do, how they do it, with what and how to deal with them.

full_output.paper_title: Strategies and molecular tools to fight antimicrobial resistance: resistome, transcriptome, and antimicrobial peptides.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses strategies to combat antimicrobial resistance, focusing on the resistome, transcriptome, and antimicrobial peptides (AMPs). It highlights the challenges posed by resistance mechanisms in bacteria and explores the potential of AMPs as alternatives to traditional antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews current research on antimicrobial resistance mechanisms, the role of the resistome, and the potential of antimicrobial peptides as novel therapeutic agents.

full_output.paper_title: Performance of the MTBDRsl assay in Georgia.

MTBDR sl assay and conventional DST

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the performance of the MTBDR sl assay in detecting resistance to fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, and other second-line drugs in Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates from Georgia. Key mutations associated with resistance included D94G and A90V in gyrA for fluoroquinolone resistance, and A1401G in rrs for aminoglycoside resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used the MTBDR sl assay combined with conventional drug susceptibility testing (DST) to evaluate resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of extended-spectrum-β-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli ST131 and ST405 clonal groups by matrix-assisted laser desorption ionization-time of flight mass spectrometry.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the performance of MALDI-TOF MS for detecting ESBL-producing E. coli ST131 and ST405 clonal groups, demonstrating high detection accuracy for these groups.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified a clonal variant of EMRSA-16 that contributed to a healthcare-associated outbreak of meticillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus bacteraemia. This variant exhibited low genetic diversity and was associated with increased neutrophil counts in affected patients.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic & genotypic characterization of vancomycin resistant Enterococcus isolates from clinical specimens.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified vanA as the most common vancomycin resistance gene in Enterococcus isolates, with 96.87% of VRE isolates carrying this gene. Additionally, a single isolate was found to possess both vanA and vanC1 genes, indicating complex resistance mechanisms.

full_output.key_findings: OXA-1 and OXA-24 β-lactamases exhibit distinct inhibition mechanisms by penems, with OXA-1 being effectively inhibited while OXA-24 shows resistance due to differences in the stability of the active site carboxylated lysine.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated phenotypic detection methods for metallo-beta-lactamases (MBLs) in Pseudomonas aeruginosa clinical isolates, identifying blaIMP and blaVIM genes as the primary MBL producers.
full_output.methodology: The study used multiplex PCR to detect blaIMP and blaVIM genes in 133 meropenem-non-susceptible P. aeruginosa isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Ferredoxin Gene Mutation in Iranian Trichomonas vaginalis Isolates.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: reduces translational regulatory protein's binding affinity leading to decreased ferredoxin expression

ferredoxin.notes: Mutation at nucleotide -239 ferredoxin gene reduces translational regulatory protein's binding affinity which concludes reduction of ferredoxin expression. For this reduction, decrease in activity and decrease in metronidazole drug delivery into the cells occur. Mutations in these four isolates may lead to resistance of them to metronidazole.

full_output.key_findings: A point mutation at nucleotide position -239 of the ferredoxin gene was detected in 8.69% of Iranian Trichomonas vaginalis isolates, which is associated with reduced ferredoxin expression and metronidazole resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification and sequencing of the ferredoxin gene from clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Reversal effect of ST6GAL 1 on multidrug resistance in human leukemia by regulating the PI3K/Akt pathway and the expression of P-gp and MRP1.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that ST6GAL1 is involved in multidrug resistance (MDR) in human leukemia cells by regulating the PI3K/Akt pathway and the expression of P-gp and MRP1.
full_output.methodology: Real-time PCR, Western blotting, shRNA silencing, and MTT assay were used to evaluate the role of ST6GAL1 in MDR.

full_output.paper_title: The RNA chaperone Hfq is involved in stress tolerance and virulence in uropathogenic Proteus mirabilis.

hfq.notes: The hfq gene was deleted, leading to increased susceptibility to multiple antibiotics.

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that the Hfq gene is involved in stress tolerance and virulence in uropathogenic Proteus mirabilis. Deletion of hfq leads to increased susceptibility to multiple antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Gene knockout, real-time RT-PCR, and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to analyze the role of Hfq in P. mirabilis.

full_output.paper_title: The role of the Staphylococcal VraTSR regulatory system on vancomycin resistance and vanA operon expression in vancomycin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that the VraTSR regulatory system enhances the expression of the vanA operon, contributing to vancomycin resistance in VRSA strains.
full_output.methodology: Deletion of the vraTSR operon and subsequent complementation, along with qRT-PCR and MIC determination.

full_output.key_findings: The study found a high rate of mecillinam treatment failure in community-acquired urinary tract infections (CA-UTI) caused by ESBL-producing E. coli. ESBL-producing strains had higher mecillinam MICs and were associated with increased treatment failure rates.
full_output.methodology: Population-based study with microbiological data and statistical analysis of treatment outcomes.

full_output.paper_title: Penam sulfones and β-lactamase inhibition: SA2-13 and the importance of the C2 side chain length and composition.

blaSHV-1.evidence_note: The paper describes the inhibition of SHV-1 β-lactamase by SA2-13 and its derivatives, but does not explicitly state that blaSHV-1 confers resistance to any specific antibiotics.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the β-lactamase SHV-1 and its inhibitor-resistant variant SHV-K234R, demonstrating that SA2-13 effectively inhibits both wild-type and resistant variants through the formation of a trans-enamine intermediate.
full_output.methodology: Kinetic assays, crystallography, and molecular modeling were used to evaluate the inhibition of SHV-1 and SHV-K234R by SA2-13 and its analogs.

full_output.paper_title: The RNA chaperone Hfq impacts growth, metabolism and production of virulence factors in Yersinia enterocolitica.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that the RNA chaperone Hfq influences growth, metabolism, and production of virulence factors in Yersinia enterocolitica, particularly affecting urease and yersiniabactin production.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized genetic manipulation, proteomic analysis, and biochemical assays to investigate the role of Hfq in Y. enterocolitica.

full_output.paper_title: Genotypically different clones of Staphylococcus aureus are diverse in the antimicrobial susceptibility patterns and biofilm formations.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that genotypically different clones of S. aureus exhibit varied antimicrobial susceptibility patterns, with tigecycline and daptomycin showing the most effectiveness. Biofilms were found to be resistant to high concentrations of most antibiotics, with daptomycin being the most effective against adhesive biofilms.
full_output.methodology: The study used macrobroth dilution and E test system for susceptibility testing, and confocal laser scanning microscopy for biofilm analysis.

full_output.paper_title: NDM-1-producing strains, family Enterobacteriaceae, in hospital, Beijing, China.

blaNDM-1.validation_method: PCR amplification and E-test MIC measurement

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies NDM-1-producing Enterobacteriaceae strains, including E. coli, K. pneumoniae, Providencia rettgeri, Enterobacter cloacae, and Raoultella ornithinolytica, highlighting the presence of blaNDM-1 gene and its association with carbapenem resistance.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective surveillance, PCR amplification, E-test, S1 nuclease pulsed-field gel electrophoresis, and multilocus sequence typing.

full_output.key_findings: The study developed a rapid and simple loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) assay targeting orfX for the detection of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA).
full_output.methodology: The study developed and validated an orfX-LAMP assay for MRSA detection, comparing it with PCR.

full_output.paper_title: Rationale for eliminating Staphylococcus breakpoints for β-lactam agents other than penicillin, oxacillin or cefoxitin, and ceftaroline.

blaZ.evidence_note: Mutations reported in this review paper are sourced from cited studies. Original experimental data is in the referenced publications.

mecA.genetic_context: carried on the mobile staphylococcal cassette chromosomal mec element (SCC mec)
mecA.evidence_note: Mutations reported in this review paper are sourced from cited studies. Original experimental data is in the referenced publications.

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the rationale for eliminating breakpoints for β-lactam agents other than penicillin, oxacillin, cefoxitin, and ceftaroline in Staphylococcus species. It highlights the role of β-lactamases like blaZ and mecA-encoded PBP2a in mediating resistance to β-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Literature review and analysis of existing data on β-lactam resistance mechanisms in Staphylococcus species.

full_output.paper_title: Real-time monitoring of New Delhi metallo-β-lactamase activity in living bacterial cells by 1H NMR spectroscopy.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates real-time monitoring of New Delhi metallo-β-lactamase (NDM-1) activity in living bacterial cells using 1H NMR spectroscopy, highlighting its role in carbapenem hydrolysis and identifying potential inhibitors.
full_output.methodology: 1H NMR spectroscopy was used to monitor meropenem hydrolysis by NDM-1 in E. coli cells.

full_output.paper_title: Structural basis for substrate specificity in ArnB. A key enzyme in the polymyxin resistance pathway of Gram-negative bacteria.

arnA.mechanism: involved in the synthesis of UDP-Ara4O

full_output.key_findings: The study elucidates the structural basis of ArnB, a key enzyme in the polymyxin resistance pathway of Gram-negative bacteria, and identifies its role in synthesizing UDP-Ara4N, which is critical for lipid A modification and resistance to polymyxin antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Crystallography, enzymatic synthesis, and biochemical analysis were used to characterize the structure and function of ArnB and its interaction with UDP-Ara4N.

full_output.key_findings: Mitrecin A, an endolysin-like bacteriolytic enzyme, was identified in the genome of Streptomyces sp. strain 212. It exhibits bacteriolytic activity against several Gram-negative bacteria, including medically important genera such as Aeromonas, Escherichia, Salmonella, Shigella, Vibrio, and Yersinia.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, gene annotation, heterologous expression, and functional assays were conducted to characterize Mitrecin A.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic epidemiology of Neisseria gonorrhoeae with reduced susceptibility to cefixime in the USA: a retrospective observational study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mosaic penA alleles, particularly penA XXXIV, as strongly associated with reduced susceptibility to cefixime in Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Additionally, tetM and 23S rRNA mutations were linked to tetracycline and azithromycin resistance, respectively.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and phylogenetic analysis were used to investigate the genetic basis of antimicrobial resistance in Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Benznidazole-resistance in Trypanosoma cruzi: evidence that distinct mechanisms can act in concert.

mutations_found.protein_change: stop codon (TGA) in the middle of the gene
mutations_found.effect_on_function: truncated protein deficient in the putative carboxyl terminal FMN-binding site

TcNTR.notes: Clones 1 and 2 were homozygous, whereas clone 3 had retained a copy of the non-mutated parental allele.
TcNTR.evidence_note: The paper explicitly states that the stop codon-generating mutation in TcNTR is linked to benznidazole-resistance and cross-resistance to nifurtimox.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified a stop-codon-generating mutation in the TcNTR gene linked to benznidazole-resistance in Trypanosoma cruzi, along with additional mechanisms contributing to resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, Southern blotting, Northern blotting, and drug resistance assays.
full_output.sample_size: Three clones from a single parasite population

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the vanA gene as the primary cause of vancomycin resistance in Enterococcus faecium isolates from a Chinese hospital, with all vancomycin-resistant isolates carrying this gene and exhibiting the VanA phenotype.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, rep-PCR, and MLST were used to analyze the molecular characteristics of the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Co-occurrence of carbapenem and aminoglycoside resistance genes among multidrug-resistant clinical isolates of Acinetobacter baumannii from Cracow, Poland.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the prevalence of carbapenem and aminoglycoside resistance genes among multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii isolates in Cracow, Poland. The most prevalent carbapenem resistance genes were bla OXA-40-like, and the dominant aminoglycoside resistance genes were aac(3)-Ia and aph(3′)-VI.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of resistance genes in 61 multidrug-resistant A. baumannii isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Spectinamides: a new class of semisynthetic antituberculosis agents that overcome native drug efflux.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Rv1258c as an efflux pump that mediates resistance to spectinomycin and spectinamides, and shows that modifying spectinomycin to avoid this efflux mechanism enhances its antitubercular activity.
full_output.methodology: Structural modification of spectinomycin, testing against M. tuberculosis strains, and evaluating efflux pump function.

full_output.paper_title: Nonclassical transpeptidases of Mycobacterium tuberculosis alter cell size, morphology, the cytosolic matrix, protein localization, virulence, and resistance to β-lactams.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies ldt Mt1 and ldt Mt2 as nonclassical transpeptidases in Mycobacterium tuberculosis that play a critical role in cell morphology, growth, virulence, and resistance to β-lactams. Loss of these genes leads to increased susceptibility to vancomycin and amoxicillin-clavulanate.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized genetic knockout strains, proteomic analysis, and MIC testing to evaluate the impact of ldt Mt1 and ldt Mt2 on M. tuberculosis physiology and antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Role of Pseudomonas aeruginosa AmpR on β-lactam and non-β-lactam transient cross-resistance upon pre-exposure to subinhibitory concentrations of antibiotics.

ampR.encodes: global antibiotic resistance and virulence regulator

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies AmpR and AmpC as key regulators in β-lactam and non-β-lactam transient cross-resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa upon pre-exposure to subinhibitory concentrations of antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative PCR, MIC testing, and mutant analysis were used to evaluate the role of AmpR and AmpC in antibiotic resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that the use of mupirocin/chlorhexidine significantly reduced methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) infections in intubated patients.
full_output.methodology: Post hoc analysis of a placebo-controlled, randomized trial assessing the effectiveness of mupirocin/chlorhexidine in reducing MRSA infections.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic resistance determinants in a Pseudomonas putida strain isolated from a hospital.

StrA.evidence_note: The gene StrA is described as having aminoglycoside 3′-phosphotransferase activity and is associated with resistance to streptomycin.

aac(6')-Ib.evidence_note: The pPC9 plasmid carries genes that encode 6 aminoglycoside modifying enzymes that are not present in the genome of P. putida strains sensitive to aminoglycosides.

blaAER-1.role_in_paper: identified as a beta-lactamase gene on the pPC9 plasmid
blaAER-1.evidence_note: The gene blaAER-1 is described as a beta-lactamase gene that is 95% identical to AER-1 from Aeromonas hydrophila, which can hydrolyze carbenicillin.

blaVIM-1.evidence_note: The gene blaVIM-1 was identified on the pPC9 plasmid and is responsible for carbapenem resistance.

gyrA.notes: Mutation in gyrA leads to fluoroquinolone resistance.

gyrB.notes: Mutation in gyrB leads to fluoroquinolone resistance.

parC.notes: Mutation in parC leads to fluoroquinolone resistance.

firA.notes: Higher copy number of firA contributes to increased resistance to polymyxin B

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple antibiotic resistance genes in Pseudomonas putida HB3267, including aminoglycoside modifying enzymes, beta-lactamases, and sulfonamide resistance genes, contributing to its multidrug resistance profile.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and comparative genomics were used to identify antibiotic resistance genes in Pseudomonas putida HB3267.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical impact of fluoroquinolone-resistant Escherichia coli in the fecal flora of hematological patients with neutropenia and levofloxacin prophylaxis.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that levofloxacin prophylaxis did not lead to a significant increase in quinolone-resistant E. coli in the fecal flora of neutropenic patients. However, approximately 20% of patients already had quinolone-resistant E. coli before starting prophylaxis.
full_output.methodology: Prospective examination of quinolone-resistant E. coli isolates from stool cultures before and after levofloxacin prophylaxis in neutropenic patients.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid molecular characterization of Acinetobacter baumannii clones with rep-PCR and evaluation of carbapenemase genes by new multiplex PCR in Hospital District of Helsinki and Uusimaa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified OXA-23-like, OXA-58, and OXA-24-like carbapenemase genes as the primary contributors to carbapenem resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii isolates. These genes were detected using a novel multiplex real-time PCR assay, highlighting their prevalence and association with specific clonal lineages.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex real-time PCR assay combined with rep-PCR for clonal analysis and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Risk factors for healthcare-associated extensively drug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii infections: a case-control study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified OXA-23 and OXA-51-like carbapenemase genes as major contributors to carbapenem resistance in XDRAB isolates.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and susceptibility testing were used to characterize resistance genes and mechanisms.

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that the negatively charged regions of LbpB are responsible for protecting Neisseria meningitidis against the cationic antimicrobial peptide lactoferricin. Removal of these regions significantly reduced this protection.
full_output.methodology: The study involved creating mutant LbpB proteins lacking the negatively charged regions, transforming them into N. meningitidis, and assessing their ability to protect against lactoferricin in killing assays.

full_output.paper_title: Application of microarray and functional-based screening methods for the detection of antimicrobial resistance genes in the microbiomes of healthy humans.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various antimicrobial resistance genes in the microbiomes of healthy humans, including erm(B), bla TEM, sul2, acrRAB, and folP, which confer resistance to macrolides, beta-lactams, sulphonamides, and other antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Microarray and functional-based screening methods were used to detect antimicrobial resistance genes in the microbiomes of healthy humans.

full_output.paper_title: A multidisciplinary intervention to reduce infections of ESBL- and AmpC-producing, gram-negative bacteria at a University Hospital.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated a multidisciplinary intervention aimed at reducing infections caused by ESBL- and AmpC-producing gram-negative bacteria. The intervention led to a significant decrease in the incidence of ESBL-producing K. pneumoniae infections and other hospital-associated infections, though some antibiotic-resistant infections increased.
full_output.methodology: The study involved a before-and-after analysis and segmented regression analysis of interrupted time series to assess the impact of the intervention on antimicrobial consumption and infection rates.

full_output.paper_title: In vivo evolution of a catalytic RNA couples trans-splicing to translation.

cat.mechanism: confers resistance to chloramphenicol through acetylation of the antibiotic
cat.validation_method: expression in E. coli and measurement of chloramphenicol resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the cat gene as a key player in chloramphenicol resistance, demonstrating that its expression enables bacterial growth in the presence of chloramphenicol.
full_output.methodology: Experimental evolution of trans-splicing ribozymes in E. coli, including mutagenic PCR, selection for chloramphenicol resistance, and functional analysis of the cat gene.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of epidemiological cut-off values indicates that biocide resistant subpopulations are uncommon in natural isolates of clinically-relevant microorganisms.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that triclosan resistance in Staphylococcus aureus is due to the duplication of the fabI gene, which encodes the triclosan target. However, no significant biocide-resistant subpopulations were found in natural isolates of clinically relevant microorganisms.
full_output.methodology: Broth microdilution method for determining MICs and MBCs, and analysis of gene sequences for resistance mechanisms.

full_output.key_findings: Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) can increase the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of tigecycline against several clinical pathogens in a concentration-dependent manner.
full_output.methodology: Agar dilution and time-kill assays were used to determine the effect of PPIs on tigecycline activity.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of the staphylococcal cassette chromosome composite island of Staphylococcus haemolyticus SH32, a methicillin-resistant clinical isolate from China.

mecA.evidence_note: The paper describes the presence of mecA in the SCC composite island of S. haemolyticus SH32 and confirms its presence through PCR and sequencing.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the SCC composite island in Staphylococcus haemolyticus SH32, identifying the mecA gene conferring methicillin resistance and the ccrA5 and ccrB3 genes involved in SCC element integration.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, PCR, and bioinformatics analysis were used to characterize the SCC composite island and identify resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Conditions Associated with the Cystic Fibrosis Defect Promote Chronic Pseudomonas aeruginosa Infection
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that conditions associated with cystic fibrosis (CF) promote the formation of Pseudomonas aeruginosa aggregates, which are highly resistant to antibiotics and host defenses. These aggregates form due to restricted bacterial motility and are influenced by neutrophil elastase in CF sputum.
full_output.methodology: The study used agar and mucus gels to examine the growth of P. aeruginosa under conditions mimicking CF airways, including the effects of CF sputum and neutrophil elastase.

full_output.paper_title: Community-onset Escherichia coli infection resistant to expanded-spectrum cephalosporins in low-prevalence countries.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla CTX-M genes as the primary resistance mechanism in community-onset ESC-R E. coli infections in Australia and New Zealand.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and case-control analysis.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the crystal structure of the OXA-58 β-lactamase, a major class D carbapenemase in Acinetobacter baumannii, providing insights into its mechanism of carbapenem hydrolysis.
full_output.methodology: X-ray crystallography and biochemical analysis.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated antimicrobial combination therapies against Neisseria gonorrhoeae and found no synergy or antagonism in the tested combinations, including third-generation cephalosporins with azithromycin, doxycycline, gentamicin, rifampicin, or fosfomycin.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic gradient synergy testing (Etest) and agar dilution were used to evaluate antimicrobial combinations.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro anti-mycobacterial activity of (E)-N'-(monosubstituted-benzylidene) isonicotinohydrazide derivatives against isoniazid-resistant strains.

inhA.notes: Mutation in the coding region of inhA

katG.notes: Mutation in the coding region of katG

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the in vitro anti-mycobacterial activity of N-acylhydrazones against isoniazid-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis strains. Derivatives 4, 14, 15, and 16 showed activity against the susceptible strain, while derivative 13 was more active than isoniazid. Compounds were inactive against RGH102, which had a mutation in the inhA gene. Several compounds showed activity against katG-mutant strains, suggesting alternative mechanisms of action.

full_output.paper_title: MDR1 expression predicts outcome of Ph+ chronic phase CML patients on second-line nilotinib therapy after imatinib failure.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that high MDR1 gene expression is associated with improved response to nilotinib therapy in Ph+ chronic phase CML patients who have failed imatinib treatment.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed MDR1 gene expression levels and their correlation with clinical outcomes in CML patients treated with nilotinib after imatinib failure.

full_output.paper_title: 4'-O-substitutions determine selectivity of aminoglycoside antibiotics.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that 4′-O-substitutions in aminoglycosides enhance their selectivity towards bacterial ribosomes over eukaryotic ones, reducing cytotoxicity. Mutations at 16S rRNA positions 1408 and 1491 influence the interaction of aminoglycosides with ribosomes, affecting their antibacterial activity.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized chemical synthesis, MIC assays, ribosomal translation assays, and crystallography to analyze the impact of 4′-O-substitutions and mutations in 16S rRNA on aminoglycoside activity.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibility profiling and genomic diversity of Acinetobacter baumannii isolates: A study in western Iran.

blaOXA-24like.evidence_note: The paper states that bla OXA-24 like was found among 19.2% of the isolates and that all isolates showed high-level resistance to imipenem and meropenem.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla OXA-23like, bla OXA-24like, and bla OXA-51like genes as the primary mechanisms of carbapenem resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii isolates from western Iran.
full_output.methodology: PCR, disk diffusion, and PFGE were used to analyze antimicrobial resistance and genetic diversity.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation of Asian endemic and livestock associated clones of methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus from ocular samples in Northeastern Iran.
full_output.key_findings: Three MRSA isolates were identified from ocular samples in Iran, showing resistance to tetracycline, gentamicin, and clindamycin, but sensitivity to vancomycin, minocycline, and trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole. All isolates were mecA-positive and belonged to SCCmec type IV.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR, and genetic typing methods were used to analyze the MRSA isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Azithromycin may antagonize inhaled tobramycin when targeting Pseudomonas aeruginosa in cystic fibrosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that azithromycin may antagonize the effectiveness of inhaled tobramycin against Pseudomonas aeruginosa in cystic fibrosis patients, leading to reduced lung function improvement and increased need for additional antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed clinical trial data and performed in vitro biofilm experiments to assess the interaction between azithromycin and tobramycin against Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

full_output.paper_title: Aedes aegypti Mos20 cells internalizes cry toxins by endocytosis, and actin has a role in the defense against Cry11Aa toxin.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the actin gene (AAEL005961) as being upregulated in response to Cry11Aa toxin, suggesting a role in the defense mechanism against the toxin in Aedes aegypti Mos20 cells.
full_output.methodology: The study used confocal microscopy, Western blotting, and RNA interference to investigate the role of actin in the response to Cry11Aa toxin.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibility of indicator bacteria isolated from chickens in Southeast Asian countries (Vietnam, Indonesia and Thailand).
full_output.key_findings: The study found high levels of antimicrobial resistance in E. coli, E. faecalis, and E. faecium isolates from chickens in Vietnam, Indonesia, and Thailand, with particular emphasis on tetracycline, fluoroquinolone, and macrolide resistance.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was conducted using the agar dilution method according to CLSI guidelines.
full_output.sample_size: 125 E. coli, 117 E. faecalis, 180 E. faecium

full_output.paper_title: Resistance markers and genetic diversity in Acinetobacter baumannii strains recovered from nosocomial bloodstream infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of multiple AMR genes, including bla VIM-1, bla AmpC, bla OXA23, and bla OXA51, in multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii strains isolated from nosocomial bloodstream infections in Brazil.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic and genotypic methods were used to detect metallo-beta-lactamases, cephalosporinases, and oxacillinases, along with ERIC-PCR for genetic diversity analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial and antibiofilm activities of tryptoquivalines and meroditerpenes isolated from the marine-derived fungi Neosartorya paulistensis, N. laciniosa, N. tsunodae, and the soil fungi N. fischeri and N. siamensis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified aszonapyrone A (4a) and sartorypyrone A (8) as having significant antibacterial activity against Gram-positive bacteria, including multidrug-resistant strains. Both compounds showed effectiveness in inhibiting biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: Isolation and structural elucidation of compounds, followed by antibacterial and antibiofilm activity testing using broth microdilution and disc diffusion methods.

full_output.paper_title: First documented outbreak of KPC-2-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae in Switzerland: infection control measures and clinical management.

blaKPC-2.evidence_note: The paper confirms the presence of the blaKPC-2 gene in K. pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study documents the first outbreak of KPC-2-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae in Switzerland, highlighting the role of the blaKPC-2 gene in carbapenem resistance and the effectiveness of infection control measures.

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that 2-aminoimidazole-based small molecules can reverse phenotypic drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis by dispersing biofilm-like microbial communities, thereby restoring isoniazid susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: Screening of 2-aminoimidazole compounds for their ability to inhibit and disperse M. smegmatis biofilms, followed by testing their efficacy in combination with isoniazid against drug-tolerant M. tuberculosis in various culture conditions.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies ArnT as a lipid A glucosamine transferase required for resistance to cationic antimicrobial peptides in Bordetella bronchiseptica, highlighting its role in bacterial transmission and infection.
full_output.methodology: Generation and analysis of an arnT mutant in B. bronchiseptica strain RB50, along with lipid A purification and mass spectrometry analysis.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies outer membrane protein P5 as essential for serum resistance of both H. influenzae strain Rd and nontypeable H. influenzae (NTHi) clinical isolate NT127, highlighting its role in resisting complement-mediated killing.
full_output.methodology: Construction of P5 mutants, serum bactericidal assays, Western blotting, and flow cytometry were used to assess the role of P5 in complement resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Active efflux influences the potency of quorum sensing inhibitors in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

mexAB-OprM.mechanism: active efflux of quorum sensing inhibitors

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that the MexAB-OprM efflux pump reduces the potency of quorum sensing inhibitors in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, highlighting the importance of efflux mechanisms in the effectiveness of these inhibitors.
full_output.methodology: Use of mutant strains and reporter assays to assess the impact of efflux pumps on quorum sensing inhibitor potency.

full_output.paper_title: Widespread dissemination of class 1 integron components in soils and related ecosystems as revealed by cultivation-independent analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the widespread presence of class 1 integron components, particularly intI1, qacE, and qacEΔ1, in various environmental samples including soils, rhizospheres, digestates, and biofilters. These genes were found to be associated with IncP-1 plasmids, highlighting their role in the dissemination of antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Lack of efflux mediated quinolone resistance in Salmonella enterica serovars Typhi and Paratyphi A.

full_output.methodology: Sequencing of QRDRs, MIC testing, and qRT-PCR were used to assess resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Adaptive change inferred from genomic population analysis of the ST93 epidemic clone of community-associated methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of blaCMY plasmids and their possible role in source attribution of Salmonella enterica serotype Typhimurium infections.

full_output.paper_title: In-feed use of heavy metal micronutrients in U.S. swine production systems and its role in persistence of multidrug-resistant salmonellae.

full_output.methodology: PCR, MIC testing, and statistical analysis were used to identify and validate the roles of pcoA and czcD in heavy metal tolerance.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic stress-induced modulation of the endoribonucleolytic activity of RNase III and RNase G confers resistance to aminoglycoside antibiotics in Escherichia coli.

sasB.notes: Mutations in sasB contribute to antimicrobial tolerance

full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the role of toxin ζ in antimicrobial sensitivity, focusing on its impact on bacterial dormancy and tolerance. It reveals that ζ toxin expression can enhance antimicrobial efficacy by inducing dormancy and altering cellular responses, particularly in the context of (p)ppGpp and GTP levels.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized bacterial strains with various genetic modifications, including deletions of relA, sasA, and sasB, to investigate the effects of ζ toxin expression on antimicrobial sensitivity. Techniques included Western blotting, MIC assays, and genetic transformations.

full_output.paper_title: PrtR homeostasis contributes to Pseudomonas aeruginosa pathogenesis and resistance against ciprofloxacin.

full_output.methodology: Experimental validation of PrtR's role in pathogenesis and resistance through genetic manipulation, RT-qPCR, Western blotting, and EMSA.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular survey of the dissemination of two blaKPC-harboring IncFIA plasmids in New Jersey and New York hospitals.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified two blaKPC-3-harboring IncFIA plasmids, pBK30661 and pBK30683, which contribute to carbapenem resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae and other Enterobacteriaceae.
full_output.methodology: Plasmid sequencing, PCR screening, and susceptibility testing were used to characterize the plasmids and their resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: CvfA protein and polynucleotide phosphorylase act in an opposing manner to regulate Staphylococcus aureus virulence.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that the CvfA protein and polynucleotide phosphorylase (PNPase) act antagonistically to regulate Staphylococcus aureus virulence. Disruption of pnpA suppresses the phenotype of the cvfA-deleted mutant, suggesting that CvfA-generated 3'-phosphorylated RNA resists PNPase-mediated degradation, thereby contributing to virulence.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized bacterial genetics, molecular biology techniques, and biochemical assays to investigate the roles of CvfA and PNPase in S. aureus virulence.

full_output.paper_title: The structure and competitive substrate inhibition of dihydrofolate reductase from Enterococcus faecalis reveal restrictions to cofactor docking.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies two trimethoprim-resistant dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) enzymes, dfrF and dfrK, in Enterococcus faecalis. dfrK contains a Leu28→Trp mutation that causes steric hindrance, contributing to trimethoprim resistance.
full_output.methodology: Structural analysis, homology modeling, and biochemical assays were used to investigate DHFR resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Fluoroquinolone-gyrase-DNA complexes: two modes of drug binding.

full_output.paper_title: Development of a Mycothiol-Specific Fluorescent Biosensor to Monitor Redox Heterogeneity in Mycobacterium tuberculosis During Infection
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a mycothiol-specific fluorescent biosensor, Mrx1-roGFP2, to monitor redox heterogeneity in Mycobacterium tuberculosis during infection. The biosensor was validated to respond specifically to changes in mycothiol redox potential (E MSH ).
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a combination of genetic engineering, fluorescence spectroscopy, and flow cytometry to develop and validate the Mrx1-roGFP2 biosensor.

full_output.paper_title: A single Sfp-type phosphopantetheinyl transferase plays a major role in the biosynthesis of PKS and NRPS derived metabolites in Streptomyces ambofaciens ATCC23877.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies three PPTase genes (alpN, samL0372, and sco6673-like) in Streptomyces ambofaciens ATCC23877, each playing a critical role in the biosynthesis of various secondary metabolites, including kinamycin, antimycin, spiramycin, and coelichelin.

full_output.paper_title: Worldwide susceptibility rates of Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates to cefixime and cefpodoxime: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
full_output.key_findings: This study analyzed the worldwide susceptibility rates of Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates to cefixime and cefpodoxime through a systematic review and meta-analysis. It found that the susceptibility rate to cefixime was 99.8%, while the susceptibility rate to cefpodoxime was 92.8%. Significant variations were observed based on geographic location, gender, and time period.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review and meta-analysis of studies published between 1984 and 2012, focusing on the susceptibility of Neisseria gonorrhoeae to cefixime and cefpodoxime.

full_output.paper_title: Selective alleviation of Mitomycin C sensitivity in lexA3 strains of Escherichia coli demands allele specificity of rif-nal mutations: a pivotal role for rpoB87-gyrA87 mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Carriage of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus by wild urban Norway rats (Rattus norvegicus).

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibility pattern in nosocomial infections caused by Acinetobacter species in Asir Region, Saudi Arabia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high resistance rates to various antibiotics among Acinetobacter species, with 100% sensitivity to Imipramine, Meropenem, and Colistin. Resistance to Nitrofurantoin and Cefoxitin was particularly high.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed 150 nosocomial infections using bacteriological tests, MIC, and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid and specific detection, molecular epidemiology, and experimental virulence of the O16 subgroup within Escherichia coli sequence type 131.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the O16 subgroup within Escherichia coli sequence type 131, highlighting its distinct phylogenetic clade, resistance profile, and virulence potential. It identifies specific mutations in fimH, gyrA, and parC associated with resistance to fluoroquinolones and other antimicrobial agents.

full_output.paper_title: Overall decrease in the susceptibility of Mycoplasma bovis to antimicrobials over the past 30 years in France.

full_output.paper_title: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus colonization: a three-year prospective study in a neonatal intensive care unit in Italy.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a non-multiresistant, tst-positive, ST22-MRSA-IVa strain as endemic in the NICU, along with sporadic or epidemic occurrences of other strains. The ST22-MRSA-IVa strain was found to be prevalent and exhibited specific molecular characteristics.

full_output.paper_title: A method for functional trans-complementation of intracellular Francisella tularensis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies pdpC and ripA as critical genes for Francisella tularensis intracellular survival and host-pathogen interactions, demonstrating their roles in phagosomal escape, cytokine suppression, and intracellular proliferation through functional complementation experiments.
full_output.methodology: Functional trans-complementation using bead-bound bacteria to investigate host-pathogen interactions and gene functionality.

full_output.paper_title: Discovery and optimization of a new class of pyruvate kinase inhibitors as potential therapeutics for the treatment of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on the development of pyruvate kinase (PK) inhibitors as potential therapeutics against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). Several bis-indole compounds were identified as potent inhibitors of MRSA PK, demonstrating strong antibacterial activity. Notably, compound 10d showed high bactericidal activity against MRSA, which was dependent on PK activity.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis and evaluation of bis-indole derivatives as inhibitors of MRSA pyruvate kinase. Enzymatic activity and antibacterial effects were assessed through in vitro assays, and the role of PK in bacterial viability was confirmed using a pyk-deficient mutant strain.

full_output.paper_title: High-density livestock production and molecularly characterized MRSA infections in Pennsylvania.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified associations between CO-PVL-negative MRSA and swine and dairy/veal livestock operations, as well as application of dairy/veal manure to crop fields. It also found that SCN-negative MRSA was linked to livestock production.
full_output.methodology: The study used spa typing, PCR for PVL and scn genes, and logistic regression to analyze associations between livestock production and MRSA infections.

full_output.paper_title: The mthA mutation conferring low-level resistance to streptomycin enhances antibiotic production in Bacillus subtilis by increasing the S-adenosylmethionine pool size.

full_output.paper_title: Regulation of Expression of abcA and Its Response to Environmental Conditions.

full_output.paper_title: A conserved streptococcal membrane protein, LsrS, exhibits a receptor-like function for lantibiotics.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies LsrS, a conserved streptococcal membrane protein, as a receptor-like molecule for the lantibiotic Smb. full_output.paper_title: Deciphering the regulon of Streptomyces coelicolor AbrC3, a positive response regulator of antibiotic production.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies AbrC3 as a positive regulator of antibiotic production in Streptomyces coelicolor, showing that its deletion leads to decreased production of actinorhodin and undecylprodiginine, and that it directly regulates the actII-ORF4 promoter region.

full_output.key_findings: The study found a 9.9% prevalence of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) among S. aureus ocular infections in a Brazilian tertiary health center. MRSA isolates showed higher resistance rates to tobramycin, gentamicin, ciprofloxacin, gatifloxacin, and moxifloxacin compared to methicillin-susceptible S. aureus (MSSA) isolates, with all isolates being susceptible to vancomycin.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of S. aureus isolates from ocular infections using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method for antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Exposure assessment of extended-spectrum beta-lactamases/AmpC beta-lactamases-producing Escherichia coli in meat in Denmark.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several ESBL/AmpC-producing E. coli genotypes in meat, with CMY-2 being the most prevalent. full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic Resistance Pattern among Biofilm Producing and Non Producing Proteus Strains Isolated from Hospitalized Patients; Matter of Hospital Hygiene and Antimicrobial Stewardship.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that infection with Salmonella Typhi strains showing intermediate susceptibility to ciprofloxacin is independently associated with severe typhoid fever.

full_output.paper_title: Ceftaroline activity tested against contemporary Latin American bacterial pathogens (2011).
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the activity of ceftaroline against various bacterial pathogens in Latin America, highlighting its effectiveness against Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pneumoniae, and other Gram-positive bacteria, but noting its lack of activity against ESBL-phenotype strains of Enterobacteriaceae.

full_output.paper_title: Carbapenemase-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae bloodstream infections: lowering mortality by antibiotic combination schemes and the role of carbapenems.

full_output.paper_title: Effect of chlorine exposure on the survival and antibiotic gene expression of multidrug resistant Acinetobacter baumannii in water.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaNDM-1 as the predominant carbapenemase gene in meropenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae isolates.
full_output.methodology: Triple-disk assay and molecular confirmation of blaNDM-1 gene.

full_output.paper_title: Notes from the field: Shigella with decreased susceptibility to azithromycin among men who have sex with men - United States, 2002-2013.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Shigella isolates with decreased susceptibility to azithromycin, primarily due to the presence of mphA and ermB macrolide resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: Analysis of Shigella isolates from public health laboratories and outbreak investigations.

full_output.paper_title: Bacteria, phages and pigs: the effects of in-feed antibiotics on the microbiome at different gut locations.
full_output.key_findings: The study examined the effects of in-feed antibiotics on the swine gut microbiome, identifying changes in bacterial communities and functions, including increased abundance of antibiotic resistance genes such as aminoglycoside O-phosphotransferases and AmpC beta-lactamases.
full_output.methodology: The study used 16S rRNA gene sequencing and metagenomic analysis to characterize the bacterial communities in the swine gut and assess the impact of antibiotics on their composition and function.

full_output.paper_title: Reduction in wound bioburden using a silver-loaded dissolvable microfilm construct.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that silver-loaded dissolvable microfilm constructs effectively reduce bacterial bioburden in wounds, particularly targeting Staphylococcus aureus, without impairing normal wound healing.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized silver-loaded polymeric nanofilms and tested their antimicrobial efficacy in vitro and in vivo using mouse wound models.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports an outbreak of vancomycin-susceptible Enterococcus faecium containing the wild-type vanA gene, which is typically associated with vancomycin resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and susceptibility testing were used to characterize the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of ocular methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus epidermidis isolates belonging predominantly to clonal complex 2 subcluster II.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the prevalence of biofilm-related genes aap and bhp in ocular methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus epidermidis isolates, highlighting their role in biofilm formation and antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized multilocus sequence typing (MLST), SCC mec typing, and detection of biofilm-related genes to analyze the molecular epidemiology and resistance profiles of MRSE isolates.

vanA.mechanism: catalyzes the linkage of d-alanine and d-lactate, replacing the typical d-alanine d-alanine precursor for peptidoglycan, thereby decreasing the affinity of glycopeptide antibiotics for their target site

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the emergence of vancomycin resistance in a vancomycin-susceptible Enterococcus faecium isolate containing the wild-type vanA gene, highlighting a novel mechanism of resistance that can develop in vivo following vancomycin exposure.
full_output.methodology: PCR, MIC testing, plasmid sequencing, and whole-genome sequencing.
full_output.sample_size: 13 hospitals in Ontario and Quebec, with over 95 patients colonized or infected.

full_output.paper_title: Distribution of Strain Type and Antimicrobial Susceptibility of Escherichia coli Isolates Causing Meningitis in a Large Urban Setting in Brazil
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla TEM, bla SHV, and various bla CTX-M genes (CTX-M-2, CTX-M-14, CTX-M-15) in E. coli isolates causing meningitis, which conferred resistance to third-generation cephalosporins.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize AMR genes in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Study the Expression of marA Gene in Ciprofloxacin and Tetracycline Resistant Mutants of Esherichia coli.

marR.notes: Mutation in marR leads to overexpression of marA, contributing to antibiotic resistance.

full_output.key_findings: Mutations in marR lead to overexpression of marA, which contributes to ciprofloxacin and tetracycline resistance in E. coli mutants.
full_output.methodology: Real-time PCR was used to measure marA expression in E. coli mutants with and without marR mutations.

full_output.paper_title: The First Korean Case of Nontuberculous Mycobacterial Lung Disease Caused by Mycobacterium abscessus Subspecies bolletii in a Patient with Bronchiectasis.

erm(41).evidence_note: The isolate has the erm (41) gene with a T28 sequevar, associated with clarithromycin resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the first Korean case of lung disease caused by Mycobacterium abscessus subsp. bolletii, which exhibits resistance to clarithromycin due to the presence of the erm(41) gene with a T28 sequevar.
full_output.methodology: Genotyping for erm(41) polymorphism and rrl mutations, drug susceptibility testing via broth microdilution, and phylogenetic analysis based on rpoB sequences.

full_output.paper_title: High incidence of oxacillin-susceptible mecA-positive Staphylococcus aureus (OS-MRSA) associated with bovine mastitis in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a high prevalence of oxacillin-susceptible mecA-positive Staphylococcus aureus (OS-MRSA) in bovine mastitis cases in China, highlighting the importance of genetic testing alongside phenotypic assays for accurate MRSA identification.
full_output.methodology: PCR, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and molecular typing.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial activity of rifamycins for M. smegmatis with comparison of oxidation and binding to tear lipocalin.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the antibacterial activity of various rifamycin derivatives against Mycobacterium smegmatis, highlighting the impact of oxidation on their efficacy and the protective role of tear lipocalin in preventing oxidation.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized spectroscopic analysis, mass spectrometry, and drug susceptibility testing to evaluate the properties and effects of rifamycins.

full_output.paper_title: Epimerization and substrate gating by a TE domain in β-lactam antibiotic biosynthesis.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the NocTE domain as a dual function epimerase/hydrolase involved in the biosynthesis of nocardicin A, demonstrating its role in epimerizing the C-terminal pHPG residue and hydrolyzing β-lactam-containing substrates.
full_output.methodology: In vitro reconstitution of TE activity, NMR spectroscopy, and HPLC analysis were used to characterize the function of NocTE.

full_output.paper_title: The aetiology and antibiotic management of community-acquired pneumonia in adults in Europe: a literature review.
full_output.key_findings: This review summarizes the aetiology of community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) in adults across Europe and highlights the prevalence of various pathogens, including Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, and others. It also discusses the antibiotic resistance profiles of these pathogens, noting penicillin and erythromycin resistance in S. pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: A systematic literature review of studies published between 2005 and 2012, focusing on the aetiology of CAP and antibiotic resistance patterns.

full_output.paper_title: Risk factors and molecular epidemiology of community-onset extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli bacteremia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla CTX-M-15 and bla CTX-M-14 as the most common ESBL genes in community-onset ESBLEC bacteremia in Korea, along with other ESBL variants such as bla CTX-M-22, bla CTX-M-24, bla CTX-M-57, bla SHV-12, bla CMY-2, and bla DHA-1.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and phenotypic confirmation of ESBL production.

full_output.paper_title: Verapamil, and its metabolite norverapamil, inhibit macrophage-induced, bacterial efflux pump-mediated tolerance to multiple anti-tubercular drugs.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Rv1258c as a bacterial efflux pump involved in macrophage-induced tolerance to anti-tubercular drugs, and shows that verapamil and its metabolite norverapamil can inhibit this tolerance.
full_output.methodology: The study uses macrophage infection assays and efflux pump inhibitor treatments to investigate drug tolerance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

full_output.paper_title: Function and localization dynamics of bifunctional penicillin-binding proteins in Caulobacter crescentus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that PbpX is crucial for resistance to d-alanine in Caulobacter crescentus, highlighting its unique role among bifunctional penicillin-binding proteins (bPBPs).
full_output.methodology: The research utilized genetic manipulation, fluorescence microscopy, and biochemical analyses to investigate the function and localization of bPBPs in C. crescentus.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high prevalence of ESBL and AmpC beta-lactamase producers among clinical isolates, highlighting the therapeutic challenges posed by these resistance mechanisms in a tertiary care center.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed 262 clinical isolates using antibiogram profiling, phenotypic confirmatory tests, and E-tests to detect ESBL and AmpC beta-lactamase production.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization of the MRPA transporter and antimony uptake in four New World Leishmania spp. susceptible and resistant to antimony.

MRPA.mechanism: sequestering metal-thiol conjugates in intracellular vesicles
MRPA.validation_method: chromosomal amplification and mRNA expression analysis
MRPA.evidence_note: The MRPA gene is involved in resistance by sequestering metal-thiol conjugates in intracellular vesicles of Leishmania parasite.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies MRPA gene amplification and increased expression as a mechanism of antimony resistance in Leishmania species.
full_output.methodology: PFGE, Southern blot, real-time RT-PCR, Western blot, and antimony uptake/efflux assays.

full_output.paper_title: Arginine deiminase pathway is far more important than urease for acid resistance and intracellular survival in Laribacter hongkongensis: a possible result of arc gene cassette duplication.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that the arginine deiminase (ADI) pathway plays a more critical role than the urease system in acid resistance and intracellular survival of Laribacter hongkongensis. The ADI pathway, encoded by the arcA1 and arcA2 genes, significantly contributes to the bacterium's ability to survive in acidic environments and within macrophages.
full_output.methodology: The study involved constructing gene deletion mutants of L. hongkongensis and assessing their survival under acidic conditions, in macrophages, and in a mouse model.

full_output.paper_title: Sequence analysis of the drug‑resistant rpoB gene in the Mycobacterium tuberculosis L‑form among patients with pneumoconiosis complicated by tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various mutations in the rpoB gene of Mycobacterium tuberculosis L-form strains from patients with pneumoconiosis complicated by tuberculosis, primarily in codons 531 and 526, leading to rifampicin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genomic DNA was extracted, PCR amplification and direct sequencing were performed to analyze rpoB gene mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation and characterization of Salmonella enterica in day-old ducklings in Egypt.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 14 Salmonella enterica serovars from imported ducklings and four from domestic ducklings, highlighting their resistance to multiple antibiotics and the presence of various virulence genes.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of virulence genes and antimicrobial susceptibility testing via disc diffusion.

full_output.paper_title: Understanding the antimicrobial mechanism of TiO₂-based nanocomposite films in a pathogenic bacterium.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the antimicrobial mechanism of TiO₂-based nanocomposite films on Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1, revealing that the treatment leads to significant changes in gene expression related to cell wall structure, detoxification, and stress response, but no AMR genes or mutations are characterized.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptomic and proteomic analyses were conducted to assess the gene and protein expression changes in P. aeruginosa PAO1 following exposure to TiO₂-based nanocomposite films.

full_output.paper_title: Metabolic and bactericidal effects of targeted suppression of NadD and NadE enzymes in mycobacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies NadD and NadE as essential enzymes in NAD biosynthesis in mycobacteria, demonstrating that their suppression leads to bactericidal effects and metabolic disruption.
full_output.methodology: Protein knockdown approach and enzymatic activity assays were used to validate the essentiality of NadD and NadE as drug targets.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro activity of plazomicin against 5,015 gram-negative and gram-positive clinical isolates obtained from patients in canadian hospitals as part of the CANWARD study, 2011-2012.
full_output.key_findings: Plazomicin showed potent in vitro activity against a wide range of Gram-negative and Gram-positive clinical isolates, including aminoglycoside-nonsusceptible E. coli and ESBL-producing E. coli and K. pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: Susceptibility testing was performed using the Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI) broth microdilution method.

full_output.paper_title: High activity of Fosfomycin and Rifampin against methicillin-resistant staphylococcus aureus biofilm in vitro and in an experimental foreign-body infection model.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that fosfomycin in combination with rifampin exhibits high efficacy against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) biofilm in both in vitro and in vivo models, achieving an 83% cure rate in an experimental foreign-body infection model.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the activity of fosfomycin and rifampin against MRSA using in vitro time-kill studies, microcalorimetry, and an in vivo foreign-body infection model in guinea pigs.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the novel ketolide RBx 14255 against multidrug-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae, demonstrating its potent in vitro and in vivo activity, particularly against telithromycin-resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: The study involved in vitro susceptibility testing, macromolecular synthesis inhibition studies, ribosome binding assays, and in vivo efficacy testing in murine models.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified livestock-associated methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (LA-MRSA) ST9 in pigs and related personnel in Taiwan, highlighting cross-species transmission and the prevalence of MRSA in pig populations and workers.
full_output.methodology: The study involved collecting nasal swabs from pigs and related workers, followed by molecular characterization of MRSA isolates using PFGE, SCC mec typing, and MLST.

full_output.key_findings: Sub-MICs of triclosan promote biofilm formation and adherence of Streptococcus mutans, with increased expression of genes such as gtfC, comD, luxS, atlA, and gtfB.
full_output.methodology: Microdilution broth method, biofilm assay, scanning electron microscopy, and quantitative RT-PCR.

full_output.paper_title: Frequency of severe malaria and invasive bacterial infections among children admitted to a rural hospital in Burkina Faso.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high antibiotic resistance rates among bacterial pathogens causing invasive bacterial infections (IBI) in children admitted to a rural hospital in Burkina Faso, with notable resistance to first-line antibiotics, including multidrug resistance (MDR) in non-typhoid Salmonella (NTS) isolates, decreased ciprofloxacin susceptibility (DCS) in one NTS isolate, and extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) production in three Escherichia coli isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed blood cultures and antibiotic susceptibility testing of bacterial isolates from children admitted to a rural hospital in Burkina Faso.

full_output.paper_title: Microevolution during an Anthrax outbreak leading to clonal heterogeneity and penicillin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Characterization of Uropathogenic Escherichia coli: Nalidixic Acid and Ciprofloxacin Resistance, Virulent Factors and Phylogenetic Background.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high prevalence of nalidixic acid (NA) and ciprofloxacin (CIP) resistance among uropathogenic E. coli (UPEC) isolates in Kolkata, India. It also found a significant reduction in virulence factors among resistant isolates and a shift in phylogenetic group distribution.
full_output.methodology: PCR and disk diffusion methods were used to analyze virulence genes and antibiotic resistance in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: blaKPC gene Detection in Clinical Isolates of Carbapenem Resistant Enterobacteriaceae in a Tertiary Care Hospital.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the blaKPC gene as a significant cause of carbapenem resistance in Enterobacteriaceae, with 67.4% of carbapenem-resistant isolates testing positive for the gene.
full_output.methodology: PCR and Modified Hodge Test were used to detect the blaKPC gene and carbapenemase production in clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular detection of integron genes and pattern of antibiotic resistance in pseudomonas aeruginosa strains isolated from intensive care unit, shahid beheshti hospital, north of iran.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified integron genes in 37% of P. aeruginosa isolates from ICU, with a high prevalence of multidrug resistance. Integron-positive strains showed significant associations with resistance to several antibiotics, including cefepime, ceftazidime, gentamicin, imipenem, and others.
full_output.methodology: PCR analysis for integron detection and disk diffusion method for antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Wild deer as potential vectors of anthelmintic-resistant abomasal nematodes between cattle and sheep farms.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified benzimidazole resistance in Haemonchus contortus from wild roe deer, demonstrating the potential for wild deer to act as reservoirs of anthelmintic-resistant nematodes.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, egg hatch test, and fecal egg count reduction test were used to detect and validate benzimidazole resistance in H. contortus.
full_output.sample_size: 48 samples from fallow, red, and roe deer

full_output.paper_title: First report of metallo-β-lactamases producing Enterobacter spp. strains from Venezuela.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first identification of bla VIM-2 in Enterobacter spp. strains from Venezuela, along with bla TEM-1 and bla CTX-M-15. These strains exhibited resistance to multiple antibiotics, including carbapenems, cephalosporins, and penicillins.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies two single-amino-acid substitutions (V2A and D8A) in the lysis protein E of bacteriophage ϕX174 that confer partial resistance to 5-fluorouracil by delaying lysis and increasing burst size.
full_output.methodology: Site-directed mutagenesis, lysis time measurement, growth curve analysis, and burst size determination.

full_output.paper_title: Spread of CTX-M-15 Extended-Spectrum β-Lactamase-Producing Escherichia coli Isolates through Household Contact and Plasmid Transfer.
full_output.key_findings: The study documents the household spread of CTX-M-15 extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli isolates, highlighting the role of plasmid transfer in the dissemination of antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, PFGE, and conjugation experiments were used to analyze the genetic characteristics and transmission of the isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study found a 5.5% prevalence of vancomycin-resistant Enterococci (VRE) among clients at the University of Gondar Teaching Hospital, with a significant association between VRE colonization and prior antibiotic treatment lasting more than two weeks.
full_output.methodology: Cross-sectional study involving 226 clients, with antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the Kary Bauer disk diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization and PCR-based replicon typing of multidrug resistant Shigella sonnei isolates from an outbreak in Thimphu, Bhutan.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multidrug-resistant Shigella sonnei isolates from Thimphu, Bhutan, which exhibited resistance to nalidixic acid, ciprofloxacin, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, streptomycin, and tetracycline. Mutations in the gyrA gene (Ser83Leu and Asp87Gly) were linked to quinolone resistance, and class 2 integrons harboring dfrA1, sat1, and aadA1 were detected.
full_output.methodology: The study employed PCR, sequencing, PFGE, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing to characterize the isolates.

full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR, sequencing, PFGE, and DNA microarray analysis were used to characterize resistance and virulence genes in Campylobacter isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Cecum lymph node dendritic cells harbor slow-growing bacteria phenotypically tolerant to antibiotic treatment.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium can persist in a slow-growing, antibiotic-tolerant state within dendritic cells of the cecum lymph node, leading to relapse after antibiotic treatment. This tolerance is not due to genetic resistance but rather to the bacteria's slow growth rate in a specific host cell niche.
full_output.methodology: The study uses a mouse model of Salmonella infection, combined with microbiological, histological, and computational approaches to analyze bacterial growth and antibiotic tolerance.

full_output.key_findings: Vancomycin-resistant enterococci (VRE) were the most common pathogens causing bloodstream infections (BSIs) in allogeneic HSCT recipients, occurring primarily in neutropenic patients receiving broad-spectrum β-lactam agents.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective review of BSIs in HSCT recipients, including microbiological testing and statistical analysis of risk factors and outcomes.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial photodynamic activity of EtNBS and its derivatives, highlighting the impact of molecular structure on their efficacy against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Elucidation of bacteria found in car interiors and strategies to reduce the presence of potential pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Staphylococcus aureus, S. epidermidis, and S. warnerii as the most prevalent staphylococcal species in car interiors, with 22.6% of S. aureus strains being methicillin-resistant. Silver-based antimicrobial coatings were effective in reducing pathogenic bacteria on car surfaces.

full_output.paper_title: Staphylococcus delphini and methicillin-resistant S. pseudintermedius in horses, Canada.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies methicillin-resistant S. pseudintermedius (MRSP) and methicillin-susceptible S. delphini in horses, highlighting the need for accurate molecular identification due to potential misclassification.
full_output.methodology: Molecular identification methods including MALDI-TOF, PCR, and sequencing were used alongside antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Combination therapy with ampicillin and azithromycin in an experimental pneumococcal pneumonia is bactericidal and effective in down regulating inflammation in mice.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the efficacy of combination therapy with ampicillin and azithromycin against a multi-drug resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae isolate, showing reduced bacterial load and inflammation in a murine model.
full_output.methodology: In vitro susceptibility tests, murine pneumonia model, and evaluation of cytokine levels and inflammatory markers.

full_output.paper_title: Concomitant multidrug-resistant pulmonary tuberculosis and susceptible tuberculous meningitis.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the coexistence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) Mycobacterium tuberculosis in the lungs and a drug-susceptible strain in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) of a patient with tuberculosis. Mutations in rpoB (S531L) and katG (S315T) were identified as responsible for rifampin and isoniazid resistance, respectively.
full_output.methodology: Line probe assay and drug susceptibility testing (DST) were used to identify resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Fluoroquinolone-resistant Escherichia coli sequence type 131 isolates causing bloodstream infections in a canadian region with a centralized laboratory system: rapid emergence of the H30-Rx sublineage.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the aac(6')-Ib-cr gene as a plasmid-mediated quinolone resistance determinant in fluoroquinolone-resistant Escherichia coli ST131 isolates, particularly in the H30-Rx sublineage.

full_output.paper_title: The emergence of linezolid resistance among Enterococci in intestinal microbiota of treated patients is unrelated to individual pharmacokinetic characteristics.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a G2447T mutation in the 23S rRNA gene (rrl) as the primary mechanism of linezolid resistance in Enterococcus faecalis strains isolated from the intestinal microbiota of treated patients.
full_output.methodology: Screening for linezolid resistance mechanisms, including mutations in the 23S rRNA gene and the presence of the cfr gene, in linezolid-resistant Enterococcus faecalis and S. aureus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: DhhP, a cyclic di-AMP phosphodiesterase of Borrelia burgdorferi, is essential for cell growth and virulence.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies DhhP as a c-di-AMP phosphodiesterase in Borrelia burgdorferi, essential for cell growth and virulence, and shows that its inactivation leads to increased intracellular c-di-AMP levels without increased resistance to β-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study used genetic manipulation, enzymatic assays, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing to characterize DhhP's role in B. burgdorferi.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiology of Staphylococcus aureus harboring the mecA or Panton-Valentine leukocidin genes in hospitals in Java and Bali, Indonesia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and PVL-positive methicillin-sensitive S. aureus (MSSA) in Indonesian hospitals, highlighting the significance of mecA and pvl genes in the epidemiology of these strains.
