full_output.paper_title: Development of pVCR94ΔX from Vibrio cholerae, a prototype for studying multidrug resistant IncA/C conjugative plasmids.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the IncA/C conjugative plasmid pVCR94 from a multidrug-resistant Vibrio cholerae isolate, identifying resistance genes sul1, sul2, and dfrA15 that confer resistance to sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic resistance profiling, plasmid sequencing, and conjugation assays were used to analyze the resistance mechanisms in the plasmid pVCR94.

full_output.paper_title: wALADin benzimidazoles differentially modulate the function of porphobilinogen synthase orthologs.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that wALADin1 and its derivatives differentially modulate the function of porphobilinogen synthase (PBGS) orthologs, categorizing them into three groups based on their response to wALADin1. Group X orthologs (plant and Wolbachia PBGS) were inhibited, group Y orthologs (gamma-proteobacteria and T. gondii PBGS) were stimulated, and group Z orthologs (metazoan PBGS) were insensitive to wALADin1.
full_output.methodology: The study used standardized biochemical assays to evaluate the inhibitory and stimulatory effects of wALADin1 and its derivatives on various PBGS orthologs, including measurements of IC50 and EC50 values.

full_output.key_findings: The study found high levels of antimicrobial resistance to ampicillin and trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole among bacterial enteropathogens in Madagascar, particularly in Shigella and E. coli isolates. Resistance to third-generation cephalosporins was rare, with only 3.1% of E. coli strains showing resistance due to extended-spectrum beta-lactamases (ESBLs).
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility was determined using agar diffusion methods for enterobacteriaceae and agar dilution methods for Campylobacter sp. ESBL production was assessed using double-disk synergy tests.
full_output.sample_size: 29 strains of Salmonella sp, 35 strains of Shigella sp, 195 strains of diarrheagenic E. coli, 203 strains of C. jejuni, and 71 strains of C. coli

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates detected in Switzerland (1998-2012): emergence of multidrug-resistant clones less susceptible to cephalosporins.

mtrR.encodes: transcriptional repressor of the MtrCDE efflux pump

mutations_found.effect_on_function: overexpression of the MtrCDE efflux pump

mtrR.notes: Deletion in the mtrR promoter leads to overexpression of the MtrCDE efflux pump, reducing susceptibility to multiple antibiotics.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes multidrug-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates in Switzerland, identifying resistance mechanisms including mutations in gyrA, parC, mtrR, and penA, as well as the presence of blaTEM and tet(M) genes. It highlights the emergence of international clones like G1407, G2992, and G225 with distinct resistance profiles.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic and molecular characterization of antibiotic resistance genes and mutations in Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Multitarget drug discovery for tuberculosis and other infectious diseases.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies SQ109 and its analogues as multitargeting agents that inhibit multiple enzymes involved in isoprenoid biosynthesis, electron transport, and respiration, leading to potent antimicrobial activity against various pathogens including Mycobacterium tuberculosis, other bacteria, fungi, and the malaria parasite Plasmodium falciparum.
full_output.methodology: The study involves the synthesis and testing of SQ109 analogues against various microbial and human cell lines, along with enzymatic inhibition assays and evaluation of respiration and proton motive force disruption.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibility of Streptococcus pneumoniae in adult patients with pneumococcal pneumonia in an urban hospital in Mozambique.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that all pneumococcal strains were penicillin susceptible, but some had MICs greater than 0.5 mg/L, suggesting that standard penicillin dosing may be insufficient. Additionally, 44% of strains were resistant to co-trimoxazole.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using disc diffusion and E-test methods.

full_output.paper_title: High-throughput screening and whole genome sequencing identifies an antimicrobially active inhibitor of Vibrio cholerae.

VC_A0531.validation_method: whole genome sequencing of resistant mutants

VC_A0531.notes: The mutation was identified in resistant mutants and confirmed through sequencing.

kdpD.notes: The mutation was introduced into the wild type strain NM06-058 and confirmed through sequencing.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified VC_A0531 (kdpD) as a novel antimicrobial target in Vibrio cholerae. A point mutation (T283M) in VC_A0531 was found to confer resistance to the inhibitor vz0825.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput screening, whole genome sequencing, and site-directed mutagenesis were used to identify and validate the target gene and mutation.

full_output.paper_title: Delayed bactericidal response of Mycobacterium tuberculosis to bedaquiline involves remodelling of bacterial metabolism
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that Bedaquiline (BDQ) causes a delayed bactericidal effect on Mycobacterium tuberculosis by inducing metabolic remodelling, including the activation of the dormancy regulon and ATP-generating pathways, allowing the bacteria to survive despite ATP synthesis inhibition.
full_output.methodology: The study uses microfluidic devices, time-lapse microscopy, transcriptomic and proteomic analyses, and biochemical assays to investigate the effects of BDQ on M. tuberculosis.

tonB.mechanism: required for entry of multiple iron sources
tonB.validation_method: loss-of-target strategy and bacteriophage adsorption assay

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the TonB system as a target for inhibitors of iron acquisition in uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC).
full_output.methodology: High-throughput screening, loss-of-target strategy, and bacteriophage adsorption assay.

full_output.paper_title: Expression of acrA and acrB Genes in Esherichia coli Mutants with or without marR or acrR Mutations.

mutations_found.nucleotide_change: G/C heterozygote genotype at nucleotide position 131 and 133
mutations_found.protein_change: Thr at codon 44 and Arg (CGC) to Pro (CCC) at codon 45

acrR.notes: No overexpression of acrA and acrB in mutants with acrR mutation

full_output.paper_title: Two cases of invasive vancomycin-resistant group B streptococcus infection.
full_output.key_findings: The paper reports the first laboratory-confirmed cases of vancomycin-resistant group B streptococcus (GBS) infections, identifying the vanG gene as responsible for vancomycin resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and susceptibility testing.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified macrolide resistance-associated mutations in domain V of the 23S rRNA gene in Mycoplasma pneumoniae specimens from Beijing, China, with a high prevalence of 85.5%, compared to 3.3% in specimens from Sydney, Australia.
full_output.methodology: MLVA typing, P1-RFLP analysis, and sequencing of domain V of the 23S rRNA gene were used to characterize Mycoplasma pneumoniae strains.

full_output.paper_title: Modified CLSI extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL) confirmatory test for phenotypic detection of ESBLs among Enterobacteriaceae producing various β-lactamases.

blaCTX-M-3.validation_method: phenotypic detection using modified CLSI ESBL confirmatory test

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated a modified CLSI ESBL confirmatory test for the phenotypic detection of extended-spectrum β-lactamases (ESBLs) among Enterobacteriaceae producing various β-lactamases, including KPC, VIM, NDM, and OXA-48. The modified test significantly improved the sensitivity and specificity of ESBL detection compared to the standard CLSI test.
full_output.methodology: The study used a modified CLSI ESBL confirmatory test involving antibiotic disks with and without clavulanate, along with boronic acid and EDTA, to detect ESBLs in clinical isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study developed a rapid, sensitive, and specific method using rolling circle amplification (RCA) with padlock probes to detect rpoB gene mutations associated with rifampin resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
full_output.methodology: The study used a padlock probe/RCA method to detect rpoB mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates and clinical samples.

full_output.paper_title: The agricultural antibiotic carbadox induces phage-mediated gene transfer in Salmonella.
full_output.key_findings: Carbadox exposure induces prophage production in Salmonella, leading to phage-mediated gene transfer, including antibiotic resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: Exposure of Salmonella to carbadox, phage titer determination, transduction experiments, and molecular analysis of gene transfer.

full_output.key_findings: DSF and its structurally related molecules enhance the antimicrobial efficacy of antibiotics against bacterial pathogens by increasing their susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: MIC assays, biofilm formation assays, persistence assays, and cytotoxicity assays in HeLa cells.

full_output.paper_title: Ostertagia ostertagi macrophage migration inhibitory factor is present in all developmental stages and may cross-regulate host functions through interaction with the host receptor.

Oos-MIF-1.1.notes: Mutation of Pro1 to Gly reduces tautomerase activity

full_output.key_findings: Oos-MIF-1.1 and Oos-MIF-1.2 are characterized as macrophage migration inhibitory factors in Ostertagia ostertagi, with Oos-MIF-1.1 showing tautomerase activity that is reduced upon mutation of Pro1 to Gly.
full_output.methodology: Gene cloning, expression, purification, mutagenesis, tautomerase assays, and immunoblotting.

full_output.paper_title: Crystal structure of the carbapenem intrinsic resistance protein CarG.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the crystal structure of the carbapenem intrinsic resistance protein CarG from Serratia sp. ATCC 39006, revealing its dimeric nature and structural characteristics, but does not identify any specific mutations or additional AMR genes beyond CarG.
full_output.methodology: X-ray crystallography, protein purification, and biochemical assays were used to determine the structure and localization of CarG.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of benzalkonium chloride resistance in community environmental isolates of staphylococci.

qacA/B.encodes: small multidrug resistance (SMR) family efflux pump

qacC.encodes: small multidrug resistance (SMR) family efflux pump

qacG.encodes: small multidrug resistance (SMR) family efflux pump

qacH.encodes: small multidrug resistance (SMR) family efflux pump

qacJ.encodes: small multidrug resistance (SMR) family efflux pump

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several qac genes (qacA/B, qacC, qacG, qacH, and qacJ) associated with benzalkonium chloride (BC) and cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTAB) resistance in community environmental isolates of staphylococci.
full_output.methodology: Real-time PCR and susceptibility testing were used to detect and characterize BC and CTAB resistance genes in staphylococcal isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies small molecules that inhibit Mycobacterium tuberculosis growth within macrophages, highlighting the potential of host-targeted therapies. Key compounds include gefitinib, imatinib, and fluoxetine, which affect host signaling pathways such as EGFR, ABL, and AKT, leading to enhanced autophagy and reduced bacterial replication.
full_output.methodology: High-content high-throughput imaging assay, CFU counting, Western blot analysis, siRNA silencing, and mouse infection models were used to evaluate the effects of small molecules on M. tuberculosis growth in macrophages.

full_output.paper_title: Title of the Paper
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes antibiotic-resistant Staphylococcus aureus strains (EryR, KanR, TetR) and demonstrates that sub-curative antibiotic doses can selectively expand resistant bacterial populations during infection.
full_output.methodology: Construction and characterization of antibiotic-resistant S. aureus strains, in vivo infection models in zebrafish and mice, and bacterial enumeration techniques.

full_output.paper_title: A multi-site validation in India of the line probe assay for the rapid diagnosis of multi-drug resistant tuberculosis directly from sputum specimens.

rpoB.mechanism: Mutations in rpoB confer resistance to rifampicin

katG.mechanism: Mutations in katG confer resistance to isoniazid

inhA.mechanism: Mutations in inhA confer resistance to isoniazid

full_output.key_findings: The study validated the GenoType MTBDR plus assay for rapid detection of rifampicin and isoniazid resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis strains directly from sputum specimens. Key mutations in rpoB (S531L), katG (S315T1), and inhA (C15T) were identified as responsible for resistance.
full_output.methodology: Line probe assay (LPA) combined with sequencing and drug susceptibility testing (DST) were used to identify and validate AMR mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Population structure of Staphylococcus aureus from Trinidad & Tobago.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various antimicrobial resistance genes in Staphylococcus aureus isolates from Trinidad and Tobago, including mecA, merA/B, blaZ/I/R, erm(A), msr(A), mph(C), aacA-aphD, aadD, aphA3, fusB, fusC, mupA, tet(K), tet(M), cat, qacA, qacC, and sat. These genes were associated with resistance to beta-lactams, macrolides, aminoglycosides, fusidic acid, mupirocin, tetracycline, chloramphenicol, quaternary ammonium compounds, and streptothricine.
full_output.methodology: The study used microarray hybridisation and multilocus sequence typing (MLST) to characterise S. aureus isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the vanA gene in a vancomycin-resistant S. aureus strain (VRS1) and demonstrates the activity of closantel against MRSA and VRSA.
full_output.methodology: Development of a liquid C. elegans-S. aureus assay for high-throughput screening of antibacterial compounds.

full_output.paper_title: An in vitro study on the effects of nisin on the antibacterial activities of 18 antibiotics against Enterococcus faecalis.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that nisin enhances the antibacterial and antibiofilm activities of multiple antibiotics against Enterococcus faecalis, particularly penicillin and chloramphenicol, through synergistic effects.
full_output.methodology: The study used MIC and MBC assays, checkerboard assays, TEM, and CLSM to evaluate the effects of nisin in combination with antibiotics on E. faecalis.

full_output.paper_title: Whole genome analysis of a community-associated methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus ST59 isolate from a case of human sepsis and severe pneumonia in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the tetracycline resistance gene tet(K) in the ST59 CA-MRSA isolate SA268, which was found to be susceptible to tetracycline despite carrying this gene.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing and susceptibility testing were conducted to identify AMR genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Two non-target recessive genes confer resistance to the anti-oomycete microtubule inhibitor zoxamide in Phytophthora capsici.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified two recessive genes responsible for zoxamide resistance in Phytophthora capsici, which do not involve mutations in the β-tubulin gene or changes in its expression levels.
full_output.methodology: The study used genetic crosses, molecular analysis, and quantitative PCR to investigate the resistance mechanism of zoxamide in P. capsici.

full_output.paper_title: Behavioral and socioeconomic risk factors associated with probable resistance to ceftriaxone and resistance to penicillin and tetracycline in Neisseria gonorrhoeae in Shanghai.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified risk factors for antibiotic-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae infections in Shanghai, focusing on resistance to ceftriaxone, penicillin, and tetracycline. Key findings include higher resistance rates in certain demographics and behavioral factors.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed antimicrobial susceptibility data from 384 N. gonorrhoeae isolates, using multivariable regression models to identify risk factors for resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibility of Vibrio vulnificus and Vibrio parahaemolyticus recovered from recreational and commercial areas of Chesapeake Bay and Maryland Coastal Bays.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that Vibrio vulnificus and V. parahaemolyticus isolates showed varying degrees of resistance to several antibiotics, with notable intermediate resistance to chloramphenicol and resistance to penicillin and ampicillin. No specific AMR genes were experimentally characterized in this paper.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the Sensititre® microbroth dilution system on PCR-confirmed isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Diversity of plasmids encoding resistance and virulence functions in Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica serovar Typhimurium monophasic variant 4,[5],12:i:- strains circulating in Europe.

full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and plasmid analysis were used to identify and characterize AMR genes in the isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high prevalence of PVL-positive S. aureus in Ghana, with low antimicrobial resistance rates except for penicillin, tetracycline, and erythromycin. MRSA isolates were rare and belonged to diverse clonal lineages.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotyping, spa typing, PCR detection of PVL and mecA genes, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were conducted.

full_output.paper_title: The complex genetic context of blaPER-1 flanked by miniature inverted-repeat transposable elements in Acinetobacter johnsonii.

blaPER-1.genetic_context: bla PER-1 was found downstream of the insertion sequence IS CR1 in a 5.7 kb region that included gts (encoding a glutathione S -transferase), abct (encoding an ABC-type transporter) and four genes of unknown function in a complex Tn 402 -like class 1 integron with the arr3 - aacA4 cassette array
blaPER-1.evidence_note: The genetic region containing bla PER-1 in XBB1 generated by assembling whole genome sequencing reads was verified by the overlapping long-range PCR and Sanger sequencing.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies blaPER-1, an extended-spectrum beta-lactamase gene, in a complex genetic context involving miniature inverted-repeat transposable elements (MITEs) in Acinetobacter johnsonii strain XBB1.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, PCR, and Sanger sequencing were used to analyze the genetic context of blaPER-1.

full_output.paper_title: Advances toward the elucidation of hypertonic saline effects on Pseudomonas aeruginosa from cystic fibrosis patients.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that NaCl exhibited antimicrobial activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from cystic fibrosis patients, with 6% NaCl inhibiting growth and 10% NaCl having bactericidal effects on 90% of isolates. Additionally, NaCl reduced biofilm formation and inhibited bacterial motility.
full_output.methodology: The study determined NaCl minimal inhibitory concentration (MIC) and minimal bactericidal concentration (MBC) using agar and broth dilution methods, evaluated biofilm formation, and assessed bacterial motility.

full_output.paper_title: Beneficial antimicrobial effect of the addition of an aminoglycoside to a β-lactam antibiotic in an E. coli porcine intensive care severe sepsis model.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the antimicrobial effect of combining a β-lactam antibiotic (cefuroxime) with an aminoglycoside (tobramycin) in a porcine model of severe sepsis. The combination showed increased antibiotic-induced blood killing activity and reduced bacterial growth in the liver compared to cefuroxime alone.
full_output.methodology: The study used a porcine model of severe sepsis with E. coli infection, analyzing bacterial killing rates in vitro and in vivo, and measuring antibiotic concentrations.

full_output.paper_title: Second and third line treatment options for Helicobacter pylori eradication.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the challenges in eradicating Helicobacter pylori due to increasing antibiotic resistance, particularly to clarithromycin, metronidazole, and fluoroquinolones. It highlights the importance of antibiotic susceptibility testing and the effectiveness of various treatment regimens including bismuth-containing quadruple therapy and levofloxacin-based triple therapy.
full_output.methodology: The paper is a review discussing treatment options for Helicobacter pylori based on existing literature and clinical studies.

full_output.paper_title: Development and antimicrobial susceptibility studies of in vitro monomicrobial and polymicrobial biofilm models with Aspergillus fumigatus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed an in vitro model for P. aeruginosa and A. fumigatus polymicrobial biofilm to evaluate antimicrobial drug efficacy. It found that tobramycin combined with posaconazole was highly effective against both monomicrobial and polymicrobial biofilms of P. aeruginosa, while cefepime showed reduced effectiveness against polymicrobial biofilms. A. fumigatus biofilms showed similar susceptibility to posaconazole regardless of the presence of P. aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro biofilm models, CFU assays, and tetrazolium reduction assays to evaluate antimicrobial susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial treatment improves mycobacterial survival in nonpermissive growth conditions.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies RaaS (encoded by bcg1279c and rv1219c) as a transcriptional regulator that represses ATP-dependent efflux pumps, enhancing mycobacterial survival under nonpermissive growth conditions.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptional profiling, mutagenesis, and survival assays in vitro and in vivo.

full_output.paper_title: Mechanism of Escherichia coli resistance to Pyrrhocoricin.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the sbmA gene as a critical factor in Escherichia coli resistance to pyrrhocoricin, with resistance arising from deletions in this gene.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, PCR, and genetic complementation experiments were used to determine the role of sbmA in pyrrhocoricin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance trends among community-acquired respiratory tract pathogens in Greece, 2009-2012.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed antimicrobial resistance trends among respiratory tract pathogens in Greece from 2009 to 2012, noting resistance to penicillin, macrolides, and tetracycline in Streptococcus pneumoniae, beta-lactamase production in Haemophilus influenzae, and beta-lactam resistance in Moraxella catarrhalis.
full_output.methodology: In vitro susceptibility testing of bacterial isolates using E-test and disk diffusion methods.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of Escherichia coli producing extended-spectrum AmpC β-lactamases (ESAC) in animals.

ampC.mechanism: overexpression due to promoter/attenuator mutations and amino acid substitutions

ampC.notes: Mutations in the promoter/attenuator region and coding sequence of ampC were identified.
ampC.source: Haenni M, Châtre P, Madec JY
ampC.evidence_note: High evidence level based on sequencing and cloning experiments.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the emergence of Escherichia coli producing extended-spectrum AmpC β-lactamases (ESAC) in animals, highlighting the identification of specific mutations in the ampC gene that confer resistance to cephalosporins.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing and cloning experiments were used to characterize the ampC gene and its mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Staphylococcus pseudintermedius and Staphylococcus schleiferi Subspecies coagulans from Canine Pyoderma Cases in Grenada, West Indies, and Their Susceptibility to Beta-Lactam Drugs.
full_output.key_findings: The study confirms the presence of Staphylococcus pseudintermedius and Staphylococcus schleiferi subspecies coagulans in dogs with pyoderma in Grenada and reports their susceptibility to beta-lactam drugs.
full_output.methodology: Bacterial culture, molecular identification, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were performed.

full_output.paper_title: Drug resistance mechanisms of Mycoplasma pneumoniae to macrolide antibiotics.

23S rRNA.notes: A2063G, A2063C, and A2064G mutations in domain V of 23S rRNA are associated with macrolide resistance.

L4.notes: Mutations in L4 may contribute to macrolide resistance, but their direct association requires further study.

L22.notes: Mutations in L22 may contribute to macrolide resistance, but their direct association requires further study.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the 23S rRNA gene (A2063G, A2063C, and A2064G) and ribosomal proteins L4 and L22 as potential contributors to macrolide resistance in Mycoplasma pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing of 23S rRNA and ribosomal protein genes, along with in vitro drug sensitivity tests.

full_output.paper_title: Incidence, pathogens and resistance patterns of nosocomial infections at a rural hospital in Gabon.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high prevalence of multidrug-resistant pathogens, including ESBL-producing E. coli and K. pneumoniae, in nosocomial infections at a rural hospital in Gabon.
full_output.methodology: Prospective surveillance study with microbiological testing and antibiotic susceptibility profiling.

GyrA.notes: Mutation M120P in GyrA leads to increased resistance to SD8.
GyrA.evidence_note: The paper explicitly states that the M120P mutation in GyrA confers resistance to SD8.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in the GyrA gene that confer resistance to simocyclinone D8 (SD8), a DNA gyrase inhibitor. Specifically, the M120P mutation in GyrA was found to increase resistance to SD8.
full_output.methodology: Crystallography, mutagenesis, and DNA supercoiling assays were used to investigate the mechanism of SD8 resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Sequential isolation in a patient of Raoultella planticola and Escherichia coli bearing a novel ISCR1 element carrying blaNDM-1.

blaNDM-1.genetic_context: bla NDM-1 was embedded in an IS CR1 complex class 1 integron
blaNDM-1.evidence_note: The paper describes the isolation of NDM-1 positive R. planticola and E. coli strains and confirms the presence of bla NDM-1 through PCR and sequencing.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel ISCR1 element carrying blaNDM-1 in Raoultella planticola and Escherichia coli, highlighting the potential for in vivo transfer of NDM-1 resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, plasmid analysis, and transformation experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Investigation of intercellular salicylic acid accumulation during compatible and incompatible Arabidopsis-pseudomonas syringae interactions using a fast neutron-generated mutant allele of EDS5 identified by genetic mapping and whole-genome sequencing.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies iap1-1 as a mutant allele of EDS5, which is crucial for salicylic acid (SA) accumulation in Arabidopsis during immune responses. EDS5 functions as a multidrug and toxin extrusion (MATE) family protein that transports SA from its site of synthesis into the cytoplasm.
full_output.methodology: Genetic mapping, whole-genome sequencing, and complementation analysis were used to identify and validate the iap1-1 mutation as an allele of EDS5.

full_output.paper_title: Bacteriophage mediated killing of Staphylococcus aureus in vitro on orthopaedic K wires in presence of linezolid prevents implant colonization.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that combining linezolid with a bacteriophage reduces bacterial adhesion to orthopedic K-wires and minimizes the emergence of resistant mutants.
full_output.methodology: The study used bacteriophage and linezolid in combination with HPMC-coated K-wires to assess bacterial adhesion and resistance development.

full_output.paper_title: Extended-spectrum-beta-lactamases, AmpC beta-lactamases and plasmid mediated quinolone resistance in klebsiella spp. from companion animals in Italy.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) and AmpC beta-lactamase genes, along with plasmid-mediated quinolone resistance (PMQR) genes, in Klebsiella isolates from companion animals in Italy. The most prevalent ESBL gene was bla CTX-M-15, and PMQR genes such as qnrS1, qnrB4, and qnrA1 were also identified. Multiple resistance mechanisms were observed, including aminoglycoside, sulfonamide, tetracycline, and trimethoprim resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize the AMR genes and mutations in Klebsiella isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic and Genetic Characterization of Carbapenemase and ESBLs Producing Gram-negative Bacteria (GNB) Isolated from Patients with Cystic Fibrosis (CF) in Tehran Hospitals.

full_output.paper_title: Travel-related carbapenemase-producing Gram-negative bacteria in Alberta, Canada: the first 3 years.

full_output.paper_title: Major variation in MICs of tigecycline in Gram-negative bacilli as a function of testing method.

full_output.methodology: The study compared tigecycline susceptibility using four different testing methods: Etest, broth microdilution (BMD), Vitek-2, and MicroScan.

full_output.paper_title: Performance of the EUCAST disk diffusion method, the CLSI agar screen method, and the Vitek 2 automated antimicrobial susceptibility testing system for detection of clinical isolates of Enterococci with low- and medium-level VanB-type vancomycin resistance: a multicenter study.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid detection of isoniazid resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates by use of real-time-PCR-based melting curve analysis.

full_output.methodology: Real-time PCR-based melting curve analysis was used to detect mutations in katG, inhA, and ahpC genes associated with isoniazid resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Teaching 'old' polymyxins new tricks: new-generation lipopeptides targeting gram-negative 'superbugs'.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents novel polymyxin lipopeptides designed to combat polymyxin-resistant Gram-negative bacteria, showing improved antibacterial activity and reduced nephrotoxicity compared to conventional polymyxins.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis and evaluation of polymyxin lipopeptides, including determination of minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs), time-kill experiments, and assessment of pharmacokinetics and safety.

full_output.paper_title: Multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii infection, colonization, and transmission related to a long-term care facility providing subacute care.

full_output.methodology: The study involved a descriptive analysis of A. baumannii isolates from facility A residents and hospital patients, along with PFGE typing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.methodology: Impedance spectroscopy and UV-visible spectroscopy were used to analyze the electrical and chemical properties of Pseudomonas aeruginosa cultures, along with mutant strains.
