full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the katG gene, particularly at codon 315 (Ser315Thr and Ser315Asn) and codon 431 (Ala431Val), which are associated with isoniazid resistance in multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis L-forms.
full_output.methodology: DNA sequencing of PCR-amplified katG gene fragments from clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: An unusual class of anthracyclines potentiate Gram-positive antibiotics in intrinsically resistant Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Antibiotic 301A 1, an anthracycline that enhances the efficacy of rifampicin and linezolid against Gram-negative bacteria by inhibiting efflux pumps.
full_output.methodology: Screening of actinomycete fermentation extracts, susceptibility testing, and efflux assays.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial resistance in sub-Saharan Africa: an underestimated emergency.
full_output.key_findings: The paper highlights the alarming rise of antibacterial resistance in sub-Saharan Africa, particularly focusing on Neisseria gonorrhoeae, non-typhi Salmonella (NTS), typhoid fever, and Escherichia coli. It emphasizes the emergence of multidrug-resistant strains and the challenges in treating infections due to limited access to effective antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews published literature and unpublished reports on antibacterial resistance in sub-Saharan Africa, analyzing resistance patterns in various bacterial pathogens.

full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the antibacterial effects of nitric oxide (NO) against multidrug-resistant ESBL-producing uropathogenic E. coli, showing that combining NO with miconazole and polymyxin B nonapeptide enhances antimicrobial efficacy.
full_output.methodology: The study used bacterial isolates, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and evaluation of bacterial viability to assess the effects of NO, miconazole, and polymyxin B nonapeptide.

full_output.paper_title: Drug-resistant and hospital-associated Enterococcus faecium from wastewater, riverine estuary and anthropogenically impacted marine catchment basin.

pbp5.validation_method: sequencing of the 3' part of the pbp5 gene

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple AMR genes in Enterococcus faecium isolates from wastewater, marine outfalls, and river environments, including pbp5, aac(6')-Ie-aph(2"), ant(6')-Ia, tet(M), and tet(L). Mutations in gyrA (S84R) were associated with ciprofloxacin resistance.
full_output.methodology: MLST, MLVA, PCR-based detection, and sequencing were used to analyze AMR genes and mutations in E. faecium isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the persistence of antibiotic resistance genes in soil following manure application, identifying increased relative abundance of erm(B), str(B), sul1, int1, and IncW repA in manured soils compared to unmanured controls.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative PCR was used to assess the relative abundance of gene targets in soil samples collected over two growing seasons.

full_output.paper_title: Deoxycytidine deaminase-deficient Escherichia coli strains display acute sensitivity to cytidine, adenosine, and guanosine and increased sensitivity to a range of antibiotics, including vancomycin.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that deoxycytidine deaminase (DCD)-deficient mutants of Escherichia coli are hypersensitive to cytidine, adenosine, and guanosine, and show increased sensitivity to various antibiotics, including vancomycin. The hypersensitivity is reversed by exogenous thymidine.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized E. coli strains, including a DCD-deficient mutant from the Keio collection, and conducted growth experiments in different media to assess sensitivity to nucleosides and antibiotics.

ompW.validation_method: plasmid complementation and methyl viologen resistance assays

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies OmpW as a critical outer membrane protein that collaborates with EmrE in the efflux of quaternary cationic compounds, demonstrating its role in microbial resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized plasmid complementation, methyl viologen resistance assays, and phenotypic growth screens to investigate the role of OmpW in conjunction with EmrE.

full_output.paper_title: The DrrAB efflux system of Streptomyces peucetius is a multidrug transporter of broad substrate specificity.

drrAB.validation_method: efflux assays in E. coli and in vitro using inside-out membrane vesicles

DrrAB.validation_method: kinetic analysis of efflux in inside-out membrane vesicles and E. coli cells

full_output.key_findings: The DrrAB efflux system of Streptomyces peucetius is a multidrug transporter capable of exporting doxorubicin, Hoechst 33342, and ethidium bromide, demonstrating broad substrate specificity.
full_output.methodology: Efflux assays in E. coli and in vitro using inside-out membrane vesicles.

full_output.paper_title: Inhibited bacterial biofilm formation and improved osteogenic activity on gentamicin-loaded titania nanotubes with various diameters.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that gentamicin-loaded titania nanotubes (NT-G) effectively inhibited bacterial adhesion and biofilm formation, particularly with larger diameters (160 nm and 200 nm). NT-G also promoted osteogenic differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells.
full_output.methodology: The study used SEM, CLSM, and biochemical assays to evaluate bacterial adhesion, biofilm formation, and osteogenic differentiation on titania nanotubes with varying diameters.

full_output.paper_title: Probing the penetration of antimicrobial polymyxin lipopeptides into gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a dansyl-polymyxin lipopeptide probe that mimics polymyxin B's structure and retains its antibacterial activity, providing insights into polymyxin penetration and resistance mechanisms in Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The probe was synthesized and characterized using NMR spectroscopy, CLSM imaging, and antimicrobial activity assays.

full_output.paper_title: Subtype analysis of Salmonella isolated from subclinically infected dairy cattle and dairy farm environments reveals the presence of both human- and bovine-associated subtypes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that approximately 25% of Salmonella isolates from subclinically infected dairy cattle and farm environments were resistant to one or more antimicrobial agents, highlighting the presence of multidrug-resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: The study conducted antimicrobial susceptibility testing on 1,349 Salmonella isolates using the Sensititre® system, identifying resistance patterns and characterizing serovars through traditional and molecular serotyping.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro activity of the new fluoroketolide solithromycin (CEM-101) against macrolide-resistant and -susceptible Mycoplasma genitalium strains.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the in vitro activity of solithromycin against Mycoplasma genitalium strains, identifying mutations in the 23S rRNA gene (A2058G, A2059G, A2058C) and in the rpl4 (H69R) and rpl22 (P81S) genes associated with macrolide resistance.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, sequencing of the 23S rRNA gene, and analysis of mutations in rpl4 and rpl22 genes.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that the antimicrobial peptide OH-CATH30 is effective against antibiotic-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa keratitis, showing potent antimicrobial activity and preventing resistance development.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antimicrobial activity of OH-CATH30 through in vitro susceptibility testing, time-kill assays, and in vivo rabbit keratitis models.

full_output.paper_title: Next science wound gel technology, a novel agent that inhibits biofilm development by gram-positive and gram-negative wound pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the efficacy of Next Science wound gel technology (NxtSc) in inhibiting biofilm development by gram-positive and gram-negative wound pathogens, demonstrating its ability to reduce bacterial counts significantly in both in vitro and in vivo models.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro and in vivo models to assess the efficacy of NxtSc in inhibiting biofilm formation and eliminating established biofilms by various wound pathogens.

full_output.paper_title: Pseudomonas aeruginosa ceftolozane-tazobactam resistance development requires multiple mutations leading to overexpression and structural modification of AmpC.

ampC.validation_method: cloning in E. coli + MIC testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in the ampC gene of Pseudomonas aeruginosa that lead to overexpression and structural modifications of AmpC, contributing to resistance against ceftolozane-tazobactam and ceftazidime.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome analysis through RNA sequencing and cloning experiments with MIC testing.

full_output.paper_title: Triclosan-induced aminoglycoside-tolerant Listeria monocytogenes isolates can appear as small-colony variants.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in heme-related genes (hemH and hemA) in triclosan-induced aminoglycoside-tolerant Listeria monocytogenes isolates, which are associated with the small-colony variant phenotype and reduced hemolytic activity.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing and biochemical assays were used to identify mutations and assess resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization of carbapenemase-producing Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae in the countries of the Gulf cooperation council: dominance of OXA-48 and NDM producers.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified OXA-48 and NDM carbapenemases as the primary resistance mechanisms in carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae in the Gulf Cooperation Council countries.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and clonal analysis were used to characterize carbapenemase-producing isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Reversing multidrug resistance in Caco-2 by silencing MDR1, MRP1, MRP2, and BCL-2/BCL-xL using liposomal antisense oligonucleotides.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that silencing MDR1, MRP1, MRP2, BCL-2, and BCL-xL using liposomal antisense oligonucleotides reverses multidrug resistance in Caco-2 cells, enhancing the effectiveness of epirubicin.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized liposomal antisense oligonucleotides to silence specific genes involved in multidrug resistance and evaluated the impact on epirubicin sensitivity in Caco-2 cells.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular dissection of the evolution of carbapenem-resistant multilocus sequence type 258 Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies blaKPC as a key carbapenem resistance gene in ST258 Klebsiella pneumoniae, highlighting its role in multidrug resistance and the genetic diversity within the ST258 lineage.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing of ST258 isolates and comparative genomics analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of integrons among Escherichia coli in a region at high incidence of ESBL-EC.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various gene cassettes within class 1 integrons in E. coli isolates, including dfrA17, aadA5, dfrA12, aadA2, aacA4, and CmlA1, which contribute to resistance against trimethoprim, aminoglycosides, and chloramphenicol.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to detect and characterize integron gene cassettes in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Multidrug resistant AmpC β-lactamase producing Escherichia coli isolated from a paediatric hospital.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified AmpC β-lactamase producing E. coli strains that exhibited high resistance to several beta-lactam antibiotics including ceftazidime, cefotaxime, cefuroxime, ceftriaxone, and cefoxitin. These strains showed low resistance to sulbactam-cefoperazone, cefepime, and piperacillin-tazobactam, with no resistance to imipenem and meropenem.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing and disc potentiation method were used to identify AmpC β-lactamase producing E. coli.

full_output.key_findings: The case report highlights the surface contamination of a vancomycin/gentamicin-impregnated PMMA spacer with a multi-resistant Staphylococcus epidermidis (MRSE) after 10 weeks of implantation, demonstrating the potential for resistance development despite antibiotic-impregnated spacers.
full_output.methodology: Case report analyzing a patient with periprosthetic joint infection who underwent two-stage exchange arthroplasty with a vancomycin/gentamicin-impregnated spacer, followed by sonication and microbiological testing.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular epidemiology of environmental MRSA at an equine teaching hospital: introduction, circulation and maintenance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified MRSA strains carrying SCC mec type IV and classified as USA500 as the most prevalent in the equine hospital environment. It also highlighted the continuous introduction and maintenance of MRSA strains in the hospital, emphasizing the need for strict cleaning and disinfection of contaminated surfaces.
full_output.methodology: Molecular typing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and pulsed-field gel electrophoresis were used to characterize MRSA isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Detection and occurrence of plasmid-mediated AmpC in highly resistant gram-negative rods.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 13 pAmpC-producing Enterobacteriaceae isolates, including 9 CMY-2, 3 DHA-1, and 1 ACC-1 type in E. coli isolates. The prevalence of pAmpC was found to be 2.6% among group I Enterobacteriaceae.
full_output.methodology: The study used multiplex PCR for detection of pAmpC genes and phenotypic tests for confirmation of AmpC production.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis and biological evaluation of 2,4-diaminopyrimidine-based antifolate drugs against Bacillus anthracis.
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on synthesizing and evaluating 2,4-diaminopyrimidine-based antifolate drugs against Bacillus anthracis, highlighting the importance of structural modifications at the C1 stereocenter of the dihydrophthalazine moiety for optimizing potency against the DHFR enzyme.
full_output.methodology: The compounds were synthesized through various chemical reactions and their biological potency was assessed using MIC and K_i values against B. anthracis and its DHFR enzyme.

full_output.paper_title: Sialylation of outer membrane porin protein D: a mechanistic basis of antibiotic uptake in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

oprD.validation_method: surface plasmon resonance study and liposome-swelling assay

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies oprD as a gene encoding the outer membrane porin protein D, which plays a role in the uptake of beta-lactam antibiotics in Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Sialylation of OprD reduces its interaction with beta-lactam antibiotics, contributing to antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: Affinity purification, SDS-PAGE, MALDI-TOF/TOF MS, surface plasmon resonance, and liposome-swelling assay.
full_output.sample_size: four clinical isolates of Pseudomonas aeruginosa

full_output.paper_title: Isolation of Escherichia coli strains with AcrAB-TolC efflux pump-associated intermediate interpretation or resistance to fluoroquinolone, chloramphenicol and aminopenicillin from dogs admitted to a university veterinary hospital.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaTEM-1 and catA1 as key resistance genes in E. coli isolates from dogs, along with QRDR mutations in gyrA and parC contributing to fluoroquinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, DNA sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify resistance genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of OXA-1 β-lactamase gene of Klebsiella pneumoniae from blood stream infections (BSI) by conventional PCR and in-silico analysis to understand the mechanism of OXA mediated resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the blaOXA-1 gene as a significant contributor to β-lactam resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae, particularly against ampicillin, cefotaxime, ceftazidime, piperacillin/tazobactam, cefepime, cefpirome, levofloxacin, amikacin, cefoxitin, ertapenem, imipenem, and meropenem. Molecular docking analysis showed that ceftazidime has the highest binding affinity with OXA-1, while tigecycline has the lowest.
full_output.methodology: Conventional PCR, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations were used to analyze the blaOXA-1 gene and its resistance mechanisms.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that cefepime was as effective as carbapenems in treating Enterobacter species bacteremia, with no resistance genes or mutations characterized in the paper.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of patients with Enterobacter species bacteremia at two academic hospitals, comparing outcomes of cefepime and carbapenem treatments.

full_output.paper_title: Complete nucleotide sequence and analysis of two conjugative broad host range plasmids from a marine microbial biofilm.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mercury resistance genes (merA, merB, merD) and a multi-drug efflux system (mexE-mexF) encoded on the marine plasmids pMCBF1 and pMCBF6. Experimental validation confirmed that these genes contribute to mercury resistance and potential multi-drug resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, disk diffusion assays, and comparative genomic analysis were used to identify and validate AMR genes.

full_output.paper_title: Discovery of novel mutations for clarithromycin resistance in Helicobacter pylori by using next-generation sequencing.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified novel mutations in the infB and rpl22 genes, as well as the A2143G mutation in the 23S rRNA gene, which contribute to clarithromycin resistance in Helicobacter pylori.
full_output.methodology: Next-generation sequencing and natural transformation experiments were used to identify and validate mutations associated with clarithromycin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic diversity and antimicrobial susceptibility of Campylobacter jejuni isolates associated with sheep abortion in the United States and Great Britain.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the tetracycline resistance gene tet(O) in Campylobacter jejuni isolates associated with sheep abortion, highlighting its role in tetracycline resistance and the impact of antimicrobial use on the prevalence of resistant clones.
full_output.methodology: MLST, PFGE, CGH, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze genetic diversity and resistance mechanisms in C. jejuni isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified various mutations in the rpoB gene associated with rifampin resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, highlighting discrepancies between Xpert MTB/RIF and LPA results.
full_output.methodology: The study compared the Xpert MTB/RIF assay with the line probe assay (LPA) for detecting rifampin resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, utilizing sequencing analysis for confirmation.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the concordance between molecular and phenotypic testing for rifampin and isoniazid resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex isolates, identifying specific mutations in rpoB, katG, and inhA associated with resistance.
full_output.methodology: DNA sequencing and phenotypic drug susceptibility testing were used to analyze resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Multiplex real-time PCR assay for rapid detection of methicillin-resistant staphylococci directly from positive blood cultures.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a multiplex real-time PCR assay for the rapid detection of methicillin-resistant staphylococci, including MRSA and MRCoNS, directly from positive blood cultures. The assay targets the mecA gene, which confers methicillin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex real-time PCR assay targeting the mecA gene for detection of methicillin resistance in staphylococci.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies compound 11 as an allosteric inhibitor of dihydropteroate synthase (DHPS), demonstrating its ability to inhibit DHPS enzymes from Bacillus anthracis, Yersinia pestis, and Staphylococcus aureus. The research elucidates the mechanism of action of compound 11, revealing its binding at the dimer interface of DHPS and its impact on loop movements critical for catalysis.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized NMR, crystallography, kinetic assays, and molecular dynamics simulations to characterize the inhibitory effects of compound 11 on DHPS.

full_output.paper_title: Effect of ampicillin, streptomycin, penicillin and tetracycline on metal resistant and non-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.

blaZ.validation_method: presence on Tn552-like transposons and resistance to β-lactam antibiotics

full_output.key_findings: The study found that lead-resistant S. aureus (RPb) showed resistance to ampicillin and streptomycin, while cadmium-resistant S. aureus (RCd) did not show resistance to these antibiotics. The zntA and zntR genes were involved in heavy metal resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: The study used growth curve analysis, spectroscopic methods, and gene expression analysis to investigate the effects of antibiotics on metal-resistant and non-resistant S. aureus strains.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of carboxylesterase genes implicated in temephos resistance in the dengue vector Aedes aegypti.

CCEae3a.validation_method: upregulation and amino acid polymorphisms correlated with temephos resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study identified CCEae3a as a carboxylesterase gene strongly associated with temephos resistance in Aedes aegypti, showing upregulation and amino acid polymorphisms in resistant populations.
full_output.methodology: Microarray analysis, RT-qPCR, and sequencing were used to identify and validate CCEae3a as a key gene in temephos resistance.
full_output.sample_size: Various populations from Thailand including Chiang Mai, Nakhon Sawan, and Phatthalung.

full_output.paper_title: Sulphonamide and trimethoprim resistance genes persist in sediments at Baltic Sea aquaculture farms but are not detected in the surrounding environment.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the persistence of sulphonamide resistance genes (sul1, sul2) and trimethoprim resistance gene (dfrA1) in sediments at Baltic Sea aquaculture farms, while these genes were not detected in the surrounding environment.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative PCR (qPCR) was used to detect and quantify the presence of antibiotic resistance genes in sediment samples.

full_output.paper_title: Detection and assessment of clarithromycin inducible resistant strains among Korean Mycobacterium abscessus clinical strains: PCR methods.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the erm(41) gene as a key factor in clarithromycin resistance in Mycobacterium abscessus clinical strains, with specific mutations at position 28 (T or C) correlating with resistance or susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: PCR-based methods including ARMS-PCR and real-time PCR for detecting mutations in the erm(41) gene, along with DNA sequencing and susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Chinese herb-resistance and adherence to human uroepithelial cells of uropathogenic Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that Chinese herb-resistant uropathogenic E. coli isolates exhibit higher adherence to human uroepithelial cells and possess a higher prevalence of virulence genes including Aer, hly, papC, and Cnf1.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of virulence genes and in vitro adherence assays to human uroepithelial cells.

full_output.paper_title: Vibrio fluvialis: an emerging human pathogen.
full_output.key_findings: Vibrio fluvialis exhibits multidrug resistance, including resistance to fluoroquinolones and beta-lactams, with mutations in gyrA and parC, and the presence of plasmid-encoded qnrVC-like genes, aac(6')-Ib-cr, blaSHV, and blaCTX-M-3.
full_output.methodology: Detection of mutations and resistance genes in clinical isolates through molecular and phenotypic analyses.

full_output.paper_title: First report of Klebsiella pneumonia carbapenemase-producing Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolated from burn patients in Iran: phenotypic and genotypic methods.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first identification of KPC-producing P. aeruginosa in Iran, highlighting the need for PCR as a reliable method for detecting KPC producers due to limitations in phenotypic tests.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic tests (Modified Hodge Test, boronic acid) and PCR were used to detect KPC-producing P. aeruginosa.

full_output.paper_title: First report of OXA-48-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae strains in Iran.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first detection of OXA-48-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae in Iran, highlighting the emergence of carbapenem resistance mediated by the blaOXA-48 gene.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic and genotypic methods including PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to detect carbapenemase-producing strains.

full_output.paper_title: Elevated levels of the second messenger c-di-GMP contribute to antimicrobial resistance of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

brlR.validation_method: restoration of c-di-GMP levels restored brlR expression and DNA binding, leading to increased resistance

full_output.key_findings: Elevated c-di-GMP levels restore brlR expression and DNA binding, leading to increased resistance to tobramycin and norfloxacin in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: Gene expression analysis, c-di-GMP quantification, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Threat of drug resistant Staphylococcus aureus to health in Nepal.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports high rates of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and resistance to various antibiotics, with 43.1% of isolates showing methicillin resistance and 12.4% displaying inducible clindamycin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing was performed using the modified Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method according to CLSI guidelines.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) in Fiji, with 6.7% of isolates being non-multidrug-resistant MRSA (nmMRSA) and all belonging to clonal complex 1 (CC1). It also found a diverse range of clonal complexes among methicillin-susceptible S. aureus (MSSA) strains, including CC75, which was named S. argenteus due to its non-pigmented phenotype.
full_output.methodology: The study used molecular typing techniques including PCR, SNP-typing, and MLST to analyze S. aureus isolates from community and hospital settings in Fiji.

full_output.paper_title: A functional peptidoglycan hydrolase characterized from T4SS in 89K pathogenicity island of epidemic Streptococcus suis serotype 2.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes VirB1-89K, a peptidoglycan hydrolase from the 89K pathogenicity island of Streptococcus suis serotype 2, which exhibits peptidoglycan-degrading and bacteriostatic activities.
full_output.methodology: Expression and purification of the CHAP domain of VirB1-89K, zymography analysis, and bacteriostatic activity tests were performed.

full_output.paper_title: Invasive Salmonella enterica serotype typhimurium infections, Democratic Republic of the Congo, 2007-2011.

cat.genetic_context: within a specific Tn21-like element, carried by the virulence-associated plasmid pSLT
cat.evidence_note: The almost complete replacement of lineage I isolates by lineage II isolates from Kenya and Malawi has also been reported ( 1 , 9 ). Our data are based on invasive S. enterica Typhimurium isolates collected in a nonsystematic health care facility–based approach and do not include noninvasive strains of S. enterica Typhimurium.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the mph(A) gene encoding a macrolide 2'-phosphotransferase and the cat gene conferring chloramphenicol resistance in Salmonella enterica serotype Typhimurium isolates from the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify AMR genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Salmonella subtypes with increased MICs for azithromycin in travelers returned to The Netherlands.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high percentage of Salmonella isolates with increased azithromycin MICs, particularly among those with ciprofloxacin resistance, highlighting potential challenges in treating enteric fever.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using broth microdilution method.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that travel to eastern and Southeast Asia was associated with increased antimicrobial resistance in nontyphoidal Salmonella isolates, particularly to ampicillin, quinolones, and trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed antimicrobial susceptibility data from Salmonella isolates collected in Oregon from 2004 to 2009, focusing on resistance patterns and risk factors such as travel history.

full_output.paper_title: High rates of antimicrobial drug resistance gene acquisition after international travel, The Netherlands.
full_output.key_findings: The study found high rates of acquisition of the extended-spectrum beta-lactamase encoding gene bla CTX-M and quinolone resistance encoding genes qnrB and qnrS after international travel, particularly to the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia.
full_output.methodology: The study used a targeted metagenomic approach and real-time PCR to detect and quantify antimicrobial resistance genes in fecal samples from travelers before and after international travel.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified genetic variation for resistance, mortality tolerance, and fecundity tolerance in the acute phase of infection with Providencia rettgeri in Drosophila melanogaster, but not in the chronic phase. It also found a diet-dependent positive relationship between resistance and fecundity tolerance.
full_output.methodology: The study measured bacterial load, survival, and fecundity in ten Drosophila melanogaster genotypes over five days post-infection with P. rettgeri, analyzing the effects of diet and genotype on resistance and tolerance.

full_output.paper_title: CdiA from Enterobacter cloacae delivers a toxic ribosomal RNase into target bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: CdiA-CT ECL from Enterobacter cloacae functions as a 16S rRNA nuclease, delivering a toxic ribosomal RNase into target bacteria. CdiI ECL neutralizes this toxin, protecting the producing cells from self-inhibition.
full_output.methodology: Structural analysis, cloning, nuclease assays, and mutagenesis experiments were used to characterize the CdiA-CT ECL toxin and its immunity protein CdiI ECL.

full_output.paper_title: Underlying mechanism of antimicrobial activity of chitosan microparticles and implications for the treatment of infectious diseases.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies OmpA as a critical binding target for chitosan microparticles (CM) in E. coli O157:H7, demonstrating that CM binding to OmpA contributes to their antimicrobial activity.
full_output.methodology: In vitro binding assays, antibacterial activity assays, and genetic manipulation of E. coli O157:H7 strains.

full_output.key_findings: Mass distribution of azithromycin for trachoma control led to a significant increase in macrolide-resistant fecal E. coli carriage in young children, with resistance prevalence peaking 1 month post-treatment and remaining elevated at 6 months.
full_output.methodology: Prospective monitoring of macrolide resistance in fecal E. coli isolates from young children in rural Tanzania using disc diffusion and minimum inhibitory concentration methods.
full_output.sample_size: 320 children enrolled in the E. coli cohort

full_output.paper_title: Inhibition of Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus-induced cytokines mRNA production in human bone marrow derived mesenchymal stem cells by 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that 1,25(OH)2D3 inhibits MRSA-induced cytokine production in hMSCs by reducing NF-κB-p65 nuclear translocation and upregulating H3K9me3 levels.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative PCR, Western blot, and ELISA were used to analyze gene expression and protein levels.

ermBL.notes: Mutations in ermBL affect ribosome stalling

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and antimicrobial resistance of Enterococcus species: a hospital-based study in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in Enterococcus species, including TEM, aac(6')/aph(2"), aph(3')-III, ant(6)-I, ant(2")-I, tetM, ermB, vanA, and emeA, which contribute to resistance against various antibiotics such as penicillin, gentamicin, tetracycline, erythromycin, vancomycin, and fluoroquinolones. Reserpine treatment was shown to reduce resistance to fluoroquinolones by inhibiting efflux pumps.
full_output.methodology: PCR assay and susceptibility testing were used to detect AMR genes and evaluate antimicrobial resistance in Enterococcus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis and biological evaluation of 2-aminobenzamide derivatives as antimicrobial agents: opening/closing pharmacophore site.
full_output.key_findings: Compound 5 showed excellent antimicrobial potential against all tested bacterial and fungal strains, being more potent than the standard drug against Aspergillus fumigatus.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of 2-aminobenzamide derivatives and evaluation of their antimicrobial activity using agar well diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Catalase (KatA) plays a role in protection against anaerobic nitric oxide in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies KatA as a crucial catalase involved in protecting Pseudomonas aeruginosa against anaerobic nitric oxide stress, demonstrating its role in reducing dinitrosyl iron complex (DNIC) levels and enhancing bacterial survival under anaerobic conditions.
full_output.methodology: The study employed genetic, biochemical, and biophysical approaches including gene knockout, complementation, catalase activity assays, and electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy to investigate KatA's role in nitric oxide protection.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) isolates harboring the mecA gene, which confers methicillin resistance. All MRSA isolates belonged to SCC mec type IV and were characterized by molecular typing methods.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of mecA gene, molecular strain typing (PFGE, MLST, spa typing)

full_output.paper_title: Clostridium difficile extracytoplasmic function σ factor σV regulates lysozyme resistance and is necessary for pathogenesis in the hamster model of infection.

pdaV.validation_method: expression in csfV mutant increased lysozyme resistance and peptidoglycan deacetylation

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies σV as a crucial factor in C. difficile's resistance to lysozyme, highlighting the role of the σV regulon, particularly the pdaV gene, in mediating this resistance.
full_output.methodology: Microarray analysis, qRT-PCR, and peptidoglycan isolation and muropeptide analysis were used to investigate the role of σV in lysozyme resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the epidemiology and prevention of carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (CRE) in the United States, focusing on the emergence and spread of carbapenemase-producing strains such as KPC, NDM, and OXA-48. It highlights the increasing incidence of CRE and the challenges in controlling their transmission in healthcare settings.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews data from surveillance systems, including the CDC's National Healthcare Safety Network, and analyzes outbreaks and risk factors associated with CRE transmission.

full_output.paper_title: Changing epidemiology of infections due to extended spectrum beta-lactamase producing bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the increasing prevalence of infections caused by extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing bacteria, particularly ESBL-producing E. coli, with high resistance rates to ciprofloxacin and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, while showing lower resistance to nitrofurantoin.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective cohort study analyzing clinical infections due to ESBL-producing bacteria from 2006 to 2011.

full_output.paper_title: The IncI1 plasmid carrying the blaCTX-M-1 gene persists in in vitro culture of a Escherichia coli strain from broilers.
full_output.key_findings: The IncI1 plasmid carrying the blaCTX-M-1 gene was found to persist in in vitro culture of an E. coli strain from broilers without antimicrobial selection pressure, indicating minimal fitness costs.
full_output.methodology: Experimental in vitro culture and mathematical modeling to assess plasmid persistence and fitness costs.

full_output.paper_title: There is no correlation between sublineages and drug resistance of Mycobacterium tuberculosis Beijing/W lineage clinical isolates in Xinjiang, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study found no correlation between the sublineages of Mycobacterium tuberculosis Beijing/W lineage and drug resistance in clinical isolates from Xinjiang, China.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR and drug susceptibility testing to analyze the sublineages and drug resistance profiles of Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid Detection of New Delhi Metallo-β-Lactamase Gene and Variants Coding for Carbapenemases with Different Activities by Use of a PCR-Based In Vitro Protein Expression Method.

blaNDM-1.validation_method: PCR-P assay and in vitro -synthesized carbapenemase activity assay

full_output.key_findings: The study presents a novel PCR-based in vitro protein expression (PCR-P) method for the rapid detection of the full-length blaNDM-1 gene and its functional variants, including blaNDM-4 and blaNDM-5, which exhibit altered carbapenemase activities.
full_output.methodology: The PCR-P method combines long-fragment real-time quantitative PCR (LF-qPCR) with in vitro cell-free expression to detect and characterize blaNDM-1 and its variants.

full_output.paper_title: High level aminoglycoside resistance and distribution of aminoglycoside resistant genes among clinical isolates of Enterococcus species in Chennai, India.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified aac(6')-Ie-aph(2'')-Ia and aph(3')-IIIa as the major aminoglycoside resistance genes in Enterococcus isolates from Chennai, India, with aac(6')-Ie-aph(2'')-Ia being prevalent in E. faecalis and E. faecium, and aph(3')-IIIa commonly found in various Enterococcus species.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of AME genes and MIC testing for aminoglycoside resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Insusceptibility to disinfectants in bacteria from animals, food and humans-is there a link to antimicrobial resistance?

qacA/B.mechanism: confers resistance to quaternary ammonium compounds
qacA/B.validation_method: qac-gene detection in isolates with DDAC-MICs > 1.4 mg/l

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the emeA gene as contributing to reduced disinfectant susceptibility in Enterococcus faecalis and Enterococcus faecium, with variations in melting curve types indicating different variants of the gene.
full_output.methodology: The study used melting curve analysis and sequencing to investigate the emeA genotype in Enterococcus isolates with elevated DDAC MICs.

full_output.key_findings: The study developed a dye uptake assay to assess the activity of antibiotics against intracellular Francisella tularensis. It found that certain antibiotics, including fluoroquinolones, doxycycline, and gentamicin, had low MICs against F. tularensis, while others like carbapenems, daptomycin, and linezolid showed higher MICs. Notably, linezolid and erythromycin exhibited increased activity against intracellular F. tularensis compared to their extracellular counterparts.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a dye uptake assay and CFU enumeration to determine the minimum inhibitory extracellular concentrations (MIECs) of antibiotics against intracellular F. tularensis, comparing results with traditional MIC measurements.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the Rhs-CT orphan toxin as a factor in contact-dependent growth inhibition of Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium, which is enabled by recombination between the main rhs gene and an orphan rhs-CT gene fragment.
full_output.methodology: The study uses serial passage experiments, genetic manipulation, PCR, Southern blotting, and immunoblotting to analyze the role of the rhs locus in growth inhibition.

full_output.paper_title: Bacillus subtilis as a platform for molecular characterisation of regulatory mechanisms of Enterococcus faecalis resistance against cell wall antibiotics.

psdAB.validation_method: expression in B. subtilis and promoter induction assays

vanR B.validation_method: expression in B. subtilis and promoter induction assays

vanS B.validation_method: expression in B. subtilis and promoter induction assays

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the functional transfer of the E. faecalis BcrR-BcrAB bacitracin resistance system to B. subtilis, showing that BcrR regulates the expression of bcrAB, which encodes a transporter responsible for bacitracin resistance. Additionally, the BceAB transporter in B. subtilis was found to affect the sensitivity of BcrR to bacitracin.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptional promoter fusions, β-galactosidase and luciferase assays, MIC determination, and genetic manipulations in B. subtilis.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic diversity and antimicrobial resistance in Streptococcus agalactiae strains recovered from female carriers in the Bucharest area.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified fluoroquinolone-resistant Streptococcus agalactiae strains carrying mutations in gyrA (Ser81Leu) and parC (Ser79Phe), which conferred resistance to levofloxacin and moxifloxacin. Additionally, tetracycline resistance was associated with the presence of tetM, sometimes in combination with tetO.
full_output.methodology: MLST, PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize the strains.

full_output.paper_title: Study of extended spectrum β-lactamase producing Enterobacteriaceae and antibiotic coresistance in a tertiary care teaching hospital.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a high prevalence of extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Enterobacteriaceae, with E. coli being the most common isolate. ESBL-producing isolates showed significant resistance to multiple antibiotics, including trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, fluoroquinolones, and gentamicin, but remained highly susceptible to imipenem.
full_output.methodology: Prospective study involving 1044 Enterobacteriaceae isolates from various clinical samples, with ESBL detection using CLSI guidelines and antimicrobial susceptibility testing via Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion.

full_output.paper_title: Development of β -lactamase as a tool for monitoring conditional gene expression by a tetracycline-riboswitch in Methanosarcina acetivorans.

bla.role_in_paper: mainly used as a reporter gene

full_output.key_findings: The study utilized the bla gene from E. coli, encoding β-lactamase, as a chromogenic reporter under anaerobic conditions in Methanosarcina acetivorans. The gene was successfully expressed and secreted, demonstrating its utility for monitoring gene expression and identifying trans-acting mutations.
full_output.methodology: Construction of plasmids with bla gene under different promoters, transformation into M. acetivorans, and assessment of β-lactamase activity through nitrocefin cleavage.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of family specific fingerprints in β-lactamase families.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies family-specific motifs and fingerprints for β-lactamase enzymes using computational methods, aiding in the classification of newly discovered β-lactamases.
full_output.methodology: The study uses MEME/MAST to identify conserved motifs in β-lactamase sequences and validates them through cross-validation against databases.

full_output.paper_title: Plasmid transferability of KPC into a virulent K2 serotype Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the successful conjugation of KPC-2 and KPC-3 plasmids into a virulent K2 serotype Klebsiella pneumoniae, resulting in resistance to all beta-lactams.
full_output.methodology: Conjugation experiments, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and PCR confirmation were used to validate the transfer and functionality of KPC genes.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibility patterns of Ureaplasma species and Mycoplasma hominis in pregnant women.
full_output.key_findings: The study found high levels of antimicrobial resistance among Ureaplasma species and Mycoplasma hominis in pregnant women, particularly to erythromycin and tetracycline. Ureaplasma parvum was identified as the primary species contributing to antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used the Mycofast Revolution assay and a multiplex PCR assay to detect and characterize antimicrobial susceptibility patterns of genital mycoplasmas in vaginal swabs from pregnant women.

full_output.paper_title: The synthetic mRNA was expressed constitutively from the P L tetO promoter

hilD.notes: The 3'UTR of hilD mRNA is involved in mRNA degradation by the RNA degradosome and Hfq-mediated regulation.

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that the 3'UTR of hilD mRNA plays a critical role in regulating mRNA stability and SPI-1 expression through interactions with the RNA degradosome and Hfq.
full_output.methodology: Northern blotting, western blotting, and mutagenesis experiments were used to analyze the role of the hilD 3'UTR in mRNA stability and SPI-1 regulation.

full_output.paper_title: A single-component multidrug transporter of the major facilitator superfamily is part of a network that protects Escherichia coli from bile salt stress.

mdtM.validation_method: MIC and IC50 measurements, complementation assays, transport assays
mdtM.source: A single-component multidrug transporter of the major facilitator superfamily is part of a network that protects Escherichia coli from bile salt stress.
mdtM.evidence_note: The paper demonstrates that MdtM functions in bile salt resistance by catalyzing secondary active transport of bile salts out of the cell cytoplasm. Deletion of mdtM resulted in increased susceptibility to bile salts, and complementation with plasmidic mdtM restored resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mdtM as a gene that contributes significantly to bile salt resistance in E. coli, demonstrating that the wild-type MdtM protein functions in bile salt efflux, thereby reducing susceptibility to bile salts.
full_output.methodology: MIC and IC50 measurements, complementation assays, transport assays, fluorescence assays, and binding affinity studies.

full_output.paper_title: Lassomycin, a ribosomally synthesized cyclic peptide, kills mycobacterium tuberculosis by targeting the ATP-dependent protease ClpC1P1P2.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: disrupting, knocking out, or mutating the gene causes SUSCEPTIBILITY

clpC1.notes: Mutations in clpC1 confer resistance to lassomycin
clpC1.evidence_note: The paper states that mutations in clpC1 confer resistance to lassomycin, and that disrupting, knocking out, or mutating the gene causes susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: Inhibition of the alternative pathway of nonhuman infant complement by porin B2 contributes to virulence of Neisseria meningitidis in the infant rat model.

porB2.validation_method: expression in isogenic mutants and measurement of C3 deposition

full_output.key_findings: PorB2 from Neisseria meningitidis regulates the alternative pathway of complement in infant rats, contributing to its virulence. This regulation is dependent on interactions with factor H and enhances resistance to complement-mediated killing.
full_output.methodology: Generation of isogenic mutants, flow cytometry for C3 deposition, and serum bactericidal assays.

full_output.paper_title: N-substituted 2-isonicotinoylhydrazinecarboxamides--new antimycobacterial active molecules.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis and evaluation of N-substituted 2-isonicotinoylhydrazinecarboxamides and N-substituted 5-(pyridine-4-yl)-1,3,4-oxadiazol-2-amines as new antimycobacterial agents. Compound 3h showed promising in vitro activity against Mycobacterium tuberculosis with MICs of 1-2 μM, while some derivatives exhibited activity against INH-resistant strains of M. avium and M. kansasii.
full_output.methodology: Chemical synthesis, in vitro antimycobacterial activity testing, molecular modeling studies.

full_output.paper_title: Structures of two new flavonoids and effects of licorice phenolics on vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus species.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified two new flavonoids, demethylglycyrol (31) and 5,7-di-O-methylluteone (32), and evaluated the antibacterial effects of licorice phenolics against vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus (VRE) strains. Among the tested compounds, gancaonin I (17) exhibited potent antibacterial activity against E. faecium and E. faecalis with MIC values of 8 μg/mL and 16 μg/mL, respectively.
full_output.methodology: The study involved isolation and structural characterization of licorice phenolics using NMR and MS techniques, followed by evaluation of their antibacterial activity against VRE strains using the liquid dilution method.

full_output.key_findings: The study describes the development of a P ywaC -lux promoter-reporter system for identifying cell wall-active compounds in Bacillus subtilis. Nine novel cell wall-active compounds were discovered through this screening method.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a P ywaC -lux promoter-reporter system combined with high-throughput screening of 26,000 small molecules to identify cell wall-active compounds.

full_output.paper_title: High proportion of heteroresistance in gyrA and gyrB in fluoroquinolone-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis clinical isolates.

gyrA.notes: mutations in gyrA and gyrB are responsible for fluoroquinolone resistance in M. tuberculosis

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in gyrA and gyrB that confer fluoroquinolone resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis clinical isolates, highlighting the prevalence of heteroresistance.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized Sanger sequencing and deep Illumina sequencing to detect mutations in gyrA and gyrB in fluoroquinolone-resistant and susceptible M. tuberculosis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Activities of ceftazidime and avibactam against β-lactamase-producing Enterobacteriaceae in a hollow-fiber pharmacodynamic model.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the effectiveness of ceftazidime and avibactam against β-lactamase-producing Enterobacteriaceae, highlighting avibactam's ability to inhibit β-lactamases and enhance ceftazidime's efficacy.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a hollow-fiber pharmacodynamic model to assess the antimicrobial activity of ceftazidime and avibactam against various β-lactamase-producing Enterobacteriaceae strains.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of mercury-resistant clinical Aeromonas species.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes mercury-resistant clinical Aeromonas species, identifying the presence of merA and merR genes in some strains, indicating a high variability in mer operons among these bacteria.
full_output.methodology: PCR, dot hybridization, and mercury volatilization assays were used to characterize mercury resistance in Aeromonas strains.

full_output.paper_title: Microbiota and anthropic interference on antimicrobial resistance profile of bacteria isolated from Brazilian Maned-wolf (Chrysocyon brachyurus).
full_output.key_findings: The study found that bacteria isolated from captive Brazilian Maned-wolves exhibited multidrug resistance, particularly to erythromycin and tetracycline, whereas bacteria from wild animals were generally susceptible to all tested antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the agar disk diffusion method on isolates from various body sites of captive and wild Brazilian Maned-wolves.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Dynamics Computer Simulations of Multidrug RND Efflux Pumps.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the molecular mechanisms of multidrug RND efflux pumps using molecular dynamics simulations, focusing on proton and substrate transport in AcrB and MexB.
full_output.methodology: Molecular dynamics simulations were used to analyze the conformational dynamics and functional mechanisms of AcrB and MexB.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic resistance and molecular characterization of ophthalmic Staphylococcus pseudintermedius isolates from dogs.

blaZ.evidence_note: The blaZ gene was detected in 42 of the 50 SP strains and was associated with penicillin resistance.

mecA.evidence_note: The paper states that mecA was observed in 18 of the 50 SP strains and that 16 (88.9%) mecA-positive SP strains were resistant to oxacillin, tetracycline and penicillin.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the blaZ and mecA genes in ophthalmic Staphylococcus pseudintermedius isolates from dogs, with blaZ conferring resistance to penicillin and mecA conferring resistance to oxacillin and penicillin.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex PCR and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize antibiotic resistance genes in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: The natural antimicrobial carvacrol inhibits quorum sensing in Chromobacterium violaceum and reduces bacterial biofilm formation at sub-lethal concentrations.
full_output.key_findings: Carvacrol inhibits quorum sensing in Chromobacterium violaceum by reducing the expression of the cviI gene, which encodes the AHL synthase, leading to decreased biofilm formation, violacein production, and chitinase activity.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative PCR, biofilm inhibition assays, and quorum sensing inhibition assays were used to evaluate the effects of carvacrol on microbial behavior.

full_output.paper_title: Relationship between the resistance genes to quaternary ammonium compounds and antibiotic resistance in staphylococci isolated from surgical site infections.

qacA/qacB.evidence_note: The paper states that qacA/qacB genes were found to be positive in 47.4% of amikacin-resistant S. aureus strains and 37.9% of CoNS strains. It also reports that chlorhexidine resistance was 50.7% among S. aureus isolates carrying qacA/B genes and 29.5% among CoNS isolates.

qacC.evidence_note: The paper states that qacA/qacB and qacC genes were detected in staphylococcal isolates and that chlorhexidine resistance was associated with the presence of these genes.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high prevalence of quaternary ammonium compound resistance genes (qacA/qacB and qacC) and aminoglycoside resistance genes (aac(6')/aph(2"), aph(3')-IIIa, ant(4')-Ia) in staphylococcal isolates from surgical site infections. These genes were associated with resistance to chlorhexidine and amikacin.
full_output.methodology: PCR and susceptibility testing were used to detect resistance genes and assess antimicrobial resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Occurrence of Methicillin Resistant and Enterotoxigenic Staphylococcus aureus in Traditional Cheeses in the North West of Iran.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) in traditional cheeses in the Northwest of Iran, with 21% of S. aureus isolates showing resistance to methicillin via the mecA gene.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic and molecular methods, including PCR for mecA gene detection and methicillin resistance testing.

full_output.paper_title: Structure-activity relationship studies of the tricyclic indoline resistance-modifying agent.
full_output.key_findings: The study focuses on the structure-activity relationship of a tricyclic indoline compound (1) that acts as a resistance-modifying agent (RMA) against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), enhancing the effectiveness of β-lactam antibiotics. Key modifications to the compound's structure were identified that improve its RMA activity and reduce mammalian toxicity, leading to the discovery of a more potent analogue, 13d.
full_output.methodology: The study involved synthesizing various analogues of compound 1, evaluating their ability to resensitize MRSA to β-lactam antibiotics through MIC and MRC assays, and assessing their cytotoxicity in HeLa cells. Structural modifications were analyzed for their impact on RMA activity and toxicity.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of genotypic clarithromycin-resistant Helicobacter pylori by string tests.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified A2143G mutation in 23S rRNA as a genotypic marker for clarithromycin resistance in Helicobacter pylori using string tests and PCR-RFLP.
full_output.methodology: The study used string tests combined with PCR-RFLP to detect genotypic clarithromycin resistance in H. pylori.

These genes were experimentally validated through cloning and MIC testing.
full_output.methodology: Cloning, MIC testing, and sequencing were used to validate the resistance mechanisms of the OXA β-lactamases.
full_output.sample_size: Multiple isolates from various locations were analyzed.

full_output.paper_title: Extended-Spectrum Beta-Lactamases Producing Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae: A Multi-Centric Study Across Karnataka.

bla.validation_method: phenotypic detection by disk diffusion and confirmatory test

blaCTX-M.validation_method: phenotypic detection by disk diffusion and confirmatory test

full_output.key_findings: The study found a high prevalence of ESBL-producing E. coli (61.4%) and K. pneumoniae (46.2%) in Karnataka. ESBLs were primarily responsible for resistance to third-generation cephalosporins, with CTX-M type ESBLs likely being the dominant variant.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic detection of ESBLs using disk diffusion and confirmatory tests, along with MIC testing and conjugation experiments.

full_output.key_findings: The case report describes a bloodstream infection caused by carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae and multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii in a neutropenic patient.
full_output.methodology: Case report and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: A random sequential mechanism of aminoglycoside acetylation by Mycobacterium tuberculosis Eis protein.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the aminoglycoside acetyltransferase Eis from Mycobacterium tuberculosis, demonstrating its random sequential bisubstrate mechanism of action and its role in conferring resistance to kanamycin A and neomycin B.
full_output.methodology: Steady-state kinetic analysis of acetylation reactions involving Eis, kanamycin A, neomycin B, and acetyl coenzyme A.

full_output.paper_title: Studies on inhibition of respiratory cytochrome bc1 complex by the fungicide pyrimorph suggest a novel inhibitory mechanism.
full_output.key_findings: Pyrimorph inhibits the respiratory cytochrome bc1 complex, showing high sensitivity towards Complex III, with 95.3% inhibition at 4 μM concentration. It acts as a mixed-type, noncompetitive inhibitor with respect to ubiquinol, targeting the QP site.
full_output.methodology: Biochemical assays, spectral analyses, and molecular docking were used to investigate the inhibitory effects of pyrimorph on the cytochrome bc1 complex.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic and phenotypic characterization of Vibrio cholerae non-O1 isolates from a US Gulf Coast cholera outbreak.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the genomic and phenotypic features of Vibrio cholerae non-O1 isolates from a US Gulf Coast cholera outbreak, identifying various genomic islands and virulence factors.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, PCR, and comparative genomic analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Mycolactone inhibits co-translational translocation into the ER via a mechanism that does not disrupt the structural integrity of the ER
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that mycolactone inhibits co-translational translocation into the ER by blocking the Sec61 translocon, preventing the glycosylation and proper localization of proteins such as TNF and Cox-2. full_output.paper_title: Determination of Extended-Spectrum β-Lactamases and AmpC Production in Uropathogenic Isolates of Escherichia coli and Susceptibility to Fosfomycin.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified ESBLs and AmpC production in uropathogenic E. coli isolates and found all strains to be fosfomycin sensitive.
full_output.methodology: Detection of ESBLs and AmpC using phenotypic methods and determination of antimicrobial susceptibility including fosfomycin MIC.
