full_output.paper_title: Genetic variations of TAP1 gene exon 3 affects gene expression and Escherichia coli F18 resistance in piglets.

TAP1.notes: The G729A mutation is a synonymous mutation but affects TAP1 mRNA expression levels.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a G729A mutation in the TAP1 gene exon 3 that correlates with increased TAP1 mRNA expression and resistance to Escherichia coli F18 in Sutai pigs.
full_output.methodology: Real-time PCR, PCR-RFLP, and sequencing were used to analyze TAP1 gene expression and genetic variations.

full_output.paper_title: Immunization against multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii effectively protects mice in both pneumonia and sepsis models.

ompA.validation_method: Western blot analysis showing specific reactivity to A. baumannii proteins

full_output.key_findings: Immunization with outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) from multidrug-resistant A. baumannii elicits protective immunity in both pneumonia and sepsis models, reducing bacterial burden and inflammatory responses.
full_output.methodology: Mouse immunization with OMVs followed by assessment of survival, bacterial load, and immune responses in pneumonia and sepsis models.

mutations_found.validated_by: experimental validation via deletion analysis and phenotypic testing

mutations_found.nucleotide_position: 8 bp replaced by 7 bp of divergent sequence
mutations_found.validated_by: experimental validation via de novo assembly and phenotypic testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the genes tetM, ermB, and cat as responsible for tetracycline, macrolide, and chloramphenicol resistance respectively in the PMEN2 pneumococcal clone. Mutations such as a 58 bp deletion upstream of tetM were found to revert resistance to tetracycline.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, genomic analysis, and phenotypic testing of isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Accumulation of phosphatidic acid increases vancomycin resistance in Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that mutations in the essential gene cdsA, which is responsible for converting phosphatidic acid (PA) to CDP-diacylglycerol, lead to increased vancomycin resistance in E. coli. These mutations cause a partial loss of function and result in PA accumulation, which enhances resistance to vancomycin.
full_output.methodology: Genetic analysis and Q-TOF LC-MS were used to investigate the effects of cdsA mutations on phospholipid content and vancomycin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Defining daptomycin resistance prevention exposures in vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium and E. faecalis.

liaF.encodes: predicted two-component regulatory system involved in cell wall homeostasis

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in the liaF and cls genes associated with daptomycin resistance in vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium and E. faecalis. These mutations were found in resistant derivatives from 4-mg/kg/day simulations and are linked to altered cell wall homeostasis and phospholipid metabolism.
full_output.methodology: PCR and Sanger sequencing were used to screen for mutations in genes associated with daptomycin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Serratia marcescens arn, a PhoP-Regulated Locus Necessary for Polymyxin B Resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the arnB and arnC genes as essential for polymyxin B resistance in Serratia marcescens, regulated by the PhoP two-component system.
full_output.methodology: Transposon mutagenesis, gene knockout, complementation, MIC assay, LPS binding assays, reporter assays, and EMSA were used to characterize the role of arnB and arnC in polymyxin B resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Long-term dissemination of CTX-M-5-producing hypermutable Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium sequence type 328 strains in Russia, Belarus, and Kazakhstan.

gyrA.notes: Mutations in gyrA QRDR confer resistance to nalidixic acid and ciprofloxacin.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the CTX-M-5 beta-lactamase gene as a major contributor to cefotaxime resistance in Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium ST328 strains, and various point mutations in the gyrA gene that confer resistance to nalidixic acid and ciprofloxacin.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, MLVA, and MLST.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies hpnJ and hpnI as genes involved in hopanoid biosynthesis, which contribute to polymyxin resistance in Burkholderia multivorans. Fosmidomycin reduces hopanoid levels, enhancing colistin susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: The study used microbial susceptibility testing, lipid extraction, and LC-MS/MS analysis to evaluate the role of hopanoids in polymyxin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Exposure of Staphylococcus aureus to subinhibitory concentrations of β-lactam antibiotics induces heterogeneous vancomycin-intermediate Staphylococcus aureus.

trfA.validation_method: generation of a trfA-knockout strain and demonstration that beta-lactam exposure of this mutated strain showed no capacity to induce vancomycin resistance

full_output.key_findings: Exposure of Staphylococcus aureus to subinhibitory concentrations of beta-lactam antibiotics can induce heterogeneous vancomycin-intermediate Staphylococcus aureus (h-VISA). The trfA gene is required for this induction.
full_output.methodology: In vitro experiments with clinical vancomycin-susceptible MRSA strains exposed to beta-lactam antibiotics and vancomycin, followed by population analyses and genetic sequencing.

full_output.paper_title: Bactericidal activity, absence of serum effect, and time-kill kinetics of ceftazidime-avibactam against β-lactamase-producing Enterobacteriaceae and Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the resistance mechanisms conferred by bla VIM and bla OXA-23 genes in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, showing that ceftazidime-avibactam effectively reduces the MICs of ceftazidime against these isolates.
full_output.methodology: MIC and MBC determination, time-kill studies, and evaluation of serum effects on antibiotic activity.

full_output.paper_title: A case control study of environmental and occupational exposures associated with methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus nasal carriage in patients admitted to a rural tertiary care hospital in a high density swine region.

scn.validation_method: PCR detection of the scn gene in MRSA isolates

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the scn gene as being present in all 49 culture-positive MRSA isolates, indicating its prevalence in MRSA nasal carriage among patients in the study area.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of the scn gene in MRSA isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Role of peptidylarginine deiminase (PPAD) in the development of experimental periodontitis and arthritis

ermF.validation_method: insertion of ermF gene in place of PG1424 ORF and confirmation of erythromycin resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that a PAD-deficient strain of Porphyromonas gingivalis was associated with reduced periodontal inflammation and decreased experimental arthritis severity in a mouse model.
full_output.methodology: Generation of a PAD-deficient P. gingivalis strain, assessment of PAD activity, and evaluation of periodontal and arthritic outcomes in a mouse model.

full_output.paper_title: Changes in capsule and drug resistance of Pneumococci after introduction of PCV7, Japan, 2010-2013.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the emergence of macrolide resistance in non-vaccine serotypes of Streptococcus pneumoniae, primarily mediated by the erm(B) gene, and notes the decline of penicillin-resistant strains following the introduction of PCV7.
full_output.methodology: Real-time PCR was used to detect resistance genes and mutations in pneumococcal isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Cefotaxime-resistant Salmonella enterica in travelers returning from Thailand to Finland.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies qnr genes (qnrA, qnrB, qnrS), CTX-M, SHV, and various AmpC beta-lactamase genes (CMY, FOX, DHA, ACC, MOX, EBC) as major contributors to cefotaxime resistance in Salmonella enterica isolates from Finland, particularly those originating from Thailand and Southeast Asia.
full_output.methodology: Screening for cefotaxime resistance, PCR for detection of ESBL and AmpC genes, and analysis of serovars and origins of isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Carbapenemase-producing organism in food, 2014.
full_output.key_findings: A carbapenemase-producing organism, identified as a Pseudomonas fluorescens-like strain, was isolated from a squid in Canada. The organism harbored the VIM-2 carbapenemase, which conferred resistance to multiple β-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification and sequencing were used to confirm the presence of the VIM-2 carbapenemase.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the prevalence of carbapenemase-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae (KPC-Kp) in bloodstream infections among patients with hematologic malignancies and highlights the high mortality rate associated with these infections.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective review of patient records, PCR, and sequencing for detection of blaKPC genes.

full_output.paper_title: Functional genomics to identify the factors contributing to successful persistence and global spread of an antibiotic resistance plasmid.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the role of six plasmid-encoded factors in the persistence and spread of the antibiotic resistance plasmid pCT. None of the inactivated genes were found to be individually essential for plasmid stability or successful vertical transfer, suggesting that the success of pCT is due to a combination of factors rather than a single gene.
full_output.methodology: Functional genomics approach involving systematic inactivation of plasmid genes and assessment of their impact on plasmid persistence, conjugation, and bacterial host biology.

blaKPC.evidence_note: The paper describes blaKPC as a gene carried by a Tn3-based transposon, Tn4401, which is associated with carbapenem resistance in K. pneumoniae.

cps.evidence_note: The paper discusses the cps region in the context of capsular polysaccharide biosynthesis and its role in genetic recombination, but does not explicitly state that the cps gene confers resistance to antibiotics.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies ST258 K. pneumoniae as a hybrid strain composed of 80% ST11-like and 20% ST442-like genomic regions, highlighting the role of recombination and capsule polysaccharide (cps) region replacement in its evolution and resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, comparative genomics, and SNP analysis were used to investigate the genetic structure and evolutionary history of ST258 K. pneumoniae strains.
full_output.sample_size: Multiple strains from different geographic locations were analyzed.

full_output.paper_title: Strength of selection pressure is an important parameter contributing to the complexity of antibiotic resistance evolution.

trkH.encodes: TrkH protein, a potassium ion transporter
trkH.notes: Mutations in trkH were responsible for increased antibiotic susceptibility in aminoglycoside-resistant strains.
trkH.evidence_note: The paper states that mutations in TrkH were responsible for increased antibiotic susceptibility in aminoglycoside-resistant strains.

folA.notes: Mutations in folA confer resistance to trimethoprim.

full_output.key_findings: Strong selection pressure leads to higher cross-resistance and more diverse genetic changes, while aminoglycoside-resistant strains under strong selection exhibited increased susceptibility to other antibiotics due to mutations in the trkH gene.
full_output.methodology: Large-scale laboratory evolution experiments combined with high-throughput phenotyping and genotyping.

full_output.paper_title: Carbapenemase-producing bacteria in patients hospitalized abroad, France.

vanA.validation_method: detection via antibiotic-containing Luria Bertani broths and selective media

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several carbapenemase-producing bacteria, including OXA-48, OXA-23, NDM-1, and VIM-2 beta-lactamases, as well as the vanA glycopeptide resistance gene in various bacterial species among repatriated patients in France.
full_output.methodology: Screening of rectal swabs from repatriated patients using antibiotic-containing Luria Bertani broths and selective media.

full_output.paper_title: Expansion of the aminoglycoside-resistance 16S rRNA (m(1)A1408) methyltransferase family: expression and functional characterization of four hypothetical enzymes of diverse bacterial origin.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the cloning, expression, and functional characterization of four hypothetical 16S rRNA (m1A1408) methyltransferases from diverse bacterial origins. Each enzyme was shown to confer resistance to aminoglycosides such as kanamycin, neomycin, and apramycin by methylating A1408 of the 16S rRNA.
full_output.methodology: Expression in E. coli, MIC assays, and biochemical analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Neisseria gonorrhoeae strain with reduced susceptibilities to extended-spectrum cephalosporins.

penA.mechanism: chromosomal mutation leading to reduced susceptibility to extended-spectrum cephalosporins

tbpB.mechanism: genetic variation associated with reduced susceptibility to extended-spectrum cephalosporins

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the Neisseria gonorrhoeae ST1407 strain, which is associated with reduced susceptibility to extended-spectrum cephalosporins (ceftriaxone and cefixime). This strain was found to have the mosaic penA XXXIV allele and the tbpB 110 allele, which are linked to decreased susceptibility to these antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Etest and multiantigen sequence typing (NG-MAST) were used to analyze antimicrobial susceptibility and molecular epidemiology of N. gonorrhoeae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates in severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: characterization and risk factors.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that P. aeruginosa was isolated from 34.7% of severe COPD patients, with 12.2% meeting criteria for chronic colonization. The extent of bronchiectasis and antibiotic usage were significant risk factors for P. aeruginosa isolation.
full_output.methodology: The study involved a case-cohort analysis of 118 severe COPD patients, with P. aeruginosa isolates characterized using PFGE and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies CXCL10 and CXCR3 as crucial components in flagellin-induced innate immunity against Candida albicans infection, demonstrating that CXCL10 exhibits fungicidal activity and recruits NK cells for fungal clearance.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a Candida albicans-infected mouse keratitis model, combined with immunohistochemistry, RT-PCR, and in vitro antifungal assays to investigate the role of CXCL10 and CXCR3 in innate immune responses.

blaNDM-1.validation_method: protein purification and enzyme inhibition assays

blaVIM-2.validation_method: protein purification and enzyme inhibition assays

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies aspergillomarasmine A (AMA) as a potent inhibitor of metallo-beta-lactamases (MBLs) such as NDM-1 and VIM-2, restoring the activity of meropenem against carbapenem-resistant bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Protein purification, enzyme inhibition assays, and in vivo mouse infection models were used to validate the efficacy of AMA.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic properties of blaCTX-M and blaPER β-lactamase genes in clinical isolates of Enterobacteriaceae by polymerase chain reaction.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the blaCTX-M-15 gene in Enterobacteriaceae isolates for the first time in Mashhad, Iran, and found that it conferred resistance to several β-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and restriction analysis were used to identify and characterize the blaCTX-M and blaPER genes.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of a Mycobacterium avium subsp. avium operon associated with virulence and drug detoxification.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the lprG and p55 genes in Mycobacterium avium subsp. avium, showing that their deletion leads to increased susceptibility to various antibiotics and ethidium bromide, indicating their role in drug resistance and detoxification.
full_output.methodology: Generation of lprG knockout mutant, drug susceptibility testing, and complementation studies.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular epidemiology and antimicrobial resistance of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus bloodstream isolates in Taiwan, 2010.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple MRSA clones with distinct antibiograms, highlighting the molecular epidemiology and antimicrobial resistance patterns of MRSA bloodstream isolates in Taiwan. Key findings include the prevalence of specific genotypes and the association of certain genes with resistance profiles.
full_output.methodology: Molecular typing, PCR, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze MRSA isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Mutations in the control of virulence sensor gene from Streptococcus pyogenes after infection in mice lead to clonal bacterial variants with altered gene regulatory activity and virulence.

covS.notes: Inactivating mutations in the covS gene were identified in multiple locations, resulting in premature stop codons and truncated proteins.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies inactivating mutations in the covS gene of Streptococcus pyogenes, which lead to increased virulence and altered gene regulatory activity. These mutations were found in various regions of the gene, resulting in premature stop codons and truncated proteins.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized sequencing, PCR, and bacterial culture techniques to analyze mutations in the covS gene and their impact on virulence.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative genomics of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus ST239: distinct geographical variants in Beijing and Hong Kong.

hutH.mechanism: frameshift mutation leading to truncated protein

sat0131_00008.mechanism: frameshift mutation leading to truncated protein

sat0131_00009.mechanism: frameshift mutation leading to truncated protein

sat0131_00089.mechanism: frameshift mutation leading to truncated protein

mw1131.mechanism: frameshift mutation leading to truncated protein

sat0131_01298.mechanism: frameshift mutation leading to truncated protein

sat0131_01299.mechanism: frameshift mutation leading to truncated protein

sat0131_01869.mechanism: orthologous gene with potential multidrug resistance function

full_output.key_findings: The study identified frameshift mutations in genes such as hutH, sat0131_00008, sat0131_00009, sat0131_00089, mw1131, sat0131_01298, sat0131_01299, and sat0131_01869, which led to truncated proteins potentially affecting histidine metabolism and methicillin resistance in ST239 strains from Beijing and Hong Kong.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, de novo assembly, and comparative genomics analysis.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae were the most common uropathogens, with E. coli showing high resistance rates to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (43.0%) and ampicillin sulbactam (47.6%).
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of urine cultures and antibiotic susceptibility testing in pediatric patients with urinary tract infections.

full_output.paper_title: Polyclonal spread and outbreaks with ESBL positive gentamicin resistant Klebsiella spp. in the region Kennemerland, The Netherlands.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 38 ESBL-G isolates classified into 18 different sequence types (STs) and 21 different AFLP types. Four clusters were detected, with two being previously unknown, indicating polyclonal transmission with several outbreaks in the region Kennemerland.
full_output.methodology: The study used AFLP and HiMLST for genotyping, along with antibiotic phenotyping to analyze the transmission dynamics of ESBL-G Klebsiella spp.

full_output.paper_title: Recombinations in staphylococcal cassette chromosome mec elements compromise the molecular detection of methicillin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies recombinations within the SCC mec element that interfere with molecular detection of methicillin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus, highlighting the limitations of current assays in detecting all MRSA isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study used RPA, MLST, spa typing, and whole-genome sequencing to characterize MRSA isolates and identify recombinations in the SCC mec element.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid emergence of daptomycin resistance in clinical isolates of Corynebacterium striatum… a cautionary tale.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the rapid emergence of daptomycin resistance in Corynebacterium striatum isolates both in vivo and in vitro, highlighting the need for caution when using daptomycin for treating infections caused by this organism.
full_output.methodology: The study used antimicrobial susceptibility testing via Etest and in vitro selection assays to investigate daptomycin resistance in Corynebacterium striatum isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Mycobacterium tuberculosis Rv1096 protein: gene cloning, protein expression, and peptidoglycan deacetylase activity.

Rv1096.validation_method: expression in E. coli and M. smegmatis, deacetylase activity assays, lysozyme susceptibility assays

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Rv1096 as a peptidoglycan deacetylase in Mycobacterium tuberculosis that confers lysozyme resistance in M. smegmatis.
full_output.methodology: Gene cloning, protein expression, deacetylase activity assays, and lysozyme susceptibility assays.

full_output.paper_title: Efficacy and Safety of Moxifloxacin in Patients Hospitalized with Community-Acquired Pneumonia
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the efficacy and safety of moxifloxacin in treating community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) in a large cohort of hospitalized patients across multiple countries. It reports high effectiveness with minimal adverse events, highlighting the importance of appropriate antibiotic use in CAP management.
full_output.methodology: Prospective, multicenter, observational study assessing the efficacy and safety of moxifloxacin in hospitalized CAP patients.

full_output.paper_title: Structural enzymology and inhibition of the bi-functional folate pathway enzyme HPPK-DHPS from the biowarfare agent Francisella tularensis.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the bifunctional enzyme FtHPPK-DHPS from Francisella tularensis, highlighting its unique structural and kinetic properties, and identifies HP-26 as a promising lead compound for the development of tularemia therapeutics.
full_output.methodology: Structural analysis, enzyme kinetics, and inhibitor binding studies were conducted to investigate the properties of FtHPPK-DHPS.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibility of enterococcal species isolated from antibiotic-treated dogs and cats.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Enterococcus gallinarum harboring vanC1 and Enterococcus casseliflavus harboring vanC2/3, indicating the presence of glycopeptide resistance genes in enterococci isolated from antibiotic-treated dogs and cats.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of resistance genes and antimicrobial susceptibility testing using microdilution method.

full_output.paper_title: Microbubble-mediated ultrasound enhances the lethal effect of gentamicin on planktonic Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: Microbubble-mediated ultrasound (MUS) enhances the bactericidal effect of gentamicin on planktonic E. coli, reducing viable counts and causing partial destruction of bacterial cell membranes.
full_output.methodology: Experimental study using E. coli ATCC 25922, measuring bacterial viability, MIC, and cell membrane integrity via TEM.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies isocitrate lyase (ICL) as a mediator of broad antibiotic tolerance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, highlighting its role in antioxidant defense rather than fatty acid metabolism.
full_output.methodology: Metabolomic profiling, qRT-PCR, and phenotypic testing of ICL-deficient mutants.

full_output.paper_title: Opposing effects of target overexpression reveal drug mechanisms.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that overexpression of drug targets can lead to either increased resistance or heightened sensitivity depending on the drug's mechanism of action, highlighting the complexity of drug-target interactions and their impact on antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used E. coli strains with inducible overexpression of various drug targets, combined with bioluminescence-based growth assays and beta-galactosidase assays to measure transcription rates and drug resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Icotinib antagonizes ABCG2-mediated multidrug resistance, but not the pemetrexed resistance mediated by thymidylate synthase and ABCG2.

ABCG2.validation_method: reversal of drug resistance in cell lines
ABCG2.evidence_note: The paper demonstrates that ABCG2 is involved in the efflux of mitoxantrone, SN-38, and topotecan, and that Icotinib reverses this resistance by inhibiting ABCG2's drug efflux function.

full_output.key_findings: Icotinib reverses ABCG2-mediated multidrug resistance by inhibiting the drug efflux function of ABCG2, but does not reverse pemetrexed resistance due to co-upregulation of thymidylate synthase (TS) and ABCG2.
full_output.methodology: Cell line experiments, drug resistance assays, ATPase activity measurements, and photo-crosslinking experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Agrobacterium tumefaciens deploys a superfamily of type VI secretion DNase effectors as weapons for interbacterial competition in planta.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Tde1 (Atu4350) and Tde2 (Atu3640) as DNase effectors of the type VI secretion system (T6SS) in Agrobacterium tumefaciens, which play a critical role in interbacterial competition. These effectors exhibit DNase activity and are counteracted by their respective immunity proteins, Tdi1 and Tdi2. Additionally, the study characterizes Atu4347 as a peptidoglycan amidase, which is part of a T6SS toxin-immunity pair.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized cloning, in vitro enzymatic assays, and bacterial competition experiments to characterize the DNase effectors and their immunity proteins.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae (hvKP) strains in bloodstream infections in mainland China, highlighting their association with community-acquired infections and the presence of two extended-spectrum-beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing hvKP strains.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized PCR, multilocus sequence typing (MLST), and pulsed-field gel electrophoresis (PFGE) to characterize the molecular features of K. pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: High prevalence of blaCTX-M-1/IncI1/ST3 and blaCMY-2/IncI1/ST2 plasmids in healthy urban dogs in France.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies blaCTX-M-1 and blaCMY-2 plasmids as highly prevalent in healthy urban dogs in France, highlighting their potential role in the spread of extended-spectrum beta-lactamase and plasmidic AmpC cephalosporinase resistance.
full_output.methodology: Plasmid characterization, conjugation experiments, and PCR-based replicon typing were used to identify and analyze the resistance genes.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that the antibiofilm peptide 1018 enhances the efficacy of conventional antibiotics against bacterial biofilms by reducing the concentration of antibiotics needed to inhibit biofilm formation and eradicating preformed biofilms.
full_output.methodology: The study used checkerboard assays, flow cell systems, and qRT-PCR to evaluate the synergistic effects of peptide 1018 with antibiotics against biofilms.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of multidrug-resistant Campylobacter species isolates with a horizontally acquired rRNA methylase.

erm(B).validation_method: experimental validation through cloning and MIC testing
erm(B).genetic_context: chromosomal multidrug resistance genomic islands (MDRGIs) of Gram-positive origin or with plasmids of various sizes
erm(B).evidence_note: The erm(B) gene is found to be associated with chromosomal multidrug resistance genomic islands (MDRGIs) of Gram-positive origin or with plasmids of various sizes.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the emergence of multidrug-resistant Campylobacter isolates carrying the horizontally acquired rRNA methylase gene erm(B), which confers high-level resistance to macrolides, lincosamides, and streptogramin B.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR, sequencing, MIC testing, PFGE, and MLST to characterize the erm(B) gene and its impact on antimicrobial resistance in Campylobacter isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Derivatives of the mouse cathelicidin-related antimicrobial peptide (CRAMP) inhibit fungal and bacterial biofilm formation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies AS10, a derivative of the mouse cathelicidin-related antimicrobial peptide (CRAMP), as a potent inhibitor of biofilm formation by Candida albicans and various bacteria. AS10 exhibits synergistic activity with antifungal agents like caspofungin and amphotericin B against mature C. albicans biofilms.
full_output.methodology: Structure-activity relationship studies, biofilm inhibition assays, and synergy testing with antifungal agents were conducted.

full_output.paper_title: Escherichia coli ST131, an intriguing clonal group.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple AMR genes, including bla CTX-M-15, aac(6')-Ib-cr, bla OXA-1, and bla TEM-1, in E. coli ST131 isolates, highlighting their role in resistance to various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Analysis of plasmid characteristics, MIC testing, and sequencing of resistance genes.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified methicillin resistance in Staphylococcus pseudintermedius isolates from canine ophthalmic samples, with a higher prevalence in isolates from dogs with ophthalmic disease. Additionally, fluoroquinolone resistance was observed, with varying levels of resistance among different fluoroquinolones.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing and PCR-based detection of mecA gene.

full_output.paper_title: Correlation between virulence genotype and fluoroquinolone resistance in carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that exoU+ strains of carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa exhibit higher levels of fluoroquinolone resistance compared to exoS+ strains, with specific mutations in the QRDRs of gyrA, gyrB, parC, and parE contributing to resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to analyze the TTSS effector genotypes and target site mutations in the QRDRs of gyrA, gyrB, parC, and parE.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiological characterizations of class 1 integrons from multidrug-resistant acinetobacter isolates in Daejeon, Korea.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified four types of class 1 integrons carrying various antimicrobial resistance genes in multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter isolates, highlighting their role in the spread of resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: PCR, DNA sequencing, and molecular typing techniques were used to characterize class 1 integrons and their gene cassettes in Acinetobacter isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Lifting the mask: identification of new small molecule inhibitors of uropathogenic Escherichia coli group 2 capsule biogenesis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies small-molecule inhibitors of uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC) capsule biogenesis, specifically highlighting compounds DU003 and DU011, which show potent inhibition of capsule formation and significant antibacterial activity.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput screening of a large chemical library, followed by confirmation using phage assays, orcinol reactivity, and dot blot analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Mechanisms of vancomycin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus.

yvqF.encodes: regulator of the vraSR genetic system

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the mechanisms of vancomycin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus, focusing on mutations in genes such as vraSR, rpoB, walKR, and yvqF, which are associated with altered cell wall synthesis and reduced susceptibility to vancomycin.
full_output.methodology: Genetic analysis and whole-genome sequencing were used to identify mutations associated with vancomycin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus.

full_output.paper_title: Dominance of CTX-M-type extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Escherichia coli isolated from patients with community-onset and hospital-onset infection in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla CTX-M-1, bla CTX-M-9, bla CTX-M-14, bla CTX-M-15, and bla CTX-M-55 as the dominant extended-spectrum beta-lactamase genes in ESBL-producing E. coli isolates from community-onset and hospital-onset infections in China.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and MLST were used to detect and characterize ESBL genes in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Engineered endolysin-based "Artilysins" to combat multidrug-resistant gram-negative pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes the development of Artilysins, which are endolysin-based antibacterials engineered to penetrate the outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria. The PCNP peptide enhances the antibacterial activity of endolysins like OBPgp279 and PVP-SE1gp146 against multidrug-resistant P. aeruginosa and A. baumannii.
full_output.methodology: Protein engineering, time-lapse microscopy, and antibacterial activity assays were used to evaluate the effectiveness of Artilysins.

aadA.validation_method: DNA-microarray analysis of E. coli isolates

tetL.validation_method: analysis of E. coli and enterococci isolates

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several antibiotic resistance genes in bacteria from Canadian poultry, including aadA, ermB, tetL, tetM, blaCMY-2, and floR, highlighting the presence of multidrug-resistant bacteria in poultry and the potential public health implications.

full_output.paper_title: Differences in epidemiological and molecular characteristics of nasal colonization with Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA-MRSA) in children from a university hospital and day care centers.

full_output.methodology: The study employed molecular typing techniques including spa typing, MLST, SCC mec typing, and PFGE to analyze the genetic diversity of S. aureus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Metabolomics analysis identifies intestinal microbiota-derived biomarkers of colonization resistance in clindamycin-treated mice.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified fecal metabolites associated with colonization resistance after antibiotic treatment, highlighting changes in bacterial metabolites linked to the recovery of colonization resistance in clindamycin-treated mice.

full_output.paper_title: Pulmonary infection with hypervirulent Mycobacteria reveals a crucial role for the P2X7 receptor in aggressive forms of tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the P2X7 receptor as a key player in the development of severe tuberculosis, demonstrating that its absence reduces disease severity and bacillary load in mice infected with hypervirulent mycobacterial strains.
full_output.methodology: The study uses mouse models to investigate the role of the P2X7 receptor in tuberculosis, analyzing disease progression, bacterial loads, and immune responses.

full_output.paper_title: Whole-genome sequencing of clarithromycin resistant Helicobacter pylori characterizes unidentified variants of multidrug resistant efflux pump genes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies variants in multidrug resistant efflux pump genes (hp0605, hp0606, hp0607) associated with clarithromycin resistance in Helicobacter pylori through whole-genome sequencing and allele-specific PCR.

full_output.paper_title: Optimizing multiplex SNP-based data analysis for genotyping of Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents an improved data analysis method for MLPA to identify Mycobacterium tuberculosis lineages and drug resistance, validating several mutations associated with resistance to streptomycin, isoniazid, rifampicin, and ethambutol.
full_output.methodology: MLPA analysis combined with phenotypic drug susceptibility testing (DST) and spoligotyping were used to identify and validate AMR mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic and molecular characterization of plasmid mediated AmpC β-lactamases among Escherichia coli, Klebsiella spp., and Proteus mirabilis isolated from urinary tract infections in Egyptian hospitals.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified plasmid-mediated AmpC β-lactamases, including CMY-2, CMY-4, CMY-42, CMY-102, and DHA-1, in Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Proteus mirabilis isolates from Egyptian hospitals.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and phenotypic tests were used to detect and characterize plasmid-mediated AmpC β-lactamases.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular analysis of vanA outbreak of Enterococcus faecium in two Warsaw hospitals: the importance of mobile genetic elements.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the vanA gene as the primary determinant of vancomycin and teicoplanin resistance in Enterococcus faecium outbreaks. Additional resistance genes such as erm(B), tet(M), aac(6')-Ie-aph(2'')-Ia, aph(3')-IIIa, and aad6 were also characterized, contributing to multidrug resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Analysis of combination drug therapy to develop regimens with shortened duration of treatment for tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the effectiveness of combination therapy with linezolid and rifampin against Mycobacterium tuberculosis, focusing on their interactions and resistance suppression. It identified that certain combination regimens could effectively reduce bacterial load and suppress resistance emergence, although none of the regimens completely eradicated the resistant subpopulations.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a hollow fiber infection model and mathematical modeling to evaluate the effects of linezolid and rifampin combinations on Mycobacterium tuberculosis, including their interactions and resistance suppression capabilities.

full_output.key_findings: Beta-lactam antibiotics stimulate biofilm formation in non-typeable Haemophilus influenzae (NTHi) by up-regulating carbohydrate metabolism, leading to increased biofilm biomass and resistance to cefuroxime.
full_output.methodology: Crystal violet biofilm assay, gene expression profiling via DNA microarray, and live/dead staining to assess biofilm formation and resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Cationic methacrylate polymers as topical antimicrobial agents against Staphylococcus aureus nasal colonization.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the antimicrobial activity of cationic methacrylate polymers (AEMPs) against Staphylococcus aureus, demonstrating their effectiveness in inhibiting bacterial growth and reducing nasal colonization in a cotton rat model.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial activity was assessed using turbidity-based microdilution assays, and bactericidal kinetics were determined by colony counting on agar plates.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiology and molecular characterization of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus nasal carriage isolates from bovines.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple AMR genes in MRSA isolates from bovines, including blaZ, blaI, blaR, tetM, ermC, aacA-aphD, aadD, aphA3, cat, sdrM, and fosB, which confer resistance to penicillin, tetracycline, erythromycin, gentamicin, kanamycin, chloramphenicol, and fosfomycin.
full_output.methodology: PCR, microarray analysis, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize AMR genes and mutations in MRSA isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of a microcolony growth monitoring method for the rapid determination of ethambutol resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated a microcolony growth monitoring method for determining ethambutol (EMB) resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, demonstrating its effectiveness in classifying strains as EMB susceptible, intermediate, or resistant within 9 days of inoculation.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a microcolony growth monitoring method involving the tracking of microcolony growth rates under various EMB concentrations to determine susceptibility.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterized synthetic variants of pandinin 2 (Pin2), namely Pin2[G], Pin2[GPG], Pin2[14], and Pin2[17], which exhibited antimicrobial activity against various bacteria, including multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis, with reduced hemolytic effects compared to the parent peptide.

The study shows that feoAB mutants exhibit a 10-fold increase in metronidazole MIC, and this resistance is reversed by iron supplementation.
full_output.methodology: Transposon mutagenesis, MIC determination, and molecular techniques were used to investigate the role of feoAB in metronidazole resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Genome sequencing, annotation and comparative genomic analysis of Shigella dysenteriae strain SD1D.

full_output.paper_title: Fluoroquinolone resistance mechanisms of Shigella flexneri isolated in Bangladesh.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic and molecular predictors of high vancomycin MIC in Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several genes associated with elevated vancomycin MIC in Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia isolates, including blaZ, sea, clfA, splA, and the ACME locus. These genes were found to be linked to higher vancomycin MICs and were associated with specific clonal complexes and virulence factors.
full_output.methodology: The study used DNA microarray and phenotype analysis to investigate genetic predictors of high vancomycin MIC in Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia isolates.

full_output.paper_title: First isolate of KPC-2-producing Klebsiella pneumonaie sequence type 23 from the Americas.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first isolation of a KPC-2-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae sequence type 23 in the Americas, highlighting the emergence of this multidrug-resistant clone.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Peptidoglycan recognition proteins kill bacteria by inducing oxidative, thiol, and metal stress.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that PGRPs induce oxidative, thiol, and metal stress in bacteria, which are required for bacterial killing but individually insufficient. These findings highlight a novel mechanism of bacterial killing by innate immunity proteins.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome expression arrays, qRT-PCR, and biochemical tests were used to analyze gene expression and stress responses in bacteria treated with PGRPs.

full_output.paper_title: Screening and characterisation of antimicrobial properties of semisynthetic betulin derivatives.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several semisynthetic betulin derivatives with antimicrobial activity against Gram-positive bacteria, particularly 28-O-(N-acetylanthraniloyl)betulin (compound 5) which showed high inhibition of S. aureus and E. faecalis.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth microdilution assays to evaluate the antimicrobial activity of 51 betulin derivatives against various bacterial and fungal strains.

full_output.key_findings: The study developed a multiplex real-time PCR assay for the rapid detection of prevalent beta-lactamase genes (bla CTX-M, bla SHV, bla TEM, and CIT-type AmpCs) in Enterobacteriaceae. The assay successfully identified these genes in various bacterial isolates, demonstrating high sensitivity and specificity.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex real-time PCR was developed and validated using 114 characterized Enterobacteriaceae isolates and 20 uncharacterized field strains.

full_output.paper_title: Human plasma enhances the expression of Staphylococcal microbial surface components recognizing adhesive matrix molecules promoting biofilm formation and increases antimicrobial tolerance In Vitro.
full_output.key_findings: Human plasma enhances biofilm formation and increases vancomycin tolerance in S. aureus clinical isolates by upregulating the expression of MSCRAMMs.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative real-time PCR, CLSM, SEM, and biofilm susceptibility assays were used to evaluate the effect of human plasma on biofilm formation and antimicrobial resistance.

full_output.paper_title: High throughput screen identifies small molecule inhibitors specific for Mycobacterium tuberculosis phosphoserine phosphatase.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified small molecule inhibitors targeting Mycobacterium tuberculosis phosphoserine phosphatase (SerB2), highlighting its potential as a drug target for tuberculosis.
full_output.methodology: High throughput screening, biochemical characterization, molecular docking, and SPR experiments were used to identify and validate SerB2 inhibitors.

full_output.paper_title: Whole-genome sequencing reveals clonal expansion of multiresistant Staphylococcus haemolyticus in European hospitals.

tet(L).evidence_note: The paper mentions that plasmids encoding resistance to tetracycline include tet(L).

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple antimicrobial resistance genes and mutations in Staphylococcus haemolyticus isolates, highlighting the clonal expansion of multidrug-resistant strains in European hospitals.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and comparative genomic analysis of 134 S. haemolyticus isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a persistent clone of Mycobacterium abscessus subsp. bolletii responsible for post-surgical infections in southern Brazil from 2007 to 2011, showing resistance to multiple antibiotics including ciprofloxacin, doxycycline, moxifloxacin, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, tobramycin, and clarithromycin.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PFGE analysis, and molecular identification techniques were used to characterize the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii as the major cause of ventilator-associated pneumonia in intensive care unit patients at an infectious disease hospital in southern Vietnam.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the emergence of carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii, particularly strains carrying bla OXA-23, bla OXA-51, and bla NDM-1 genes, contributing to the rise in ventilator-associated pneumonia cases in an ICU setting.
full_output.methodology: Molecular characterization through PCR and MLVA analysis, along with antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Intestinal decontamination of multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae after recurrent infections in an immunocompromised host.

full_output.paper_title: The biofilm matrix destabilizers, EDTA and DNaseI, enhance the susceptibility of nontypeable Hemophilus influenzae biofilms to treatment with ampicillin and ciprofloxacin.
full_output.key_findings: EDTA and DNaseI enhance the susceptibility of NTHi biofilms to ampicillin and ciprofloxacin by disrupting the biofilm matrix.
full_output.methodology: Microtiter plate assays, CLSM, and checkerboard assays were used to assess biofilm formation and antibiotic susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: Biological effects of paenilamicin, a secondary metabolite antibiotic produced by the honey bee pathogenic bacterium Paenibacillus larvae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the pam gene cluster responsible for the biosynthesis of paenilamicin, a nonribosomal peptide antibiotic produced by Paenibacillus larvae, and shows that this compound exhibits antibacterial, antifungal, and cytotoxic activities.
full_output.methodology: Construction of a gene inactivation mutant, mass spectrometric analysis, and bioactivity assays.

full_output.key_findings: Nemonoxacin exhibits strong in vitro activity against various pathogens, particularly multidrug-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus. Resistance to nemonoxacin requires three distinct mutations in the quinolone resistance-determining regions of gyrA, gyrB, and parE.

full_output.paper_title: High prevalence of Panton-Valentine leukocidin (PVL) genes in nosocomial-acquired Staphylococcus aureus isolated from tertiary care hospitals in Nepal.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a high prevalence of PVL genes in nosocomial S. aureus isolates in Nepal, with PVL carriage associated with heterogeneous MRSA and MS B resistance type, confirmed by the presence of the msr(A) gene.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic-potentiation activities of four Cameroonian dietary plants against multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria expressing efflux pumps.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antibiotic-potentiating activities of four Cameroonian plant extracts against multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria. The extracts showed synergistic effects with various antibiotics, suggesting the presence of bioactive compounds that enhance antibiotic efficacy.
full_output.methodology: The study involved phytochemical screening, determination of minimum inhibitory concentrations (MIC), and evaluation of synergistic effects of plant extracts with antibiotics using broth micro-dilution and fractional inhibitory concentration (FIC) assays.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies KYE28, a peptide derived from heparin cofactor II, as having broad antimicrobial activity against various bacteria and fungi, and as reducing LPS-induced pro-inflammatory responses.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial assays, viable count assays, radial diffusion assays, and NF-κB activation assays were used to evaluate the effects of KYE28.

full_output.paper_title: Mycobacterial gene cuvA is required for optimal nutrient utilization and virulence.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies cuvA as a gene required for optimal nutrient utilization and virulence in mycobacteria, with evidence of growth defects, morphological abnormalities, and hypersusceptibility to certain antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation, growth assays, microscopy, and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterisation and control of Acinetobacter baumannii isolates resistant to multi-drugs emerging in inter-intensive care units.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla OXA-51-like and bla OXA-23-like genes as the primary mechanisms of carbapenem resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii isolates from an outbreak in intensive care units.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification, 16S rRNA sequencing, and pulsed-field gel electrophoresis (PFGE) were used to characterize the isolates and identify resistance genes.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that the acquisition of a large-scale megaplasmid in Pseudomonas stutzeri leads to decreased resistance to quinolone antibiotics and increased sensitivity to various stresses, including heat and antibacterial substances produced by other bacterial species.
full_output.methodology: The study used competitive fitness assays, thermal tolerance assays, antibiotic resistance assays, biofilm formation assays, and motility assays to evaluate the phenotypic changes associated with megaplasmid acquisition.

full_output.paper_title: Synergy of silver nanoparticles and aztreonam against Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1 biofilms.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that 10-nm silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) synergistically enhance the antimicrobial effects of aztreonam against Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1 biofilms, improving biofilm disruption and reducing viability.
full_output.methodology: The study used MBEC assays, FFOCT, and TEM to evaluate the efficacy of AgNPs and aztreonam against P. aeruginosa biofilms.

full_output.paper_title: Transient and sustained bacterial adaptation following repeated sublethal exposure to microbicides and a novel human antimicrobial peptide.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that repeated sublethal exposure to microbicides and a novel antimicrobial peptide leads to changes in bacterial susceptibility, with some effects being reversible and others persistent. Specific bacteria exhibited increased minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) and minimum bactericidal concentrations (MBCs) after exposure, indicating adaptive responses to antimicrobial stress.
full_output.methodology: The study used serial passage experiments with microbicides and a novel antimicrobial peptide, measuring MICs and MBCs before and after exposure to assess changes in bacterial susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: Mutations in mmpL and in the cell wall stress stimulon contribute to resistance to oxadiazole antibiotics in methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in mmpL and trx genes contributing to oxadiazole resistance in methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, with mmpL playing a significant role in resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Gene deletion, complementation experiments, and whole-genome sequencing were used to investigate resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Bacterial drug tolerance under clinical conditions is governed by anaerobic adaptation but not anaerobic respiration.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that the gene narG in Burkholderia pseudomallei plays a role in regulating persister cell frequency, particularly under anaerobic conditions, affecting ceftazidime tolerance.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of Escherichia coli virulence genes, pathotypes and antibiotic resistance properties in diarrheic calves in Iran.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antibiotic resistance genes in E. coli isolates from diarrheic calves in Iran, including aadA1, sul1, aac[3]-IV, dfrA1, tetA, and tetB, which confer resistance to streptomycin, sulfonamide, gentamicin, trimethoprim, and tetracycline.

full_output.paper_title: Microbiological features of KPC-producing Enterobacter isolates identified in a U.S. hospital system.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies blaKPC-2 and blaKPC-3 as the primary carbapenem resistance genes in KPC-producing Enterobacter isolates, along with various ESBL genes such as blaSHV-5, blaSHV-12, blaSHV-154, blaCTX-M-15, and blaTEM-1. full_output.paper_title: vanG element insertions within a conserved chromosomal site conferring vancomycin resistance to Streptococcus agalactiae and Streptococcus anginosus.

full_output.methodology: Gene sequencing, MIC testing, and gene inactivation experiments were conducted to validate the role of vanG elements in vancomycin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Shielding of a lipooligosaccharide IgM epitope allows evasion of neutrophil-mediated killing of an invasive strain of nontypeable Haemophilus influenzae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies genes involved in lipooligosaccharide (LOS) biosynthesis that are crucial for resistance to neutrophil-mediated killing in nontypeable Haemophilus influenzae (NTHi). Key genes include galE, rfaE, rfaD, rfaF, lic2A, galU, waaQ, and lgtC. Phase-variable incorporation of galactose onto HepIII-β1,2-Glc by Lic2A was shown to prevent IgM binding and enhance resistance to neutrophil-mediated killing.
full_output.methodology: Transposon sequencing (Tn-seq) and mutant analysis were used to identify genes important for survival in the presence of human neutrophils and serum.

full_output.paper_title: Singly modified amikacin and tobramycin derivatives show increased rRNA A-site binding and higher potency against resistant bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis and evaluation of 6"-modified tobramycin and amikacin derivatives, highlighting improved A-site binding and antibacterial activity against resistant strains, particularly demonstrating the enhanced potency of 6"-deoxy-6"-(2-(aminoethyl)amino)amikacin (2e) against various bacterial strains.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of aminoglycoside derivatives, FRET-based A-site affinity assays, MIC determination, and cytotoxicity testing.

full_output.paper_title: Interspecies transfer of blaIMP-4 in a patient with prolonged colonization by IMP-4-producing Enterobacteriaceae.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first case of prolonged colonization with in vivo interspecies transfer of the blaIMP-4 gene from Enterobacter cloacae to Escherichia coli, demonstrating the potential for horizontal plasmid transfer of carbapenem resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, plasmid conjugation, and MIC testing were used to characterize the resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Extensive drug resistance acquired during treatment of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the acquisition of extensive drug resistance during treatment of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis, emphasizing the importance of adhering to specific program criteria to reduce resistance development.
full_output.methodology: The study followed adults with multidrug-resistant tuberculosis, analyzing drug susceptibility testing and genotyping to assess resistance development.

full_output.paper_title: Drug-efflux and target-site gene expression patterns in Haemonchus contortus larvae able to survive increasing concentrations of levamisole in vitro.

full_output.methodology: Gene expression analysis using quantitative PCR to examine changes in nAChR subunit, ancillary protein, and P-gp genes in subpopulations of H. contortus larvae with varying levels of levamisole resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Whole-Genome Sequence of CMY-2 β-Lactamase-Producing Salmonella enterica Serovar Typhimurium Strain L-3553.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the whole-genome sequence of Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium strain L-3553, which harbors the blaCMY-2 gene responsible for extended-spectrum cephalosporin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing using Illumina MiSeq platform and bioinformatics analysis.

full_output.paper_title: First Polish outbreak of Clostridium difficile ribotype 027 infections among dialysis patients.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first outbreak of Clostridium difficile infection (CDI) caused by fluoroquinolone-resistant PCR ribotype 027 strains among dialysis patients in Poland.
full_output.methodology: Microbiological analysis and antimicrobial susceptibility testing of C. difficile isolates.

full_output.paper_title: An experimentally informed evolutionary model improves phylogenetic fit to divergent lactamase homologs.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the beta-lactamase gene blaTEM-1 and its resistance mechanisms using deep mutational scanning data, demonstrating the effectiveness of experimentally informed evolutionary models in improving phylogenetic fits for divergent lactamase homologs.

It identifies various ESBL genes, including blaCTX-M-1, blaCTX-M-15, blaCTX-M-3, blaTEM-1, blaSHV-1, and blaTEM-24, which confer resistance to cefotaxime, ceftazidime, and cefepime.
full_output.methodology: The ESBL NDP test was used for rapid detection, combined with molecular characterization of ESBL-encoding genes through PCR and sequencing.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular typing of Treponema pallidum in the Czech Republic during 2011 to 2013: increased prevalence of identified genotypes and of isolates with macrolide resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified macrolide resistance-associated mutations (A2058G and A2059G) in the 23S rRNA gene of Treponema pallidum subsp. pallidum isolates from the Czech Republic, with 66.7% of clinical isolates exhibiting these mutations.
full_output.methodology: Molecular typing and sequencing of the 23S rRNA gene to identify macrolide resistance mutations in Treponema pallidum isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Integrating forecast probabilities in antibiograms: a way to guide antimicrobial prescriptions more reliably?
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the increased risk of erroneous antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) reports for isolates producing beta-lactamases, particularly extended-spectrum beta-lactamases (ESBL) and AmpC. It emphasizes the need for improved AST reporting by incorporating probability indicators to enhance the reliability of antimicrobial prescriptions.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed disk diffusion susceptibility testing data for 7,148 clinical isolates, focusing on error rates in categorizing bacteria as susceptible or resistant to beta-lactam antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of bla TEM Type Extended-Spectrum β -Lactamase Producing Salmonella spp. in the Urban Area of Bangladesh.

blaTEM.validation_method: PCR and detection of β-lactamase genes

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the emergence of bla TEM gene-mediated extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) production among Salmonella spp. in Bangladesh, highlighting the increasing prevalence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) Salmonella strains.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing via Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion and PCR for detection of β-lactamase genes.

full_output.paper_title: Reversal of ampicillin resistance in MRSA via inhibition of penicillin-binding protein 2a by Acalypha wilkesiana.

full_output.methodology: Microdilution assay, Western blot analysis, and FIC index calculation were used to evaluate the synergistic effects of 9EA-FC-B and ampicillin.

full_output.paper_title: Comprehensive identification of single nucleotide polymorphisms associated with beta-lactam resistance within pneumococcal mosaic genes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies 51 loci, including 301 SNPs, associated with beta-lactam non-susceptibility in Streptococcus pneumoniae, focusing on genes involved in peptidoglycan biosynthesis and other pathways.
full_output.methodology: Genome-wide association study using whole-genome sequences and beta-lactam susceptibility data from 3,701 pneumococcal isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Proteomic analysis of the action of the Mycobacterium ulcerans toxin mycolactone: targeting host cells cytoskeleton and collagen.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that mycolactone, a toxin from Mycobacterium ulcerans, affects the cytoskeleton and collagen biosynthesis in host cells, leading to structural and functional disruptions.
full_output.methodology: Proteomic analysis using two-dimensional electrophoresis (2-DE) to examine changes in the L929 mouse fibroblast proteome following mycolactone exposure.

The E117Q mutation showed significant improvements in both in vitro and in vivo toxin neutralization assays.
full_output.methodology: Computational design using FoldX, protein purification, binding affinity assays, and in vitro/in vivo toxin neutralization tests.

full_output.paper_title: Monitoring and comparison of antibiotic resistant bacteria and their resistance genes in municipal and hospital wastewaters.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of antibiotic-resistant bacteria and their corresponding resistance genes, including aac(3)-1, cmlA1, and ctx-m-32, in municipal and hospital wastewaters. These genes were detected in raw wastewater samples and showed varying frequencies in treated effluents.
full_output.methodology: PCR-based detection of resistance genes in isolated antibiotic-resistant bacteria from wastewater samples.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation of environmental bacteria from surface and drinking water in mafikeng, South Africa, and characterization using their antibiotic resistance profiles.

gyrB.mechanism: resistance to antibiotics via altered target

full_output.key_findings: The study identified Pseudomonas and Aeromonas species in water samples from Mafikeng, South Africa, and found that these isolates exhibited resistance to multiple antibiotics, including erythromycin, trimethoprim, and amoxicillin. The research highlights the presence of antibiotic-resistant bacteria in drinking water sources, emphasizing the need for improved water quality monitoring and control measures.
full_output.methodology: The study involved isolation and identification of environmental bacteria from water samples, followed by antibiotic susceptibility testing and molecular identification using PCR.

full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and resistome analysis using bioinformatics tools such as ResFinder and PlasmidFinder.

full_output.paper_title: Virulence profiles, phylogenetic background, and antibiotic resistance of Escherichia coli isolated from turkeys with airsacculitis.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes 225 Avian Pathogenic Escherichia coli (APEC) isolates from turkeys with airsacculitis, highlighting their multidrug resistance and virulence profiles. Key findings include high resistance to sulfamethazine (94%) and tetracycline (83%), with 92% of strains showing multidrug resistance. Virulence genes such as iroN, iss, and tsh were prevalent, and the B2 phylogenetic group was strongly associated with higher virulence and antibiotic susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: PCR for virulence genotyping, disc diffusion for antibiotic resistance testing, and phylogenetic analysis based on the presence of chuA, yjaA, and TSPE4.C2.

full_output.paper_title: Export of a single drug molecule in two transport cycles by a multidrug efflux pump.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that the multidrug transporter MdfA can actively export certain dicationic drugs with a unique architectural feature, where the two cationic moieties are separated by a long linker, in two successive transport cycles.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized drug resistance assays, transport experiments with everted membrane vesicles, and fluorescence-based techniques to analyze the interaction of MdfA with various dicationic drugs.

full_output.key_findings: The study compares biofilm formation among different methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) clones, highlighting that SCC mec type IV strains, including USA300 and EMRSA-15, exhibit robust biofilm formation, which may contribute to their epidemic success.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed biofilm formation in 76 MRSA strains using static and dynamic models, assessing biomass and structural characteristics of biofilms.

full_output.paper_title: Type II and type IV topoisomerase mutations in clinical isolates of Morganella morganii harbouring the qnrD gene.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first detection of the qnrD gene in Morganella morganii in Tunisia, along with two novel gyrB mutations (S463A, S464Y) and one parC mutation (S80I) contributing to quinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, nucleotide sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Stress response of Salmonella enterica serovar typhimurium to acidified nitrite.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies cadA as an important gene involved in the acidified-nitrite stress tolerance of Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium, demonstrating that its deletion leads to increased sensitivity to acidified NaNO2.
full_output.methodology: RNA sequencing, qPCR, and growth analysis using Bioscreen C were employed to analyze the stress response and validate the role of cadA.

full_output.paper_title: Diversity and antimicrobial resistance of Salmonella enterica isolates from surface water in Southeastern United States.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multidrug-resistant (MDR) Salmonella enterica serovar Newport isolates with resistance to multiple antibiotics, including amoxicillin-clavulanic acid, ampicillin-sulbactam, ceftazidime, ceftriaxone, cephalothin, chloramphenicol, streptomycin, tetracycline, and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. These isolates were found to have a PFGE pattern indistinguishable from clinical isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study used qPCR, PFGE, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing to analyze Salmonella isolates from surface water.

full_output.paper_title: A 24-well plate assay for simultaneous testing of first and second line drugs against Mycobacterium tuberculosis in a high endemic setting.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated a 24-well plate assay for drug susceptibility testing of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, demonstrating its effectiveness in detecting resistance to first-line drugs and highlighting the low prevalence of resistance to second-line drugs, except for ethionamide.
full_output.methodology: The 24-well plate assay was used for drug susceptibility testing of Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates, comparing results with molecular assays and evaluating resistance patterns.

full_output.paper_title: Controlling resistant bacteria with a novel class of β-lactamase inhibitor peptides: from rational design to in vivo analyses.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes the development of two novel β-lactamase inhibitor peptides, dBLIP-1 and dBLIP-2, which effectively neutralize bacterial resistance by inhibiting β-lactamase activity, thereby enhancing the efficacy of β-lactam antibiotics against resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized rational design, molecular modeling, in silico docking, and in vitro/in vivo experiments to develop and validate the β-lactamase inhibitor peptides.
full_output.sample_size: Clinical isolates from Priyamvada Birla Aravind Eye Hospital in Kolkata, India

full_output.paper_title: A study of Mycobacterium tuberculosis genotypic diversity & drug resistance mutations in Varanasi, north India.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the Beijing genotype as the most frequent spoligotype and strongly associated with multidrug-resistant (MDR)-TB isolates in Varanasi, north India. Mutations in katG (315Thr), rpoB (516Leu, 526Arg, 531Leu), and embB (306Val, 306Ile) were detected, which confer resistance to isoniazid, rifampicin, and ethambutol, respectively.
full_output.methodology: MAS-PCR assay for detection of drug resistance mutations in M. tuberculosis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing for Helicobacter pylori in times of increasing antibiotic resistance.

H. pylori.notes: Mutations in the 23S rRNA gene confer resistance to clarithromycin.

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the increasing antibiotic resistance in Helicobacter pylori, particularly focusing on clarithromycin and quinolone resistance. It highlights the importance of molecular testing for detecting resistance-associated mutations.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews various methods for antimicrobial susceptibility testing, including culture, disc diffusion, Etest, and molecular tests for detecting resistance mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Highly drug-resistant pathogens implicated in burn-associated bacteremia in an Iraqi burn care unit.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies highly drug-resistant pathogens, including Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Staphylococcus aureus, as significant causes of burn-associated bacteremia in Iraq. Many of these isolates showed resistance to multiple antibiotics, highlighting the urgent need for effective empirical treatment strategies.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of blood culture isolates from burn patients with sepsis, including antibiotic susceptibility testing and identification of multidrug-resistant organisms.

full_output.paper_title: Mutations in the Primary Sigma Factor σA and Termination Factor Rho That Reduce Susceptibility to Cell Wall Antibiotics.

The sigA G336C mutation reduces susceptibility to vancomycin and fosfomycin, while the rho G56C mutation reduces susceptibility to cefuroxime.
full_output.methodology: Genetic reconstruction, MIC assays, and transcriptomic analysis were used to validate the resistance mechanisms conferred by the mutations in sigA and rho.

full_output.paper_title: Bacteriophage as effective decolonising agent for elimination of MRSA from anterior nares of BALB/c mice.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that bacteriophage MR-10 effectively reduces MRSA colonization in the nasal passages of BALB/c mice, with a synergistic effect when combined with mupirocin.
full_output.methodology: The study used a nasal colonization model in BALB/c mice, assessing the effects of bacteriophage MR-10 and mupirocin on MRSA adherence, invasion, and cytotoxicity in cultured nasal epithelial cells.

full_output.paper_title: Spread of carbapenemase-producing enterobacteria in a southwest hospital in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified IMP-4 and KPC-2 as carbapenemase genes responsible for carbapenem resistance in Enterobacteriaceae isolates from a hospital in China.
full_output.methodology: PCR, MIC testing, and PFGE analysis were used to identify and characterize carbapenemase-producing Enterobacteriaceae.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of Acinetobacter baumannii Serum-Associated Antibiotic Efflux Pump Inhibitors.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies two novel efflux pump inhibitors, ABEPI1 and ABEPI2, which enhance the antimicrobial activity of minocycline and ciprofloxacin against serum-grown Acinetobacter baumannii by inhibiting efflux pump activity.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput screening, ethidium bromide efflux assays, and cytotoxicity assays were used to identify and characterize the efflux pump inhibitors.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular mechanism of MBX2319 inhibition of Escherichia coli AcrB multidrug efflux pump and comparison with other inhibitors.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the molecular mechanism of MBX2319, a novel pyranopyridine efflux pump inhibitor, and compares its interaction with the AcrB multidrug efflux pump of Escherichia coli to other inhibitors. MBX2319 binds tightly to the lower part of the distal pocket in the B protomer of AcrB, interacting with phenylalanines in the hydrophobic trap. The study highlights the importance of the hydrophobic trap in inhibitor binding and the structural changes induced by inhibitors that affect substrate binding and efflux.
full_output.methodology: The study uses computational methods including docking and molecular dynamics simulations to analyze the interaction between MBX2319 and the AcrB efflux pump, comparing it with other inhibitors and substrates.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that inhibition of UDP-N-acetylmuramic acid l-alanine ligase (MurC) in a tolC mutant Escherichia coli strain leads to cell death, highlighting MurC as a potential target for novel antibacterial agents.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized biochemical assays, MIC measurements, and LC-MS/MS analysis to evaluate the effects of compound A on MurC inhibition and cellular activity.

full_output.paper_title: Comparison of the antibiotic activities of Daptomycin, Vancomycin, and the investigational Fluoroquinolone Delafloxacin against biofilms from Staphylococcus aureus clinical isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study compared the antibiotic activities of daptomycin, vancomycin, and delafloxacin against biofilms from Staphylococcus aureus clinical isolates, highlighting delafloxacin's superior effectiveness due to its penetration and activity in acidic environments.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro models, confocal microscopy, and susceptibility testing to evaluate antibiotic activities against biofilms.

full_output.paper_title: Enhanced killing of antibiotic-resistant bacteria enabled by massively parallel combinatorial genetics.
full_output.key_findings: The study utilized CombiGEM to identify genetic combinations that enhance the killing of antibiotic-resistant bacteria, particularly those harboring NDM-1, by modulating antibiotic activity through transcription factor overexpression.
full_output.methodology: The study employed CombiGEM, a high-throughput platform for generating and characterizing combinatorial genetic perturbations, along with high-throughput sequencing to analyze the effects of these combinations on antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Drug resistance is conferred on the model yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae by expression of full-length melanoma-associated human ATP-binding cassette transporter ABCB5.

full_output.key_findings: Full-length ABCB5 confers resistance to multiple substrates in Saccharomyces cerevisiae when expressed, demonstrating its role as an efflux pump.
full_output.methodology: Heterologous expression of ABCB5 in yeast followed by drug susceptibility assays.

full_output.paper_title: Mobile elements and chromosomal changes associated with MLS resistance phenotypes of invasive pneumococci recovered in the United States.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies various mutations in the 23S rRNA, rplD, and rplV genes associated with MLS resistance in Streptococcus pneumoniae, along with the presence of ermB and mef genes.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification, sequencing, and analysis of resistance mechanisms in pneumococcal isolates.

full_output.methodology: Enzymatic activity assays, DNA relaxation, catenation, and cleavage assays were performed to evaluate the impact of ParC mutations on quinolone activity.
