full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, PCR, and histopathological analysis were used to identify and characterize the PirA and PirB toxins in Vibrio punensis.

full_output.paper_title: Drug Resistance and Molecular Epidemiology of Carbapenem Resistant Gram-negative Bacilli Isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies blaNDM-1 as the most prevalent metallo-beta-lactamase gene among carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative bacilli, followed by blaVIM and blaIMP. These genes confer resistance to carbapenems.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic detection (Modified Hodge test, IMP-EDTA DDST, IMP-EDTA CDST) and genotypic detection (PCR and sequencing) of metallo-beta-lactamase genes.

full_output.paper_title: A prospective surveillance study for multidrug-resistant bacteria colonization in hospitalized patients at a Thai University Hospital.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a high baseline prevalence of colonization by ESBL-producing Enterobacteriaceae (52.2%) and identified risk factors such as diabetes mellitus and previous cephalosporin exposure. It also noted increases in colonization by CR-PA, CR-AB, and MRSA during hospitalization.
full_output.methodology: Prospective surveillance study involving microbiological sampling and analysis of antimicrobial resistance patterns in hospitalized patients.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that Campylobacter isolates from dogs and cats in Iran exhibited high resistance to tetracycline, with 87.5% resistance in dogs and 81.8% in cats. Resistance to other antibiotics such as ciprofloxacin, nalidixic acid, and cefazolin was also noted.
full_output.methodology: The study involved isolation and characterization of Campylobacter species from fecal samples of dogs and cats, followed by antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: A Multi-Centered Case-Case-Control Study of Factors Associated With Klebsiella pneumoniae Carbapenemase-Producing Enterobacteriaceae Infections in Children and Young Adults.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaKPC-2 and blaKPC-3 as the primary carbapenemase genes responsible for resistance in KPC-CRE isolates from pediatric patients, highlighting their role in multidrug resistance and the importance of monitoring their spread.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective case-case-control study with molecular analysis including PCR, DNA sequencing, and MLST.

full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify AMR genes and mutations in Salmonella Heidelberg strains.

full_output.paper_title: Genomics-guided discovery and structure identification of cyclic lipopeptides from the Bacillus siamensis JFL15.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified three gene clusters (srf, dhb, and fen) involved in the biosynthesis of cyclic lipopeptides (surfactin, bacillibactin, and fengycin) in Bacillus siamensis JFL15. These lipopeptides exhibited antifungal activity against several phytopathogens.

The phages showed lytic activity against the target bacteria and were effective in reducing bacterial load and increasing larval survival, particularly with multiple doses.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro lytic activity tests, in vivo Galleria mellonella infection models, and statistical analysis of survival rates and bacterial counts.

full_output.paper_title: A systematic review: the current status of carbapenem resistance in East Africa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several carbapenem resistance genes including blaVIM, blaIMP, blaNDM, blaOXA-48, blaOXA-23, blaOXA-24, and blaOXA-58 in various bacterial species in East Africa.

full_output.paper_title: Occurrence and Distribution of Tetracycline Antibiotics and Resistance Genes in Longshore Sediments of the Three Gorges Reservoir, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of tetracycline resistance genes tet(A), tet(C), and tet(M) in longshore sediments of the Three Gorges Reservoir, with varying abundances across different zones and seasons.
full_output.methodology: Real-time quantitative PCR was used to quantify the abundance of tetracycline resistance genes and class 1 integrons in sediment samples.

full_output.paper_title: Study of Benzofuroquinolinium Derivatives as a New Class of Potent Antibacterial Agent and the Mode of Inhibition Targeting FtsZ.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies benzofuroquinolinium derivatives as potent antibacterial agents targeting FtsZ, demonstrating effective inhibition of bacterial cell division and GTPase activity. Compound 5 showed particularly strong activity against multidrug-resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: Antibacterial activity was assessed through MIC determination, time-killing curves, and evaluation of GTPase and polymerization inhibition. Molecular modeling was used to predict binding modes.

full_output.paper_title: Trichomonas vaginalis Transports Virulent Mycoplasma hominis and Transmits the Infection to Human Cells after Metronidazole Treatment: A Potential Role in Bacterial Invasion of Fetal Membranes and Amniotic Fluid.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the presence of virulence genes goiC, alr, and goiB in Mycoplasma hominis associated with Trichomonas vaginalis, highlighting their potential role in amniotic cavity invasion and preterm labor.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and qPCR were used to analyze the presence and functionality of the virulence genes in Mycoplasma hominis.

full_output.paper_title: Distribution of Microbes and Drug Susceptibility in Patients with Diabetic Foot Infections in Southwest China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the microbial distribution and drug susceptibility patterns in diabetic foot infections, highlighting the prevalence of Gram-negative bacteria and multidrug-resistant strains, particularly in advanced Wagner grades and chronic wounds.
full_output.methodology: Microbial culture and drug susceptibility testing were conducted on samples from diabetic foot ulcers.

full_output.paper_title: Efficacy of Andrographis paniculata against extended spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL) producing E. coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that the CEA extract of A. paniculata could downregulate the expression of the bla CTX-M-15 gene in ESBL-producing E. coli strains, indicating its potential in reducing beta-lactam resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study involved phytochemical and FTIR analysis, antibiotic susceptibility testing, antibacterial and biofilm assays, and PCR gene expression analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Identification, Recombinant Expression, and Characterization of LHG2, a Novel Antimicrobial Peptide of Lactobacillus casei HZ1.
full_output.key_findings: LGH2, a novel antimicrobial peptide from Lactobacillus casei HZ1, shows strong activity against Staphylococcus aureus with an MIC of 4 μM. It disrupts the cell membrane integrity of S. aureus.
full_output.methodology: Genome analysis, recombinant expression in E. coli, antimicrobial testing, and membrane disruption assays.

full_output.paper_title: Epigenetic modulator UVI5008 inhibits MRSA by interfering with bacterial gyrase.
full_output.key_findings: UVI5008 inhibits MRSA by interfering with bacterial gyrase, showing potent antibacterial activity against methicillin-sensitive and resistant S. aureus strains.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial activity assays, biofilm production and degradation assays, structure-activity relationship studies, and enzymatic assays were conducted to evaluate UVI5008's mechanism of action and effectiveness.

full_output.paper_title: Global spread of three multidrug-resistant lineages of Staphylococcus epidermidis.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes mutations in the rpoB gene (D471E and I527M) that confer rifampicin resistance in S. epidermidis.

full_output.paper_title: Substrate-assisted enzymatic formation of lysinoalanine in duramycin.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies DurN as the enzyme responsible for catalyzing the formation of lysinoalanine (Lal) in duramycin, revealing its unique structural features and mechanism involving substrate-assisted catalysis.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized in vitro enzymatic assays, structural biology techniques, and mutational analysis to characterize the function and mechanism of DurN in Lal formation.

full_output.paper_title: Association Between agr Type, Virulence Factors, Biofilm Formation and Antibiotic Resistance of Staphylococcus aureus Isolates From Pork Production.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that S. aureus isolates from pork production exhibited diverse agr types, with agr I being the most prevalent. It also found a significant association between the prevalence of MSCRAMM, capsule type, and ica group genes with biofilm formation. Additionally, the study noted high levels of resistance to several antibiotics among moderate and weak biofilm producers.

full_output.paper_title: Rose Bengal-Mediated Photoinactivation of Multidrug Resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa Is Enhanced in the Presence of Antimicrobial Peptides.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies amiN and amiO as genes responsible for self-resistance to amicoumacin A (Ami) in Bacillus pumilus. AmiN acts as a kinase that phosphorylates Ami, rendering it inactive, while AmiO functions as a phosphatase that dephosphorylates Ami, reactivating it. This dynamic interplay between AmiN and AmiO regulates Ami's activity and contributes to self-resistance mechanisms in Bacillus species.
full_output.methodology: Genome mining, proteomics, metabolomics, and functional assays including transformation experiments and enzymatic activity tests were used to characterize the roles of amiN and amiO in Ami resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of cytotoxicity features of antimicrobial peptides with potential to control bacterial diseases of citrus.

full_output.paper_title: The trend of resistance to antibiotics for ocular infection of Staphylococcus aureus, coagulase-negative staphylococci, and Corynebacterium compared with 10-years previous: A retrospective observational study.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a significant decrease in the prevalence of methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) and methicillin-resistant coagulase-negative staphylococci (MR-CNS) over a 10-year period, while fluoroquinolone-resistant Corynebacterium remained consistently resistant. Resistance trends for MRSA and MR-CNS to antibiotics remained stable, and fluoroquinolone-resistant Corynebacterium showed high susceptibility to cefmenoxime (CMX).

full_output.paper_title: Hospital-acquired colonization and infections in a Vietnamese intensive care unit.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a high rate of ICU-acquired colonization with antimicrobial-resistant organisms (AROs), including methicillin-resistant S. aureus (16.2%) and ESBL-producing Enterobacteriaceae (39.8% for E. coli and 13.7% for Klebsiella spp.).

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple AMR genes in multidrug-resistant E. coli from pigs, including blaTEM-1, aadA1, strA/B, tetA, tetB, tetC, dfrA1, dfrA5, dfrA7, dfrA12, sul1, sul2, sul3, and qnrS, highlighting the complex nature of resistance in this environment.
full_output.methodology: PCR, antibiotic susceptibility testing, PFGE, and molecular analysis of mobile genetic elements.

full_output.paper_title: Systematic Identification and Classification of β-Lactamases Based on Sequence Similarity Criteria: β-Lactamase Annotation.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a systematic approach for identifying and classifying β-lactamases based on sequence similarity. It introduces a new class of β-lactamases with fused domains (SCD) and improves the classification of existing classes (SA, SC, SD, MB, ME).
full_output.methodology: The study uses Hidden Markov Models (HMM) and phylogenetic analysis to classify β-lactamases from a non-redundant dataset, validated through comparisons with existing databases and functional assays.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Characterization of Vancomycin, Mupirocin and Antiseptic Resistant Staphylococcus aureus Strains.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mupA, norA, smr, and qacA/B genes as prevalent in MRSA isolates, with mupA showing high prevalence in high-level mupirocin-resistant strains. No vanA gene was detected in vancomycin-resistant strains.

full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the increasing resistance rates of Pseudomonas aeruginosa to meropenem and imipenem, as well as high ertapenem resistance in ESBL-positive Klebsiella and E. coli isolates in pediatric nosocomial UTIs.

full_output.paper_title: Two novel mutations in parE among Shigella flexneri isolated from Jiangsu Province of China, 2016.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified two novel mutations in the parE gene of Shigella flexneri, Ser458Leu and Gly408Asp, which contribute to fluoroquinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used sequencing and PCR to identify mutations in the quinolone resistance-determining regions (QRDR) of S. flexneri isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic requirements for growth of Escherichia coli in isolation and in interaction with other cheese-associated bacteria
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies genes important for E. coli growth in isolation and in interaction with other cheese-associated bacteria, revealing changes in gene expression and metabolic requirements in different growth conditions.
full_output.methodology: The study uses RB-TnSeq and transcriptomic analysis to identify genes important for E. coli growth in various conditions.

full_output.paper_title: Natural variations in the promoter of OsSWEET13 and OsSWEET14 expand the range of resistance against Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae.

full_output.paper_title: Plant A20/AN1 protein serves as the important hub to mediate antiviral immunity.
full_output.key_findings: Pha13 and its Arabidopsis homolog AtSAP5 are involved in antiviral immunity by regulating the expression of SA-mediated immune responsive genes, including NPR1-dependent and -independent genes.
full_output.methodology: Transgenic plant generation, qRT-PCR, VIGS, and yeast two-hybrid assays were used to analyze the role of Pha13 and AtSAP5 in antiviral immunity.

full_output.paper_title: Great phenotypic and genetic variation among successive chronic Pseudomonas aeruginosa from a cystic fibrosis patient.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various AMR genes and mutations in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from a cystic fibrosis patient, including class 1 integrons with genes like aadA, cmlA, qacE, and sul1, as well as mutations in efflux pump genes (mexC, mexD, mexS, mexT, mexX, mexY, mexZ, nalC, nalD) and the porin oprD, contributing to multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used molecular typing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, efflux pump analysis, porin characterization, and integron structure determination to identify AMR genes and mutations in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Crystal structure of TcpK in complex with oriT DNA of the antibiotic resistance plasmid pCW3.

full_output.key_findings: TcpK is a winged helix-turn-helix transcription factor that binds to the oriT DNA of the pCW3 plasmid, playing a crucial role in the efficient conjugative transfer of the plasmid.
full_output.methodology: X-ray crystallography, gel mobility shift assays, surface plasmon resonance (SPR) analysis, and conjugation experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Converting organosulfur compounds to inorganic polysulfides against resistant bacterial infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a strategy to convert natural organosulfur compounds into nano-iron sulfides (nFeS) that exhibit enhanced antibacterial activity against pathogenic and drug-resistant bacteria. nFeS releases polysulfanes, which contribute to its antibacterial effects.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized solvothermal synthesis to produce nFeS from organosulfur compounds and evaluated their antibacterial activity through colony-forming unit (CFU) analysis, reactive oxygen species (ROS) measurement, and biofilm disruption assays.

full_output.paper_title: Critical steps in clinical shotgun metagenomics for the concomitant detection and typing of microbial pathogens.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes various AMR genes involved in resistance to multiple antibiotics, including beta-lactams, aminoglycosides, macrolides, tetracyclines, and others, in different bacterial species such as Staphylococcus aureus, Enterococcus faecium, and Serratia marcescens.
full_output.methodology: The study uses shotgun metagenomics combined with WGS and phenotypic resistance testing to identify and characterize AMR genes in clinical samples.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies NLRP1 as a key regulator of gut microbiota composition, particularly affecting the abundance of Clostridiales, which produce butyrate. Loss of NLRP1 protects against DSS-induced colitis by increasing butyrate-producing bacteria, while activation of NLRP1 exacerbates colitis by reducing these bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The study uses genetic knockout and overexpression models in mice, along with microbiome analysis and cytokine profiling to investigate the role of NLRP1 in inflammatory bowel disease.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of Aminoglycoside Resistance Genes in Enterococcus Strains in Kermanshah, Iran.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified aac(6′)-Ie-aph(2”)-Ia, ant(6’)-Ia, and ant(3”)-III as prevalent aminoglycoside resistance genes in Enterococcus strains from Kermanshah, Iran, with aac(6′)-Ie-aph(2”)-Ia being the most common.
full_output.methodology: PCR and disc diffusion method for detecting aminoglycoside resistance genes and phenotypic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Chitosan-polyvinyl alcohol nanoscale liquid film-forming system facilitates MRSA-infected wound healing by enhancing antibacterial and antibiofilm properties.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that the chitosan-polyvinyl alcohol nanoscale liquid film-forming system (LFFS) enhances antibacterial and antibiofilm properties against MRSA, showing superior efficacy compared to benzalkonium bromide (BZL) in reducing bacterial load and promoting wound healing.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antibacterial and antibiofilm properties of the LFFS through in vitro and in vivo experiments, including MIC determination, time-kill assays, biofilm disruption, and wound healing assessments in a murine model.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiology of and risk factors for infection with extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae: results of a double case-control study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various β-lactamase genes (CTX-M, TEM, SHV, NDM, KPC, IMP, OXA) associated with resistance to carbapenems and cephalosporins in Enterobacteriaceae isolates. These genes were detected through PCR and correlated with resistance profiles in clinical isolates.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of β-lactamase and carbapenemase genes, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and statistical analysis of risk factors for ESBL-CRE and non-ESBL-CRE infections.

full_output.paper_title: Resistance pattern and maternal knowledge, attitude and practices of suspected Diarrheagenic Escherichia coli among children under 5 years of age in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia: cross sectional study.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a high frequency of multidrug-resistant E. coli among children under 5 with acute diarrhea, with high resistance rates to ampicillin, augmentin, and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, but low resistance to ciprofloxacin and ceftriaxone.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the disk diffusion method on E. coli isolates from stool samples of children with acute diarrhea.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Epidemiology and Mechanisms of 43 Low-Level Linezolid-Resistant Enterococcus faecalis Strains in Chongqing, China.

full_output.paper_title: Bacteria richness and antibiotic-resistance in bats from a protected area in the Atlantic Forest of Southeastern Brazil.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several bacteria with antibiotic resistance, including Serratia marcescens, Acinetobacter baumannii, Escherichia coli, and Klebsiella oxytoca, which showed resistance to various antibiotics such as ampicillin, cephalexin, and amoxicillin-clavulanate.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing using Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid detection of NDM, KPC and OXA-48 carbapenemases directly from positive blood cultures using a new multiplex immunochromatographic assay.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a new multiplex immunochromatographic assay (ICT) for the rapid detection of NDM, KPC, and OXA-48 carbapenemases directly from positive blood cultures, achieving 100% sensitivity and specificity.
full_output.methodology: Development and evaluation of a new ICT for detecting carbapenemases in blood cultures.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that enrofloxacin-resistant Escherichia coli isolates were prevalent in turkeys after therapeutic exposure, while amplicillin resistance was also observed. No specific AMR genes or mutations were experimentally characterized in this paper.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth microdilution to determine antimicrobial resistance in E. coli isolates from turkeys exposed to enrofloxacin.

full_output.key_findings: Exogenous polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) alter phospholipid composition, membrane permeability, and resistance to antimicrobial peptides in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: Analysis of phospholipid profiles, membrane permeability assays, and antimicrobial peptide susceptibility testing.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the structure and function of SkfB, a sactisynthase involved in the biosynthesis of sactipeptides, focusing on its modular architecture and iron-sulfur cluster binding properties.
full_output.methodology: Structural and spectroscopic analyses, including X-ray crystallography and Mössbauer spectroscopy.

full_output.paper_title: InhA, the enoyl-thioester reductase from Mycobacterium tuberculosis forms a covalent adduct during catalysis.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: partial loss of stereospecificity of proton donation

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in InhA, a key enzyme in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, that affect catalytic efficiency and protonation specificity, highlighting the role of specific residues in the enzymatic mechanism.
full_output.methodology: Kinetic analysis, isotopic labeling, and structural studies were used to characterize the role of InhA mutations in catalysis and protonation.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified that Escherichia coli O157:H7 adapted to sublethal concentrations of thymol, carvacrol, and trans-cinnamaldehyde exhibited enhanced resistance to subsequent lethal treatments with these essential oils, heat, and oxidative stress. Transcriptomic analysis revealed upregulation of stress response genes and downregulation of virulence genes.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized RNA sequencing to analyze transcriptomic changes in E. coli O157:H7 adapted to sublethal concentrations of essential oils, along with resistance assays to evaluate stress resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Phage-Antibiotic Synergy via Delayed Lysis
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates phage-antibiotic synergy (PAS) and reveals that sublethal concentrations of antibiotics and other stressors can enhance phage production by delaying lysis in filamented bacterial hosts.
full_output.methodology: The study used bacterial cultures, phages, and various antibiotics to examine the effects on phage production and bacterial morphology.

full_output.paper_title: The binding of Class II sRNA MgrR to two different sites on matchmaker protein Hfq enables efficient competition for Hfq and annealing to regulated mRNAs.

mgrR.notes: MgrR is a small RNA that binds to Hfq and facilitates the annealing of MgrR to target mRNAs.

ygqD.notes: Mutations in the uridine-rich sequences of ygdQ mRNA disrupt Hfq-mediated annealing of MgrR.

full_output.key_findings: The study reveals that the Class II sRNA MgrR binds to both the proximal and distal faces of Hfq, facilitating efficient competition for Hfq and annealing to target mRNAs eptB and ygdQ. Mutations in specific uridine-rich sequences of these mRNAs affect the efficiency of MgrR annealing, highlighting the importance of these sequences in Hfq-mediated interactions.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized gel shift assays, structure probing with RNases, and global kinetic modeling to analyze the interactions between MgrR, Hfq, and target mRNAs eptB and ygdQ.

full_output.paper_title: Proteolysis of ToxR is controlled by cysteine-thiol redox state and bile salts in Vibrio cholerae.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes deletions in the toxS and degS genes in Vibrio cholerae, highlighting their roles in gene regulation and protein stability.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of Missing Carbon Fixation Enzymes as Potential Drug Targets in Mycobacterium Tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified and characterized carbon fixation enzymes in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, particularly those involved in the reductive TCA cycle for CO2 fixation, highlighting their potential as drug targets.
full_output.methodology: Pathway analysis, enzyme annotation, and comparative genomics were used to identify and characterize carbon fixation enzymes in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance of pathogens causing nosocomial bloodstream infection in Hubei Province, China, from 2014 to 2016: a multicenter retrospective study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified E. coli, S. aureus, and K. pneumoniae as the most common pathogens causing nosocomial bloodstream infections in Hubei Province, China. It highlighted the prevalence of multidrug-resistant strains, including methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA), extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing E. coli and K. pneumoniae, and carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of data from the China Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance System (CARSS) from 2014 to 2016, involving antimicrobial susceptibility testing using CLSI guidelines.
full_output.sample_size: Data from 11 secondary care hospitals and 41 tertiary care hospitals

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial activities of flavonoid glycosides from Graptophyllum grandulosum and their mechanism of antibacterial action.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified five flavonoid glycosides from Graptophyllum grandulosum with antimicrobial activities, showing cell lysis and disruption of the cytoplasmic membrane as their mechanism of action.
full_output.methodology: The antimicrobial activities of extracts and isolated compounds were evaluated using broth microdilution, time-kill kinetic, and cell membrane integrity assays.

full_output.paper_title: Longitudinal development of the dust microbiome in a newly opened Norwegian kindergarten.
full_output.key_findings: The study detected the presence of antibiotic resistance genes mecA, ermA, and aac(6')-aph(2'') in dust samples from a newly opened Norwegian kindergarten, indicating the presence of resistant bacteria and a potential for resistance spread.
full_output.methodology: 16S rRNA gene sequencing and PCR detection of antibiotic resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular analysis of Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolated from clinical, environmental and cockroach sources by ERIC-PCR.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from clinical, environmental, and cockroach sources, highlighting their multidrug resistance and virulence factors. No specific AMR genes or mutations were experimentally validated in this study.
full_output.methodology: The study used ERIC-PCR for molecular typing and disk diffusion for antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Discovery of novel fragments inhibiting O-acetylserine sulphhydrylase by combining scaffold hopping and ligand-based drug design.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several novel pyrazole derivatives that inhibit O-acetylserine sulphhydrylase (OASS), an enzyme involved in cysteine biosynthesis in bacteria. These compounds show varying degrees of inhibitory activity against OASS-A and OASS-B isoforms from Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium.
full_output.methodology: The research employed a combination of scaffold hopping and ligand-based drug design approaches, along with biochemical assays to evaluate the inhibitory activity of the synthesized compounds against OASS.

full_output.paper_title: Ceftazidime-Avibactam Population Pharmacokinetic Modeling and Pharmacodynamic Target Attainment Across Adult Indications and Patient Subgroups.
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on the pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic properties of ceftazidime-avibactam, highlighting its effectiveness across various patient subgroups and indications, but did not identify any specific AMR genes or mutations.
full_output.methodology: Population pharmacokinetic modeling and pharmacodynamic target attainment analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Effect of natural curcuminoids-intercalated layered double hydroxide nanohybrid against Staphylococcus aureus, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Enterococcus faecalis: A bactericidal, antibiofilm, and mechanistic study.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antibacterial and antibiofilm effects of curcuminoids-intercalated Mg/Al layered double hydroxide (curcuminoids-LDH) against Staphylococcus aureus, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Enterococcus faecalis. It demonstrated that curcuminoids-LDH exhibited significant antibacterial activity, with MIC values of 0.200 g/ml for P. aeruginosa, 0.025 g/ml for S. aureus, and 0.100 g/ml for E. faecalis. The nanohybrid also showed effective biofilm inhibition, reducing biofilm biomass by over 50% at concentrations as low as 0.010 g/ml.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial activity was assessed using agar well diffusion, broth microdilution, and MTT/CV assays. Biofilm inhibition was evaluated using MBIC 50 measurements. SEM and UV-visible spectroscopy were employed to analyze structural changes and mechanisms of action.

full_output.paper_title: Colistin resistance due to insertional inactivation of the mgrB in Klebsiella pneumoniae of clinical origin: First report from India.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified insertional inactivation of the mgrB gene due to IS Kpn14 as a cause of colistin resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from India.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial susceptibility of slowly growing non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) using the SLOMYCO test system, revealing differences in resistance patterns among M. avium, M. intracellulare, M. kansasii, and M. xenopi to various drugs.

full_output.paper_title: Topoisomerase I and III Control R-Loop Formation and cSDR in E. coli

full_output.methodology: The study uses genetic mutants, qPCR, and NGS to analyze the effects of topoisomerase deficiencies on R-loop formation and DNA replication.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular epidemiology and drug resistance patterns of Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex isolates from university students and the local community in Eastern Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified MTBC lineages and sub-lineages, with Ethiopia_3 being the most prevalent and associated with strain clustering. Drug resistance was observed in 30% of participants, with resistance to first-line drugs most common for streptomycin and isoniazid.

full_output.paper_title: The Use of Liquids Ionic Fluids as Pharmaceutically Active Substances Helpful in Combating Nosocomial Infections Induced by Klebsiella Pneumoniae New Delhi Strain, Acinetobacter Baumannii and Enterococcus Species.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the potential of ionic liquids as alternatives to antibiotics for combating multidrug-resistant bacteria, including Klebsiella pneumoniae NDM-1, Acinetobacter baumannii, and Enterococcus species. It highlights the antimicrobial properties of quaternary ammonium halides and their mechanisms of action against bacterial and fungal pathogens.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews existing literature on the antimicrobial properties of ionic liquids and their applications in combating nosocomial infections.

full_output.methodology: Mutagenesis, reporter assays, pyocyanin production, animal infection models, and molecular biology techniques.

full_output.paper_title: Synergistic Antimicrobial Activity of Colistin in Combination with Rifampin and Azithromycin against Escherichia coli Producing MCR-1.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the mcr-1 gene as a critical factor in colistin resistance in Escherichia coli, demonstrating that colistin-based combinations with rifampin and azithromycin show synergistic antimicrobial activity against E. coli producing MCR-1.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antimicrobial activity of colistin combinations with rifampin and azithromycin using time-kill assays and in vivo mouse models.

full_output.paper_title: Novel Clade C-I Clostridium difficile strains escape diagnostic tests, differ in pathogenicity potential and carry toxins on extrachromosomal elements.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies three novel Clostridium difficile strains (HMX-149, HMX-152, HSJD-312) belonging to Clade C-I that exhibit unique toxin loci structures and escape conventional diagnostic tests. These strains carry tcdB and cdtB genes, but lack tcdA and tcdC, indicating atypical PaLoc structures. The strains show varied pathogenicity and antibiotic susceptibility profiles.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, PCR, toxin detection assays, and animal infection models were used to characterize the novel C. difficile strains.

full_output.paper_title: Mycobacterium tuberculosis carrying a rifampicin drug resistance mutation reprograms macrophage metabolism through cell wall lipid changes.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the rpoB-H445Y mutation as a cause of rifampicin resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis and shows that this mutation reprograms macrophage metabolism through changes in cell wall lipids.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, Sanger sequencing, and drug susceptibility testing were used to identify and validate the rpoB-H445Y mutation.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular typing and profiling of topoisomerase mutations causing resistance to ciprofloxacin and levofloxacin in Elizabethkingia species.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the gyrA gene, specifically Ser83Ile, Ser83Arg, and Asp87Asn, as the primary mechanisms of resistance to ciprofloxacin and levofloxacin in Elizabethkingia species.
full_output.methodology: The study used DNA sequencing and a high-resolution melting assay to detect mutations in the gyrA gene and determine fluoroquinolone susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotics Resistance Genes Screening and Comparative Genomics Analysis of Commensal Escherichia coli Isolated from Poultry Farms between China and Sudan.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antibiotic resistance genes in commensal E. coli isolates from poultry farms in China and Sudan, highlighting differences in resistance profiles between the two regions.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification and whole genome sequencing were used to identify and compare antibiotic resistance genes in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Whole-genome sequence data and analysis of a Staphylococcus aureus strain SJTUF_J27 isolated from seaweed.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the complete genome sequence of S. aureus SJTUF_J27, identifying several antimicrobial resistance genes including those for fluoroquinolone, beta-lactam, fosfomycin, mupirocin, trimethoprim, and aminocoumarin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Multilocus Sequence Typing of Mycoplasma pneumoniae, Japan, 2002-2016.

full_output.methodology: Multilocus sequence typing (MLST) and MIC determination were used to analyze genetic diversity and antimicrobial resistance in Mycoplasma pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid Increase in Carriage Rates of Enterobacteriaceae Producing Extended-Spectrum β-Lactamases in Healthy Preschool Children, Sweden.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a rapid increase in carriage rates of ESBL-producing Enterobacteriaceae in healthy preschool children in Sweden, with CTX-M-15, CTX-M-14, CTX-M-14-like, CTX-M-55, CTX-M-57, CTX-M-27, and various TEM variants being prevalent.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic Diversity and Antimicrobial Drug Resistance of Serotype VI Group B Streptococcus, Canada.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several AMR genes associated with resistance to erythromycin, clindamycin, and tetracycline in serotype VI Group B Streptococcus isolates from Canada.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and in silico multilocus sequence typing were used to analyze the genetic diversity and AMR profiles of the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro test systems to determine tetracycline residue binding to human feces.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates tetracycline residue binding to human feces using chemical and microbiological assays, showing that tetracycline binds significantly to fecal materials, affecting its availability to intestinal microorganisms.
full_output.methodology: Chemical and microbiological assays were used to analyze tetracycline binding to human feces, including HPLC, LC-MS/MS, and microbiological susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Amycomicin is a potent and specific antibiotic discovered with a targeted interaction screen.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies amycomicin (AMY) as a potent and specific antibiotic targeting fatty acid biosynthesis in Staphylococcus aureus. AMY inhibits the enzyme FabH, which is crucial for fatty acid biosynthesis, and shows effectiveness in a mouse skin-infection model.
full_output.methodology: The study used a targeted interaction screen involving actinomycete communities to discover AMY, followed by biochemical and genetic analyses to confirm its mechanism of action.

full_output.paper_title: Inhibition of Rho Activity Increases Expression of SaeRS-Dependent Virulence Factor Genes in Staphylococcus aureus, Showing a Link between Transcription Termination, Antibiotic Action, and Virulence.
full_output.key_findings: The study reveals that Rho deficiency in Staphylococcus aureus leads to increased expression of SaeRS-dependent virulence factor genes, highlighting a link between transcription termination, antibiotic action, and virulence regulation.
full_output.methodology: Proteome and transcriptome analyses were conducted using mass spectrometry and microarray techniques.

full_output.paper_title: Both toxic and beneficial effects of pyocyanin contribute to the lifecycle of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that pyocyanin (PYO) exhibits dual effects on Pseudomonas aeruginosa, acting as both a toxin and a beneficial compound depending on the physiological state of the cells. PYO-induced cell death is influenced by nutrient availability, with carbon limitation exacerbating toxicity. Additionally, a subpopulation of cells shows intrinsic resistance to PYO, suggesting a complex interplay between PYO's toxic and protective roles in biofilm development.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized biofilm development assays, planktonic culture experiments, and fluorescence microscopy to investigate PYO's effects on P. aeruginosa, along with transcriptomic analysis to understand defense mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Heavy metal sensitivities of gene deletion strains for ITT1 and RPS1A connect their activities to the expression of URE2, a key gene involved in metal detoxification in yeast.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies URE2 as a key gene involved in metal detoxification in yeast, showing that deletion of ITT1 or RPS1A increases yeast sensitivity to heavy metals, linking their activities to URE2 expression.

full_output.paper_title: Design, Synthesis and Evaluation of N-pyrazinylbenzamides as Potential Antimycobacterial Agents.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated N-pyrazinylbenzamides as potential antimycobacterial agents, focusing on their activity against Mycobacterium tuberculosis and other mycobacterial strains. Some compounds showed promising antimycobacterial activity with low MIC values, while others exhibited lower activity or were inactive. The study also highlighted the impact of structural modifications on the compounds' biological activity.
full_output.methodology: The compounds were synthesized through benzoylation of aminopyrazine, 5-chloropyrazin-2-amine, or 6-chloropyrazin-2-amine. Their antimycobacterial, antibacterial, and antifungal activities were assessed using various in vitro assays, including Microplate Alamar Blue Assays and microdilution methods.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the yefM-yoeB and relBE toxin-antitoxin operons in Streptococcus pneumoniae, showing their roles in oxidative stress response and biofilm formation.

full_output.paper_title: The effects of ultrasound exposure on P-glycoprotein-mediated multidrug resistance in vitro and in vivo.

full_output.methodology: In vitro and in vivo experiments using cell lines and xenograft models, along with molecular techniques such as Western blot, Q-PCR, and luciferase assays.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of antibiotic resistance in Campylobacter jejuni isolates from Shenzhen, with the highest resistance rates observed for ciprofloxacin (89.7%), tetracycline (74.6%), and nalidixic acid (69.0%).
full_output.methodology: Multilocus sequence typing and agar dilution methods were used to analyze the genetic profiles and antibiotic resistance of C. jejuni isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the increasing prevalence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) nontyphoidal Salmonella serotype Typhimurium in southern Brazil, particularly among hospitalized patients. full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance in Enterobacteriaceae from healthy broilers in Egypt: emergence of colistin-resistant and extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli.

full_output.methodology: PCR, E-test, microarray analysis, and phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to identify resistance genes and determine antimicrobial resistance profiles.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Activity of Gallium Compounds on ESKAPE Pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antibacterial activity of gallium compounds (GaN, GaM, and GaPPIX) against ESKAPE pathogens, revealing that certain strains were susceptible to GaPPIX, particularly in iron-poor environments. The presence of heme-uptake systems significantly influenced GaPPIX susceptibility in A. baumannii.
full_output.methodology: The study used microdilution and disk diffusion assays to determine the minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) of gallium compounds against various ESKAPE pathogens in different media.

full_output.key_findings: Nitric oxide (•NO) reverses drug resistance by inhibiting the ATPase activity of P-glycoprotein (P-gp) in human multi-drug resistant cancer cells, leading to increased drug accumulation and reversal of adriamycin and taxol resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies che-3 and dhc-3 as novel IVM resistance genes in C. elegans, highlighting the role of intraflagellar transport defects in IVM resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae strains in children with acute otitis media- high risk of persistent colonization after treatment.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a high prevalence of antibiotic-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae strains in children with acute otitis media, particularly those with treatment failure and recurrent infections. Multidrug resistance was common, with 84% of strains being multidrug resistant. The study highlights the association between persistent pneumococcal colonization after treatment and the risk of infection recurrence.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed 55 pneumococcal isolates from middle ear fluid and nasopharyngeal/oropharyngeal samples using serotyping, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and multilocus sequence typing.

full_output.paper_title: Environmental transmission of Clostridioides difficile ribotype 027 at a long-term care facility; an outbreak investigation guided by whole genome sequencing.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaTEM-1D, a beta-lactamase gene, in two strains (clinical strain FCH-4 and environmental strain LTC-7B) as part of an outbreak investigation of Clostridioides difficile ribotype 027 in a long-term care facility.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and molecular typing techniques were used to investigate the outbreak and identify antimicrobial resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: TFPI-2 Protects Against Gram-Negative Bacterial Infection.
full_output.key_findings: EDC34, a C-terminal peptide of TFPI-2, exhibits antimicrobial activity by binding to immunoglobulins and enhancing complement activation, thereby protecting against Gram-negative bacterial infections.

full_output.paper_title: Powering the ABC multidrug exporter LmrA: How nucleotides embrace the ion-motive force.

full_output.paper_title: Fluoroquinolone Prophylaxis Selects for Meropenem-nonsusceptible Pseudomonas aeruginosa in Patients With Hematologic Malignancies and Hematopoietic Cell Transplant Recipients.

full_output.methodology: The study assessed the probiotic properties of 35 LAB strains through in vitro tests including acid, pepsin, and bile salt tolerance, antibiotic susceptibility, and antimicrobial activity against P. aeruginosa using agar diffusion assays.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative genome analysis provides deep insights into Aeromonas hydrophila taxonomy and virulence-related factors.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antibiotic resistance genes in Aeromonas hydrophila, including beta-lactamases, aminoglycoside modifying enzymes, quinolone resistance gene qnrA4, and multidrug efflux pumps. full_output.paper_title: Deciphering Resistome and Virulome Diversity in a Porcine Slaughterhouse and Pork Products Through Its Production Chain.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several AMR genes in M. abscessus, including erm(41) for macrolide resistance, aac(2') and eis2 for aminoglycoside resistance, aph(3")-Ic for streptomycin resistance, bla_Mab for beta-lactam resistance, arr_Mab for rifamycin resistance, and mabtetx for tetracycline resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genetic studies, drug susceptibility testing, and biochemical analysis were used to characterize the AMR genes in M. abscessus.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Runx3 as a critical transcription factor that enhances the function of group 1 ILCs and NCR+ILC3s in combating intracellular bacterial infections by promoting IL12Rβ2 expression and IFNγ secretion.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized genetic knockout models, flow cytometry, and functional assays to analyze the role of Runx3 in innate immune responses against intracellular pathogens.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of Salmonella enterica serovars recovered from meat products legally and illegally imported into the EU reveals the presence of multiresistant and AmpC-producing isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiresistant Salmonella enterica isolates from legally and illegally imported meat, including AmpC-producing isolates carrying blaCMY-2, tet(A), and sul2 genes, which confer resistance to cephalosporins, tetracycline, and sulfonamides.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR, sequencing, and conjugation experiments were used to characterize resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Ail provides multiple mechanisms of serum resistance to Yersinia pestis.

mutations_found.validated_by: co-sedimentation assays and serum resistance assays
co-sedimentation assays and serum resistance assays

Ail.notes: Mutation of F80 reduces recruitment of vitronectin, factor H, and C4BP

full_output.key_findings: Ail provides multiple mechanisms of serum resistance to Yersinia pestis, including the recruitment of complement regulatory factors and interference with MAC assembly. Mutations in Ail, such as F80A, F130A, E43K, and G122D, affect serum resistance through different mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Co-sedimentation assays, serum resistance assays, and western blotting were used to investigate the role of Ail in serum resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Self-derived structure-disrupting peptides targeting methionine aminopeptidase in pathogenic bacteria: a new strategy to generate antimicrobial peptides.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies self-derived structure-disrupting peptides, such as KFF-Ec H3 and KFF-Ng H1, which target methionine aminopeptidase (MetAP) in pathogenic bacteria, leading to bacterial growth inhibition and no detectable resistance development.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized biophysical experiments, cell inhibition assays, molecular dynamics simulations, and structural analysis to evaluate the efficacy and mechanism of action of the peptides.

full_output.paper_title: In planta expression of nanobody-based designer chicken antibodies targeting Campylobacter.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes the design and expression of chimeric antibodies derived from nanobodies targeting Campylobacter's major outer membrane protein (MOMP) and flagella. These antibodies were successfully expressed in plant tissues and shown to bind to their targets, reducing bacterial motility.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized genetic engineering techniques to fuse nanobodies with chicken immunoglobulin constant domains, expressed in plants, and evaluated their functionality through various biochemical and microbiological assays.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of a novel zinc-binding protein, C1orf123, as an interactor with a heavy metal-associated domain.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies C1orf123 as a novel zinc-binding protein that interacts specifically with the HMA domain of CCS dI. C1orf123 binds a Zn2+ ion in a tetrahedral coordination with four cysteine residues from two CxxC motifs.
full_output.methodology: Yeast two-hybrid screening, X-ray crystallography, and biochemical analyses were used to characterize C1orf123 and its interaction with CCS dI.

full_output.paper_title: The development and deployment of a field-based loop mediated isothermal amplification assay for virulent Dichelobacter nodosus detection on Australian sheep.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a field-based LAMP assay for detecting the virulent Dichelobacter nodosus strain carrying the aprV2 gene, which is associated with severe footrot in sheep. The assay effectively distinguished aprV2 from the benign aprB2 gene variant.
full_output.methodology: Development and optimization of a LAMP assay for detecting aprV2 and aprB2 genes in Dichelobacter nodosus.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic structure of four plasmids found in Acinetobacter baumannii isolate D36 belonging to lineage 2 of global clone 1.

aphA1a.evidence_note: aphA1a gene is located within Tn 4352 ::ISAba1

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies four plasmids in Acinetobacter baumannii isolate D36, including pRAY* carrying aadB, pD36-4 carrying aphA1a, sul2, and a mercury resistance module, and others with no resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: Plasmid sequencing, functional analysis, and conjugation experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of putative effectors of the Type IV secretion system from the Wolbachia endosymbiont of Brugia malayi.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies wBm0076 and wBm0152 as putative effectors of the Type IV secretion system from Wolbachia, which disrupt yeast actin cytoskeleton dynamics and endosome: vacuole cargo trafficking, respectively.
full_output.methodology: Yeast expression and analysis of vacuole dynamics and actin cytoskeleton.

full_output.paper_title: Manipulation of the silkworm immune system by a metalloprotease from the pathogenic bacterium Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies elastase B from Pseudomonas aeruginosa as a virulent factor that manipulates the silkworm immune system by suppressing PPO activation and stimulating AMP production.
full_output.methodology: Purification of elastase B, creation of lasB deletion and complemented mutants, PO activity and AMP measurements, and analysis of gene expression.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the feasibility of real-time nanopore-based metagenomic sequencing for detecting bacterial infections in prosthetic joint infections, showing concordance with traditional culture and Illumina sequencing methods.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized Oxford Nanopore MinION sequencing for real-time analysis of DNA extracted from sonication fluids of orthopaedic devices, employing a custom bioinformatics pipeline (CRuMPIT) for pathogen detection and analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial Activity and Mechanism of Action of Bovine Lactoferricin Derivatives with Symmetrical Amino Acid Sequences.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the antibacterial activity of engineered peptides derived from bovine lactoferricin (LFcinB18-28) with symmetrical amino acid sequences. The peptides KW-WK, FP-PF, and KK-KK showed enhanced antibacterial activity compared to the original peptide, while FW-WF exhibited hemolytic activity. The mechanism involved membrane permeabilization and disruption of bacterial cell integrity.
full_output.methodology: The study used peptide synthesis, antimicrobial activity assays, hemolytic activity tests, and microscopic analyses to evaluate the effects of the engineered peptides.

full_output.paper_title: A rapid identification technique for drug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates using mismatch specific cleavage enzyme.

rpoB.notes: Mutations in rpoB are associated with rifampicin resistance.

inhA.notes: Mutations in inhA are associated with isoniazid resistance.

katG.notes: Mutations in katG are associated with isoniazid resistance.

gyrA.notes: Mutations in gyrA are associated with fluoroquinolone resistance.

rrs.notes: Mutations in rrs are associated with aminoglycoside resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study presents a rapid technique for identifying drug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates by detecting mutations in rpoB, inhA, katG, gyrA, and rrs genes using a mismatch-specific cleavage enzyme.
full_output.methodology: The methodology involves generating PCR products for specific genes, hybridizing them with a reference strain, and using a cleavage enzyme to detect mismatches through agarose gel electrophoresis.

full_output.paper_title: Comparison of antibiotic resistance phenotypes in laboratory strains and clinical isolates of Staphylococcus aureus, Salmonella Typhimurium, and Klebsiella pneumoniae.

bla.validation_method: MIC testing with and without beta-lactamase inhibitor

full_output.key_findings: The study identified beta-lactamase activity in various bacterial strains, indicating resistance to multiple beta-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility assays, lactamase inhibition assays, and efflux pump inhibition assays were performed.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of β-lactamase- and efflux pump-mediated multiple antibiotic resistance in Salmonella Typhimurium.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaTEM as a β-lactamase gene contributing to ampicillin and ceftriaxone resistance in Salmonella Typhimurium. The gene was experimentally validated through β-lactamase activity assays.
full_output.methodology: The study used β-lactamase activity assays, efflux pump activity assays, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing to characterize resistance mechanisms.

full_output.key_findings: The study explores how chemical gradients, such as pH and oxygen, influence the cystic fibrosis lung microbiome, revealing that these gradients partition the microbial community into distinct groups. It also highlights the impact of inhaled therapies like tobramycin and sodium bicarbonate on microbial community structure and resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a WinCF microcosm system to analyze microbial community changes under varying pH and oxygen gradients, along with metabolomic and microbiome sequencing approaches.
full_output.sample_size: 18 patients for pH experiments, 19 patients for oxygen experiments

full_output.paper_title: Association between possession of ExoU and antibiotic resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in gyrA, parC, mexR, ampC, and ampR genes associated with increased resistance to fluoroquinolones and beta-lactams in Pseudomonas aeruginosa strains carrying the exoU gene.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, MIC testing, and qRT-PCR were used to analyze mutations and gene expression related to antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Evidence for the critical role of transmembrane helices 1 and 7 in substrate transport by human P-glycoprotein (ABCB1).
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that mutations in transmembrane helices 1 and 7 of P-glycoprotein (ABCB1) significantly impair its ability to transport substrates, highlighting the critical role of these helices in the transport function of the protein.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized site-directed mutagenesis, baculovirus expression systems, and flow cytometry to analyze the transport function of the TMH1,7 mutant P-gp.

full_output.paper_title: Exploring benzimidazole resistance in Haemonchus contortus by next generation sequencing and droplet digital PCR.

blaTBU-1.mechanism: The F200Y mutation in the beta-tubulin isotype 1 gene confers resistance to benzimidazole drugs.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the F200Y mutation in the beta-tubulin isotype 1 gene as a key determinant of benzimidazole resistance in Haemonchus contortus, validated through next-generation sequencing and droplet digital PCR.
full_output.methodology: Next-generation sequencing and droplet digital PCR were used to analyze the beta-tubulin isotype 1 gene for mutations associated with benzimidazole resistance in Haemonchus contortus.

full_output.paper_title: Transcriptional and Functional Analysis of Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis Exposure to Tetracycline.

tet(W).validation_method: transcriptomic analysis and gene expression profiling

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the tet(W) gene as a key contributor to tetracycline resistance in Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis strains Bl-04 and HN019, with differential gene expression patterns observed between the strains.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptomic analysis and gene expression profiling were used to investigate tetracycline resistance mechanisms in Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis.

full_output.paper_title: N-Deacetylases required for muramic-δ-lactam production are involved in Clostridium difficile sporulation, germination, and heat resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies pdaA1 and pdaA2 as the N-deacetylases responsible for muramic-δ-lactam synthesis in Clostridium difficile, highlighting their roles in sporulation, germination, and heat resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized UHPLC coupled with HRMS for muropeptide analysis, genetic mutants, and transmission electron microscopy to investigate the role of pdaA1 and pdaA2 in C. difficile spore formation and resistance.

full_output.key_findings: Usp18 is an important IFN-I-induced gene that promotes susceptibility to both primary and secondary bacterial infection by attenuating antibacterial TNF-α signaling and subsequent ROS production.
full_output.methodology: Use of transgenic mice, bacterial infection models, and biochemical assays to investigate the role of Usp18 in IFN-I signaling and bacterial infection.

full_output.paper_title: Sphaerocyclamide, a prenylated cyanobactin from the cyanobacterium Sphaerospermopsis sp. LEGE 00249.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the sph gene cluster responsible for the biosynthesis of sphaerocyclamide, a prenylated cyanobactin from Sphaerospermopsis sp. LEGE 00249.
full_output.methodology: The sph gene cluster was identified through PCR amplification, sequencing, and heterologous expression in E. coli, confirming its role in sphaerocyclamide biosynthesis.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial genes from Allium sativum and Pinellia ternata revealed by a Bacillus subtilis expression system.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 19 novel antimicrobial genes from Allium sativum and Pinellia ternata using a Bacillus subtilis expression system. These genes encode proteins with broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, fungi, and nematodes.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized Bacillus subtilis and E. coli expression systems to screen for antimicrobial genes. Proteins were extracted and tested for antimicrobial activity against various pathogens.

full_output.paper_title: The cotton laccase gene GhLAC15 enhances Verticillium wilt resistance via an increase in defence-induced lignification and lignin components in the cell walls of plants.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies GhLAC15, a laccase gene from cotton, which enhances resistance to Verticillium wilt by increasing lignification and altering lignin composition in plant cell walls.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized qRT-PCR, transgenic Arabidopsis overexpression, and VIGS to analyze the function of GhLAC15 in Verticillium wilt resistance.

full_output.paper_title: High prevalence and clonal dissemination of OXA-72-producing Acinetobacter baumannii in a Chinese hospital: a cross sectional study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaOXA-72 as a prevalent carbapenemase gene in Acinetobacter baumannii isolates from a Chinese hospital, contributing to carbapenem resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, DNA sequencing, and Rep-PCR genotyping were used to identify and characterize OXA-72-producing A. baumannii isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of a streptomycin-resistant Mycobacterium bovis strain through antitubercular drug susceptibility testing of Tunisian Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex isolates from cattle.

rpsL.evidence_note: The paper explicitly states that a non-synonymous mutation at codon 43 (K43R) was found in the rpsL gene and that this mutation is associated with streptomycin resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first detection of a streptomycin-resistant Mycobacterium bovis isolate from animal origin, with a non-synonymous mutation (K43R) in the rpsL gene associated with high-level streptomycin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Antitubercular drug susceptibility testing using agar proportion method and d-REMA, along with DNA sequencing of resistance-associated genes.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Activity of 3D-Printed Poly(ε-Caprolactone) (PCL) Composite Scaffolds Presenting Vancomycin-Loaded Polylactic Acid-Glycolic Acid (PLGA) Microspheres.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a novel composite scaffold incorporating vancomycin-loaded PLGA microspheres, which exhibits sustained antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus for over four weeks.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized 3D printing technology to create PCL scaffolds coated with PDA, which were then loaded with vancomycin-containing PLGA microspheres. Antibacterial efficacy was evaluated through in vitro release studies and agar diffusion assays.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of factors that promote biogenesis of tRNA(CGA)(Ser).
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several genes involved in tRNA biogenesis, including DUS2, MOD5, SES1, LOS1, RPA49, RRN3, MOT1, and ALR1, which are critical for the growth of sup61-T47:2C cells. Mutations in these genes lead to reduced levels of the altered tRNA(CGA)Ser, highlighting their roles in tRNA modification, transport, aminoacylation, and transcription.
full_output.methodology: Genetic screening, growth assays, northern blotting, and HPLC analyses were used to characterize the roles of the identified genes in tRNA biogenesis.

full_output.paper_title: High-level artemisinin-resistance with quinine co-resistance emerges in P. falciparum malaria under in vivo artesunate pressure.

Pfmdr1.mechanism: gene copy number duplication and N86Y mutation

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a non-synonymous mutation in the RAD5 gene associated with high-level artemisinin resistance in P. falciparum, alongside co-resistance to quinine.
full_output.methodology: In vivo and in vitro drug sensitivity assays, genetic sequencing, and restriction fragment length polymorphism analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Dimethyl adenosine transferase (KsgA) contributes to cell-envelope fitness in Salmonella Enteritidis.

mutations_found.validated_by: expression of catalytically inactive KsgA (ksgA E66A) in S. Enteritidis and E. coli

full_output.paper_title: Myo-inositol-1-phosphate synthase (Ino-1) functions as a protection mechanism in Corynebacterium glutamicum under oxidative stress.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Ino-1 as a crucial gene for oxidative stress resistance in Corynebacterium glutamicum, showing that its deletion leads to increased sensitivity to various stressors, including oxidants, alkylating agents, heavy metals, and antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized genetic manipulation, including deletion and complementation of the ino-1 gene, along with biochemical assays to assess the impact of Ino-1 on cellular resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Synergistic Antimicrobial Effect of Lonicera japonica and Magnolia obovata Extracts and Potential as a Plant-Derived Natural Preservative.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified caffeic acid, luteolin, magnolol, and honokiol as active components in Lonicera japonica and Magnolia obovata extracts with antimicrobial activity against several bacterial and fungal strains.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial activity was assessed using MIC, MBC, disc diffusion assay, and HPLC analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Five-Year Antimicrobial Susceptibility of Pseudomonas aeruginosa from a Local Tertiary Hospital in Bacolod City, Philippines.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial susceptibility of 646 P. aeruginosa isolates over five years, revealing varying resistance rates to antibiotics such as amikacin (7.5%), piperacillin/tazobactam (8.5%), gentamicin (13.5%), and levofloxacin (26.7%). AmpC production was detected in nearly 100% of isolates, suggesting inducible resistance against extended-spectrum beta-lactamases.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing was performed using the disc diffusion method, and AmpC production was screened using cefoxitin discs.

full_output.paper_title: The Historical Case for and the Future Study of Antibiotic-Resistant Scrub Typhus.

gyrA.mechanism: Mutations in the QRDR domain of gyrA
gyrA.validation_method: Genome sequencing and comparison with other Rickettsiaceae
gyrA.evidence_note: Mutations reported in this review paper are sourced from cited studies. Original experimental data is in the referenced publications.

full_output.key_findings: The study discusses the emergence of antibiotic-resistant scrub typhus, focusing on the detection of resistance-associated genes such as gyrA, which exhibits mutations linked to fluoroquinolone resistance. It highlights challenges in detecting resistance due to the intracellular nature of O. tsutsugamushi and emphasizes the need for improved diagnostic methods.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing and comparative genomics of O. tsutsugamushi isolates to identify potential resistance genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa from sputum of patients with cystic fibrosis demonstrates a high rate of susceptibility to ceftazidime-avibactam.

ampC.notes: elevated AmpC gene expression was noted in 66.67% of strains

mexC.notes: elevated MexC expression was noted in 22.22% of strains

mexX.notes: moderate expression of MexX was noted in 22.2% of strains

mexA.notes: moderate expression of MexA was noted in 22.2% of strains

full_output.key_findings: Ceftazidime-avibactam shows high in vitro susceptibility against multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from cystic fibrosis patients, with resistance mechanisms involving OprD loss and elevated AmpC expression.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR screening for β-lactamases, and qRT-PCR for gene expression analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Klebsiella grimontii, a New Species Acquired Carbapenem Resistance.

blaKPC-2.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and plasmid analysis

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first carbapenem-resistant strain of Klebsiella grimontii, which harbors the blaKPC-2 gene on a plasmid, leading to resistance against imipenem and meropenem.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, plasmid analysis, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Characterization, Phylogenetic, Expression, and Protective Immunity Analysis of OmpF, a Promising Candidate Immunogen Against Yersinia ruckeri Infection in Channel Catfish.

rtOmpF.validation_method: expression, purification, western blotting, immune response analysis

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the OmpF gene from Yersinia ruckeri, demonstrating its immunogenicity and potential as a vaccine candidate against Y. ruckeri infection in channel catfish.
full_output.methodology: Molecular cloning, expression, purification, western blotting, cell surface staining, and immunofluorescence assays were used to analyze OmpF.

full_output.paper_title: Acquisition of resistance to carbapenem and macrolide-mediated quorum sensing inhibition by Pseudomonas aeruginosa via ICE(Tn4371) 6385.

blaNDM-1.validation_method: cloning in P. aeruginosa and MIC testing

msr(E).validation_method: expression in P. aeruginosa and phenotypic assays

floR.validation_method: cloning in P. aeruginosa and MIC testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel integrative and conjugative element (ICE) carrying blaNDM-1, msr(E), and floR, which confers resistance to carbapenems, macrolides, and florfenicol in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, cloning, and phenotypic assays were used to validate the resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Raman spectral signature reflects transcriptomic features of antibiotic resistance in Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that Raman spectroscopy can reflect transcriptomic features of antibiotic resistance in Escherichia coli, identifying correlations between gene expression and spectral intensities for genes involved in cell wall, DNA gyrase, and protein synthesis pathways.
full_output.methodology: Raman spectroscopy combined with gene expression analysis was used to investigate antibiotic resistance mechanisms in E. coli strains.

full_output.paper_title: CHAOS: A Strategy to Slow Bacterial Adaptation to Antibiotics Through Multiplexed Gene Perturbations
full_output.key_findings: The study introduces CHAOS, a method using multiplexed CRISPR-Cas9 gene expression perturbations to induce negative epistasis and slow bacterial adaptation to antibiotics. It shows that multiplexed perturbations lead to significant fitness loss and reduced adaptation rates in E. coli, especially under antibiotic exposure.
full_output.methodology: The study uses CRISPR-Cas9 to perturb gene expression in E. coli, assessing fitness and adaptation rates under antibiotic exposure.

full_output.paper_title: Resolution of fluoroquinolone-resistant Escherichia coli keratitis with a PROSE device for enhanced targeted antibiotic delivery.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports a case of fluoroquinolone-resistant Escherichia coli keratitis that was resolved with the use of a PROSE device for enhanced targeted delivery of moxifloxacine. The E. coli isolate carried multiple mutations in the quinolone resistance-determining region (QRDR) of gyrA, parC, and parE genes, leading to resistance to ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin, and moxifloxacin.
full_output.methodology: Microbial culture, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and molecular analysis of resistance mechanisms.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified CG258 Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates without β-lactam resistance at the onset of the carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae epidemic in New York City. Some isolates were phenotypically susceptible to carbapenems despite carrying ESBLs and mutations in porin genes.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective molecular analysis of strain types, capsular polysaccharide types, and plasmid types in K. pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Novel linezolid resistance plasmids in Enterococcus from food animals in the USA.

optrA.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and conjugation experiments

cfr.mechanism: methylation of 23S rRNA

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies novel linezolid resistance plasmids containing optrA and cfr genes in Enterococcus isolates from food animals in the USA, highlighting the potential for horizontal transfer of resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, conjugation experiments, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize the resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Profiling antimicrobial peptides from the medical maggot Lucilia sericata as potential antibiotics for MDR Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified two antimicrobial peptides, LS-sarcotoxin and LS-stomoxyn, derived from the medical maggot Lucilia sericata, which exhibited potent and selective activity against multidrug-resistant (MDR) Gram-negative bacteria, including those resistant to colistin and meropenem. These peptides showed no cross-resistance with conventional antibiotics and demonstrated synergistic activity with colistin.
full_output.methodology: The peptides were tested against a panel of MDR clinical isolates, and their antimicrobial activity, resistance development, and pharmacokinetic properties were analyzed.

full_output.paper_title: Decline in AmpC β-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli in a Dutch teaching hospital (2013-2016).

blaCMY-2-like.evidence_note: The paper mentions that 18 of 19 pAmpC-producing isolates harbored bla CMY-2-like, indicating that blaCMY-2-like is a plasmid-encoded AmpC β-lactamase gene that confers resistance to cephalosporins.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports a decline in rectal carriage of cAmpC hyperproducing E. coli in a Dutch hospital, with bla CMY-2-like and bla DHA-like genes being the primary plasmid-encoded AmpC β-lactamases identified.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic and genotypic analysis of AmpC-producing E. coli isolates using microarrays, Sanger sequencing, and AFLP typing.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance in Class 1 Integron-Positive Shiga Toxin-Producing Escherichia coli Isolated from Cattle, Pigs, Food and Farm Environment.
full_output.key_findings: Class 1 integron-positive Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli (STEC) isolates from various sources were found to carry multiple antimicrobial resistance genes, including dfrA1, aadA, aadA23, dfrA16, sul1, sul2, tetA, tetB, and blaTEM, contributing to multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of class 1 integrons, microarray analysis for antimicrobial resistance genes, and disk diffusion for antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Dibasic Derivatives of Phenylcarbamic Acid against Mycobacterial Strains: Old Drugs and New Tricks?
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several dibasic phenylcarbamic acid derivatives with potent in vitro antimycobacterial activity against various Mycobacterium species, including Mycobacterium tuberculosis and Mycobacterium kansasii, with MIC values ranging from 1.9 to 8 μM.
full_output.methodology: The compounds were synthesized and characterized for their physicochemical properties, and their antimycobacterial activity was assessed using in vitro susceptibility testing against multiple mycobacterial strains.

full_output.paper_title: Recombinant BCG Overexpressing phoP-phoR Confers Enhanced Protection against Tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that overexpression of the M. bovis allele of phoP or phoP-phoR in BCG-Japan enhances immunogenicity and provides superior protection against Mtb infection in guinea pigs.
full_output.methodology: The study involved complementation of BCG-Prague with the M. bovis allele of phoP, construction of recombinant BCG-Japan strains, and assessment of immunogenicity and protective efficacy in mouse and guinea pig models.

full_output.paper_title: Synergistic effects of functionally distinct substitutions in β-lactamase variants shed light on the evolution of bacterial drug resistance.

blaCTX-M-14.notes: Both mutations are functionally distinct and synergistically affect resistance levels.
