full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a carbapenemase-producing hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae isolate (CP-hvKP) in the United States, which carries the blaKPC-2 gene on a plasmid, along with other resistance genes such as blaSHV-36, fosA, oqxA, and oqxB. The isolate also possesses hypervirulence factors, highlighting the dual threat of antimicrobial resistance and virulence.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and molecular detection methods were used to characterize the isolate.

full_output.paper_title: In Vivo Pharmacodynamic Profile of Ceftibuten-Clavulanate Combination against Extended-Spectrum-β-Lactamase-Producing Enterobacteriaceae in the Murine Thigh Infection Model.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the pharmacodynamic profile of the ceftibuten-clavulanate (CTB-CLA) combination against extended-spectrum-β-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Enterobacteriaceae in a murine thigh infection model. The results suggested a susceptibility breakpoint of 4 mg/L for CTB-CLA.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of 16S rRNA methylases in Gram-negative bacteria derived from companion animals and livestock in Japan.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of rmtB and armA genes in Gram-negative bacteria from companion animals in Japan, indicating the prevalence of 16S rRNA methylases, which confer high-level resistance to aminoglycosides.
full_output.methodology: PCR, DNA sequencing, and MIC testing were used to detect and characterize 16S rRNA methylase genes in bacterial isolates.
full_output.sample_size: 212 and 234 Escherichia coli from dogs, 1,029 and 1,418 E. coli from livestock, 103 Klebsiella spp., 60 Enterobacter spp., and 81 Acinetobacter spp. from clinical specimens.

full_output.paper_title: Appearance of vanD-positive Enterococcus faecium in a tertiary hospital in the Netherlands: prevalence of vanC and vanD in hospitalized patients.

full_output.paper_title: The Mycobacterium tuberculosis CRISPR-Associated Cas1 Involves Persistence and Tolerance to Anti-Tubercular Drugs.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that the Cas1 gene deletion in Mycobacterium tuberculosis is associated with increased drug susceptibility and reduced persistence during anti-tubercular treatment. full_output.paper_title: Risk factor analysis, antimicrobial resistance and pathotyping of Escherichia coli associated with pre- and post-weaning piglet diarrhoea in organised farms, India.

full_output.paper_title: Zoonotic approach to Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli: integrated analysis of virulence and antimicrobial resistance in ruminants and humans.

full_output.paper_title: Bacteremia by colistin-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii isolate: a case report.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Peptides, Polymorphic Toxins, and Self-Nonself Recognition Systems in Archaea: an Untapped Armory for Intermicrobial Conflicts.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies various antimicrobial peptides, polymorphic toxin systems, and self-nonself recognition systems in archaea, highlighting the diversity and complexity of these systems in intermicrobial conflicts.

full_output.paper_title: Methicillin- and Inducible Clindamycin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus among Patients with Wound Infection Attending Arba Minch Hospital, South Ethiopia.

full_output.paper_title: Inhibition of the type III secretion system by syringaldehyde protects mice from Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium.

full_output.paper_title: Intermicrobial interaction: Aspergillus fumigatus siderophores protect against competition by Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

full_output.methodology: The study utilized genetic mutants, biochemical assays, and biofilm experiments to investigate the role of siderophores in microbial interactions.

full_output.paper_title: Activity and characterization of a pH-sensitive antimicrobial peptide.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the eIF4E-1 gene as a key player in resistance to Potato virus Y (PVY) in tobacco. Additionally, the study highlights the importance of the genetic locus on chromosome 14, which contains multiple eIF4E copies, in determining the stability of resistance.

full_output.paper_title: High degree of fluoroquinolone resistance among pulmonary tuberculosis patients in New Delhi, India.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a high prevalence of fluoroquinolone (FQ) resistance among both drug-sensitive and multidrug-resistant (MDR) Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates in New Delhi, India. FQ monoresistance was observed in 3.2% of drug-sensitive isolates, and 27.3% of MDR isolates exhibited additional FQ resistance.
full_output.methodology: Drug susceptibility testing (DST) for fluoroquinolones was performed using the BACTEC MGIT-960 system on Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates from sputum samples.

full_output.key_findings: Striatisporolide A (SA) exhibits antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli by damaging the cell wall and membrane, altering protein levels, and causing morphological changes.

full_output.paper_title: Non-clonal occurrence of pmrB mutations associated with polymyxin resistance in carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae in Brazil.

Additionally, some isolates exhibited mutations in the mgrB gene, although these were less frequent.
full_output.methodology: PCR, DNA sequencing, and PROVEAN prediction were used to identify and validate mutations in pmrB and mgrB genes associated with polymyxin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: PGRP-SA and PGRP-LC Mediate Immune Responses to Peptidoglycan Variants in Drosophila
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the roles of PGRP-SA and PGRP-LC in recognizing peptidoglycan (PG) variants in Drosophila, revealing that both receptors contribute to immune responses against WTA-less bacteria, challenging the traditional Lys/DAP discrimination model.
full_output.methodology: The research utilized binding assays, survival experiments, CFU measurements, and gene expression analyses to explore the functions of PGRP-SA and PGRP-LC in immune responses to peptidoglycan variants.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified KPHS_33600 as a gene that, when complemented, increased susceptibility to meropenem in K. pneumoniae, suggesting its role in carbapenem resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial activity and mode of action of acetone crude leaf extracts of under-investigated Syzygium and Eugenia (Myrtaceae) species on multidrug resistant porcine diarrhoeagenic Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antibacterial activity of acetone crude leaf extracts from nine under-investigated Syzygium and Eugenia species against multidrug-resistant porcine diarrhoeagenic E. coli. The extracts exhibited significant antibacterial activity, with S. legatii showing the best mean MIC of 0.05 mg/mL. The extracts also demonstrated anti-adhesion properties, reducing E. coli adherence to Caco-2 cells.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth microdilution to determine MIC values, TLC bioautography for phytochemical analysis, and Caco-2 cell adherence assays to assess anti-adhesion activity.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of Escherichia coli from broiler chickens in Jordan, their antimicrobial resistance, gene characterization and the associated risk factors.

full_output.paper_title: Diverse Commensal Escherichia coli Clones and Plasmids Disseminate Antimicrobial Resistance Genes in Domestic Animals and Children in a Semirural Community in Ecuador.

full_output.paper_title: Low prevalence of resistance genes in sheltered homeless population in Marseille, France, 2014-2018.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a low prevalence of antibiotic resistance genes in the nasal/pharyngeal samples of sheltered homeless individuals in Marseille, France, compared to non-homeless controls. Specifically, bla TEM, bla SHV, and bla OXA-23 were detected, but mcr-1 to mcr-5 genes were absent.
full_output.methodology: The study used qPCR and sequencing to detect antibiotic resistance genes in nasal/pharyngeal samples from homeless individuals and controls.

full_output.paper_title: Investigation of the prevalence of genes conferring resistance to carbapenems in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from burn patients.

blaNDM.evidence_note: The paper states that blaNDM was detected in 14 (28%) isolates and that NDM-1 renders bacteria resistant to almost all β-lactam antibiotics, aminoglycosides, and fluoroquinolones.

blaOXA-48.evidence_note: The paper states that blaOXA-48 was detected in 18% of isolates and that it is a carbapenemase gene.

blaBIC-1.evidence_note: The paper states that blaBIC-1 was detected in 14% of isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaNDM, blaOXA-48, and blaBIC-1 genes as the primary contributors to carbapenem resistance in P. aeruginosa isolates from burn patients, with blaNDM being the most prevalent.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing and multiplex PCR were used to identify carbapenem resistance genes in P. aeruginosa isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of Staphylococcus aureus carriage and pattern of antibiotic resistance, including methicillin resistance, among contact sport athletes in Italy.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that 42.4% of contact sport athletes in Italy were colonized with Staphylococcus aureus, with 1.3% carrying methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA). Resistance to clindamycin (24.8%) and erythromycin (15.8%) was observed, while no resistance was found to sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim.
full_output.methodology: Cross-sectional study involving 238 athletes, with swab samples collected from the nares, oropharynx, and fingers for S. aureus isolation and antibiotic susceptibility testing using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Investigation of Dipicolinic Acid Isosteres for the Inhibition of Metallo-β-Lactamases.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates dipicolinic acid (DPA) isosteres as inhibitors of metallo-β-lactamases, particularly NDM-1, highlighting the impact of carboxylate isostere choice on inhibition potency and mechanism.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis and evaluation of DPA isosteres against NDM-1, including inhibition assays, equilibrium dialysis, and UV-visible spectroscopy.

full_output.paper_title: Polymer Masked-Unmasked Protein Therapy: Identification of the Active Species after Amylase Activation of Dextrin-Colistin Conjugates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the active species of dextrin-colistin conjugates after amylase activation, highlighting the importance of conjugate unmasking for antimicrobial activity.
full_output.methodology: The study used SEC, LC-MS, and biological assays to characterize the active species of dextrin-colistin conjugates.

full_output.paper_title: Reduced ceftazidime and ertapenem susceptibility due to production of OXA-2 in Klebsiella pneumoniae ST258.

blaOXA-2.validation_method: expression in E. coli TOP10 and K. pneumoniae ATCC 13883, MIC testing, purification and kinetic studies of OXA-2 enzyme

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies OXA-2 as a beta-lactamase responsible for reduced susceptibility to ceftazidime and ertapenem in a K. pneumoniae ST258 isolate, highlighting its role in carbapenem resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, MIC testing, qRT-PCR, immunoblotting, and kinetic studies of the OXA-2 enzyme.
full_output.sample_size: Three K. pneumoniae isolates from a single patient.

full_output.paper_title: Resistance of early stationary phase E. coli to membrane permeabilization by the antimicrobial peptide Cecropin A.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that early stationary phase E. coli is more resistant to membrane permeabilization by Cecropin A compared to mid-log phase cells, with a tenfold higher concentration needed for permeabilization. The spatial pattern of permeabilization shifts from localized to global in stationary phase cells.
full_output.methodology: Single-cell microscopy and microfluidics chamber experiments were used to analyze the effects of Cecropin A on E. coli membrane permeabilization.

full_output.paper_title: Multiomics Assessment of Gene Expression in a Clinical Strain of CTX-M-15-Producing ST131 Escherichia coli.

gyrA.notes: mutation in gyrA gene

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple AMR genes and mutations in the CTX-M-15-producing ST131 E. coli strain C999, including beta-lactamases (blaCTX-M-15, blaTEM-1, blaOXA-1), aminoglycoside resistance gene (aac(6')-Ib-cr), tetracycline resistance gene (tet(A)), sulfonamide resistance gene (sul1), and aadA5 gene cassette. Mutations in gyrA and parC contribute to fluoroquinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, RNA sequencing, and proteomic analysis were used to identify and characterize AMR genes and mutations in the E. coli strain C999.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies genes such as brlR, PA1874-1877, and ndvB that contribute to antibiotic tolerance in P. aeruginosa biofilms through mechanisms like efflux pump regulation and drug sequestration.
full_output.methodology: Gene expression analysis, mutant studies, and biofilm susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Dual RNA-Seq Unveils Pseudomonas plecoglossicida htpG Gene Functions During Host-Pathogen Interactions With Epinephelus coioides.

htpG.mechanism: chaperone that enables the optimal folding of newly synthesized proteins under stress conditions

full_output.key_findings: The study reveals that the htpG gene in Pseudomonas plecoglossicida plays a critical role in virulence and host immune response during infection with Epinephelus coioides. Silencing htpG led to reduced virulence, delayed disease onset, and altered gene expression profiles in both the pathogen and host.
full_output.methodology: Dual RNA-seq, qRT-PCR, and bioinformatics analysis were used to investigate the effects of htpG silencing on P. plecoglossicida virulence and host immune responses.

full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed antimicrobial use (AMU) and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in broiler chickens and turkeys in British Columbia, Canada, from 2013 to 2017. It highlighted trends in AMU and AMR, emphasizing the need for integrated AMU and AMR indicators to monitor the impact of stewardship activities.
full_output.methodology: The study used data from the Canadian Integrated Program for Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance (CIPARS) to analyze AMU and AMR in broiler chickens and turkeys, employing statistical methods to evaluate trends and resistance patterns.

full_output.paper_title: Asymmetry in catalysis by Thermotoga maritima membrane-bound pyrophosphatase demonstrated by a nonphosphorus allosteric inhibitor.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies ATC as the first nonphosphorus allosteric inhibitor of Thermotoga maritima membrane-bound pyrophosphatase (TmPPase), demonstrating its ability to bind asymmetrically and inhibit the enzyme's catalytic activity.
full_output.methodology: Structural biology techniques including X-ray crystallography and kinetic assays were used to characterize ATC's binding and inhibitory effects on TmPPase.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic and genotypic characterization of glycopeptide, aminoglycoside and macrolide resistance among clinical isolates of Enterococcus faecalis: a multicenter based study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified vanA, ermB, and aac(6')-Ie aph(2") genes as the primary drivers of glycopeptide, macrolide, and aminoglycoside resistance in vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecalis isolates.
full_output.methodology: PCR and phenotypic susceptibility testing were used to identify resistance genes and their association with antibiotic resistance patterns.

full_output.paper_title: Modulation of antibiotic sensitivity and biofilm formation in Pseudomonas aeruginosa by interspecies signal analogues.

PA1396.notes: variant shows reduced sensitivity to DSF
PA1396.evidence_note: The paper describes mutations in PA1396 (T121A/L123A/L128A) that reduce sensitivity to DSF, but does not explicitly state that these mutations confer resistance to antibiotics.

full_output.key_findings: PA1396 is a histidine kinase that senses DSF signals and regulates biofilm formation and antibiotic tolerance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Mutations in PA1396, particularly in transmembrane helices IV and V, reduce its responsiveness to DSF.
full_output.methodology: Mutagenesis, functional assays, and biochemical analyses were used to investigate the role of PA1396 in DSF signaling and its impact on biofilm formation and antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Exploiting chitosan and gold nanoparticles for antimycobacterial activity of in silico identified antimicrobial motif of human neutrophil peptide-1.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Pep-H, an antimicrobial motif of human neutrophil peptide-1 (HNP-1), as effective against Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Nanoformulations of Pep-H, specifically chitosan and gold nanoparticles, enhance its antimycobacterial activity.
full_output.methodology: In silico identification of antimicrobial motifs, in vitro and ex vivo assays, nanoparticle characterization, and antimycobacterial activity evaluation.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of Resistance Genes and Response to Arsenic in Rhodococcus aetherivorans BCP1.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies three arsenate reductase genes (arsC1, arsC2, arsC3) and other ars genes involved in arsenic resistance in Rhodococcus aetherivorans BCP1. These genes are transcriptionally induced in response to arsenate and play a role in the detoxification of inorganic and organic arsenic compounds.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, transcriptomic analysis, and bioinformatics approaches were used to identify and characterize the arsenic resistance genes in R. aetherivorans BCP1.

full_output.paper_title: Fitness of Spontaneous Rifampicin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus Isolates in a Biofilm Environment.

rpoB.notes: Mutation detected in RifR1 and RifR2

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies rpoB mutations (A477D) in rifampicin-resistant S. aureus mutants that confer resistance and enhance biofilm fitness.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing of rpoB gene and MIC measurements for rifampicin.

full_output.paper_title: ABCA1 transporter reduces amphotericin B cytotoxicity in mammalian cells.
full_output.key_findings: ABCA1 expression reduces amphotericin B cytotoxicity in mammalian cells by promoting cholesterol efflux, which prevents AmB from penetrating the cell membrane.
full_output.methodology: Cell transfection, MTT assay, FLIM analysis, cholesterol efflux studies

full_output.paper_title: HGA Mediates Interspecies and Intraspecies Inhibition in Legionella pneumophila
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies lpg1681 as a gene that modulates HGA susceptibility in Legionella pneumophila, revealing a density-dependent resistance mechanism to HGA.
full_output.methodology: Genetic screens, mutant analysis, and biochemical assays were used to investigate HGA-mediated inhibition and resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of the tuberculosis culture color plate test for rapid detection of drug susceptible and drug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis in a resource-limited setting, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The TB-CX test was evaluated for rapid detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis and drug resistance to isoniazid (INH), rifampin (RIF), and pyrazinamide (PZA). The test showed high sensitivity and specificity for detecting M. tuberculosis and drug resistance, with notable performance for INH and PZA resistance.
full_output.methodology: The TB-CX test was compared to conventional culture methods and the GeneXpert test for detection of M. tuberculosis and drug resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial activity of lysozyme-chitosan oligosaccharide conjugates (LYZOX) against Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Acinetobacter baumannii and Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antibacterial activity of lysozyme-chitosan oligosaccharide conjugates (LYZOX) against Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Acinetobacter baumannii, and Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, demonstrating its effectiveness in killing these bacteria and inhibiting their growth.
full_output.methodology: The study assessed the antibacterial activity of LYZOX through bactericidal tests, growth inhibition tests, and mechanisms of action including cell membrane integrity assays, NPN assays, ONPG assays, and electron microscopy.

full_output.paper_title: Oral Beta-Lactamase Protects the Canine Gut Microbiome from Oral Amoxicillin-Mediated Damage.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the presence of beta-lactamase genes (blaTEM and blaOXA) in the canine gut microbiome following amoxicillin exposure, highlighting their role in antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic analysis of fecal DNA to identify antibiotic resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Discovery of (3-Benzyl-5-hydroxyphenyl)carbamates as New Antitubercular Agents with Potent In Vitro and In Vivo Efficacy.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified (3-benzyl-5-hydroxyphenyl)carbamates as new antitubercular agents with potent in vitro and in vivo efficacy against Mycobacterium tuberculosis, including multidrug-resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: Chemical synthesis and biological evaluation of carbamates against M. tuberculosis.

full_output.paper_title: Transposon libraries identify novel Mycobacterium bovis BCG genes involved in the dynamic interactions required for BCG to persist during in vivo passage in cattle.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several genes involved in the persistence of BCG in cattle, including those related to mycobactin synthesis, PDIM synthesis, reductive sulfate assimilation, sugar transport, and cholesterol metabolism. Additionally, three novel genes (BCG_2988c, BCG_1063, and BCG_3780) were found to be critical for BCG's in vivo survival.
full_output.methodology: Transposon mutagenesis and knockout mutant analysis were used to identify genes involved in BCG persistence in cattle.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic analyses of two novel biofilm-degrading methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus phages.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies two novel bacteriophages, UPMK_1 and UPMK_2, capable of degrading biofilms formed by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). These phages demonstrate lytic activity against MRSA biofilms, reducing biofilm biomass significantly. The genomic analysis reveals unique features of these phages, including the presence of endolysin-like proteins and other genes potentially involved in biofilm degradation.
full_output.methodology: Genomic sequencing, electron microscopy, and biofilm degradation assays were employed to characterize the phages and their lytic capabilities.

full_output.paper_title: Virulence-associated genes and antibiotic resistance patterns of Vibrio spp. isolated from cultured marine fishes in Malaysia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antibiotic resistance (MAR) in Vibrio spp. isolates from marine fishes in Malaysia, with high resistance to ampicillin, penicillin, polypeptides, cephems, and streptomycin. No AMR genes were functionally characterized in this study.
full_output.methodology: PCR and disc diffusion methods were used to detect virulence genes and antibiotic resistance patterns in Vibrio isolates.

full_output.key_findings: Colistin showed high in vitro activity against multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Acinetobacter baumannii isolates from Iran.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing using E-test strips to determine MICs of colistin, imipenem, and ceftazidime.
full_output.sample_size: 18 A. baumannii and 21 P. aeruginosa isolates

full_output.paper_title: Epinecidin-1, a highly potent marine antimicrobial peptide with anticancer and immunomodulatory activities.
full_output.key_findings: Epinecidin-1 is a cationic antimicrobial peptide with broad-spectrum antimicrobial, antiviral, anticancer, and wound-healing properties. It exhibits potent activity against various bacterial, fungal, and protozoan pathogens, as well as viruses like Betanodavirus and Foot-and-Mouth Disease Virus. Additionally, it shows promise in cancer therapy and wound healing.
full_output.methodology: Review of existing literature on Epinecidin-1's structure, function, and applications.

full_output.paper_title: Ceftriaxone-resistant Salmonella enterica serotype Typhi in a pregnant traveller returning from Karachi, Pakistan to Denmark, 2019.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports a ceftriaxone-resistant Salmonella Typhi isolate carrying multiple resistance genes, including blaCTX-M-15, blaTEM-1B, qnrS1, sul1, sul2, dfrA7, aph[3]-1b, aph[6]-1d, aac[6]-1aa, and catA1. Additionally, a fluoroquinolone resistance mutation (gyrA S83F) was identified.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing, whole genome sequencing, and molecular characterization of resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: In Vitro Study of Stepwise Acquisition of rv0678 and atpE Mutations Conferring Bedaquiline Resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies rv0678 and atpE mutations as key contributors to bedaquiline resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, with rv0678 mutations being dynamic and atpE mutations being fixed once they occur.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and MIC determination were used to analyze bedaquiline resistance in M. tuberculosis mutant populations.
full_output.sample_size: five sequential M. tuberculosis mutant populations

full_output.paper_title: The Arginine Deiminase Operon Is Responsible for a Fitness Trade-Off in Extended-Spectrum-β-Lactamase-Producing Strains of Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the arginine deiminase (ADI) operon as a factor contributing to a fitness trade-off in extended-spectrum-beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing strains of Escherichia coli, enhancing fitness in certain environments while being detrimental in others.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, PCR, mutagenesis, and competition experiments in vitro and in vivo.

full_output.paper_title: The Likelihood of Developing a Carbapenem-Resistant Enterobacteriaceae Infection during a Hospital Stay.

blaKPC.validation_method: modified carbapenem inactivation method and Xpert Carba-R assay

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies carbapenemase-producing CRE strains carrying bla KPC, bla NDM, and bla OXA-48 genes, highlighting the association between carbapenemase production and increased risk of CRE infections.
full_output.methodology: Screening of rectal swabs, carbapenem susceptibility testing, and molecular detection of carbapenemase genes.

full_output.paper_title: Impact of Species Diversity on the Design of RNA-Based Diagnostics for Antibiotic Resistance in Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified four RNA transcripts (rpsO, rplN, omp3, and NGO1079) that showed differential expression in response to azithromycin exposure, demonstrating potential as diagnostic markers for azithromycin resistance in Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
full_output.methodology: The study combined whole-transcriptome profiling with RT-qPCR to analyze gene expression changes in response to antibiotic exposure and validate candidate diagnostic markers.

full_output.paper_title: Intercellular Transfer of Chromosomal Antimicrobial Resistance Genes between Acinetobacter baumannii Strains Mediated by Prophages.

armA.validation_method: clone in A. baumannii ATCC 17978 and MIC testing

tet(B).validation_method: clone in A. baumannii ATCC 17978 and MIC testing

gyrA -81L.validation_method: mutation in A. baumannii ATCC 17978 and MIC testing

blaNDM-1.validation_method: chromosomal gene transfer and functional assay

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that chromosomal antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) can be transferred between Acinetobacter baumannii strains via prophages, highlighting the role of generalized transduction in the spread of resistance.
full_output.methodology: Experimental validation through cloning, MIC testing, and genetic analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Indole Reverses Intrinsic Antibiotic Resistance by Activating a Novel Dual-Function Importer.

btuD.notes: Mutations in btuD affect the dual-function importer's ability to transfer vitamin B 12 and antibiotics.
btuD.source: Wang Y, Tian T, Zhang J, Jin X, Yue H, Zhang XH, Du L, Bai F
btuD.evidence_note: The paper describes mutations G48Y and K49D in btuD and their effects on vitamin B 12 uptake and antibiotic resistance.

full_output.key_findings: Indole reverses intrinsic antibiotic resistance in Lysobacter spp. by activating a novel dual-function importer, btuD, which facilitates the uptake of both vitamin B 12 and antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Genetic experiments, biochemical assays, and transcriptional profiling were used to investigate the role of btuD in antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: A Substrate-Activated Efflux Pump, DesABC, Confers Zeamine Resistance to Dickeya zeae.

desA.validation_method: in-frame deletion and complementation, MIC assay

desB.validation_method: in-frame deletion and complementation, MIC assay

desC.validation_method: in-frame deletion and complementation, MIC assay

desAB.validation_method: heterologous expression in E. coli DH5α and MIC determination

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the RND efflux pump DesABC as crucial for Dickeya zeae EC1's resistance to zeamines, demonstrating that its inactivation leads to decreased resistance and that its expression is induced by zeamines.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation, MIC assays, and transcriptional analysis were used to validate the role of DesABC in zeamine resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Catechol cross-linked antimicrobial peptide hydrogels prevent multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii infection in burn wounds.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a catechol cross-linked antimicrobial peptide hydrogel (EPL-catechol hydrogel) that shows potent antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity against multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (MRAB).
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antimicrobial activity of EPL-catechol hydrogels through in vitro and in vivo experiments, including zone of inhibition tests, contact antimicrobial assays, and burn wound infection models.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the intracellular activity of the peptide H2 against multidrug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus strains, demonstrating its effectiveness in reducing bacterial load in bovine mammary epithelial cells and a mouse mastitis model.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the intracellular activity of H2 using MAC-T cells and a mouse mastitis model, assessing bacterial load and histopathological changes.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic characterization of Escherichia coli LCT-EC001, an extremely multidrug-resistant strain with an amazing number of resistance genes.

blaKPC-2.mechanism: Hydrolyzes a broad range of beta-lactam antibiotics

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies 68 antibiotic resistance determinants in E. coli LCT-EC001, including 8 beta-lactamase genes (blaTEM-1, blaCTX-M-14, blaKPC-2), 31 multidrug efflux system genes, 6 outer membrane transport system genes, 4 aminoglycoside-modifying enzyme genes, 10 two-component regulatory system genes, and 9 other enzyme or transcriptional regulator genes.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, BLAST searches against resistance gene databases, PCR, and Sanger sequencing.

full_output.paper_title: Derivation and validation of a simple score to predict the presence of bacteria requiring carbapenem treatment in ICU-acquired bloodstream infection and pneumonia: CarbaSCORE.
full_output.key_findings: The study derived and validated the CarbaSCORE, a simple score to predict the presence of bacteria requiring carbapenem treatment in ICU-acquired bloodstream infection and pneumonia.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective study using a prospective database of nosocomial infections in an ICU, with statistical analysis and development of a predictive score.

full_output.paper_title: Enhanced acquisition of antibiotic-resistant intestinal E. coli during the first year of life assessed in a prospective cohort study
full_output.key_findings: The study found that antibiotic-resistant E. coli was present in 33% of meconium samples from healthy Thai neonates, with resistance increasing significantly during the first year of life. Resistance to tetracycline, ampicillin, and co-trimoxazole was particularly common, with resistance proportions reaching up to 80%, 72%, and 66%, respectively, by age 1 year. Persistent and transmitted strains of resistant E. coli were identified in a small percentage of cases.
full_output.methodology: The study used a prospective cohort design, analyzing stool samples from 142 infants and their parents over the first year of life. E. coli isolates were characterized using culture, disc diffusion, and molecular techniques such as PFGE and MLST.

full_output.paper_title: Distribution of bla(CTX - M) , bla(TEM) , bla(SHV) and bla(OXA) genes in Extended-spectrum-β-lactamase-producing Clinical isolates: A three-year multi-center study from Lahore, Pakistan.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla CTX-M-15, bla OXA-1, and bla TEM-1B as the most prevalent genes among ESBL-producing isolates, highlighting the widespread occurrence of extended-spectrum beta-lactamases in clinical isolates from Lahore, Pakistan.
full_output.methodology: PCR and amplicon sequencing were used to detect and characterize ESBL genes in clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Toxin gene profiles, genetic diversity, antimicrobial resistance, and coagulase type of Staphylococcus aureus from cream-filled bakery products.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) strains in cream-filled bakery products, with the mecA gene conferring resistance to oxacillin and the mupA gene conferring resistance to mupirocin. Additionally, the sea gene was found to be the predominant enterotoxin gene.
full_output.methodology: PCR, RPLA, and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to detect AMR genes and assess antimicrobial resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Occurrence and Characterization of Salmonella Isolated from Large-Scale Breeder Farms in Shandong Province, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Salmonella Enteritidis as the predominant serovar in large-scale breeder farms in Shandong, China, with high resistance rates to nalidixic acid, streptomycin, ampicillin, and erythromycin. All isolates carried the blaTEM gene, which confers resistance to ampicillin.
full_output.methodology: PCR, MLST, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and serotyping were used to analyze Salmonella isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Targeting Mobilization of Ferrous Iron in Pseudomonas aeruginosa Infection with an Iron(II)-Caged LpxC Inhibitor.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes the synthesis and evaluation of an iron(II)-caged LpxC inhibitor (compound 9) for targeting Pseudomonas aeruginosa infections. The compound showed efficacy in an in vivo mouse model despite low activity in cell culture experiments, highlighting the potential of iron(II)-activated prodrugs for targeted antibiotic delivery.
full_output.methodology: The study involved chemical synthesis, microbiological testing, pharmacokinetic studies, and an in vivo infection model to evaluate the efficacy of the iron(II)-caged LpxC inhibitor.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that methylated metabolite of arsenite (MAs(III)) inhibits glycerol-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (Gpd1) activity by targeting cysteine residues, particularly Cys306, leading to reduced glycerol production and preventing cell wall stress in yeast exposed to arsenite.
full_output.methodology: The study used genetic manipulation, biochemical assays, and molecular techniques to investigate the mechanism of arsenite toxicity and its effect on glycerol production in yeast.

full_output.paper_title: Empirical ways to identify novel Bedaquiline resistance mutations in AtpE.

atpE.notes: These mutations were identified as resistance-associated variants through structural and functional analysis.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several mutations in the atpE gene that are associated with bedaquiline resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. These mutations disrupt key interactions with bedaquiline, leading to reduced binding affinity and resistance.
full_output.methodology: Structural and functional analysis combined with machine learning to predict bedaquiline resistance mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Restoration of susceptibility to amikacin by 8-hydroxyquinoline analogs complexed to zinc.

aac(6')-Ib.mechanism: Enzymatic inactivation of amikacin by acetylation
aac(6')-Ib.validation_method: Enzymatic acetylation assays and growth inhibition experiments

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies aac(6')-Ib as a gene responsible for amikacin resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii and demonstrates that Zn2+ complexed with certain 8-hydroxyquinoline analogs can restore susceptibility by inhibiting the enzymatic acetylation of amikacin.
full_output.methodology: Enzymatic acetylation assays, growth inhibition experiments, and time-kill assays were used to evaluate the effect of Zn2+ complexes with 8-hydroxyquinoline analogs on amikacin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Bedaquiline Microheteroresistance after Cessation of Tuberculosis Treatment.

mutations_found.validated_by: targeted deep sequencing and phenotypic bedaquiline DST

Rv0678.notes: Mutations in Rv0678 associated with bedaquiline resistance
Rv0678.evidence_note: The paper states that isolates with a variant frequency of >1% in Rv0678 were resistant to bedaquiline at 1µg/ml in MGIT.

full_output.paper_title: Galleria mellonella as a consolidated in vivo model hosts: New developments in antibacterial strategies and novel drug testing.
full_output.key_findings: The review highlights the use of Galleria mellonella as an in vivo model for studying antibacterial strategies and novel drug testing, emphasizing its advantages over traditional animal models.
full_output.methodology: Review of existing literature and experimental studies on Galleria mellonella as an in vivo model for antibacterial research.

full_output.paper_title: Differences in gram-positive bacterial colonization and antimicrobial resistance among children in a high income inequality setting.
full_output.key_findings: The study found differences in S. aureus and BHS colonization rates among children from different socioeconomic status (SES) communities. MRSA colonization was higher in middle/low SES children, and all MRSA strains were susceptible to clindamycin, nitrofurantoin, and rifampin. BHS isolates were susceptible to all tested antimicrobials.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed nasal and throat swabs from children attending private and public clinics to assess colonization and antimicrobial resistance profiles.

full_output.key_findings: The study found high rates of antimicrobial resistance in Streptococcus pneumoniae isolates from school children in South Ethiopia, with 48.9% resistance to tetracycline, 45.3% to co-trimoxazole, and 28.3% to oxacillin.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing was performed using the Kirby-Bauer disc-diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: The S. Typhi effector StoD is an E3/E4 ubiquitin ligase which binds K48- and K63-linked diubiquitin.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies StoD as a novel E3/E4 ubiquitin ligase from S. Typhi that binds K48- and K63-linked diubiquitin, highlighting its potential role in modulating host cell processes through ubiquitination.
full_output.methodology: The research utilized biochemical assays, structural analysis, and yeast two-hybrid experiments to investigate StoD's function as an E3 ubiquitin ligase.

full_output.paper_title: ICE SXT vs. ICESh95: Co-existence of Integrative and Conjugative Elements and Competition for a New Host.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the dfrA15 gene within ICE Sh31 and ICE Sh95, which confers resistance to trimethoprim. It also highlights the co-existence and competition of different ICEs in Shewanella spp.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, conjugation assays, and qPCR were used to analyze the presence and functionality of AMR genes in ICEs.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first case of meningitis caused by Burkholderia cepacia in the Central African Republic, highlighting its multidrug-resistant nature with resistance to several antibiotics except cotrimoxazole.
full_output.methodology: Conventional bacteriology, API 20 NE identification, antibiotic susceptibility testing via disc diffusion, and 16S rRNA gene sequencing.

full_output.paper_title: Staphylococcus lugdunensis: antimicrobial susceptibility and optimal treatment options.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that Staphylococcus lugdunensis isolates were mostly susceptible to antibiotics, with 74.6% susceptible to penicillin G. Two isolates carrying the mecA gene were found to harbor the SCC mec type IVa(2B), and the blaZ gene was identified in one isolate, contributing to penicillin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing using disc diffusion and Etest, along with whole-genome sequencing for resistance gene identification.

full_output.paper_title: Inhibition of Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilm formation and expression of virulence genes by selective epimerization in the peptide Esculentin-1a(1-21)NH(2).
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that the diastereomer Esc(1-21)-1c effectively inhibits biofilm formation and reduces the expression of virulence genes in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, likely through interactions with the bacterial alarmone ppGpp.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized biofilm formation assays, motility assays, gene expression analysis, and 31P-NMR spectroscopy to investigate the effects of Esc(1-21) and its diastereomer Esc(1-21)-1c on P. aeruginosa.

full_output.paper_title: A Lysine-Targeted Affinity Label for Serine-β-Lactamase Also Covalently Modifies New Delhi Metallo-β-lactamase-1 (NDM-1).
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that the O-aryloxycarbonyl hydroxamate 1 covalently modifies Lys211 in NDM-1, leading to inactivation. This highlights a potential strategy for targeting lysine residues in both serine and metallo-beta-lactamases.
full_output.methodology: Mass spectrometry, X-ray crystallography, site-directed mutagenesis, and kinetic analysis were used to investigate the covalent modification of NDM-1 by 1.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that close proximity interactions (CPIs) supported the transmission of ESBL-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae (ESBL-KP) but not ESBL-producing Escherichia coli (ESBL-EC) in a long-term care facility. ESBL-KP transmission was more strongly associated with CPIs, while ESBL-EC transmission was less influenced by such interactions.
full_output.methodology: The study used wearable sensors to track close proximity interactions and weekly ESBL-carriage data to analyze transmission patterns of ESBL-EC and ESBL-KP in a long-term care facility.

full_output.paper_title: A significant therapeutic effect of silymarin administered alone, or in combination with chemotherapy, in experimental pulmonary tuberculosis caused by drug-sensitive or drug-resistant strains: In vitro and in vivo studies.
full_output.key_findings: Silymarin (Sm) and silibinin (Sb) exhibit microbicidal activity against drug-sensitive and multidrug-resistant (MDR) mycobacteria, enhance the effectiveness of anti-TB drugs, and stimulate protective immune responses in TB treatment.
full_output.methodology: In vitro and in vivo studies evaluating the antimicrobial activity of Sm and Sb against Mycobacterium tuberculosis strains, including assessment of cytotoxicity, cytokine expression, and bacterial load in macrophages and mouse models.

full_output.paper_title: Exploration of antibiotic resistance risks in a veterinary teaching hospital with Oxford Nanopore long read sequencing.

ant(6)-Ia.evidence_note: Detected in ICU cages and LT samples

full_output.key_findings: The study identified various antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) in a veterinary hospital environment using Oxford Nanopore long read sequencing, highlighting the presence of high-risk ARGs associated with mobile genetic elements and the potential for their spread through contaminated surfaces and equipment.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized Oxford Nanopore long read sequencing, ABRicate for ARG detection, and comparative analysis with Illumina sequencing and qPCR to characterize ARGs in environmental samples from a veterinary hospital.
full_output.sample_size: Multiple samples collected from different areas of the veterinary hospital.

full_output.paper_title: Genotypes, Enterotoxin Gene Profiles, and Antimicrobial Resistance of Staphylococcus aureus Associated with Foodborne Outbreaks in Hangzhou, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the prevalence of enterotoxin genes such as sea, seg, sei, selm, seln, selo, selu, sec, sell, sed, selj, and ser in S. aureus isolates from foodborne outbreaks in Hangzhou, China. High resistance to penicillin, erythromycin, tetracycline, clindamycin, gentamicin, and sulfamethoxazole was observed.
full_output.methodology: The study used molecular typing techniques including MLST, spa typing, PFGE, and PCR analysis to identify enterotoxin genes and assess antimicrobial resistance in S. aureus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis of Hydrazone Derivatives of 4-[4-Formyl-3-(2-oxochromen-3-yl)pyrazol-1-yl]benzoic acid as Potent Growth Inhibitors of Antibiotic-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis and antimicrobial evaluation of 27 new pyrazole derivatives, which showed potent growth inhibition against antibiotic-resistant strains of Staphylococcus aureus and Acinetobacter baumannii, with some compounds exhibiting MIC values as low as 1.56 μg/mL.
full_output.methodology: The compounds were synthesized and evaluated for antimicrobial activity using broth microdilution techniques and cytotoxicity studies in HEK293 cells.

full_output.paper_title: Clonal diversity, virulence genes content and subclone status of Escherichia coli sequence type 131: comparative analysis of E. coli ST131 and non-ST131 isolates from Iran.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various AMR genes including CTX-M-G1, CTX-M-G9, CTX-M-15, bla OXA-48, bla NDM, aac6-Ib-cr, qnrB, and qnrS in E. coli isolates from Iran, highlighting their role in resistance to multiple antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Molecular determination of resistance genes and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Microbial epidemiology and antimicrobial resistance patterns of wound infection in Ethiopia: a meta-analysis of laboratory-based cross-sectional studies.
full_output.key_findings: This study identified the prevalence of antimicrobial resistance among bacterial isolates from wound infections in Ethiopia, highlighting high resistance rates to β-lactam antibiotics and lower resistance to ciprofloxacin and gentamicin.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review and meta-analysis of laboratory-based cross-sectional studies.

full_output.paper_title: Linking the resistome and plasmidome to the microbiome.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Aeromonadaceae, Moraxellaceae, and Bacteroidetes as major reservoirs of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in wastewater, using Hi-C to link ARGs, plasmids, and integrons to their host genomes.
full_output.methodology: Hi-C and metagenomic analysis were used to identify and characterize ARGs, plasmids, and integrons in wastewater samples.
full_output.sample_size: Wastewater sample from a municipal wastewater treatment plant.

full_output.paper_title: Structural and biochemical characterization of Rv0187, an O-methyltransferase from Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

Rv0187.notes: The wild-type Rv0187 gene was not associated with antimicrobial resistance, but the mutation (K142A) affected regioselectivity.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes Rv0187, an O-methyltransferase from Mycobacterium tuberculosis, highlighting its structural features, substrate specificity, and the impact of a mutation (K142A) on regioselectivity. No AMR genes were identified.
full_output.methodology: Crystallography, isothermal titration calorimetry, and in vitro activity assays were used to analyze Rv0187.

full_output.paper_title: Generation of a fully erythromycin-sensitive strain of Clostridioides difficile using a novel CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing system.

ermB.mechanism: removal of both ermB genes from Tn 5398

full_output.key_findings: The study generated a fully erythromycin-sensitive strain of Clostridioides difficile by removing both ermB genes using CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing.
full_output.methodology: CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing and colony PCR screening.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and antibiogram study of Staphylococcus aureus isolated from clinical and selected drinking water of Dutsin-Ma, Katsina state, Nigeria.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that all isolated Staphylococcus aureus (165) were multidrug resistant with various antibiotic resistance patterns, showing high resistance to cloxacillin and erythromycin, and varying levels of resistance to other antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing was performed using the agar diffusion technique according to CLSI guidelines.

full_output.paper_title: Extracellular DNA release, quorum sensing, and PrrF1/F2 small RNAs are key players in Pseudomonas aeruginosa tobramycin-enhanced biofilm formation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies PrrF1/F2 small RNAs as key players in tobramycin-enhanced biofilm formation in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, highlighting their role in eDNA release and biofilm architecture modification.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized confocal laser scanning microscopy, proteomic profiling, gene expression assays, and phenotypic studies to investigate the adaptive mechanisms of P. aeruginosa in response to tobramycin exposure.

full_output.paper_title: Amikacin exposure and susceptibility of macrolide-resistant Mycobacterium abscessus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified an A1408G mutation in the 16S rRNA gene of M. abscessus that confers aminoglycoside resistance. This mutation was found in a single patient who developed amikacin resistance despite prolonged amikacin exposure.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing and sequencing of the 16S rRNA gene were performed to identify resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: MLST typing of Treponema pallidum subsp. pallidum in the Czech Republic during 2004-2017: Clinical isolates belonged to 25 allelic profiles and harbored 8 novel allelic variants.

23S rDNA.notes: The A2059G mutation results in macrolide resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified 25 allelic profiles of Treponema pallidum subsp. pallidum in the Czech Republic from 2004 to 2017, including 8 novel allelic variants. Mutations at positions 2058 and 2059 in the 23S rRNA gene were associated with macrolide resistance.
full_output.methodology: Multilocus sequence typing (MLST) and sequencing of the 23S rRNA gene were used to analyze TPA isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Plasma activated water as resistance inducer against bacterial leaf spot of tomato.
full_output.key_findings: Plasma activated water (PAW) did not show direct antimicrobial activity against Xanthomonas vesicatoria (Xv) but enhanced tomato plant defenses, reducing disease severity by up to 61%. The pal gene was involved in the plant's response to PAW treatment and the pathogen.
full_output.methodology: In vitro and in planta experiments, RT-qPCR analysis, and transcriptomic studies were used to evaluate the effects of PAW on plant defense mechanisms and gene expression.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports multidrug resistance (MDR) in Salmonella enterica serotype Typhi isolates from Zimbabwe, with a high prevalence of the H58 haplotype. Resistance to ciprofloxacin, ampicillin, and chloramphenicol was observed, with increasing trends in ciprofloxacin resistance from 2012 to 2017.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR, and pulsed-field gel electrophoresis (PFGE) were used to analyze S. Typhi isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the role of the gut microbiome in drug metabolism and its impact on drug efficacy and toxicity, highlighting the importance of microbiome-drug interactions in clinical settings.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews experimental and computational approaches to understand microbiome-drug interactions, focusing on the mechanisms by which the gut microbiota affects drug metabolism.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Activity of Polyphenols and Alkaloids in Middle Eastern Plants.
full_output.key_findings: This review discusses the antimicrobial activity of polyphenols and alkaloids found in Middle Eastern plants, highlighting their potential as alternative treatments against multidrug-resistant microorganisms.
full_output.methodology: The study reviews existing literature on the antimicrobial properties of plant-derived compounds, focusing on polyphenols and alkaloids.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic Resistance of E. coli Isolated From a Constructed Wetland Dominated by a Crow Roost, With Emphasis on ESBL and AmpC Containing E. coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla ctx-M and bla cmy-2 genes as major contributors to extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) and AmpC beta-lactamase resistance in E. coli isolates from a constructed wetland dominated by a crow roost. Tetracycline resistance was primarily mediated by tet (A), tet (B), and tet (M), while streptomycin resistance was linked to strA, strB, and aadA. Sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim resistance was associated with the sul1 gene.
full_output.methodology: PCR, qPCR, sequencing, and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to characterize AMR genes and mutations in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Clonal dissemination of Staphylococcus aureus isolates causing nosocomial infections, Tehran, Iran.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antimicrobial resistance genes in Staphylococcus aureus isolates, including ant(4')-Ia, aac(6')-Ie/aph(2''), aph(3')-IIIa, erm(A), erm(B), erm(C), msr(A), msr(B), tet(M), and mupA, which contribute to resistance against aminoglycosides, macrolides, tetracycline, and mupirocin.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR, and molecular typing methods were used to characterize resistance genes and clones.

full_output.paper_title: Detailed Soluble Proteome Analyses of a Dairy-Isolated Enterococcus faecalis: A Possible Approach to Assess Food Safety and Potential Probiotic Value.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a beta-lactamase gene in the dairy-isolated Enterococcus faecalis D27, indicating potential resistance to beta-lactam antibiotics. The clinical isolate UW3114 showed resistance to erythromycin, likely due to the presence of a pathogenicity island.
full_output.methodology: Proteomic analysis and antibiotic susceptibility testing were conducted to assess the AMR profile of the strains.
full_output.sample_size: Three strains of Enterococcus faecalis were analyzed.

full_output.paper_title: Endocarditis Caused by Highly Penicillin-Resistant Viridans Group Streptococci: Still Room for Vancomycin-Based Regimens.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports two cases of endocarditis caused by highly penicillin-resistant viridans group streptococci (VGS) successfully treated with vancomycin-based regimens. It also evaluates the effectiveness of various antibiotic combinations against these strains in vitro and in vivo.
full_output.methodology: The study includes in vitro antibiotic susceptibility testing, time-kill studies, and an in vivo experimental endocarditis model in rabbits.

full_output.paper_title: β-Lactam Antibiotics Enhance the Pathogenicity of Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus via SarA-Controlled Lipoprotein-Like Cluster Expression.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a cluster of lipoprotein-like genes (lpl) in MRSA that are upregulated in response to subinhibitory concentrations of β-lactam antibiotics. The expression of these genes is controlled by the global regulator SarA and contributes to increased pathogenicity by enhancing proinflammatory cytokine production through TLR2 activation.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized SDS-PAGE, RT-PCR, Western blot analysis, and mouse infection models to investigate the role of lpl genes in MRSA pathogenicity.

full_output.paper_title: YhjX Regulates the Growth of Escherichia coli in the Presence of a Subinhibitory Concentration of Gentamicin and Mediates the Adaptive Resistance to Gentamicin.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies yhjX as a gene that regulates the growth of E. coli in the presence of subinhibitory concentrations of gentamicin and mediates adaptive resistance to gentamicin.
full_output.methodology: The study used RNA-Seq, qRT-PCR, and growth curve analysis to investigate the role of yhjX in E. coli's response to gentamicin.

full_output.paper_title: Gamma-glutamylcysteine synthetase and tryparedoxin 1 exert high control on the antioxidant system in Trypanosoma cruzi contributing to drug resistance and infectivity.
full_output.key_findings: Overexpression of gamma-glutamylcysteine synthetase and tryparedoxin 1 increases trypanothione levels and enhances resistance to benznidazole and hydrogen peroxide, highlighting their roles in drug resistance and infectivity in Trypanosoma cruzi.
full_output.methodology: Gene overexpression, enzyme activity assays, flux control analysis, and resistance assays.

full_output.paper_title: Tn6674 Is a Novel Enterococcal optrA-Carrying Multiresistance Transposon of the Tn554 Family.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Tn6674, a novel transposon carrying the optrA gene, which confers resistance to oxazolidinones and phenicols, along with fexA, spc, and erm(A) genes, in an Enterococcus faecalis strain.

full_output.methodology: The study used crystal violet staining, confocal microscopy, and resazurin assays to evaluate biofilm formation and antibiotic susceptibility.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that retapamulin shows in vitro synergistic activity with erythromycin and quinupristin against Enterococcus faecalis, including strains with high-level erythromycin resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used disk diffusion, checkerboard, and time-kill assays to evaluate the synergistic effects of retapamulin with MLS antibiotics against E. faecalis.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that approximately 30% of MRSA isolates from blood cultures were hVISA strains, which are associated with higher teicoplanin MIC and multidrug resistance. Diabetes mellitus was linked to an increased risk of hVISA infections.
full_output.methodology: The study used Etest methods (Macrodilution Etest and Glycopeptide Resistance Detection Etest) to screen for hVISA strains among MRSA isolates from blood cultures.

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the challenges posed by drug-resistant tuberculosis, emphasizing the need for improved diagnostics, treatment regimens, and prophylactic strategies to combat the rising global burden of antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews existing literature and discusses the implications of drug-resistant tuberculosis on transmission, diagnosis, and treatment.

full_output.methodology: Site-directed mutagenesis, MIC testing, Galleria mellonella killing assays, and real-time RT-PCR.

full_output.paper_title: Transmission and Drug Resistance Genotype of Multidrug-Resistant or Rifampicin-Resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis in Chongqing, China.

These mutations were linked to resistance against ethambutol, levofloxacin, moxifloxacin, amikacin, kanamycin, ethionamide, isoniazid, rifampicin, bedaquiline, and clofazimine.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance Profile of Bacteria Causing Pediatric Infections at the University Teaching Hospital in Rwanda.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high resistance rates to commonly used antibiotics among bacteria causing pediatric infections, particularly Klebsiella pneumoniae, Escherichia coli, and Staphylococcus aureus. Resistance to ampicillin, amoxicillin-clavulanic acid, and ceftazidime was particularly notable.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the disk diffusion method on 177 positive cultures from pediatric patients.

full_output.paper_title: A high-efficiency scar-free genome-editing toolkit for Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified craA and cmlA5 as genes involved in chloramphenicol resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii AB5075. Deletion of these genes increased susceptibility to chloramphenicol, demonstrating their role in resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genome editing techniques were used to create mutants lacking craA and cmlA5, followed by antibiotic susceptibility testing via disc diffusion and MIC assays.

full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the importance of deep sequencing in detecting pneumococcal within-host diversity, revealing higher rates of multiple colonization and resistance elements compared to traditional methods. It also identifies GPSC1 as a multidrug-resistant lineage that persists after antimicrobial treatment.
full_output.methodology: Deep sequencing of pneumococcal populations from longitudinal nasopharyngeal samples to analyze genetic diversity and resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Quinoline-imidazole/benzimidazole derivatives as dual-/multi-targeting hybrids inhibitors with anticancer and antimicrobial activity.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents the design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of novel quinoline-imidazole/benzimidazole derivatives with potential anticancer and antimicrobial activities. Compounds such as 11h, 12h, and 12f showed significant anticancer activity against various cancer cell lines and notable antibacterial activity against Gram-negative bacteria like E. coli.
full_output.methodology: The compounds were synthesized through a four-step process involving N-acylation, N-alkylation, quaternization, and a Huisgen 3 + 2 cycloaddition. Their biological activities were assessed using in vitro assays including the NCI 60 cell line screen, disk diffusion method, and broth microdilution assay.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic and Epidemiological Features of Two Dominant Methicillin-Susceptible Staphylococcus aureus Clones from a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit Surveillance Effort.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mupA as a gene conferring high-level mupirocin resistance in ST1898 MSSA clones, which were prevalent in the NICU and associated with decolonization efforts.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and phylogenetic analysis were used to characterize the genomic features of MSSA clones in the NICU.

full_output.paper_title: Sharing of Antimicrobial Resistance Genes between Humans and Food Animals.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies shared antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) between humans and food animals, highlighting the role of mobile genetic elements in their dissemination. Notably, ARGs such as bla CTX-M, erm(B), tet(34), tet(Q), oqxAB, fosA, and aph were found to be prevalent in both human and swine gut microbiomes, emphasizing the potential for cross-species transmission of resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic analysis of gut microbiomes from humans and food animals to identify and characterize ARGs.

full_output.paper_title: Noncanonical Mismatch Repair Protein NucS Modulates the Emergence of Antibiotic Resistance in Mycobacterium abscessus.

rrl.notes: Mutations in rrl gene confer resistance to macrolides.

rrs.notes: Mutations in rrs gene confer resistance to aminoglycosides.

full_output.key_findings: Inactivation of the noncanonical MMR pathway via nucS leads to increased mutation rates and resistance to macrolides and aminoglycosides in Mycobacterium abscessus.
full_output.methodology: Generation of nucS knockout and complemented strains, mutation rate determination via fluctuation tests, and sequencing of rRNA genes to identify resistance mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of 5-(Aryl/Heteroaryl)amino-4-quinolones as Potent Membrane-Disrupting Agents to Combat Antibiotic-Resistant Gram-Positive Bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies 5-(aryl/heteroaryl)amino-4-quinolones as potent membrane-disrupting agents against antibiotic-resistant Gram-positive bacteria, demonstrating strong antibacterial activity with minimal inhibitory concentrations (MICs) as low as 0.06 μg/mL against clinical isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis and evaluation of quinoline derivatives for antibacterial activity, including structure-activity relationship (SAR) analyses, mechanism of action studies, and pharmacokinetic evaluations.

full_output.paper_title: Dynamic Intramolecular Cap for Preserving Metallodrug Integrity─A Case of Catalytic Fluoroquinolones.
full_output.key_findings: The study introduces a dynamic intramolecular cap strategy for improving the stability and efficacy of metallodrugs, particularly focusing on the Co(III) complex of 11, which shows enhanced antibacterial activity and resistance to endogenous chelators.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of ciprofloxacin-nuclease conjugates, metal complexation, DNA cleavage assays, and antibacterial activity testing.

full_output.paper_title: Lysyl-tRNA synthetase, a target for urgently needed M. tuberculosis drugs.

full_output.methodology: The study involved generating a resistant mutant of M. tuberculosis to LysRS inhibitor 7, whole-genome sequencing, and evaluating the sensitivity of the mutant to various compounds through growth assays and biochemical analyses.

full_output.paper_title: Investigation of Streptomyces sp. Strain EMB24 Secondary Metabolite Profile Has Unraveled Its Extraordinary Antibacterial Potency Against Drug-Resistant Bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several secondary metabolites produced by Streptomyces sp. strain EMB24, including naphthyridinomycin, antimycin, splenocin, alkylresorcinols, curamycin, ectoine, desferrioxamine B, desferrioxamine E, albaflavenone, geosmin, venezuelin, aborycin, MS-271, and siamycin, which exhibit strong antibacterial activity against drug-resistant bacteria such as MRSA, tetracycline-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae, and azithromycin-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antiSMASH analysis were used to identify secondary metabolite biosynthesis gene clusters, and agar-plug assays were conducted to assess antimicrobial activity against drug-resistant bacterial strains.

full_output.paper_title: Pathogenic potential and antimicrobial resistance of Staphylococcus pseudintermedius isolated from human and animals.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of the mecA and blaZ genes in Staphylococcus pseudintermedius isolates, indicating resistance to methicillin and penicillin, respectively. Animal isolates exhibited higher antibiotic resistance compared to human isolates.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of resistance genes and MLST analysis for genetic diversity.

full_output.paper_title: Zinc oxide nanoparticles reduce biofilm formation, synergize antibiotics action and attenuate Staphylococcus aureus virulence in host; an important message to clinicians.
full_output.key_findings: Zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO-NPs) effectively reduce biofilm formation and enhance the antibacterial effects of antibiotics against Staphylococcus aureus. They also decrease bacterial virulence in a mouse infection model.
full_output.methodology: The study used a combination of in vitro assays, including biofilm formation tests, antibiotic susceptibility testing, and qRT-PCR, along with in vivo mouse infection models to evaluate the effects of ZnO-NPs on S. aureus.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of extended-spectrum β-lactamases, AmpC, and carbapenemases in Proteus mirabilis clinical isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of extended-spectrum beta-lactamases (ESBLs), AmpC beta-lactamases, and carbapenemases in Proteus mirabilis clinical isolates, highlighting the high prevalence of these resistance mechanisms, particularly in urinary tract isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized phenotypic detection methods, PCR, and molecular typing techniques to identify and characterize AMR genes in P. mirabilis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Multi-drug resistant bacteria isolates from lymphatic filariasis patients in the Ahanta West District, Ghana.

blaCTX-M.validation_method: PCR amplification and detection of the gene in multidrug-resistant isolates

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of multidrug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) harboring the mecA gene, and multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli with the blaCTX-M gene, indicating resistance to penicillin and cephalosporins, respectively.

full_output.paper_title: Intimin (eae) and virulence membrane protein pagC genes are associated with biofilm formation and multidrug resistance in Escherichia coli and Salmonella enterica isolates from calves with diarrhea.

full_output.paper_title: Survey of Oxolinic Acid-Resistant Erwinia amylovora in Korean Apple and Pear Orchards, and the Fitness Impact of Constructed Mutants.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the gyrA gene of Erwinia amylovora that confer resistance to oxolinic acid (OA). These mutations, G81C and S83R, were associated with reduced growth and virulence of the mutants compared to the wild-type.

full_output.paper_title: Redesign of Rifamycin Antibiotics to Overcome ADP-Ribosylation-Mediated Resistance.

arr.validation_method: cloning, expression, purification, and LC-MS enzymatic assay

full_output.paper_title: Efficient Suppression of Natural Plasmid-Borne Gene Expression in Carbapenem-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae Using a Compact CRISPR Interference System.

bla_SHV-12.validation_method: CRISPRi-mediated gene silencing and MIC testing

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the effective use of a CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) system to suppress the expression of plasmid-borne resistance genes, specifically bla_NDM-1 and bla_SHV-12, in carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae, leading to reduced antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: First Isolation of Vancomycin-Resistant Enterococcus faecium Carrying Plasmid-Borne vanD1.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first isolation of a vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium strain carrying the plasmid-borne vanD1 gene, which confers resistance to vancomycin.

full_output.paper_title: Evolution of Virulence, Fitness, and Carbapenem Resistance Transmission in ST23 Hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae with the Capsular Polysaccharide Synthesis Gene wcaJ Inserted via Insertion Sequence Elements.

full_output.paper_title: Baicalin acts as an adjuvant to potentiate the activity of azithromycin against Staphylococcus saprophyticus biofilm: an in vitro, in vivo, and molecular study.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic resistance and pathogenicity assessment of various Gardnerella sp. strains in local China.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiological, clinical, and laboratory features of patients infected with Elizabethkingia meningoseptica at a tertiary hospital in Hefei City, China.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic characterization of two community-acquired methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus with novel sequence types in Kenya.

full_output.paper_title: Efficacy of Co-Trimoxazole against Experimental Melioidosis Acquired by Different Routes of Infection.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic Characterization and Antimicrobial Susceptibility of Dromedary-Associated Staphylococcaceae from the Horn of Africa.

full_output.paper_title: A machine learning model trained on a high-throughput antibacterial screen increases the hit rate of drug discovery.

full_output.paper_title: Unravelling the Diversity and Abundance of the Red Fox (Vulpes vulpes) Faecal Resistome and the Phenotypic Antibiotic Susceptibility of Indicator Bacteria.

full_output.methodology: High-throughput qPCR was used to screen for ARGs and mobile genetic elements (MGEs) in red fox fecal samples, and antibiotic susceptibility testing (AST) was performed on E. coli and Enterococcus spp. isolates.

Additionally, NSE improved growth performance and immune responses in rabbits, reducing MRSA infection risks.
