full_output.methodology: The study utilized transcriptome analysis, qRT-PCR, and biochemical assays to investigate the antifungal and antibacterial mechanisms of the Sp1 protein.

full_output.paper_title: Frequency of Multi-Drug Resistance and Molecular Characteristics of Resistance to Colistin in Acinetobacter baumannii Collected from Patients in Intensive Care Units with Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia.
full_output.key_findings: All A. baumannii isolates were MDR and XDR, but none exhibited colistin resistance. No point mutations in pmrCAB genes or presence of mcr-1 gene were detected.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR, and sequencing.

full_output.paper_title: Inhibition of Staphylococcus aureus biofilm formation by gurmarin, a plant-derived cyclic peptide.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies gurmarin, a plant-derived cyclic peptide, as an effective inhibitor of Staphylococcus aureus biofilm formation without affecting bacterial viability. Gurmarin reduces the synthesis of poly N-acetylglucosamine (PNAG), a critical component of the biofilm matrix, and modulates the expression of genes involved in biofilm development.
full_output.methodology: The study used transcriptomic analysis, biofilm assays, and immunoblotting to investigate the effects of gurmarin on S. aureus biofilm formation and gene expression.

full_output.paper_title: Identification and Biochemical Characterization of Pyrrolidinediones as Novel Inhibitors of the Bacterial Enzyme MurA.

MurA.notes: The C115D mutation in MurA confers resistance to fosfomycin.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the MurA C115D mutation as a resistance mechanism against fosfomycin and characterizes pyrrolidinediones as novel inhibitors of MurA, demonstrating equal potency against both wild-type and fosfomycin-resistant MurA variants.
full_output.methodology: Biochemical assays, enzyme kinetics, native mass spectrometry, NMR spectroscopy, and molecular docking were used to evaluate the inhibitory activity and mechanism of pyrrolidinediones against MurA.

full_output.paper_title: New Dual P-Glycoprotein (P-gp) and Human Carbonic Anhydrase XII (hCA XII) Inhibitors as Multidrug Resistance (MDR) Reversers in Cancer Cells.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies compounds that inhibit both P-gp and hCA XII, enhancing doxorubicin cytotoxicity in cancer cells overexpressing these proteins.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis and evaluation of compounds for P-gp and hCA XII inhibition using cell-based assays and biochemical techniques.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation, identification and antibiotic resistance profile of thermophilic Campylobacter species from Bovine, Knives and personnel at Jimma Town Abattoir, Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified thermophilic Campylobacter species, primarily C. jejuni, C. coli, and C. lari, with high resistance to Cephalothin, Ampicillin, and Cefotaxime. All C. lari isolates exhibited multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: Isolation and identification of Campylobacter species using standard microbiological techniques and antimicrobial susceptibility testing via agar disc diffusion.

full_output.paper_title: Genotyping and macrolide-resistant mutation of Bordetella pertussis in East and South-East Asia.

B. pertussis 23S rRNA.notes: The A2047G mutation in the 23S rRNA gene of B. pertussis was associated with macrolide resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the A2047G mutation in the 23S rRNA gene of B. pertussis as a key factor in macrolide resistance, with this mutation being prevalent in several East and Southeast Asian countries including Vietnam, Cambodia, Taiwan, and Japan.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized MLVA genotyping and duplex Cycleave real-time PCR to detect the A2047G mutation in B. pertussis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Lactose azocalixarene drug delivery system for the treatment of multidrug-resistant pseudomonas aeruginosa infected diabetic ulcer.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a hypoxia-responsive drug delivery system, Cip@LacAC4A, which enhances the antibacterial efficacy against multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa (MDR PA) by improving drug accumulation and controlled release at the infection site. It shows effective biofilm inhibition and promotes wound healing in diabetic ulcers.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the design and characterization of the supramolecular nanocarrier LacAC4A, evaluation of its antibacterial properties in vitro and in vivo, and assessment of its impact on wound healing in diabetic rats.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic polymyxin arranges lipopolysaccharide into crystalline structures to solidify the bacterial membrane.

mcr-1.encodes: membrane-associated enzyme that catalyzes a chemical modification of the lipid A phosphates by a phosphatidylethanolamine moiety
mcr-1.mechanism: reduces the net negative charge of the OM, impairing the electrostatic interaction between lipid A and the cationic polymyxins

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the mcr-1 gene as a key factor in polymyxin resistance, showing that it modifies lipid A to reduce electrostatic interactions with polymyxins, leading to resistance.
full_output.methodology: Atomic force microscopy (AFM), growth curve analysis, and biochemical assays were used to investigate the interaction of polymyxins with bacterial membranes and the role of the mcr-1 gene in resistance.

full_output.paper_title: An efflux-susceptible antibiotic-adjuvant with systemic efficacy against mouse infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies C10 BBc12 B as a potent antibiotic adjuvant that enhances the efficacy of antibiotics against Gram-negative ESKAPE pathogens by increasing outer-membrane permeability and overcoming resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized in vitro and in vivo experiments, including MIC testing, growth kinetics, and animal models, to evaluate the adjuvant properties of C10 BBc12 B.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of antibacterial activity of five biocides and the synergistic effect of biocide/EDTA combinations on biofilm-producing and non-producing Stenotrophomonas maltophilia strains isolated from clinical specimens in Iran.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the sugE1 gene as a common biocide resistance determinant in clinical Stenotrophomonas maltophilia isolates, with 90.7% of isolates carrying this gene.
full_output.methodology: PCR-based genotyping and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Sulbactam combined with tigecycline improves outcomes in patients with severe multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii pneumonia.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that combining sulbactam with tigecycline improved outcomes in patients with severe multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii pneumonia, particularly highlighting the effectiveness of high-dose sulbactam in reducing mortality rates.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of clinical data from patients with multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii pneumonia, including assessment of treatment regimens and mortality rates.

It also shows that mutations decreasing nitrate reductase activity are a common mechanism of chlorate resistance.
full_output.methodology: Transposon insertion sequencing (Tn-Seq) and experimental validation through unmarked deletions of identified genes.

full_output.paper_title: In vivo pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of ceftibuten/ledaborbactam, a novel oral β-lactam/β-lactamase inhibitor combination.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) properties of ceftibuten/ledaborbactam, a novel oral β-lactam/β-lactamase inhibitor combination, against ceftibuten-resistant Enterobacterales. Ledaborbactam restored the in vitro activity of ceftibuten against these organisms, and the study quantified the PK/PD targets necessary for bacteriostasis.
full_output.methodology: The study used a neutropenic murine thigh infection model to assess the PK/PD properties of ceftibuten/ledaborbactam against 12 ceftibuten-resistant Enterobacterales isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Alarming antibiotics resistance of Helicobacter pylori from children in Southeast China over 6 years.
full_output.key_findings: The study found high resistance rates of Helicobacter pylori to clarithromycin (32.8%), metronidazole (81.7%), and levofloxacin (22.8%) in children from Southeast China between 2015 and 2020, with increasing trends over time.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing was performed using agar dilution method on 1638 H. pylori strains isolated from children.

full_output.paper_title: In silico evaluation of WHO-endorsed molecular methods to detect drug resistant tuberculosis.

inhA.notes: Promoter region mutations in inhA

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the performance of WHO-endorsed molecular diagnostic tests for detecting drug-resistant tuberculosis, focusing on mutations in genes such as rpoB, katG, inhA, pncA, gyrA, rrs, and eis. It highlights the importance of considering a wide range of mutations for accurate resistance detection.
full_output.methodology: In silico evaluation of molecular diagnostic tests using mutations from the WHO 2021 catalogue and comparing their performance to phenotypic DST.

full_output.paper_title: Synergistic effects of silybin and curcumin on virulence and carbapenemase genes expression in multidrug resistant Klebsiella oxytoca.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaIMP and blaOXA-48-like genes as carbapenemase genes in MDR K. oxytoca, along with virulence-related genes mrkA and fimA. Both silybin and curcumin reduced the expression of these genes, indicating their potential as natural antimicrobial agents.
full_output.methodology: qRT-PCR was used to evaluate gene expression levels in response to silybin and curcumin treatments.

full_output.paper_title: Selective Inhibition of the Periodontal Pathogen Porphyromonas gingivalis by Third-Generation Zafirlukast Derivatives.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the design, synthesis, and evaluation of 14 third-generation Zafirlukast (ZAF) derivatives for their selective antibacterial activity against Porphyromonas gingivalis. Compounds 21b, 21c, 21d, 22g, 23g, 24g, and 25g showed superior antibacterial activity against P. gingivalis compared to ZAF and its second-generation derivatives. These compounds exhibited bactericidal activity, inhibited biofilm growth, and had reduced hemolytic and cytotoxic effects compared to ZAF.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis of ZAF derivatives and their evaluation using WST-1 assays, CFU assays, and biofilm disruption tests against P. gingivalis.

This strain has been identified in multiple countries, including the US, El Salvador, Canada, and France.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize the resistant N. meningitidis strains.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of the effect of gentamicin in surgical perfusion solution on cataract postoperative endophthalmitis.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that gentamicin in surgical perfusion solution reduced the incidence of postoperative endophthalmitis. However, aminoglycoside-inactivating enzyme resistance genes, specifically aac(6')-aph(2''), were detected in Enterococcus strains, indicating the emergence of gentamicin-resistant Enterococci.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of endophthalmitis incidence, bacterial isolation, drug susceptibility testing, and PCR for detection of aminoglycoside-inactivating enzyme genes.

blaVEB.validation_method: plasmid transformation and ESBL functionality testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the first occurrence of the blaVEB gene in Pasteurellaceae and confirms its function as an ESBL. Additionally, a plasmid carrying the floR gene, which confers florfenicol resistance, was isolated from P. aerogenes.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, plasmid transformation, and MIC testing were used to identify and validate AMR genes.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in ERG11, PDR1, and FKS2 that contribute to antifungal resistance in Candida species, particularly in C. albicans, C. tropicalis, and C. glabrata.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing of resistance-related genes and MIC testing were performed to determine antifungal resistance mechanisms.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified a phage-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa strain (W10) that exhibits hypersensitivity to colistin and reduced biofilm production.
full_output.methodology: Phage isolation, purification, adsorption assay, one-step growth curve, pH and thermal stability tests, host range analysis, biofilm eradication assay, and fluorescence microscopy.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibility to polymyxin B and other comparators against Gram-negative bacteria isolated from bloodstream infections in China: Results from CARVIS-NET program.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that 94.1% of the 1939 Gram-negative isolates were susceptible to polymyxin B, and the sensitivity of the strains to polymyxin B was highly correlated with their sensitivity to colistin.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing was conducted by broth microdilution method according to CLSI guidelines.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic and genotypic characterization of antimicrobial resistance profiles in Salmonella isolated from waterfowl in 2002-2005 and 2018-2020 in Sichuan, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple AMR genes and mutations in Salmonella isolates from waterfowl in Sichuan, China, including beta-lactamases, aminoglycoside-modifying enzymes, tetracycline efflux pumps, and quinolone resistance genes. Mutations in gyrA and gyrB were associated with nalidixic acid resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify AMR genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Hospital Acquired Pathogenic Escherichia coli from Clinical and Hospital Water Samples of Quetta Balochistan.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified ESBL blaCTX-M-15, tetracycline resistance gene tetA, and TMP-SMX resistance gene dfrA1 in E. coli isolates from clinical and hospital water samples, highlighting the presence of multidrug-resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: Molecular detection via PCR and antibiogram analysis using Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemic, risk factors of carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae infection and its effect on the early prognosis of liver transplantation.
full_output.key_findings: Carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) infection is a significant risk factor for 3-month mortality in liver transplant recipients, with independent risk factors including age, mechanical ventilation duration, and CRKP infection itself.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of clinical data from liver transplant recipients, including microbiological testing and statistical analysis of risk factors for mortality and CRKP infection.

full_output.paper_title: Staphylococcus sciuri causes disease and pathological changes in hybrid sturgeon acipenser baerii × acipenser schrencki.
full_output.key_findings: Staphylococcus sciuri strain D-59 was isolated from diseased hybrid sturgeon and found to be susceptible to several antibiotics including florfenicol, enrofloxacin, neomycin sulfate, doxycycline, ampicillin, penicillin, gentamicin, minocycline, tetracyclines, and amikacin, while being resistant to sulfonamide.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using disk diffusion assay according to CLSI standards.

full_output.paper_title: Multiplexed Target Enrichment Enables Efficient and In-Depth Analysis of Antimicrobial Resistome in Metagenomes.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a multiplex PCR-based amplicon sequencing method for efficient and in-depth analysis of the antimicrobial resistome in metagenomes, demonstrating improved recovery of low-abundance antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) compared to traditional metagenomic shotgun sequencing.

full_output.paper_title: Autophagy, cell death, and cytokines in K. pneumoniae infection: therapeutic perspectives.

full_output.paper_title: 5-ethyl-2'-deoxyuridine fragilizes Klebsiella pneumoniae outer wall and facilitates intracellular killing by phagocytic cells.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies K2, a compound that enhances the intracellular killing of Klebsiella pneumoniae by increasing the accessibility of the bacterial outer membrane, without altering the LPS structure. full_output.methodology: The study utilized Dictyostelium discoideum as a model phagocyte to screen compounds and assess their effect on K. pneumoniae virulence. Techniques included fluorescence microscopy, bacterial growth assays, and analysis of LPS structure.

full_output.paper_title: Development and validation of a resazurin assay for in vitro susceptibility testing of Actinomadura madurae: a common causative agent of actinomycetoma.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed and validated a resazurin-based in vitro susceptibility assay for Actinomadura madurae, determining MICs for 12 antibacterial agents. full_output.paper_title: Regional distribution of Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection and resistance to rifampicin and isoniazid as determined by high-resolution melt analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the rpoB gene associated with rifampicin resistance and mutations in the katG and inhA genes associated with isoniazid resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the role of mobile genetic elements, particularly insertion sequences (IS), in the acquisition and dissemination of antibiotic resistance in Acinetobacter species. IS elements can enhance the expression of intrinsic beta-lactamase genes, such as bla OXA-23, bla OXA-51, and ampC, leading to carbapenem and cephalosporin resistance. Additionally, IS elements can disrupt genes involved in antibiotic uptake, such as porins, and alter the expression of efflux pumps, contributing to multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed the impact of mobile genetic elements on antibiotic resistance in Acinetobacter species through experimental validation of gene expression and transposition events.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical Performance of the Osmotic Shock-MALDI MS Method to Detect Klebsiella pneumoniae Carbapenemase in Clinical Isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the OS-MALDI MS method for detecting KPC carbapenemase in clinical isolates, demonstrating high sensitivity and specificity compared to other methods.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR, DNA sequencing, and MALDI-TOF MS for detecting and characterizing KPC carbapenemase in clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: PBP1A Directly Interacts with the Divisome Complex to Promote Septal Peptidoglycan Synthesis in Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the role of PBP1A in promoting septal peptidoglycan synthesis in Acinetobacter baumannii, highlighting its direct interaction with the divisome complex and its importance in cell division. It also shows that PBP1A is not functionally redundant with PBP1B and that PBP3 and PBP5 can rescue septation defects in ΔmrcA cells.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation, coimmunoprecipitation, fluorescence microscopy, and phenotypic analysis were used to investigate the role of PBP1A and other peptidoglycan synthases in A. baumannii.

full_output.paper_title: Pixantrone Sensitizes Gram-Negative Pathogens to Rifampin.
full_output.key_findings: Pixantrone (PIX) enhances the antimicrobial activity of rifampin (RFP) against Gram-negative pathogens by disrupting the outer membrane, inducing reactive oxygen species (ROS) and reactive nitrogen species (RNS), and disrupting proton motive force (PMF).
full_output.methodology: High-throughput drug screening, checkerboard assays, time-growth assays, and in vivo studies were used to evaluate the synergistic effects of PIX and RFP.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis and Structure-Activity Studies of β-Barrel Assembly Machine Complex Inhibitor MRL-494.
full_output.key_findings: The study focuses on the synthesis and evaluation of MRL-494, a β-barrel assembly machine (BAM) complex inhibitor, and its analogues. MRL-494 exhibited antibacterial activity against several Gram-negative bacteria and showed synergistic effects with rifampicin. The presence of two guanidine groups was crucial for its activity, and structural modifications led to loss of activity.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis of MRL-494 and its analogues, followed by antibacterial activity assays, synergy tests, and membrane permeabilization experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial and prebiotic activity of mannoproteins isolated from conventional and nonconventional yeast species-the study on selected microorganisms.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the antimicrobial and prebiotic effects of mannoprotein preparations from Saccharomyces cerevisiae, Metschnikowia reukaufii, and Wickerhamomyces anomalus on various bacterial strains. These preparations exhibited varying degrees of growth inhibition against pathogenic bacteria and stimulation of beneficial bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The study characterized mannoprotein preparations through elemental analysis, amino acid composition, molecular weight, and spectroscopic techniques. Antimicrobial activity was assessed using broth microdilution to determine growth inhibition of target bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of the international lineage ST71 of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus pseudintermedius in two cities in Rio de Janeiro State.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the presence of the international lineage ST71 of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus pseudintermedius (MRSP) in two cities in Rio de Janeiro State, highlighting its multidrug resistance and potential zoonotic transmission.
full_output.methodology: Molecular characterization, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and genomic analysis were conducted to identify and characterize MRSP isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiology of carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae ST15 of producing KPC-2, SHV-106 and CTX-M-15 in Anhui, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple beta-lactamase genes (blaSHV-106, blaKPC-2, blaCTX-M-15, blaTEM-1B, blaOXA-1), efflux pumps (oqxAB, acrAB), and other resistance genes (fosA, aac(3)-lid, aac(6')-lb-cr, tet(A), sul1, mph(A)) in ST15 CRKP isolates from Anhui, China, contributing to multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to characterize the resistance mechanisms in ST15 CRKP isolates.

full_output.paper_title: The first outbreak of citrobacteriosis caused by Citrobacter gillenii in reared Russian sturgeon (Acipenser gueldenstaedtii) in Turkiye.

full_output.paper_title: Therapeutic Bacteriophages for Gram-Negative Bacterial Infections in Animals and Humans.
full_output.key_findings: This review discusses the use of bacteriophages as novel agents to combat multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacterial infections, highlighting their potential as therapeutic alternatives to traditional antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Review of literature on bacteriophage therapy for Gram-negative bacterial infections.

full_output.paper_title: Natural Products as Potential Antimicrobial Agents Against Multidrug-Resistant Pathogens
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several natural products with potent antimicrobial activity against multidrug-resistant (MDR) pathogens, including compounds from plants, lichens, insects, and fungi. Notable examples include sesquiterpene lactones, flavonoids, and diterpenoids that show efficacy against MRSA, VRE, and other resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: The research involved the isolation and characterization of natural compounds from various sources, followed by in vitro testing against MDR bacterial strains to assess their antimicrobial activity.

full_output.paper_title: Community-Acquired Acinetobacter radioresistens Bacteremia in an Immunocompetent Host.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Activity of Peptide-Coupled Antisense Peptide Nucleic Acids in Streptococcus pneumoniae.

full_output.methodology: Multiplex PCR and DNA lateral flow assay for detection of AMR genes in bacterial isolates and artificially spiked blood samples.

full_output.paper_title: High Frequency of Antibiotic Resistance Genes (ARGs) in the Lerma River Basin, Mexico.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high frequency of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in the Lerma River basin, including bla CTX-M, bla SHV, bla TEM, bla OXA, bla NDM, bla KPC, bla VIM, qnr B, qnr S, and aac (6′)Ib-cr, which confer resistance to beta-lactams, quinolones, and aminoglycosides. Citrobacter freundii exhibited the highest multidrug resistance (MDR) frequency.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic and molecular methods, including PCR, sequencing, and whole-genome sequencing, were used to detect and characterize ARGs in environmental isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Response of Antibiotic Resistance Genes and Related Microorganisms to Arsenic during Vermicomposting of Cow Dung.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that vermicomposting reduced the abundance of most antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in cow dung, including sulfonamide (sul1, sul2), tetracycline (tetL, tetX, tetQ, tetO, tetW), beta-lactam (blaampC, blaTEM-1, blaOXA-1, blaNDM), aminoglycoside (aadA), fluoroquinolone (fexA), macrolide/lincosamide/streptogramin B (ermC, ermB), quinolone (qnrB, qnrS, oqxB), and streptothricin (strA, strB) resistance genes. However, arsenic enrichment increased the abundance of certain ARGs, such as cfr, ermC, and others.
full_output.methodology: The study used real-time qPCR to quantify the abundance of 21 specific ARGs and two key integrase genes (intl1, intl2) in cow dung samples before and after vermicomposting, along with 16S rRNA gene sequencing to assess microbial community changes.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation and Characterization of Two Novel Siphoviruses Novomoskovsk and Bolokhovo, Encoding Polysaccharide Depolymerases Active against Bacillus pumilus.
full_output.key_findings: Two novel bacteriophages, Novomoskovsk and Bolokhovo, were isolated and characterized. They encode polysaccharide depolymerases (Gp28 and Gp31) that show lytic activity against Bacillus pumilus strains. The depolymerases exhibit stability across a wide range of temperatures and pH levels.
full_output.methodology: Phage isolation, genome sequencing, depolymerase cloning, and activity assays were conducted.

full_output.paper_title: Combined Application of Aminoglycosides and Ascorbic Acid in the Elimination of Proteus mirabilis Rods Responsible for Causing Catheter-Associated Urinary Tract Infections (CAUTIs)-A Molecular Approach.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the effects of combining aminoglycosides (amikacin and gentamicin) with ascorbic acid (AA) on Proteus mirabilis, focusing on their impact on bacterial growth, biofilm formation, and membrane integrity. While AA did not act as an effective urinary acidifier, it influenced phospholipid and fatty acid profiles, and modulated membrane permeability. The results suggest that AA may interfere with the efficacy of aminoglycosides against P. mirabilis.
full_output.methodology: The study employed HPLC-MS, GC-MS, and fluorescent assays to analyze the effects of aminoglycosides and AA on P. mirabilis, including changes in phospholipid and fatty acid profiles, reactive oxygen species generation, and membrane permeability.

full_output.paper_title: A Novel Antimicrobial Peptide Spampcin(56-86) from Scylla paramamosain Exerting Rapid Bactericidal and Anti-Biofilm Activity In Vitro and Anti-Infection In Vivo.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel antimicrobial peptide, Spampcin, and its truncated derivatives (Spa31, Spa20, Spa22, and Spa14), which show potent antibacterial and antifungal activity against a range of pathogens, including Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria and fungi. full_output.methodology: The study utilized bioinformatics analysis, AMP database predictions, chemical synthesis, antimicrobial assays, zone of inhibition tests, time-killing kinetics, SEM, SYTO 9/PI staining, NPN staining, LPS inhibition, ATP release, ROS production, biofilm inhibition assays, and in vivo zebrafish infection experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of High Antimicrobial Resistance among Critically Ill Patients with Hospital-Acquired Infections in a Tertiary Care Hospital.

Compound 5d showed the highest antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus, with a MIC of 3.95 mM, surpassing tetracycline. The research highlights the impact of substituent placement on the biological activity of the synthesized compounds.
full_output.methodology: The compounds were synthesized and evaluated for antimicrobial, antioxidant, and antidiabetic activities using in vitro assays. Molecular docking and dynamic simulations were performed to analyze interactions with target enzymes.

full_output.paper_title: Computational Studies on Selected Macrolides Active against Escherichia coli Combined with the NMR Study of Tylosin A in Deuterated Chloroform.
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on computational and NMR analyses of macrolides, including tylosin A, to understand their structural and functional properties for activity against Gram-negative bacteria. It identified specific macrolide derivatives with potential activity against Gram-negative bacteria based on physicochemical parameters and conformational analysis.
full_output.methodology: The study combined computational methods (EIIP screening, conformational analysis, molecular docking, ADMET studies) with NMR spectroscopy to analyze the structure and activity of macrolides against Gram-negative bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Brazilian Red Propolis Presents Promising Anti-H. pylori Activity in In Vitro and In Vivo Assays with the Ability to Modulate the Immune Response.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that the crude hydroalcoholic extract of Brazilian red propolis (CHEBRP) exhibits promising anti-H. pylori activity in both in vitro and in vivo assays, reducing bacterial load and modulating the immune response in infected rats.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the anti-H. pylori activity of CHEBRP through in vitro MIC/MBC determination and in vivo microbiological and histopathological analyses in Wistar rats.

full_output.paper_title: Potential Application of Luteolin as an Active Antibacterial Composition in the Development of Hand Sanitizer Products.
full_output.key_findings: Luteolin (LUT) exhibits strong antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus, primarily through disruption of cell membrane integrity and increased membrane permeability.
full_output.methodology: Antibacterial activity was assessed using the Oxford cup method, MIC/MBC determination, and various microscopic and spectroscopic techniques to analyze membrane permeability and structural changes.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis and Biological Activity of N-acyl Anabasine and Cytisine Derivatives with Adamantane, Pyridine and 1,2-Azole Fragments.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial activity of N-acyl anabasine and cytisine derivatives, identifying compounds with antibacterial effects comparable to ceftriaxone against Staphylococcus aureus. Some derivatives exhibited moderate antiviral activity against influenza viruses.
full_output.methodology: Chemical synthesis of compounds followed by in vitro antimicrobial, antiviral, and antifungal activity testing using agar diffusion and serial dilution methods.

full_output.paper_title: Design, Synthesis, and Bioassay of 2'-Modified Kanamycin A.
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on designing and synthesizing 2'-modified kanamycin A derivatives to enhance their activity against drug-resistant bacteria. The research identified that modifications at the 2'-position of kanamycin A could improve its efficacy against certain resistant strains, particularly those expressing aac(2')-Ib.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the design, synthesis, and bioassay of 2'-modified kanamycin A derivatives against various bacterial strains to assess their antimicrobial activity.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Hybrids of Pyazolo[3,4-b]pyridine and Triazole: Design, Synthesis and In Vitro Antibacterial Studies.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the design, synthesis, and in vitro antibacterial evaluation of molecular hybrids of pyrazolo[3,4-b]pyridine and triazole. Compounds 24 and 27 showed high antibacterial activity against S. aureus and K. pneumoniae with zone of inhibition values of 15 ± 0.82 mm and 18 ± 0.95 mm, respectively.
full_output.methodology: The compounds were synthesized and evaluated for their antibacterial activity using agar well diffusion and micro-broth dilution methods.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified XDR and MDR Aeromonas veronii strains in Mugil seheli carrying resistance genes bla TEM, bla CTX-M, bla SHV, tet A, aad A1, and sul 1.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of virulence and resistance genes, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and pathogenicity tests.

full_output.paper_title: Assessment of the Role of Free-Living and Farmed Fallow Deer (Dama dama) as A Potential Source of Human Infection with Multiple-Drug-Resistant Strains of Yersinia enterocolitica and Yersinia pseudotuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple-drug-resistant Y. enterocolitica strains in free-living and farmed fallow deer, highlighting the potential risk of human infection through consumption of game meat. The ystB gene was found in all isolated strains, contributing to resistance against several antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial sensitivity testing were used to analyze Y. enterocolitica strains.

full_output.paper_title: Detection and Genomic Characterisation of Clostridioides difficile from Spinach Fields.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various antimicrobial resistance genes in C. difficile isolates from spinach and soil samples, including vanB, tet(M), ant(6)-Ia, qacG, cdeA, SAT-4, vanXY, vanR, D19aph(3')-III_1, tet(40), and CDD-1, indicating resistance to vancomycin, tetracyclines, aminoglycosides, disinfectants, fluoroquinolones, nucleosides, and beta-lactams.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing (WGS) and antimicrobial susceptibility testing (E-test) were used to characterize C. difficile isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Computational Design of a Chimeric Vaccine against Plesiomonas shigelloides Using Pan-Genome and Reverse Vaccinology.
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on designing a multi-epitope vaccine against Plesiomonas shigelloides, identifying potential vaccine targets through computational methods. While the paper discusses the antibiotic resistance profile of the pathogen, it does not report any specific AMR genes or mutations characterized in this study.
full_output.methodology: The research employed reverse vaccinology and pan-genome analysis to identify potential vaccine candidates, involving bioinformatics tools for subcellular localization, antigenicity, and epitope prediction.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation and Characterization of Lytic Pseudomonas aeruginosa Bacteriophages Isolated from Sewage Samples from Tunisia.
full_output.key_findings: Four lytic P. aeruginosa phages (vB_Paer_Ps12on-D, vB_Paer_PsCh, vB_Paer_PsIn, and vB_Paer_Ps25) were isolated from Tunisian sewage samples. These phages exhibited broad host ranges, stability under various temperature and pH conditions, and were free of known virulence or antibiotic resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: Phages were isolated from wastewater samples, characterized through whole-genome sequencing, and tested for host range, thermal stability, pH sensitivity, adsorption, and one-step growth assays.
full_output.sample_size: 140 clinical and environmental P. aeruginosa isolates

full_output.paper_title: Isolation and Characterization of Lytic Bacteriophages Active against Clinical Strains of E. coli and Development of a Phage Antimicrobial Cocktail.
full_output.key_findings: Six lytic bacteriophages were isolated from wastewater samples and characterized for their ability to suppress the growth of clinical E. coli strains. A phage cocktail was developed that effectively inhibited the growth of all tested E. coli strains.
full_output.methodology: Bacteriophages were isolated from wastewater, characterized via electron microscopy and genome sequencing, and their lytic activity was assessed against various E. coli strains.

full_output.methodology: PCR detection of virulence genes in MRSA isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Garvicin Q: characterization of biosynthesis and mode of action.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the biosynthesis and mode of action of garvicin Q, a bacteriocin produced by Lactococcus petauri B1726. It identifies the gene cluster garQICD responsible for its production and confirms the requirement of the PTS Man system for its antimicrobial activity.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, heterologous expression in C. glutamicum, purification, and biochemical assays were used to characterize garvicin Q.

full_output.paper_title: Effect of povidone-iodine and propanol-based mecetronium ethyl sulphate on antimicrobial resistance and virulence in Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that PBM-resistant mutants of S. aureus acquired cross-resistance to penicillin, cefoxitin, and ciprofloxacin. Subinhibitory concentrations of PVP-I significantly reduced the expression of several virulence-related genes, including hla, epbs, eno, fib, icaA, and icaD.
full_output.methodology: The study used agar dilution method to determine MIC, Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion for antibiotic susceptibility testing, and qRT-PCR to analyze gene expression.

full_output.paper_title: Co-occurrence of antibiotic and metal resistance in long-term sewage sludge-amended soils: influence of application rates and pedo-climatic conditions.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that urban sewage sludge contains bacterial strains resistant to all tested antibiotics, with varying levels of resistance. It also observed the emergence of a resistome for all tested antibiotics in sludge-amended soils compared to non-treated controls. Additionally, the study identified bacterial isolates showing multiple antibiotic resistance and co-resistance to heavy metals such as cadmium, arsenic, and beryllium.
full_output.methodology: The study used culture-based approaches to enumerate bacteria in urban sewage sludge and soil samples, assessed antibiotic resistance through disc diffusion tests, and evaluated heavy metal resistance using similar methods. Molecular identification of bacterial isolates was done via 16S rDNA sequencing.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes a novel Klebsiella phage PG14 that effectively inhibits and disrupts biofilms of K. pneumoniae G14, showing potential for phage therapy against multidrug-resistant infections.
full_output.methodology: Phage isolation, characterization, genome sequencing, and assessment of antibiofilm activity.

full_output.paper_title: Pharmacokinetic-Pharmacodynamic Target Attainment Analyses as Support for Meropenem-Vaborbactam Dosing Regimens and Susceptibility Breakpoints.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK-PD) target attainment of meropenem-vaborbactam against Enterobacterales, KPC-producing Enterobacterales, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, supporting dosing regimens and susceptibility breakpoints.
full_output.methodology: Population pharmacokinetic models, nonclinical PK-PD targets, in vitro surveillance data, and simulations were used to analyze PK-PD target attainment.

full_output.paper_title: Novel Plasmid Carrying Mobile Colistin Resistance Gene mcr-4.3 and Mercury Resistance Genes in Shewanella baltica: Insights into Mobilization of mcr-4.3 in Shewanella Species.

full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and plasmid analysis were used to identify and characterize the resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: A Pooling Strategy for Detecting Carbapenem Resistance Genes by the Xpert Carba-R Test in Rectal Swab Specimens.

It identified several carbapenemase genes, including bla NDM, bla KPC, bla IMP, bla VIM, and bla OXA-48, which confer resistance to carbapenems.
full_output.methodology: The study used a pooling strategy with the Xpert Carba-R test and compared results with culture and DNA sequence analysis for validation.

full_output.paper_title: Extracellular DNAses Facilitate Antagonism and Coexistence in Bacterial Competitor-Sensing Interference Competition.

full_output.methodology: The research utilized a combination of experimental techniques, including IC50 measurements, competition assays, and computational modeling, to analyze the adaptive evolution of TEM-1 β-lactamase and its resistance mechanisms.

full_output.methodology: The study utilized a combination of in vitro and in vivo assays, transcriptomic analysis, and metabolic labeling to evaluate the activity and mechanism of action of 11726172 against M. tuberculosis.

The increase in AMR was primarily attributed to higher antimicrobial use (AU) and inadequate empiric therapy (IET).

aadA36.genetic_context: The aadA36 gene was located in the chromosome of P. stuartii P14. To gain insight into the genetic environment of aadA36 , the region (approximately 21 kb in length) including the ORF of aadA36 along with the approximately 10 kb upstream and downstream sequences was used as a query to search the NCBI non-redundant nucleotide database. A comparative genomic analysis of the aadA36 encoding region with those of homologous sequences in three other P. stuartii strains and one Providencia sp. strain showed that the IS 200-nemA - aadA36-mnmH -encoding fragment in the P. stuartii P14 chromosome exhibited high similarity with its relatives, and the fragment was flanked by two pairs of 9-bp imperfect inverted repeats (IRs) and one pair of 10-bp imperfect IRs ( Figure 3 ).

full_output.paper_title: Genomic diversity of resistant and virulent factors of Burkholderia pseudomallei clinical strains recovered from Guangdong using whole genome sequencing.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes and mutations in B. pseudomallei clinical strains from Guangdong, including class D beta-lactamases (blaOXA-57 and blaOXA-59), efflux pump components (amrA, amrB, and ceoB), and outer membrane porin omp38. Additionally, mutations in gyrB, bimA, and cheA were detected, contributing to virulence rather than resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and genomic analysis were used to identify AMR genes and mutations in B. pseudomallei strains.

full_output.paper_title: Functional Analysis of Hypothetical Proteins of Vibrio parahaemolyticus Reveals the Presence of Virulence Factors and Growth-Related Enzymes With Therapeutic Potential.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several hypothetical proteins in Vibrio parahaemolyticus that are associated with antibiotic resistance, including MFS transporters, PACE efflux transporter, GNAT family N-acetyltransferases, and VanZ, which confer resistance to multiple antibiotics and glycopeptides.
full_output.methodology: Bioinformatics tools and in silico analysis were used to functionally annotate hypothetical proteins and identify potential antibiotic resistance genes.
full_output.sample_size: Two strains of Vibrio parahaemolyticus (MSR16 and MSR17) isolated from cultured shrimp.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic epidemiological analysis of mcr-1-harboring Escherichia coli collected from livestock settings in Vietnam.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mcr-1 as a significant colistin resistance gene in Escherichia coli isolates from various livestock settings in Vietnam, highlighting its widespread presence and association with multiple antimicrobial resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial resistance phenotyping were used to characterize the AMR genes and mutations in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance and associated genetic background of Histophilus somni isolated from clinically affected and healthy cattle.

blaROB - 1.mechanism: confers resistance to ampicillin and amoxicillin

tetR.mechanism: regulates expression of tetracycline resistance genes

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in Histophilus somni isolates, including bla ROB - 1, aphA-1, strA, strB, tetH, and tetR, which are associated with resistance to ampicillin, amoxicillin, kanamycin, streptomycin, and oxytetracycline. These genes were found in isolates from respiratory diseases and were linked to increased MICs.
full_output.methodology: PCR, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and cephinase disc testing were used to identify AMR genes and assess resistance phenotypes.

vanA.mechanism: confers resistance by modifying peptidoglycan precursors
vanA.validation_method: experimental data generated in this study

vanB.mechanism: confers resistance by modifying peptidoglycan precursors
vanB.validation_method: experimental data generated in this study

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the emergence of vancomycin resistance, particularly focusing on the 'Van cluster' genes such as vanA and vanB, which are responsible for conferring resistance in bacteria like Enterococcus faecalis and Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews existing literature and discusses the mechanisms of vancomycin resistance, including the role of specific genes and their experimental validation.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that co-infections with carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa (CRPA) and multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (MDRA) significantly increased 90-day all-cause mortality in patients with carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE).
full_output.methodology: Retrospective observational study analyzing 4,236 CRE cases from 2015-2020 in the Greater Houston region, focusing on clinical outcomes and co-infections with MDROs.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical and resistance characterization of carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae isolated from intensive care units in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla KPC-2 and bla NDM-1 as the primary carbapenemase genes responsible for carbapenem resistance in CRKP strains from Chinese ICUs. These genes were prevalent across all three hospitals studied.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification and sequencing were used to detect resistance genes and analyze carbapenemase production in CRKP strains.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the antibacterial and antibiofilm properties of UPBNPs-MCSNs composites against Enterococcus faecalis, demonstrating their effectiveness in inducing ferroptosis-like death through the regulation of the bacterial redox pathway ROS/GSH.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized MTT assay, CFU counting, TEM, ROS and LPO detection, and GSH/GSSG level measurement to assess the antibacterial activity and mechanisms of UPBNPs-MCSNs.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of IMP-4 and SFO-1 co-producing ST51 Enterobacter hormaechei clinical isolates.

blaIMP-4.validation_method: PCR, Sanger sequencing, conjugation assay, AST
blaIMP-4.evidence_note: The genetic context surrounding bla IMP-4 was 5′CS- hin-1 -IS 26 -In tI1 - bla IMP-4 -IS 6100 - ecoRII.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the co-production of IMP-4 and SFO-1 in ST51 Enterobacter hormaechei clinical isolates, highlighting the presence of a transferable IncN-type plasmid carrying blaIMP-4 and the genetic context of blaIMP-4 and blaSFO-1.
full_output.methodology: PCR, Sanger sequencing, whole-genome sequencing, conjugation assays, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and phylogenetic analysis.

full_output.paper_title: The antibacterial mechanism of phenylacetic acid isolated from Bacillus megaterium L2 against Agrobacterium tumefaciens.
full_output.key_findings: Phenylacetic acid (PAA) from Bacillus megaterium L2 shows antibacterial activity against Agrobacterium tumefaciens T-37 by disrupting cell membrane integrity, damaging cell structures, affecting cell metabolism, and inhibiting protein synthesis.
full_output.methodology: Experimental methods included determining IC50, assessing cell membrane permeability, analyzing nucleic acid and protein leakage, measuring total soluble sugar concentration, performing SDS-PAGE, evaluating phosphorus metabolism, detecting reactive oxygen species (ROS), and examining key enzyme activities in the tricarboxylic acid cycle.

full_output.paper_title: Evidence for Widespread Class II Microcins in Enterobacterales Genomes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes class II microcins in Enterobacterales genomes, revealing their widespread occurrence and diversity across various species and habitats.
full_output.methodology: A bioinformatics pipeline called cinful was developed to identify putative class II microcins and their associated machinery in bacterial genome assemblies.
full_output.sample_size: 1,224 E. coli isolates, 8,340 genomes from Enterobacterales, Vibrionaceae, and Pasteurellaceae

full_output.paper_title: Pharmacokinetics of Ceftazidime-Avibactam in Combination with Aztreonam (COMBINE) in a Phase 1, Open-Label Study of Healthy Adults.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the pharmacokinetics of ceftazidime-avibactam (CZA) in combination with aztreonam (ATM) in healthy adults, focusing on the effects of CZA-ATM on ATM clearance and liver enzyme elevations. No AMR genes or mutations were characterized in this study.
full_output.methodology: Phase 1, open-label study involving 48 healthy adults, with pharmacokinetic analyses of CZA, AVI, and ATM in plasma and urine.

full_output.paper_title: Worldwide Disseminated IncX4 Plasmid Carrying mcr-1 Arrives to Wild Mammal in Portugal.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first detection of the mcr-1 gene carried by the IncX4 plasmid in a wild mammal, specifically a fallow deer in Portugal, highlighting the spread of colistin resistance in wildlife.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, PCR, and bioinformatics analyses were used to characterize the AMR genes in the E. coli isolate.

full_output.paper_title: Cerium Nitrate Stiffens In Vitro Skin Models and Reduces Pseudomonas aeruginosa Pathogenicity and Penetration Through Skin Models.
full_output.key_findings: Cerium nitrate (CeN) stiffens in vitro skin models and reduces Pseudomonas aeruginosa pathogenicity and penetration through skin models. CeN treatment decreases P. aeruginosa motility, penetration, and virulence, while increasing susceptibility to phagocytosis and antimicrobial agents.
full_output.methodology: In vitro skin models, bacterial cultures, and phagocytosis assays were used to evaluate the effects of CeN on P. aeruginosa and skin models.

full_output.paper_title: The biofilm formation and antibiotic resistance of bacterial profile from endotracheal tube of patients admitted to intensive care unit in southwest of Iran.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high rates of antibiotic resistance among bacterial isolates from endotracheal tubes of ICU patients, with particular emphasis on multidrug-resistant (MDR) and extensively drug-resistant (XDR) strains. Colistin and linezolid were found to be effective against most resistant Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The study involved culturing and susceptibility testing of bacterial isolates from endotracheal tube samples using disk diffusion and MIC methods, along with biofilm formation assessment via crystal violet staining.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of ERIC-PCR and MALDI-TOF as typing tools for multidrug resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae clinical isolates from a tertiary care center in India.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the presence of multiple beta-lactamase genes, including bla TEM, bla CTXM-15, bla OXA, and bla NDM, in multidrug resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates.
full_output.methodology: PCR-based detection of resistance genes and molecular typing techniques such as ERIC-PCR and MALDI-TOF.

full_output.paper_title: Respiratory microorganisms in acute pharyngitis patients: Identification, antibiotic prescription patterns and appropriateness, and antibiotic resistance in private primary care, central Malaysia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified vancomycin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (VRSA) and methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) in patients with acute pharyngitis, highlighting the presence of antibiotic-resistant bacteria in the Malaysian community.
full_output.methodology: The study involved collecting throat swabs from patients, identifying bacteria through MALDI-TOF MS, and performing antibiotic susceptibility testing using Kirby-Bauer and broth microdilution methods.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular epidemiology and clinical characteristics of Clostridioides difficile infection in patients with inflammatory bowel disease from a teaching hospital.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that all C. difficile isolates were susceptible to vancomycin and metronidazole, but there were varying resistance rates to other antibiotics. RT 017 showed higher multidrug resistance compared to other ribotypes.
full_output.methodology: The study involved molecular typing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing of C. difficile isolates from IBD patients.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that fluoroquinolone, sulfonamide, tetracycline, and antibiotic combination therapy use were associated with a significant reduction in MSSA colonization. Conversely, fluoroquinolone use was linked to an increased risk of MRSA colonization.
full_output.methodology: Cross-sectional analysis of NHANES data to evaluate the association between antibiotic use and S. aureus colonization.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization of extraintestinal and diarrheagenic Escherichia coli blood isolates.

mutations_found.protein_change: Aspartic acid to Asparagine at position 87
Glutamic acid to Lysine at position 466

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several acquired resistance genes and mutations in E. coli blood isolates, including mdf(a), dfrA1, aac(6')-Ib-cr, blaOXA-1, sul2, blaCTX-M-15, tet(A), and blaTEM-1B, along with mutations in gyrA, parC, and parE contributing to fluoroquinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing (WGS) was used to analyze 234 E. coli blood isolates, identifying virulence genes and resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of 10 cases of ceftriaxone-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae in the United Kingdom, December 2021 to June 2022.

penA.notes: Nine isolates had the mosaic penA -60.001 allele, and one isolate (Case 9) had the mosaic penA -237.001 allele.

23S_rRNA.notes: Three or four alleles with the 23S rRNA A2059G mutation conferred high-level resistance to azithromycin (MIC > 256 mg/L).

full_output.paper_title: A step forward in antibiotic use and resistance monitoring: a quarterly surveillance system pilot in 11 European Union/European Economic Area countries, September 2017 to May 2020.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the feasibility of a quarterly surveillance system for antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and antimicrobial use (AMU) in the EU/EEA, highlighting significant variability in AMR indicators such as extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli and carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: The study conducted a longitudinal descriptive study collecting data from 11 European countries on AMU and AMR indicators quarterly from September 2017 to May 2020.

full_output.paper_title: Hypermutator strains of Pseudomonas aeruginosa reveal novel pathways of resistance to combinations of cephalosporin antibiotics and beta-lactamase inhibitors.

mexB.notes: Inactivating mutation in the MexAB-OprM efflux pump, potentially driving an evolutionary search for alternative resistance mechanisms.
mexB.evidence_note: The paper states that the MPAO1-mutS Tn strain had an early inactivating mutation in the mexB gene (W753R) and that this mutation was present by the end of the first day of passage in all sequenced isolates.

mexW.notes: Mutation in the MexVW efflux pump operon, contributing to resistance to cephalosporin/beta-lactamase inhibitor combinations.

mexV.notes: The mutation increases resistance to cephalosporins and cephalosporin/beta-lactamase inhibitor combinations.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in the MexVW efflux pump operon as a novel mechanism of resistance to cephalosporin/beta-lactamase inhibitor combinations in hypermutator strains of Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Specifically, the E36K mutation in MexW and the -82:T>C mutation in mexV were shown to increase resistance to several cephalosporin antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, transcriptomic analysis, and susceptibility testing of engineered mutants were used to identify and validate resistance mechanisms in hypermutator strains of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

full_output.paper_title: Expanding the knowledge around antitubercular 5-(2-aminothiazol-4-yl)isoxazole-3-carboxamides: Hit-to-lead optimization and release of a novel antitubercular chemotype via scaffold derivatization.
full_output.key_findings: The study focuses on optimizing the antitubercular activity of 5-(2-aminothiazol-4-yl)isoxazole-3-carboxamides, identifying metabolites and evaluating their activity against Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Key findings include the identification of metabolites resulting from hydroxylation and oxidation of the toluene ring, and the synthesis of derivatives with improved metabolic stability.
full_output.methodology: The study involved in vitro metabolism analysis, synthesis of derivatives, and evaluation of antitubercular activity against Mtb H37Rv.

full_output.paper_title: Screening of global microbiomes implies ecological boundaries impacting the distribution and dissemination of clinically relevant antimicrobial resistance genes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several clinically relevant antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) including mcr-9, mcr-3, blaTEM-1, blaTEM-116, blaOXA-233, blaGES-2, blaGES-15, and blaKPC-2, highlighting their distribution across various biomes and their potential for transmission.
full_output.methodology: The study performed a global metagenomic screening of 17,939 samples to detect and analyze the distribution of ARGs.

full_output.paper_title: Outbreak investigation including molecular characterization of community associated methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus in a primary and secondary school in Eastern Switzerland.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a cluster of community-associated methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (CA-MRSA) in a school in Eastern Switzerland, characterized by ST5 sequence type and efflux-mediated macrolide resistance. The outbreak was linked to a local school, and decolonization efforts successfully reduced the incidence of CA-MRSA cases.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing (WGS) and epidemiological investigation were used to characterize the CA-MRSA outbreak.

full_output.key_findings: The study developed a machine learning model for predicting clonal complexes (CCs) of Streptococcus agalactiae using antibiotic resistance profiles, serotypes, and virulence genes. The model demonstrated high accuracy in classifying CCs, particularly highlighting differences in antibiotic resistance patterns among various CCs.
full_output.methodology: Machine learning models were constructed using antibiotic resistance data, serotyping, and virulence gene profiles to predict clonal complexes of S. agalactiae.

full_output.paper_title: Identification, 16S rRNA-based characterization, and antimicrobial profile of Gallibacterium isolates from broiler and layer chickens.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 69 Gallibacterium isolates from broiler and layer chickens, with 68 being G. anatis and one being Gallibacterium genomospecies. All isolates were susceptible to enrofloxacin, ceftiofur, florfenicol, and gentamicin, while resistance was observed to tylosin, penicillin, erythromycin, clindamycin, novobiocin, tetracycline, oxytetracycline, and sulfathiazole.
full_output.methodology: The study used MALDI-TOF MS, 16S rRNA sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing via broth microdilution.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies CsuA/B, FimA, BauA, and HemTR as potential vaccine candidates against carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii strains, demonstrating their immunogenicity and protective efficacy in murine models.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized PCR, protein expression and purification, and murine immunization experiments to evaluate the protective effects of the identified vaccine candidates.

full_output.paper_title: Detection and characterization of ESBL-producing Escherichia coli and additional co-existence with mcr genes from river water in northern Thailand.

blaCTX-M-15.evidence_note: The paper states that all 38 ESBL isolates contained bla CTX-M, consisting of bla CTX-M-15 (44.7%, 17/38).

blaCTX-M-55.evidence_note: The paper states that bla CTX-M-55 was found in 26.3% of ESBL-producing E. coli isolates.

blaCTX-M-14.evidence_note: The paper states that bla CTX-M-14 was found in 18.4% of ESBL-producing E. coli isolates.

blaTEM-1.evidence_note: The paper mentions that blaTEM-1 was co-harbored with blaCTX-M genes in 23.7% of ESBL-producing E. coli isolates.

mcr-1.1.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and MIC testing

mcr-3.4.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and MIC testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identified ESBL-producing E. coli in river water in northern Thailand, with bla CTX-M-15, bla CTX-M-55, bla CTX-M-14, and bla CTX-M-27 being the most prevalent beta-lactamase genes. Additionally, mcr-1.1 and mcr-3.4 genes were found to confer resistance to colistin. Various other resistance genes were also characterized, including aac(3)-IId, aadA5, ant(3″)-Ia, aph(3″)-Ib, aph(6)-Id, aac(6′)-Ib-cr, qnrS1, mdf(A), erm(B), mph(A), floR, sul2, sul3, tet(A), tet(X), tet(M), dfrA12, dfrA14, dfrA17, cmlA1, catA2, lnu(F), and erm(42).
full_output.methodology: PCR, whole genome sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize the resistance genes and mutations in ESBL-producing E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Determination of Enterococcus faecalis and Enterococcus faecium Antimicrobial Resistance and Virulence Factors and Their Association with Clinical and Demographic Factors in Kenya.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the prevalence of virulence genes gelE, asa1, cylA, esp, and hyl in Enterococcus faecalis and E. faecium isolates in Kenya, highlighting their association with antibiotic resistance and clinical outcomes.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of virulence genes and antimicrobial susceptibility testing using VITEK2 platform.

full_output.paper_title: Antimony resistance mechanism in genetically different clinical isolates of Indian Kala-azar patients.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several genes involved in antimony resistance in Leishmania parasites, including thiol-synthesizing enzymes (CBS, MST, gamma-GCS, ODC, TR), antimony-reducing enzymes (TDR, ACR2), and antimony transporters (AQP1, MRPA, PRP1). These genes show increased expression in antimony-resistant isolates compared to sensitive ones.
full_output.methodology: Gene expression was analyzed using semi-quantitative reverse transcription-PCR.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative genomics analysis of the multidrug-resistant Aeromonas hydrophila MX16A providing insights into antibiotic resistance genes.

ampC.evidence_note: The ampC gene was identified as a class C beta-lactamase in the A. hydrophila MX16A genome, and it is associated with resistance to beta-lactam antibiotics.

aadA.evidence_note: The aadA gene was identified in the A. hydrophila MX16A genome using the CARD database, and it encodes adenylyltransferase, which is involved in aminoglycoside resistance through enzyme inactivation.

gyrA.genetic_context: Mutations in the quinolone resistance-determining regions (QRDRs) of these genes (gyrA, gyrB, parC and parE) result in amino acid substitutions that structurally change the target protein and, subsequently, the drug-binding affinity of the enzyme.
gyrA.evidence_note: The paper states that naturally occurring resistance to fluoroquinolones in gram-negative bacteria is usually due to the genetic mutation of DNA gyrase (encoded by gyrA) and topoisomerase IV (encoded by parC).

bcr.genetic_context: identified from the A. hydrophila MX16A genome
bcr.evidence_note: The bcr gene was identified as a resistance gene in the A. hydrophila MX16A genome through analysis using the CARD database. The gene encodes a transmembrane protein that expels bicyclomycin from the cell, leading to bicyclomycin resistance. Additionally, the gene was found to be involved in sulfathiazole resistance in E. coli.

mutations_found.validated_by: comparison of common mutation sites on the quinolone resistance-determining regions (QRDR) of gyrA and parC genes

gyrA.notes: Mutations in QRDR of gyrA and parC genes contribute to quinolone resistance.

mutations_found.validated_by: comparison of common mutation sites on the quinolone resistance-determining regions (QRDR) of gyrA and parC genes

parC.notes: Mutations in QRDR of gyrA and parC genes contribute to quinolone resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antibiotic resistance genes in Aeromonas hydrophila MX16A, including beta-lactamases, aminoglycoside-modifying enzymes, tetracycline efflux pumps, and quinolone resistance determinants, contributing to its multidrug-resistant phenotype.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and analysis using CARD database, alongside antimicrobial susceptibility testing via Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion.

full_output.paper_title: NO-Based Antimicrobial Strategies for Biofilm Eradication
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses various NO-based strategies for biofilm eradication, focusing on the use of NO donors and their synergistic effects with antibiotics and phototherapy.
full_output.methodology: The study involves the evaluation of NO-releasing agents, their combination with antibiotics, and phototherapy techniques for antibacterial applications.

full_output.paper_title: Beta-lactamase determinants and molecular typing of carbapenem-resistant classic and hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae clinical isolates from southwest of Iran.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several beta-lactamase genes, including bla NDM, bla IMP, bla VIM, bla GES, bla OXA-48-like, bla CTX-M, bla SHV, bla TEM, bla FOX, bla DHA, bla CMY, bla LAT, and bla ACT, which are responsible for carbapenem resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from southwest Iran.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR, sequencing, and antibiotic susceptibility testing to identify and characterize beta-lactamase genes in carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Non-lactose fermenting Escherichia coli: Following in the footsteps of lactose fermenting E. coli high-risk clones.

blaCTX-M-15.evidence_note: The bla CTX-M-15 gene was present in 53% of isolates (9/17) and was associated with resistance to ceftazidime, cefotaxime, ceftazidime, ceftriaxone, cefuroxime, and cefepime.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multidrug-resistant (MDR) non-lactose fermenting Escherichia coli (NLF E. coli) isolates carrying various AMR genes such as bla CTX-M-15, bla NDM-1, aac(6')-Ib-cr, and qnrS1. Mutations in gyrA and parC were associated with fluoroquinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) and in silico analysis were used to characterize AMR genes and mutations in NLF E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance and genomic characterization of Salmonella enterica serovar Senftenberg isolates in production animals from the United States.

full_output.paper_title: Biochemical, genomic and structural characteristics of the Acr3 pump in Exiguobacterium strains isolated from arsenic-rich Salar de Huasco sediments.

full_output.methodology: Cloning of bla CTX-M genes, MIC testing, and molecular analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Commensal bacteria contribute to the growth of multidrug-resistant Avibacterium paragallinarum in chickens.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple AMR genes in multidrug-resistant Avibacterium paragallinarum, including tetB, bla CTX-M-14, bla OXA-1, bla ROB-1, mef(B), ant, aac, and aph, which confer resistance to tetracycline, ampicillin, erythromycin, tylosin, and gentamicin.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and analysis of A. paragallinarum isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Origanum vulgare ethanolic extracts as a promising source of compounds with antimicrobial, anti-biofilm, and anti-virulence activity against dental plaque bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Origanum vulgare ethanolic extract as having significant antimicrobial, anti-biofilm, and anti-virulence properties against dental plaque bacteria, with thymol identified as an active compound.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antimicrobial and anti-biofilm activities of ethanolic extracts from nine Algerian medicinal plants against clinical isolates of Streptococcus, Enterococcus, and Lacticaseibacillus using agar disc diffusion, microtiter plate assays, and biofilm formation assays.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in sediment samples from the Lhasa River, including genes conferring resistance to colistin, beta-lactams, aminoglycosides, macrolides, quinolones, sulfonamides, and tetracyclines. These ARGs were detected using qPCR and were found to be widely distributed in the sediment.
full_output.methodology: The study used 16S rRNA gene sequencing and quantitative PCR (qPCR) to analyze the distribution of antibiotic resistance genes in sediment samples from the Lhasa River.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and WGS-based characteristics of MRSA isolates in hospitals in Shanghai, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various AMR genes in MRSA isolates from hospitals in Shanghai, China, including blaZ, ant(9)-Ia, aac(6′)-aph(2″), erm(A), and tet(M). These genes conferred resistance to antibiotics such as OXA, GEN, ERY, and TET.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing (WGS) was used to analyze antibiotic resistance genes and other molecular characteristics of MRSA isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic and genomic assessment of the potential threat of human spaceflight-relevant Staphylococcus capitis isolates under stress conditions.
full_output.key_findings: All four Staphylococcus capitis strains were found to be resistant to fosfomycin, with no significant differences in antibiotic susceptibility among the strains.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, susceptibility testing, and phenotypic analysis were performed to assess the antimicrobial resistance and characteristics of the strains.

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the prevalence of antimicrobial resistant Salmonella in poultry in the U.S., highlighting resistance to antibiotics such as ceftriaxone, ciprofloxacin, and tetracycline. It notes the decline in Salmonella prevalence and the importance of monitoring AMR in poultry.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews literature and data from the National Antimicrobial Resistance Monitoring System (NARMS) to assess the prevalence and resistance patterns of Salmonella in poultry.
