full_output.methodology: The study involved isolation, phenotypic testing, PCR-based detection of resistance genes, and phylogenetic analysis of E. coli isolates from dogs.

full_output.paper_title: Klebsiella pneumoniae infection in canaries (Serinus canaria Domestica): a case report.
full_output.key_findings: Klebsiella pneumoniae was identified as the causative agent of infection in canaries, showing resistance to several antibiotics including cefazolin, cefixime, ampicillin, erythromycin, chloramphenicol, and florfenicol, while being susceptible to ciprofloxacin and gentamycin.
full_output.methodology: Biochemical tests, PCR, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were conducted to identify and characterize the K. pneumoniae isolate.

full_output.paper_title: Whole genome sequence data of Stenotrophomonas maltophilia SCAID WND1-2022 (370).
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the whole genome sequence of Stenotrophomonas maltophilia SCAID WND1-2022 (370), identifying multiple antibiotic resistance genes including beta-lactamases, efflux pumps, and other multidrug resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, annotation, and analysis using various bioinformatics tools.

full_output.paper_title: Plasmid sequence dataset of multidrug-resistant Enterobacterales isolated from hospital effluents and wastewater treatment plant.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents plasmid sequences of 21 multidrug-resistant Enterobacterales isolates, identifying various AMR genes including beta-lactamases (blaCTX-M-27, blaTEM-1, blaOXA-1, blaCTX-M-15, blaSHV-12, blaCTX-M-30, blaCTX-M-1), aminoglycoside resistance genes (aadA5, aph(3")-Ib, aph(6)-Id, aac(6')-Ib-cr), sulfonamide resistance genes (sul1, sul2), tetracycline resistance gene (tet(A)), macrolide resistance gene (mph(A)), chloramphenicol resistance gene (catB3), folate inhibitors (dfrA17, dfrA14), quinolone resistance gene (qnrB1), and quaternary ammonium compound resistance gene (qacE∆).
full_output.methodology: Plasmid DNA was isolated, sequenced, and analyzed using bioinformatics tools to identify AMR genes.

full_output.paper_title: Identification and Antimicrobial Resistance in Klebsiella spp. Isolates from Turkeys in Poland between 2019 and 2022.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that colistin, neomycin, florfenicol, and amoxicillin/clavulanic acid were the most effective against Klebsiella spp. isolates from turkeys. It also noted a decrease in the number of multi-resistant Klebsiella spp. strains between 2019 and 2021.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing via disk diffusion and identification of Klebsiella spp. using MALDI-TOF.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of Extended-Spectrum β-Lactamase-Resistant Genes in Escherichia coli Isolates from Central China during 2016-2019.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla TEM, bla CTX-M, and bla SHV as the most prevalent ESBL genes in E. coli isolates from chickens in central China, with bla CTX-M being the most common. The study also developed a novel multiplex qPCR method for rapid detection of these genes.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and multiplex qPCR for gene detection and characterization.

full_output.paper_title: Relationships between Virulence Genes and Antibiotic Resistance Phenotypes/Genotypes in Campylobacter spp. Isolated from Layer Hens and Eggs in the North of Tunisia: Statistical and Computational Insights.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes and mutations in Campylobacter isolates from layer hens and eggs in Tunisia, including tet(O), cmeB, erm(B), blaOXA-61, and mutations in gyrA and 23S rRNA. These genes and mutations were associated with resistance to tetracycline, fluoroquinolones, macrolides, and beta-lactams.
full_output.methodology: PCR, MAMA-PCR, and statistical analysis were used to identify AMR genes and mutations in Campylobacter isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Are Enterobacteriaceae and Enterococcus Isolated from Powdered Infant Formula a Hazard for Infants? A Genomic Analysis.

blaACT-7.evidence_note: The paper mentions blaACT-7 in the context of resistance genes detected in Enterobacteriaceae and Enterococcus strains, and it is listed among other resistance genes like AcrAB-TolC, marA, msbA, knpEF, oqxAB, fosA, and others.

blaACT-14.evidence_note: The paper mentions blaACT-14 in the context of resistance genes in Enterobacter hormaechei and Kosakonia cowanii.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antibiotic resistance genes in Enterobacteriaceae and Enterococcus isolates from powdered infant formula, including marA, AcrAB-TolC, aac(6')-Ii, msr(C), bla ACT-7, and bla ACT-14, which confer resistance to various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and genomic analysis were used to identify antibiotic resistance and virulence genes in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Insights into the Mode of Action of Antibacterial Peptides Derived from Chicken Plasma Hydrolysates.
full_output.key_findings: Two novel antibacterial peptides, VSDH and CCCPKAF, were isolated from chicken plasma hydrolysates and showed effective antibacterial activity against Bacillus cereus DMST 5040. VSDH targeted intracellular molecules, while CCCPKAF caused cell membrane disintegration.
full_output.methodology: Antibacterial activity assay, SR-FTIR, molecular docking, and NMR were used to analyze the mode of action of the peptides.

full_output.paper_title: Occurrence of Antibiotic Resistant Bacteria in Flours and Different Plant Powders Used in Cuisine.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of antibiotic-resistant coliform bacteria and enterococci in flour, plant powders, and dough samples. The blaSHV, tetA, and tetE genes were detected in isolates, indicating resistance to ampicillin and tetracycline. Enterococci were less prevalent compared to coliform bacteria and were found only in non-cereal flours.
full_output.methodology: Microbial analysis, PCR detection of resistance genes, and susceptibility testing were conducted.
full_output.sample_size: 60 samples of flours and powders, 13 samples of dough

full_output.paper_title: Characterisation of Listeria monocytogenes Isolates from Hunted Game and Game Meat from Finland.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of fosX and lin genes in all 55 L. monocytogenes isolates, indicating native resistance to fosfomycin and lincosamides. No acquired AMR genes were found, suggesting that the isolates are sensitive to most antimicrobials.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing was used to characterize the genetic diversity, virulence, and antimicrobial resistance genes of L. monocytogenes isolates from hunted game and game meat in Finland.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of Antimicrobial Resistance and Respective Genes among Bacillus spp., a Versatile Bio-Fungicide.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antimicrobial resistance genes in Bacillus spp., including VmiR, ImrB, tetL, mphK, penp, ant-6, and bla OXA, which confer resistance to various antimicrobial classes such as β-lactams, macrolides, lincosamide, tetracycline, and aminoglycosides.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic resistance testing via disk diffusion, molecular typing of AMR genes via PCR, and statistical analysis of correlations between resistance profiles and traits.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiofilm Activity of Sundew Species against Multidrug-Resistant Escherichia coli Strains.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies plumbagin, 7-methyl juglone, 2"-O-galloyl hyperoside, and ellagic acid as compounds with biofilm inhibitory activity against multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli strains.
full_output.methodology: Extraction, fractionation, HPLC quantification, and biofilm inhibition assays were conducted to evaluate the antimicrobial and biofilm inhibitory activities of sundew compounds.

full_output.paper_title: Hemolytic Activity, Cytotoxicity, and Antimicrobial Effects of Silver Nanoparticles Conjugated with Lincomycin or Cefazolin.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that silver nanoparticles conjugated with cefazolin (CEZ) or lincomycin (LCM) exhibit enhanced antimicrobial activity against various bacterial strains, including S. aureus, E. coli, K. pneumoniae, and P. aeruginosa. The conjugation improves the antimicrobial efficacy compared to free antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of silver nanoparticles, functionalization with glutathione or albumin, conjugation with antibiotics, and assessment of antimicrobial activity using disk-diffusion agar tests.

full_output.paper_title: May Sulfonamide Inhibitors of Carbonic Anhydrases from Mammaliicoccus sciuri Prevent Antimicrobial Resistance Due to Gene Transfer to Other Harmful Staphylococci?

full_output.methodology: Recombinant expression, purification, and kinetic analysis of MscCAγ and MscCAβ, along with sulfonamide inhibition profiling.

full_output.paper_title: Effect of the pH on the Antibacterial Potential and Cytotoxicity of Different Plasma-Activated Liquids.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antibacterial effects of various plasma-activated liquids (PALs) against Escherichia coli and their cytotoxicity on mammalian cells. It found that certain PALs, particularly those with low pH, showed significant antimicrobial activity against E. coli without demonstrating cytotoxic effects.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed the physicochemical properties of PALs, including pH, ORP, conductivity, and TDS, and assessed their antimicrobial efficacy against E. coli and cytotoxicity on mammalian cells.

full_output.paper_title: Biological Activity of Picrorhiza kurroa: A Source of Potential Antimicrobial Compounds against Yersinia enterocolitica.
full_output.key_findings: The ethanolic extract of Picrorhiza kurroa showed effective antimicrobial activity against Yersinia enterocolitica, with picroside-1 identified as a potent antimicrobial compound. Picroside-1 was found to lyse Yersinia enterocolitica cells and interact with the dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) protein, suggesting its potential as a drug candidate.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial activity was assessed using agar-well diffusion, MIC, and MBC assays. Picroside-1 was isolated and characterized using LC-MS and NMR. Molecular docking studies were performed to evaluate the interaction of picroside-1 with DHFR.

full_output.key_findings: The study focuses on the activity and synergy of Cu-ATCUN antimicrobial peptides, highlighting their potential to enhance antimicrobial efficacy through various mechanisms, including membrane disruption and intracellular targeting.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antimicrobial activity of various peptides, including SMAP-29 derivatives, indolicidin, tritrpticin, and others, using MIC and FIC assays to assess their synergistic interactions.

full_output.paper_title: New Chalcone-Triazole Hybrids with Promising Antimicrobial Activity in Multidrug Resistance Strains.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified chalcone-triazole hybrids that showed potential to potentiate antibiotic activity and inhibit efflux pumps in multidrug-resistant bacteria, although no specific AMR genes or mutations were characterized in this paper.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis and evaluation of chalcone-triazole hybrids for antimicrobial activity and efflux pump inhibition.

full_output.methodology: High-throughput virtual screening, fluorescence spectroscopy, molecular docking, and in vitro antibacterial assays were used to identify and characterize the inhibitory effects of natural compounds on LolB.

full_output.paper_title: A Modified Vancomycin Molecule Confers Potent Inhibitory Efficacy against Resistant Bacteria Mediated by Metallo-β-Lactamases.
full_output.key_findings: A novel vancomycin derivative, Vb, was developed and showed potent antibacterial activity against multidrug-resistant bacteria, particularly enhancing the efficacy of β-lactam antibiotics against strains producing metallo-β-lactamases (MβLs).
full_output.methodology: Synthesis and characterization of Vb via HPLC and MALDI-TOF MS, along with evaluation of antibacterial activity and synergy with β-lactam antibiotics through MIC assays and time-kill curve experiments.

full_output.methodology: The study utilized UV-Vis spectroscopy, FTIR, XRD, SEM, TEM, and molecular docking to analyze the properties and mechanisms of CuO@OVLe NCs.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes, including aadA1, aadA2, aadA5, aadA12, aac(6')-Ib, and dfrA17, in multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii isolates from aquatic environments in South Africa.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antibiotic sensitivity testing were used to identify and characterize AMR genes in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antibioflm effects of extracellular matrix degradative agents on the biofilm of different strains of multi-drug resistant Corynebacterium striatum.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that multidrug-resistant Corynebacterium striatum isolates exhibited strong biofilm formation abilities, and extracellular matrix degradative agents such as proteinase K, dispersin B, and DNase I effectively reduced biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR to detect spaD, spaE, and spaF genes, PFGE for genotyping, and biofilm degradation assays to evaluate the effects of degradative agents on biofilm formation.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several beta-lactam and phenicol resistance genes, including bla TEM-1, bla SHV, bla CTX-M1-like, bla CMY-2, floR, and cmlA, which were found to be associated with the chicken gut microbiota following amoxicillin and thiamphenicol treatments.
full_output.methodology: 16S rRNA sequencing and quantitative PCR (qPCR) were used to analyze the gut microbiota and the abundance of antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs).

full_output.paper_title: Seasonal hydrological dynamics govern lifestyle preference of aquatic antibiotic resistome.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified seasonal hydrological dynamics as a major driver of antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) profiles in particle-attached (PA) and free-living (FL) fractions in a deep freshwater reservoir. It revealed that PA and FL ARGs responded differently to physicochemical changes caused by vertical mixing and thermal stratification, with PA ARGs being more abundant during mixed seasons and FL ARGs increasing during stratified periods. The research also highlighted the role of mobile genetic elements (MGEs) in ARG dissemination and the influence of environmental factors like dissolved oxygen and nutrients on ARG transitions between PA and FL lifestyles.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput quantitative PCR (HT-qPCR) and 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing were used to analyze ARG profiles in PA and FL fractions across different seasons in the Shuikou Reservoir.

full_output.paper_title: Common recognition topology of mex transporters of Pseudomonas aeruginosa revealed by molecular modelling.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the molecular mechanisms of substrate recognition and transport by MexB, MexF, and MexY transporters in Pseudomonas aeruginosa using molecular dynamics simulations and fragment-based mapping. It identifies conserved and unique binding sites, highlighting the importance of these transporters in multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: The research utilized molecular dynamics simulations, homology modeling, and fragment-based mapping to analyze the structure and function of MexB, MexF, and MexY transporters.

full_output.paper_title: Synergistic and antibiofilm potential of Curcuma aromatica derived silver nanoparticles in combination with antibiotics against multidrug-resistant pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the antibacterial and antibiofilm activity of Curcuma aromatica derived silver nanoparticles (CAAgNPs) against multidrug-resistant (MDR) pathogens, including Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Staphylococcus aureus. CAAgNPs show synergistic effects when combined with antibiotics, enhancing their efficacy against both planktonic and biofilm forms of MDR/XDR pathogens.
full_output.methodology: The study involves the synthesis and characterization of CAAgNPs using aqueous rhizome extract of Curcuma aromatica, followed by evaluation of their antibacterial and antibiofilm activities through MIC, MBC, MBIC assays, biofilm disruption, and fluorescence microscopy. Synergistic effects with antibiotics were assessed via checkerboard assays.

full_output.paper_title: A subtractive proteomics approach for the identification of immunodominant Acinetobacter baumannii vaccine candidate proteins.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 34 unique proteins from drug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii that were specifically captured by patient sera, highlighting potential vaccine candidates. Notably, B0V885 was identified as a highly immunogenic protein with potential for vaccine development.
full_output.methodology: The study used a subtractive proteomics approach involving immunoprecipitation with patient and control sera, followed by LC-MS/MS analysis to identify immunodominant proteins.
full_output.sample_size: 29 infection-positive cases, 13 non-infected patients, and 3 healthy individuals

full_output.paper_title: A nomogram for predicting the risk of mortality in patients with acute pancreatitis and Gram-negative bacilli infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified carbapenem resistance as a significant risk factor for mortality in patients with severe acute pancreatitis (SAP) and Gram-negative bacilli (GNB) infection. A nomogram was developed to predict mortality risk based on clinical variables including septic shock, carbapenem resistance, platelet counts, and hemoglobin levels.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized logistic regression analysis and feature selection to identify risk factors for mortality in patients with SAP and GNB infection, leading to the development of a nomogram for risk prediction.

full_output.paper_title: Novel insights related to the rise of KPC-producing Enterobacter cloacae complex strains within the nosocomial niche.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel conjugative IncM1 plasmid, pDCCK1-KPC, carrying the bla KPC-2 gene, which confers resistance to carbapenems and beta-lactams in KPC-producing Enterobacter hormaechei and Klebsiella pneumoniae strains.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, plasmid conjugation assays, and minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) testing were used to characterize the resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Enhancing activity of β-lactam and fluoroquinolones antibiotics by artemisinin and its derivatives against MDR Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that artemisinin and its derivatives, including dihydroartemisinin (DHA), artesunate (AS), and artemisinic acid (AA), enhanced the activity of β-lactam and fluoroquinolone antibiotics against multidrug-resistant (MDR) Escherichia coli. Specifically, DHA and AA showed significant reductions in MIC values for several antibiotics, indicating improved antibacterial efficacy.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized antibiotic strip tests, Kirby-Bauer disc tests, broth microdilution, and checkerboard assays to evaluate the synergistic effects of artemisinin and its derivatives with antibiotics against E. coli.

full_output.paper_title: Microbiological characteristics and risk factors on prognosis associated with Acinetobacter baumannii bacteremia in general hospital: A single-center retrospective study.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that Acinetobacter baumannii bacteremia has a high drug resistance rate, with carbapenem-resistant A. baumannii (CRAB) being the most common. The survival time of patients with multidrug-resistant (MDR) A. baumannii bacteremia was significantly shorter than that of non-MDR patients. Colistin was the most effective antibiotic against A. baumannii, but its usage was relatively low. Both SOFA and APACHE II scores were effective in predicting the 28-day prognosis of patients with A. baumannii bacteremia.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of antibiotic resistance data from 110 patients with A. baumannii bacteremia, including drug susceptibility testing and survival analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of Escherichia coli and other bacteria isolated from condemned broilers at a Danish abattoir.

full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify AMR genes and mutations in E. coli isolates.

full_output.methodology: The research employed metagenomic sequencing and bioinformatics tools to identify and characterize antibiotic resistance genes and mutations in the Caspian Sea microbial community.
full_output.sample_size: 3 metagenomes from different depths (15 m, 40 m, 150 m)

full_output.paper_title: Oral ciprofloxacin activity against ceftriaxone-resistant Escherichia coli in an in vitro bladder infection model.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes mutations in quinolone resistance-determining regions (QRDRs) of E. coli, including parC_S80I, gyrA_S83L, parE_I529L, gyrA_D87N, qnrS1, and marR_S3N, which contribute to ciprofloxacin resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used a dynamic bladder infection in vitro model to test the effectiveness of various ciprofloxacin dosing regimens against ceftriaxone-resistant E. coli isolates with different ciprofloxacin MICs.

full_output.paper_title: Small-angle x-ray and neutron scattering of MexR and its complex with DNA supports a conformational selection binding model.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the binding of MexR, a MarR family transcriptional regulator, to PII DNA, revealing its conformational changes upon DNA binding and supporting a conformational selection model.
full_output.methodology: The research utilized small-angle x-ray and neutron scattering, along with isothermal titration calorimetry and size-exclusion chromatography coupled with multiangle laser light scattering to analyze the structural and thermodynamic aspects of MexR-DNA interactions.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis and Characterization of GAGO Nanocomposite for Antimicrobial Applications
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the GAGO nanocomposite, composed of graphene oxide (GO) and gallic acid (GA), for its antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus strains, including MRSA and MSSA. GAGO exhibits lower toxicity compared to GA and GO, with effective antibacterial activity at lower concentrations.
full_output.methodology: The study employs in vitro cytotoxicity assays, zebrafish embryo toxicity tests, and antibacterial activity assessments using disk diffusion and time-kill experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Association of CRISPR-Cas System with the Antibiotic Resistance and Virulence Genes in Nosocomial Isolates of Enterococcus.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that the CRISPR-Cas system is associated with reduced antibiotic resistance and virulence in Enterococcus isolates. Specific resistance genes such as ermB, aadE, ant(6), aac(6')-aph(2"), tetM, and vanA were identified in the isolates.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of antibiotic resistance and virulence genes in Enterococcus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Extended-Spectrum Beta-Lactamase and Carbapenem-Resistant Gram-Negative Pathogens in Makkah, Saudi Arabia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high prevalence of ESBL-producing and carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative bacteria (GNB) in ICU patients at King Faisal Hospital in Makkah, Saudi Arabia. ESBL-producing GNB accounted for 20.6% of the samples, while carbapenem-resistant GNB accounted for 79.4%. The most common ESBL-producing organisms were Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae, and the most prevalent carbapenem-resistant organisms were Klebsiella pneumoniae, followed by Acinetobacter baumannii complex/hemolyticus.
full_output.methodology: Cross-sectional study involving 175 GNB isolates from ICU patients, with antimicrobial susceptibility testing performed using the MicroScan automated microbiology system.

full_output.paper_title: Disparate Regions of the Human Chemokine CXCL10 Exhibit Broad-Spectrum Antimicrobial Activity against Biodefense and Antibiotic-Resistant Bacterial Pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: Peptides P1 and P9 derived from CXCL10 exhibit broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity against various antibiotic-resistant bacterial pathogens, including multidrug-resistant and carbapenem-resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: Synthetic peptides were tested for antimicrobial activity using bacterial viability assays and analyzed for structural characteristics using circular dichroism spectroscopy.

full_output.paper_title: Penicillin Binding Protein 7/8 Is a Potential Drug Target in Carbapenem-Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies PBP 7/8 as a crucial target for combating carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii, showing that its loss increases susceptibility to lysozyme and other antimicrobials.
full_output.methodology: Growth experiments, complementation studies, permeability assays, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Resveratrol Increases Sensitivity of Clinical Colistin-Resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa to Colistin In Vitro and In Vivo.
full_output.key_findings: Resveratrol enhances the effectiveness of colistin against colistin-resistant P. aeruginosa by increasing membrane permeability and synergistically reducing bacterial load in vitro and in vivo.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, checkerboard assays, time-kill assays, biofilm formation inhibition, SEM, and in vivo models in G. mellonella and mice.

full_output.paper_title: Experiences from 4 Years of Organization of an External Quality Assessment for Mycobacterium tuberculosis Whole-Genome Sequencing in the European Union/European Economic Area.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes various resistance-associated mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, including those affecting isoniazid, rifampicin, ethambutol, pyrazinamide, streptomycin, fluoroquinolones, bedaquiline, clofazimine, and delamanid. Key mutations include inhA c-15t, embB M306V, panD M117T, pncA A46V and deletion, katG S315T, rpoB S450L, rpsL K43R, gyrA D94G, and others.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) was used to identify and validate resistance-associated mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates.
full_output.sample_size: Participating laboratories: 13 in 2017, 12 in 2018, 14 in 2019, and 15 in 2020.

full_output.key_findings: The study explores the ecological benefits of commensal antibiotic resistance, suggesting that resistant commensals can enhance pathogen clearance and reduce the spread of resistant pathogens in polymicrobial infections.
full_output.methodology: Mathematical modeling and ecological analysis of commensal-pathogen interactions under antibiotic exposure.

full_output.paper_title: Mechanism of Action of Isopropoxy Benzene Guanidine against Multidrug-Resistant Pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: IBG enhances colistin activity against multidrug-resistant pathogens by disrupting bacterial membranes and reducing colistin resistance development.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, time-kill assays, transcriptome and metabolome analysis, and in vivo models.

full_output.paper_title: Clonal Complex 12 Serotype Ib Streptococcus agalactiae Strain Causing Complicated Sepsis in Neonates: Clinical Features and Genetic Characteristics.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the presence of the integrative and conjugative element ICE Sag37 in type Ib ST12 GBS isolates, which carries multiple antibiotic resistance genes such as erm(B), tet(O), aadE, aphA, ant-6, lsa(E), and lun(B), contributing to high resistance rates to erythromycin and clindamycin. Additionally, the virulence gene pezT was found in these isolates.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and PCR were used to characterize the genetic elements and antibiotic resistance genes in the GBS isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the roles of intrinsic and acquired resistance determinants, including oprD, ampC, and oprM, in affecting PBP occupancy and β-lactam efficacy in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: The study used whole-cell PBP binding assays and isogenic knockout mutants to analyze the effects of resistance mechanisms on β-lactam activity.

Horizontal gene transfer of the MEGA element was observed between H. parainfluenzae and H. influenzae.

full_output.paper_title: In Vitro Antimicrobial Activities of Tigecycline, Eravacycline, Omadacycline, and Sarecycline against Rapidly Growing Mycobacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the in vitro activities of four tetracycline antibiotics (tigecycline, eravacycline, omadacycline, and sarecycline) against various rapidly growing mycobacteria (RGM) species, demonstrating their effectiveness with varying MIC levels.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth microdilution method to determine MICs and CFU enumeration for MBCs.

full_output.paper_title: Draft Genomic Sequence for Klebsiella pneumoniae 060517CS3-g, a Bacterium Harboring Multidrug Resistance Genes, Isolated from Retail Ground Chicken Meat.
full_output.key_findings: The draft genomic sequence of Klebsiella pneumoniae 060517CS3-g, isolated from retail ground chicken meat, reveals the presence of six antibiotic resistance genes, including fosA, oqxA, oqxB, tet(D), blaSHV-11, and catA2, indicating multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genomic sequencing and annotation were performed to identify resistance and virulence genes in the isolate.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic Characterization and Heterogeneity among Modern Clinical Isolates of Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies variations in AMR genes such as adeIJK, adeABC, adeFGH, and bap in modern clinical isolates of Acinetobacter baumannii, highlighting the genetic and phenotypic diversity among these isolates compared to established strains.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, phenotypic assays, and database comparisons (VFDB 2022 and MEGARes 2.0) were used to analyze AMR genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Spore-Forming Clostridium (Clostridioides) difficile in Wastewater Treatment Plants in Western Australia.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that C. difficile was commonly present in wastewater treatment plants in Western Australia, with resistance to clindamycin, erythromycin, and tetracycline being relatively frequent. Specific ribotypes such as RT014/020 and RT039 were noted for their resistance profiles.
full_output.methodology: The study involved sampling and culturing of C. difficile from various stages of wastewater treatment processes, followed by antimicrobial susceptibility testing and molecular typing.
full_output.sample_size: 126 influents, 104 effluents, 5 irrigation water samples, and 70 biosolids

full_output.paper_title: Polynucleotide Phosphorylase Mediates a New Mechanism of Persister Formation in Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies polynucleotide phosphorylase (PNPase) as a key regulator of persister formation in Escherichia coli. The pnp gene's wild-type form confers resistance to antibiotics and stresses, and its absence leads to increased susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: The study used genetic knockout and complementation experiments, RNA-seq analysis, and biochemical assays to investigate the role of PNPase in persister formation.

full_output.paper_title: A Temporin Derived Peptide Showing Antibacterial and Antibiofilm Activities against Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies GHa4R, a temporin-derived peptide with potent antibacterial and antibiofilm activities against Staphylococcus aureus, including methicillin-resistant strains. GHa4R exhibits strong bactericidal effects, maintains stability under various conditions, and prevents biofilm formation without inducing resistance.
full_output.methodology: Antibacterial and antibiofilm activities of GHa4R were assessed through MIC, MBC, time-kill kinetics, PI uptake, SEM, and biofilm assays.

full_output.paper_title: A novel virulent Litunavirus phage possesses therapeutic value against multidrug resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel virulent phage, VL1, which effectively targets multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa. VL1 shows high lytic activity against 56% of tested MDR P. aeruginosa strains and demonstrates significant biofilm disruption and therapeutic potential in a Galleria mellonella infection model.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, plaque assays, biofilm disruption experiments, and in vivo infection models in Galleria mellonella larvae were used to evaluate the phage's characteristics and therapeutic potential.

full_output.paper_title: High prevalence of antimicrobial resistance and multidrug resistance among bacterial isolates from diseased pets: Retrospective laboratory data (2015-2017).
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the high prevalence of antimicrobial resistance and multidrug resistance among bacterial isolates from diseased pets, particularly Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus pseudintermedius, and Klebsiella pneumoniae, with notable resistance rates to antibiotics such as doxycycline, tetracycline, cephalexin, and fluoroquinolones.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of antibiotic susceptibility testing data from veterinary diagnostic laboratories.

full_output.paper_title: Novel configurations of type I-E CRISPR-Cas system in Corynebacterium striatum clinical isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies novel configurations of the type I-E CRISPR-Cas system in Corynebacterium striatum clinical isolates, including a divergent gene arrangement termed type I-E'.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis and CRISPR-Cas system characterization using bioinformatics tools and phylogenetic analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of the in vitro activity of ceftaroline, ceftazidime/avibactam and comparator antimicrobial agents against clinical isolates from paediatric patients in Kuwait: ATLAS data 2012-19.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the in vitro activity of ceftaroline, ceftazidime/avibactam, and other antimicrobial agents against clinical isolates from paediatric patients in Kuwait. It found that ceftaroline was effective against most Gram-positive isolates, including resistant phenotypes, and ESBL-negative Enterobacterales. Ceftazidime/avibactam showed high susceptibility rates against Enterobacterales, including ESBL-positive isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study used CLSI broth microdilution method to determine antimicrobial susceptibility and molecular techniques to detect ESBL genes.
full_output.sample_size: 515 Enterobacterales isolates, 111 P. aeruginosa isolates, 449 S. aureus isolates, 168 S. pneumoniae isolates, and 90 S. pyogenes isolates

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic and genotypic characterization of metallo-β-lactamase producing Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolated from burn patients.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaVIM and blaIMP genes in imipenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from burn patients, highlighting the prevalence of metallo-β-lactamase production.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR, and phenotypic detection of MβL enzymes.

full_output.key_findings: BacARscan is an in silico tool designed to detect, predict, and characterize antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in -omics datasets, including short sequencing reads and fragmented contigs. It outperforms existing methods in terms of precision and F-measure, demonstrating effectiveness in identifying ARGs in both protein and gene datasets.
full_output.methodology: BacARscan uses profile Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) built from curated antibiotic resistance proteins and gene sequences. It was evaluated using various datasets, including positive and negative protein sequences, short reads, and metagenomic data.

full_output.paper_title: In Situ Sprayed Biotherapeutic Gel Containing Stable Microbial Communities for Efficient Anti-Infection Treatment.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports an in situ-formed biotherapeutic gel containing stable microbial communities (kombucha) that exhibits broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity against various pathogens, including multidrug-resistant bacteria. The gel shows superior efficacy in pathogen removal and wound healing compared to conventional antibacterial gels.
full_output.methodology: The study characterizes the antimicrobial properties of kombucha through in vitro assays, including agar disk diffusion, bacterial growth inhibition, and biofilm disruption. The biotherapeutic gel was evaluated for its performance in wound healing models.

full_output.paper_title: Exploring the in situ evolution of nitrofurantoin resistance in clinically derived uropathogenic Escherichia coli isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies loss-of-function mutations in the nitroreductase genes nfsA and nfsB as the primary mechanisms of nitrofurantoin resistance in uropathogenic E. coli. Specifically, a T37M point mutation in nfsA and a complete deletion of nfsB were found to confer resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation, MIC assays, and growth curve analyses were used to characterize the resistance mechanisms.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that Pseudomonas putida isolates exhibited high resistance rates to certain antibiotics, including aztreonam, levofloxacin, and ciprofloxacin, while remaining sensitive to colistin, amikacin, and meropenem.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation, Identification, and Genetic Characterization of Antibiotic Resistance of Salmonella Species Isolated from Chicken Farms.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in Salmonella isolates from chicken farms in Egypt, including blaTEM, blaSHV, ermB, ereA, and mphA, which conferred resistance to ampicillin, erythromycin, and lincomycin.

full_output.paper_title: Sepsis Due to Pandoraea sputorum Infection After Multiple Trauma in a Non-Cystic Fibrosis Patient: A Case Report from Southeast China.

full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing using the Vitek2 compact system and molecular identification via 16S rRNA PCR and MALDI-TOF MS.

full_output.paper_title: Increased zinc levels facilitate phenotypic detection of ceftazidime-avibactam resistance in metallo-β-lactamase-producing Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several metallo-beta-lactamase genes (blaIMP-1, blaNDM-1, blaNDM-5, blaVIM-1, blaVIM-2, and blaVIM-4) that confer resistance to ceftazidime-avibactam in various Gram-negative bacteria. It highlights the importance of zinc supplementation in improving the detection of ceftazidime-avibactam resistance in metallo-beta-lactamase-producing isolates.
full_output.methodology: PCR, Sanger sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize the metallo-beta-lactamase genes.

full_output.paper_title: The combination effect of meropenem/sulbactam/polymyxin-B on the pharmacodynamic parameters for mutant selection windows against carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the bla OXA-23 gene as a significant factor in carbapenem resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii, demonstrating its role in conferring resistance to meropenem and polymyxin-B.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized MIC testing and pharmacodynamic analysis to evaluate the resistance mechanisms in carbapenem-resistant A. baumannii isolates.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro antimicrobial activity and resistance mechanisms of the new generation tetracycline agents, eravacycline, omadacycline, and tigecycline against clinical Staphylococcus aureus isolates.

mepB.mechanism: frameshift mutation contributes to reduced omadacycline susceptibility
mepB.validation_method: cloning in E. coli DH5α and MIC testing

mepB.notes: Frameshift mutation in mepB was associated with reduced susceptibility to omadacycline.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified tetracycline resistance genes tet(K), tet(L), and tet(M) and a frameshift mutation in mepB contributing to reduced susceptibility to omadacycline in Staphylococcus aureus isolates.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, cloning, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Increased carbapenemase testing following implementation of national VA guidelines for carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE).
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the increase in carbapenemase testing for carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) following the implementation of national VA guidelines. KPC was the most frequently detected carbapenemase, followed by NDM and OXA-48.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective cohort study analyzing data from VA corporate data warehouse to evaluate trends in carbapenemase testing and detection.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial activity of metal-phenanthroline complexes against multidrug-resistant Irish clinical isolates: a whole genome sequencing approach.

various mutations in cellular respiration, polyamine biosynthetic pathway, and virulence mechanisms

full_output.key_findings: The study identified various mutations in the P. aeruginosa genome that conferred resistance to metal-phenanthroline complexes, affecting cellular respiration, polyamine biosynthesis, and virulence mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing was used to analyze mutations in P. aeruginosa strains exposed to metal-phenanthroline complexes.
full_output.sample_size: Multiple clinical isolates from Irish hospitals

full_output.paper_title: Peptide Stability Is Important but Not a General Requirement for Antimicrobial and Antibiofilm Activity In Vitro and In Vivo.
full_output.key_findings: The study compares the stability and antimicrobial activity of two peptides, GF-17 and 17BIPHE2, derived from human LL-37. It finds that 17BIPHE2 is more stable to proteases and human serum, and more effective in disrupting preformed biofilms of MRSA and other bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluates peptide stability through HPLC, assesses antimicrobial activity using MIC assays, and tests antibiofilm effects in in vitro and in vivo models.

full_output.paper_title: Synergistic antibacterial activity of baicalin and EDTA in combination with colistin against colistin-resistant Salmonella.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mcr-1 as a gene responsible for colistin resistance in Salmonella and demonstrates that the combination of baicalin and EDTA can inhibit mcr-1 expression and restore colistin susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: Antibacterial tests, checkerboard assays, time-kill studies, transcriptomic analysis, RT-PCR, molecular docking, and mouse infection models.

full_output.paper_title: Suicidal chemotaxis in bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: Pseudomonas aeruginosa exhibits suicidal chemotaxis towards antibiotics, moving towards high concentrations and subsequently lysing to release bacteriocins, suggesting a counter-attack behavior against competitors.
full_output.methodology: Microfluidic devices and automated cell tracking were used to analyze bacterial movement in antibiotic gradients.

full_output.paper_title: Whole genome sequencing reveals new links between spa t172/CC59 methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus cases in low-endemicity region of Southwest Finland, 2007‒2016.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified spa t172/CC59 methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) cases in Southwest Finland, highlighting the molecular epidemiology and transmission dynamics of this strain. Whole genome sequencing (WGS) revealed genetic clusters and provided insights into the spread of t172 MRSA in both healthcare and community settings.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing (WGS) was used to analyze 64 t172 MRSA isolates, along with epidemiological data, to investigate the molecular epidemiology and transmission patterns of the strain.

full_output.paper_title: Wastewater-based surveillance in Italy leading to the first detection of mcr-10-positive Klebsiella quasipneumoniae.

mcr-10.genetic_context: An insertion sequence (IS5 family) was located further upstream.
mcr-10.evidence_note: The mcr-10 gene was found in strains of Klebsiella quasipneumoniae isolated from samples of human raw sewage.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first detection of the mcr-10 gene in Italy, found in Klebsiella quasipneumoniae strains isolated from wastewater samples, highlighting the importance of wastewater-based surveillance for detecting emerging antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.methodology: Wastewater sampling, PCR, sequencing, and bioinformatic analysis were used to identify and characterize the mcr-10 gene.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence, antimicrobial resistance, and staphylococcal toxin genes of bla(TEM-1a)-producing Staphylococcus aureus isolated from animals in Chongqing, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla TEM-1a as a prevalent gene in Staphylococcus aureus isolates from animals in Chongqing, China, contributing to resistance against penicillin and ampicillin.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Activating alternative transport modes in a multidrug resistance efflux pump to confer chemical susceptibility.

emre.mechanism: confers susceptibility to harmane through uncoupled proton transport
emre.validation_method: in vitro electrophysiology assays and bacterial growth assays

emrE.mechanism: mediates proton leak and efflux of toxic cations

full_output.key_findings: EmrE, a small multidrug resistance efflux pump from E. coli, can confer susceptibility to harmane through uncoupled proton transport, demonstrating that alternative transport modes can be activated to disrupt bacterial metabolism and growth.
full_output.methodology: In vitro electrophysiology assays, NMR spectroscopy, and bacterial growth assays were used to investigate the role of EmrE in harmane susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Characterization of Salmonella spp. Isolates from Wild Colombian Babilla (Caiman crocodilus fuscus) Isolated In Situ.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antibiotic resistance genes in Salmonella isolates from wild Colombian babilla, including blaTEM, strB, sul1, blaCMY2, blaCTX-M, sul2, dfrA1, floR, and qnrD, indicating the potential of these reptiles as carriers of multidrug-resistant bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Endpoint PCR was used to detect the presence of antibiotic resistance and virulence genes in Salmonella isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Analysis of Gut Microbial Communities and Resistance Genes in Pigs and Chickens in Central China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antibiotic resistance genes in the gut microbiota of pigs and chickens in central China, including tetW, lnuA, mdtB, and others, indicating the presence of multidrug resistance in these animals.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic sequencing was used to analyze the gut microbial communities and identify resistance genes in fecal samples from pigs and chickens.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic Relationship between Salmonella Isolates Recovered from Calves and Broilers Chickens in Kafr El-Sheikh City Using ERIC PCR.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the blaTEM gene as a determinant of beta-lactam resistance in multidrug-resistant Salmonella isolates from calves and broiler chickens in Egypt.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of blaTEM gene and class 1 integron, ERIC PCR for genetic relationship analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Effects of Oxytetracycline/Lead Pollution Alone and in the Combined Form on Antibiotic Resistance Genes, Mobile Genetic Elements, and Microbial Communities in the Soil.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that the application of oxytetracycline (OTC) and lead (Pb) altered the abundance of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) and mobile genetic elements (MGEs) in soil. Specifically, the genes tetB, sul1, sul2, sul3, intl1, intl2, and tetQ were identified as being affected by OTC and Pb pollution.
full_output.methodology: The study used qPCR to quantify the abundance of ARGs and MGEs in soil samples exposed to different concentrations of OTC and Pb.

full_output.paper_title: Transcriptome Analysis of Acinetobacter baumannii in Rapid Response to Subinhibitory Concentration of Minocycline.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified differentially expressed genes and sRNAs in Acinetobacter baumannii in response to subinhibitory concentrations of minocycline, including upregulation of RtcB family protein and ABC transporter ATP-binding protein, and downregulation of class C beta-lactamase ADC-158, chaperonin GroL, and molecular chaperone GroES.
full_output.methodology: RNA-seq and qRT-PCR were used to analyze the transcriptome of A. baumannii under minocycline stress.

full_output.paper_title: Phage-Based Control of Methicillin Resistant Staphylococcus aureus in a Galleria mellonella Model of Implant-Associated Infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the effectiveness of the bacteriophage Sb-1 in controlling and preventing methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) colonization on stainless steel K-wires in a Galleria mellonella model. Sb-1 significantly reduced bacterial counts compared to untreated controls and showed comparable efficacy to vancomycin in preventing infection.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a Galleria mellonella larval infection model to assess the efficacy of Sb-1 phage and daptomycin in reducing MRSA colonization on K-wires. Colony counts and statistical analyses were performed to evaluate the outcomes.

full_output.paper_title: An Improved Real-Time Viability PCR Assay to Detect Salmonella in a Culture-Independent Era.
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on optimizing a viability PCR (vPCR) protocol using PMAxx™ to detect Salmonella Enteritidis, aiming to minimize false positives and negatives. Key findings include the effectiveness of a 100 μM PMAxx™ concentration in eliminating 10^8 CFU/mL heat-killed cells and the importance of a tube change after photoactivation to prevent residual PMAxx™ effects on live cells.
full_output.methodology: The study involved optimizing PMAxx™ treatment conditions, evaluating its effects on live and heat-killed cells, and testing different protocols to improve vPCR accuracy.

full_output.paper_title: Effect and Mechanism Analysis of Pig FUT8 Gene on Resistance to Escherichia coli F18 Infection.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: inhibited the transcriptional binding activity of C/EBPα

FUT8.notes: The 1 bp C base insertion mutation at the -774 bp region of the FUT8 promoter was found to inhibit the transcriptional binding activity of C/EBPα, leading to decreased FUT8 expression and increased resistance to E. coli F18.
FUT8.evidence_note: The 1 bp C base insertion mutation at the -774 bp region of the FUT8 promoter was found to inhibit the transcriptional binding activity of C/EBPα, leading to decreased FUT8 expression and increased resistance to E. coli F18.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified a 1 bp C base insertion mutation in the FUT8 promoter region that inhibits C/EBPα binding, reducing FUT8 expression and enhancing resistance to E. coli F18 in pigs.
full_output.methodology: The study used RT-qPCR, Western blot, luciferase assays, and promoter analysis to investigate the role of FUT8 in E. coli F18 resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Transcriptomic and proteomic analysis of Streptomyces coelicolor and Streptomyces lividans under phosphate limitation and proficiency
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies various transcriptional regulators and sensory histidine kinases involved in the response to phosphate limitation and proficiency in Streptomyces coelicolor and Streptomyces lividans.
full_output.methodology: The study uses proteomic and transcriptomic analysis to identify differentially abundant proteins under varying phosphate conditions.

full_output.paper_title: Polyenic Antibiotics and Other Antifungal Compounds Produced by Hemolytic Streptomyces Species.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several polyene and non-polyene antibiotics produced by hemolytic Streptomyces species, including novel compounds such as polyene A, B, C, and D, along with actiphenol. These compounds exhibit antifungal activity against various fungi.
full_output.methodology: The research utilized LC-MS analysis, hemolytic activity testing, and antifungal activity assays to characterize the secondary metabolites produced by Streptomyces strains.

full_output.paper_title: Design, Synthesis and Antimicrobial Properties of New Tetracyclic Quinobenzothiazine Derivatives.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes the synthesis and evaluation of new tetracyclic quinobenzothiazine derivatives with potent antimicrobial activity against a range of bacterial and mycobacterial strains, including multidrug-resistant isolates. Compounds 6j, 6a, and 6d exhibited high activity against the tested microbial spectrum.
full_output.methodology: Chemical synthesis, structural analysis via NMR and X-ray, and in vitro antimicrobial and cytotoxicity testing.

full_output.paper_title: Trifluoromethylcinnamanilide Michael Acceptors for Treatment of Resistant Bacterial Infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several trifluoromethylcinnamanilide derivatives with antibacterial and antimycobacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus, Enterococcus faecalis, Mycobacterium smegmatis, and Mycobacterium marinum. Compounds 1j, 1o, 2i, and 2p exhibited strong activity against all tested microorganisms.
full_output.methodology: In vitro antimicrobial activity testing, MTT assay, and docking studies were conducted to evaluate the compounds' effectiveness and mechanism of action.

full_output.paper_title: Structural Basis of Cysteine Ligase MshC Inhibition by Cysteinyl-Sulfonamides.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies cysteinyl-sulfonamide compounds that inhibit MshC, a critical enzyme in Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) mycothiol biosynthesis. Two compounds, 7b and 7d, show binding affinity to MshC, with EC50 values of 219 and 231 µM, respectively. The compounds induce conformational changes in MshC, providing insights into their mechanism of action.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized thermal shift assays, X-ray crystallography, and biochemical analyses to evaluate the binding and inhibitory effects of cysteinyl-sulfonamide compounds on MshC.

full_output.paper_title: Selectively Halogenated Flavonolignans-Preparation and Antibacterial Activity.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that certain halogenated flavonolignans can modulate antibiotic resistance in bacteria, particularly reversing the resistant phenotype of S. aureus to a sensitive one. However, no specific AMR genes or mutations were experimentally characterized in this paper.
full_output.methodology: Chemical synthesis and biological activity testing of halogenated flavonolignans.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis, Biological Evaluation and Computational Studies of New Hydrazide Derivatives Containing 1,3,4-Oxadiazole as Antitubercular Agents.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis and evaluation of new hydrazide derivatives containing a 1,3,4-oxadiazole core as antitubercular agents. Five compounds showed high antimycobacterial activity against M. tuberculosis H37Ra, and two were effective against pyrazinamide-resistant strains. However, no AMR genes or mutations were characterized in this paper.
full_output.methodology: Chemical synthesis, antimycobacterial activity testing, cytotoxicity assessment, and molecular modeling.

full_output.paper_title: Occurrence and Variability of the Efflux Pump Gene norA across the Staphylococcus Genus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the widespread occurrence of the norA gene across the Staphylococcus genus and highlights the variability of norA alleles, particularly norAI and norAII, which are prevalent in S. aureus strains. It also demonstrates the applicability of a PCR-based algorithm for rapid detection and differentiation of norA alleles.
full_output.methodology: PCR-based allele screening, sequencing, and phylogenetic analysis were used to characterize norA gene variability and its association with S. aureus clonal lineages.

full_output.paper_title: Mechanism of Synergy between Piceatannol and Ciprofloxacin against Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that piceatannol (PIC) enhances the antibacterial effect of ciprofloxacin (CIP) against Staphylococcus aureus by dissipating the bacterial proton motive force (PMF), particularly the ∆ψ component, and reducing ATP synthesis. PIC also exhibits low resistance development potential.
full_output.methodology: The study used MIC, MBC, time-killing assays, membrane permeability assays, PMF assays, ATP assays, and resistance induction tests to evaluate the antibacterial activity and mechanisms of PIC and CIP.

full_output.paper_title: Biocidal Activity of Tannic Acid-Prepared Silver Nanoparticles towards Pathogens Isolated from Patients with Exacerbations of Chronic Rhinosinusitis.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the biocidal activity of tannic acid-prepared silver nanoparticles (TA-AgNPs) against pathogens isolated from patients with acute exacerbations of chronic rhinosinusitis (AECRS). TA-AgNPs showed varying minimal inhibitory concentrations (MIC) against different bacterial isolates, with some isolates demonstrating resistance at non-toxic concentrations for human cells.
full_output.methodology: The study used the well diffusion method to determine MIC values of TA-AgNPs against clinical isolates and reference strains. Cytotoxicity was assessed using MTT and trypan blue exclusion assays.

full_output.paper_title: Effects of EOs vs. Antibiotics on E. coli Strains Isolated from Drinking Waters of Grazing Animals in the Upper Molise Region, Italy.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a total absence of microbial resistance in 23 E. coli strains isolated from drinking waters of grazing animals in the Upper Molise region, Italy.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antibacterial activity of essential oils (EOs) and antibiotics against 23 E. coli strains using agar diffusion methods.

full_output.paper_title: Development and Validation of a Method for Determination of 43 Antimicrobial Drugs in Western-Style Pork Products by UPLC-MS/MS with the Aid of Experimental Design.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed and validated a method for determining 43 antimicrobial drugs in Western-style pork products using UPLC-MS/MS with a modified QuEChERS method. The method successfully detected sulfadiazine and moxifloxacin in actual samples.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a modified QuEChERS method combined with UPLC-MS/MS for the determination of antimicrobial drugs in pork products.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis and Characterization of Colistin-Functionalized Silica Materials for Rapid Capture of Bacteria in Water.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a novel colistin-functionalized silica material (SiO2@NH2@COOH@CST) designed for the rapid capture of bacteria, particularly Gram-negative bacteria, through electrostatic interactions.
full_output.methodology: The material was synthesized through a series of chemical modifications involving amino and carboxyl groups on silica, followed by characterization using techniques such as SEM, TEM, FT-IR, and zeta potential measurements.

full_output.paper_title: Natural Products Targeting Type III Secretion Systems (T3SS) in Pathogenic Bacteria
full_output.key_findings: This paper identifies several natural products that inhibit the type III secretion system (T3SS) in pathogenic bacteria, including caminoside A, caminoside B, cytosporone B, piericidin A1, fusaric acid, (-)-hopeaphenol, sanguinarine chloride, thymol, carvacrol, syringaldehyde, paeonol, cinnamaldehyde, baicalin, quercetin, epigallocatechin-3-gallate, licoflavonol, naringenin, rhusflavanone, mesuaferrone B, myricetin, obacunone, limonin, divergolide R, divergolide S, tanshinone, myricanol, and tannic acid. These compounds inhibit T3SS by various mechanisms, such as blocking effector protein secretion, reducing gene transcription, and interfering with regulatory pathways.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a combination of biological tests, structure-activity studies, reporter gene assays, phosphatase assays, in vivo and in vitro experiments, and molecular biology techniques to evaluate the T3SS inhibitory activity of the natural products.

full_output.paper_title: Indonesian Mangrove Sonneratia caseolaris Leaves Ethanol Extract Is a Potential Super Antioxidant and Anti Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus Drug.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies azelaic acid, aspirin, isorvitexin, and quercitrin as potential antibacterial compounds in the ethanol extract of Sonneratia caseolaris leaves, showing significant antioxidant and anti-MRSA activity.
full_output.methodology: Phytochemical analysis, DPPH radical scavenging assay, brine shrimp lethality test, agar disk-diffusion assay, and LC-MS/MS for compound characterization.

PBP-14.mechanism: mutant penicillin-binding protein that confers resistance to β-lactams

full_output.key_findings: The study identified a mutant penicillin-binding protein (PBP-14) that confers resistance to β-lactams through structural modifications, enhancing resistance by 19.86% compared to the original PNC.
full_output.methodology: Molecular docking, mutagenesis, and computational modeling were used to analyze resistance mechanisms and optimize β-lactam substitutes.

full_output.paper_title: Purification and Characterization of Novel Anti-MRSA Peptides Produced by Brevibacillus sp. SPR-20.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies P1, a novel antimicrobial peptide produced by Brevibacillus sp. SPR-20, which exhibits potent anti-MRSA activity with a MIC of 2 μg/mL against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus strains.
full_output.methodology: Purification of anti-MRSA substances via ammonium sulfate precipitation, cation-exchange chromatography, and reversed-phase chromatography, followed by characterization using LC-MS/MS and assessment of antimicrobial activity via microdilution method.

full_output.paper_title: O(2) Carrier Myoglobin Also Exhibits β-Lactamase Activity That Is Regulated by the Heme Coordination State.

mb.mechanism: catalytic hydrolysis of the β-lactam ring

full_output.key_findings: Myoglobin (Mb) exhibits β-lactamase activity by catalyzing the hydrolysis of ampicillin, and this activity is regulated by the heme coordination state.
full_output.methodology: HPLC, ESI-MS, and E. coli growth experiments were used to assess the β-lactamase activity of Mb.

full_output.paper_title: The Anti-Multidrug-Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii Study on 1,3-diamino-7H-pyrrolo[3,2-f]quinazoline Compounds.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies 1,3-diamino-7H-pyrrolo[3,2-f]quinazoline (PQZ) compounds, particularly OYYF-171, -172, and -175, as potent inhibitors of Acinetobacter baumannii DHFR, showing strong antibacterial activity against both antibiotic-susceptible and multidrug-resistant (MDR) strains. These compounds exhibit significant synergy with sulfamethoxazole (SMZ) in inhibiting A. baumannii growth.
full_output.methodology: Molecular modeling, in vitro antibacterial activity testing, time-killing assays, and synergy tests were conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of PQZ compounds against A. baumannii.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of Colletotrichum spp. Resistant to Benomyl by Using Molecular Techniques.

β-tubulin.notes: observed in 5 isolates of C. gloeosporioides s. lat.
β-tubulin.evidence_note: The paper states that the GCG (alanine) codon at the 198th amino acid position of five isolates of C. gloeosporioides s. lat. conferred resistance to benomyl.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified a point mutation at the 198th amino acid position of the β-tubulin gene in five isolates of C. gloeosporioides s. lat., which conferred resistance to benomyl. Molecular techniques such as allele-specific PCR and PCR-RFLP were developed for rapid detection of this resistance.
full_output.methodology: Agar dilution method, gene sequencing, allele-specific PCR, and PCR-RFLP were used to detect benzimidazole resistance in Colletotrichum isolates.
full_output.sample_size: 24 isolates of Colletotrichum acutatum s. lat. and Colletotrichum gloeosporioides s. lat.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies AMR genes blaADC-18 and blaOXA-500 in ISS-associated A. pittii strains, along with the transcriptional repressor lexA, which may contribute to enhanced resistance mechanisms in the extreme ISS environment.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, phylogenetic analysis, and genome-wide association studies were used to analyze AMR genes and mutations in A. pittii strains from the ISS and Earth.

full_output.paper_title: The global distribution and environmental drivers of the soil antibiotic resistome.

fox5.evidence_note: The paper mentions that fox5 is a beta-lactamase gene and one of the most dominant ARGs in global soils.

oprJ.evidence_note: The paper mentions that oprJ is part of multidrug resistance genes and efflux pump machineries, but does not provide direct evidence that oprJ confers resistance to specific drugs or that it is experimentally characterized as an AMR gene.

oprD.evidence_note: The paper mentions that oprD is part of the multidrug resistance genes and efflux pump machineries, but does not provide direct evidence that oprD confers resistance to specific drugs or that it is experimentally characterized as a resistance gene.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies 14 dominant and ubiquitous antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in global soils, including the beta-lactamase gene fox5 and multidrug resistance genes oprJ, oprD, and acrA-05. These genes are prevalent in various biomes and are associated with multidrug resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized high-throughput quantitative PCR to analyze the relative abundance of 285 ARGs and 10 MGEs across 1012 soil samples from diverse ecosystems.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial properties of a multi-component alloy.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the antimicrobial properties of a multi-component alloy composed of copper, silver, nickel, and cobalt, demonstrating significant antimicrobial activity against various microorganisms, including bacteriophages and bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The study used combinatorial sputtering to create thin-film alloys and tested their antimicrobial activity against surrogate microorganisms.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance and molecular epidemiological analysis of Escherichia fergusonii harboring the mcr gene in pigs and broiler chickens in Okinawa, Japan.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mcr-1 and mcr-5 genes in Escherichia fergusonii isolates from pigs and chickens in Okinawa, Japan, which conferred resistance to colistin. The mcr-1 gene was found in all isolates, while mcr-5 was present in one isolate. The IncI2 plasmid was implicated in the transfer of the mcr-1 gene.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PFGE, conjugation tests, and PCR-based replicon typing were used to analyze the resistance mechanisms and transmission of mcr-harboring E. fergusonii.

full_output.paper_title: Impact of fluoroquinolones and aminoglycosides on P. aeruginosa virulence factor production and cytotoxicity.
full_output.key_findings: Tobramycin reduced T3SS expression and secretion of ExoU and ExoS in P. aeruginosa, while fluoroquinolones increased T3SS expression and toxin secretion.
full_output.methodology: Western blotting, RT-qPCR, and cytotoxicity assays were used to analyze the effects of antibiotics on T3SS expression and virulence factor production.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of phenotypic and genotypic antimicrobial resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified specific SNPs in genes associated with isoniazid resistance (katG, inhA, fabG1, kasA) and rifampicin resistance (rpoB, rpoC) in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, demonstrating the emergence of genotypic resistance under varying drug concentrations.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing of samples from static kill curve experiments to analyze the emergence of genotypic and phenotypic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: How to survive pig farming: Mechanism of SCCmec element deletion and metabolic stress adaptation in livestock-associated MRSA.

clpB.encodes: ATPase subunit of an ATP-dependent protease ClpB

ctsR.encodes: class III stress genes transcriptional repressor

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies resistance genes in MRSA ST398, including aadD, fexA, blaZ, dfrG, tet(K), tet(M), lnu(B), and lsa(E), and characterizes the loss of a complete SCC mec Vc element in an MSSA derivative.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, transcriptomic analysis, and bioinformatic comparisons were used to identify resistance genes and characterize genetic changes in MRSA ST398.

full_output.paper_title: Formic acid, an organic acid food preservative, induces viable-but-non-culturable state, and triggers new Antimicrobial Resistance traits in Acinetobacter baumannii and Klebsiella pneumoniae.

ompH.notes: Upregulation of ompH contributes to increased resistance.

ompA.notes: Upregulation of ompA contributes to increased resistance.

macAB.notes: Upregulation of macAB contributes to increased resistance.

fusBCD.notes: Upregulation of fusBCD contributes to increased resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Mechanism of Chloramphenicol and Thiamphenicol Resistance Mediated by a Novel Oxidase, CmO, in Sphingomonadaceae.

cmO.validation_method: cloning in E. coli and biochemical characterization

full_output.key_findings: A novel oxidase gene, cmO, was identified and characterized as conferring resistance to chloramphenicol and thiamphenicol in Sphingomonadaceae. The gene was shown to oxidize the C-3' position of these antibiotics, leading to the formation of detoxified products.
full_output.methodology: Gene cloning, biochemical characterization, molecular docking, and site-directed mutagenesis were used to validate the function of cmO.

full_output.paper_title: Polymyxin Resistance and Heteroresistance Are Common in Clinical Isolates of Achromobacter Species and Correlate with Modifications of the Lipid A Moiety of Lipopolysaccharide.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that lipid A modifications, including the addition of glucosamine and palmitate, are associated with polymyxin B (PmB) resistance in Achromobacter species. These modifications were observed in clinical isolates and linked to increased resistance, highlighting the importance of lipid A alterations in PmB resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry, broth microdilution, and Etest assays to analyze lipid A modifications and PmB resistance in Achromobacter clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Oral flora of domestic cats in Hong Kong: Identification of antibiotic-resistant strains.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multidrug-resistant bacteria in the oral flora of domestic cats in Hong Kong, including Pasteurella species, Bacillus species, Neisseria species, Escherichia coli, and Staphylococcus species. These bacteria exhibited resistance to multiple antibiotics, highlighting the importance of monitoring antimicrobial resistance in cat oral flora.
full_output.methodology: Bacterial identification was performed using matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time of flight mass spectrometry, and antibiotic susceptibility testing was conducted using the disk diffusion method according to CLSI guidelines.

full_output.paper_title: Precise spatial structure impacts antimicrobial susceptibility of S. aureus in polymicrobial wound infections.

mutations_found.validated_by: co-infection with mutant strain and antibiotic tolerance assay

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that the P. aeruginosa gene pqsL, involved in HQNO biosynthesis, affects S. aureus aminoglycoside tolerance in coinfected wounds.
full_output.methodology: The study uses a murine surgical wound model, confocal microscopy, and antibiotic tolerance assays to investigate the role of pqsL in S. aureus aminoglycoside resistance.

lysostaphin.validation_method: expression in S. epidermidis and activity assay

full_output.key_findings: The study engineered a 'detect and destroy' skin probiotic using S. epidermidis to produce lysostaphin in response to S. aureus quorum sensing signals, aiming to combat MRSA colonization.
full_output.methodology: Genetic engineering of S. epidermidis to express lysostaphin under quorum sensing regulation, followed by in vitro and in vivo testing.
full_output.sample_size: n=5 mice per group in initial trial, n=12 for repeat trial

full_output.paper_title: Internal and external microbiota of home-caught Anopheles coluzzii (Diptera: Culicidae) from Côte d'Ivoire, Africa: Mosquitoes are filthy.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterized the bacterial communities of Anopheles coluzzii mosquitoes, identifying several genera such as Bacillus, Staphylococcus, Enterobacter, and Rickettsia. Notably, Rickettsia bellii and Rickettsia typhi were found internally, suggesting potential implications for human health.
full_output.methodology: The study used 16S rRNA gene sequencing to analyze the bacterial communities of Anopheles coluzzii mosquitoes collected from homes in Côte d'Ivoire.

full_output.paper_title: Endophytic bacteria of Fagonia indica Burm. f revealed to harbour rich secondary antibacterial metabolites.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified endophytic bacteria from Fagonia indica that produce secondary metabolites with antibacterial properties, including compounds that show high affinity for the MurF ligase enzyme, a key target in bacterial cell wall synthesis.
full_output.methodology: The study used 16S rRNA sequencing for bacterial identification, GC-MS for metabolite analysis, and molecular docking to evaluate compound interactions with bacterial targets.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of the bioresistance profile of enterobacteria isolated from faeces of children with diarrhoea in the town of Koula-Moutou, Gabon: prospective study.
full_output.key_findings: The study found high levels of antibiotic resistance among enterobacteria isolated from children with diarrhoea in Gabon, with significant resistance to β-lactams, quinolones, aminoglycosides, and other antibiotics. Carbapenemase-producing strains were prevalent, contributing to multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing was conducted using the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method on 98 enterobacterial isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Novel oxazolidinones harbor potent in vitro activity against the clinical isolates of multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the in vitro activity of five oxazolidinones against Mycobacterium tuberculosis clinical isolates and reference strains, identifying mutations in rrl and rplD genes associated with linezolid resistance.
full_output.methodology: Microplate alamarBlue assay (MABA) for MIC determination, whole genome sequencing for mutation analysis, and intracellular antibacterial assays.

full_output.paper_title: Aspartate α-decarboxylase a new therapeutic target in the fight against Helicobacter pylori infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies aspartate α-decarboxylase (ADC) as a novel therapeutic target for combating Helicobacter pylori infection, demonstrating that malonic acid (MA) effectively inhibits ADC without inducing resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized molecular docking, MIC/MBC determination, enzymatic activity assays, and in vivo rat models to evaluate ADC inhibition by malonic acid.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic characterization of Staphylococcus aureus isolated from Norway rats in Boston, Massachusetts.

norA.evidence_note: The paper states that all S. aureus isolates were resistant to penicillin and shared the gene norA. It does not explicitly state that norA confers resistance to tetracycline, chloramphenicol, erythromycin, or penicillin beyond what is already noted.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified S. aureus isolates from Norway rats in Boston, MA, carrying resistance genes mepR, mgrA, arlR, and norA. All isolates were methicillin-susceptible, penicillin-resistant, and two showed erythromycin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis and antibiotic susceptibility testing were conducted on S. aureus isolates from wild Norway rats.

full_output.key_findings: Non-caloric artificial sweeteners increase the conjugative transfer of plasmid-mediated antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in gut microbiota, promoting horizontal gene transfer between bacterial species, including human pathogens like Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: In vitro conjugation assays using mouse fecal bacteria and K. pneumoniae as recipients, combined with flow cytometry, confocal microscopy, and 16S rRNA sequencing to analyze plasmid transfer and microbial community changes.

full_output.paper_title: Thiophene derivatives activity against the protozoan parasite Leishmania infantum.
