full_output.paper_title: Inhibitory activities of vitamins K2 against clinical isolates of quinolone-resistant and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (QR-MRSA) with different multi-locus sequence types (MLST), SCCmec, and spa types.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several mutations in the norA, grlA, grlB, gyrA, and gyrB genes associated with ciprofloxacin resistance in QR-MRSA isolates. Vitamin K2 was found to significantly down-regulate the expression of these genes.
full_output.methodology: The study used real-time PCR to analyze gene expression and identify mutations in QR-MRSA isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study developed an implantable 3D biofilm model to investigate infected wounds, focusing on the behavior of Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Staphylococcus aureus, and Enterococcus faecalis. The model demonstrated biofilm formation, antibiotic tolerance, and systemic and local inflammatory responses in mice.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized 3D collagen-based scaffolds seeded with bacterial strains, followed by in vitro and in vivo analyses including MTT assays, microscopy, and cytokine measurements.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that fig latex exhibits antibacterial activity against pathogenic bacteria isolated from diabetic wounds, including Staphylococcus haemolyticus, Pseudomonas sp., Bacillus sp., and Paenibacillus sp. It also showed potential in enhancing wound healing in diabetic mice.
full_output.methodology: The study used GC-MS analysis to characterize the chemical composition of fig latex, followed by in vitro antibacterial assays and in vivo experiments on a diabetic mouse model to evaluate its effects on wound healing.

full_output.paper_title: Charge neutralization of the active site glutamates does not limit substrate binding and transport by small multidrug resistance transporter EmrE.
full_output.key_findings: EmrE, a small multidrug resistance transporter from Escherichia coli, was shown to bind +2 substrates and protons simultaneously without limitation from charge neutralization of the active site glutamates, E14A and E14B.
full_output.methodology: NMR pH titrations, isothermal titration calorimetry, and solid-supported membrane electrophysiology were used to analyze EmrE's substrate binding and transport mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of the antibacterial, antibiofilm, and anti-virulence effects of acetic acid and the related mechanisms on colistin-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: Acetic acid (AA) exhibits antibacterial, antibiofilm, and anti-virulence effects against colistin-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa by increasing membrane permeability, altering membrane potential, and reducing reduction potential. AA also inhibits the expression of T3SS and QS-related genes, thus reducing virulence factors such as pyocyanin and elastase.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, biofilm formation and eradication assays, motility assays, pyocyanin and elastase production measurements, membrane permeability assays, and qRT-PCR for gene expression analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of mcr-8.2-harboring hypervirulent ST412 Klebsiella pneumoniae strain from pediatric sepsis: A comparative genomic survey.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies an mcr-8.2-harboring hypervirulent ST412 Klebsiella pneumoniae strain from pediatric sepsis, highlighting the emergence of colistin resistance in this pathogen.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, PCR, and susceptibility testing were used to characterize the isolate and its resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Microbial Water Quality through a Full-Scale Advanced Wastewater Treatment Demonstration Facility.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of antibiotic resistance genes sul1 and bla TEM in wastewater treatment processes, highlighting their persistence through advanced treatment steps.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative PCR was used to analyze the fate of antibiotic resistance genes and microbial communities in advanced wastewater treatment processes.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular epidemiology and antimicrobial resistance of Haemophilus influenzae in Guiyang, Guizhou, China.

ftsI.notes: Mutations in the ftsI gene were detected in ampicillin-resistant strains.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the TEM-1 gene as a major contributor to ampicillin resistance in Haemophilus influenzae isolates, along with PBP3 mutations that alter penicillin-binding protein 3, leading to ampicillin resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze the resistance mechanisms in H. influenzae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Sputum smear conversion and treatment outcomes among drug-resistant pulmonary tuberculosis patients in eastern Ethiopia: A 9-years data analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified factors associated with sputum smear conversion and treatment outcomes among drug-resistant tuberculosis (DR-TB) patients in eastern Ethiopia, including the impact of baseline sputum smear results, HIV status, and treatment adherence.
full_output.methodology: A cross-sectional study analyzing medical records of 273 DR-TB patients, focusing on sputum smear conversion and treatment outcomes using statistical analyses.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of virulence factors and antibiotic resistance pattern of uropathogenic Escherichia coli strains in a tertiary care center.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified hlyA, iutA, papC, and cnf1 as significant virulence factors in UPEC strains, with hlyA showing a positive association with resistance to imipenem, norfloxacin, and ceftazidime.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic and genotypic methods including PCR and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to characterize virulence factors and resistance patterns in UPEC strains.

full_output.paper_title: Growth kinetics of multiple Acinetobacter baumannii resistotype after meropenem-based antibiotic combination exposure.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the growth kinetics of Acinetobacter baumannii isolates after exposure to meropenem and ampicillin-sulbactam or meropenem and amikacin combinations, showing that meropenem and ampicillin-sulbactam had bactericidal effects on certain isolates.
full_output.methodology: Experimental laboratory study involving turbidity measurements and agar plate enumeration to assess bacterial growth kinetics after antibiotic exposure.
full_output.sample_size: Four isolates: one standard reference (ATCC 19606) and three clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Streptococcus pseudopneumoniae as an emerging respiratory tract pathogen at Assiut University hospitals.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 20 isolates of Streptococcus pseudopneumoniae, which showed resistance to multiple antibiotics including penicillin, erythromycin, clindamycin, ciprofloxacin, cefopime, and co-trimoxazole. The isolates were distinguished from Streptococcus pneumoniae through phenotypic and genotypic methods.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic and genotypic methods, including PCR for specific genes, were used to identify and characterize the isolates. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the agar disc diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Serotype distribution and antibiotic resistance of Streptococcus pneumoniae isolates collected from unvaccinated children with pneumonia at a province in central Vietnam.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified eight pneumococcal serotypes, with 19F, 23F, and 19A being the most prevalent. High levels of resistance to macrolides, tetracyclines, and clindamycin were observed, with 100% resistance to azithromycin, clarithromycin, and erythromycin. Penicillin and cephalosporin resistance rates were also significant.
full_output.methodology: The study used multiplex PCR, VITEK® 2 Compact system, and 16S rRNA gene sequencing to identify serotypes and assess antimicrobial resistance patterns.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic analysis of Fosfomycin resistance in multi-drug resistant uropathogens and comparison of in-vitro susceptibility methods uropathogens.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the uhpT gene and the presence of plasmid-mediated fosA5 or fosA6 genes as mechanisms of Fosfomycin resistance in multi-drug resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing using agar dilution, disc diffusion, and E-test methods.

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the use of metal complexes as antimicrobial agents, highlighting their mechanisms of action and effectiveness against various pathogens.
full_output.methodology: Review of literature on metal-based antimicrobial compounds and their mechanisms of action.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic characteristics, antimicrobial resistance, and prevalence of Arcobacter spp. isolated from various sources in Shenzhen, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in Arcobacter spp., including beta-lactamase genes (blaOXA464, blaOXA491), tetracycline resistance genes (tet(L), tet(H), tet(M)), a macrolide resistance gene (ere(A)), and aminoglycoside resistance genes (APH(3')-IIIa, ant(6)-Ia, SAT-4). Additionally, a mutation in the gyrA gene (C254T) was found to confer fluoroquinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify AMR genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: D1018 with higher stability and excellent lipopolysaccharide binding affinity has potent anti-bacterial and anti-inflammatory activity.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory activities of the peptides IDR-1018, D1018, 1018M, and D1018M against E. coli ATCC25922, highlighting their stability, efficacy, and lack of resistance development.
full_output.methodology: MIC determination, time-kill curves, protease stability assays, hemolysis, cytotoxicity, and membrane permeabilization analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of virulence and antimicrobial resistance genes of Aeromonas media strain SD/21-15 from marine sediments in comparison with other Aeromonas spp.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterized multiple antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes in Aeromonas media strain SD/21-15, including beta-lactamases (bla MOX-9, bla OXA-427), carbapenemases (crp), polymyxin resistance genes (mcr, mcr-3, mcr-3.6), tetracycline resistance (tet(E)), quinolone resistance (qnrS2), and multidrug efflux pumps (mexB).
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and comparative genomics analyses were performed to identify and characterize AMR genes in Aeromonas media strain SD/21-15 and related isolates.

full_output.paper_title: The metal chaperone protein MtmA plays important roles in antifungal drug susceptibility in Aspergillus fumigatus.
full_output.key_findings: Repression of MtmA leads to enhanced resistance to multiple antifungal drugs, including itraconazole, voriconazole, bifonazole, terbinafine, amphotericin B, and caspofungin, through upregulation of drug efflux pumps and persistent nuclear localization of the transcription factor CrzA.
full_output.methodology: Conditional gene expression, RNA-seq, RT–PCR, Western blotting, HPLC, fluorescence microscopy, and β-galactosidase assays.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that experimentally passing tetracycline-treated microbiomes across honey bee generations leads to heritable dysbiosis, affecting host survival and gene expression under antibiotic stress.
full_output.methodology: The study used controlled lab experiments to pass microbiomes across honey bee generations, analyzed microbial composition via 16S sequencing, and assessed host gene expression through RNA-seq.
full_output.sample_size: Multiple cages with ~25-28 bees per cage

full_output.paper_title: Horizontal gene transfer via OMVs co-carrying virulence and antimicrobial-resistant genes is a novel way for the dissemination of carbapenem-resistant hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae.

full_output.paper_title: Mobile colistin resistance (MCR), extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) and multidrug resistance monitoring in Escherichia coli (commensal and pathogenic) in pig farming: need of harmonized guidelines and clinical breakpoints.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mcr-1 and mcr-4 genes conferring colistin resistance, along with blaTEM-1B, aph(3")-Ib, aph(6)-Id, sul2, and tet(A) genes responsible for resistance to various antibiotics in E. coli isolates from pig farming.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and in silico analysis were used to identify AMR genes and mutations in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Glutamine potentiates gentamicin to kill lab-evolved gentamicin-resistant and clinically isolated multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies glutamine as a critical metabolite that potentiates gentamicin-mediated killing of lab-evolved gentamicin-resistant and clinically isolated multidrug-resistant E. coli. It highlights the importance of metabolic reprogramming in overcoming antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used GC-MS-based metabolomics to analyze the metabolic profiles of gentamicin-resistant and control E. coli strains, followed by experiments to assess the effect of glutamine on gentamicin efficacy.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization and Identification of a novel chromosome-encoded metallo-β-lactamase WUS-1 in Myroides albus P34.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes a novel chromosomally-encoded metallo-β-lactamase gene, bla WUS-1, in Myroides albus P34, which confers resistance to several β-lactam antibiotics including carbapenems.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, cloning, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize the novel metallo-β-lactamase gene bla WUS-1.

full_output.paper_title: Aeromonas species isolated from aquatic organisms, insects, chicken, and humans in India show similar antimicrobial resistance profiles.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes in Aeromonas species isolated from various hosts in India, including beta-lactamases (bla OXA-12, bla OXA-427, bla OXA-724, bla OXA-780, bla FOX-2, bla FOX-4, bla FOX-5, bla FOX-7, bla AQU-2, bla MOX-7), metallo-beta-lactamases (cphA3, cphA4, cphA5, cphA8, ImiH), and other resistance genes (dfrA12, aadA2, ANT(3")-IIa, sul1). Additionally, multidrug efflux pump genes (mdtH, zntA, emrD, blR, crp) were found to contribute to AMR in these isolates.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing (WGS) and bioinformatic analysis were used to identify and characterize AMR genes in Aeromonas isolates from different host species in India.

full_output.paper_title: A systematic review and meta-analysis on antimicrobial resistance in marine bivalves.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the prevalence of antimicrobial resistance in bacterial isolates from marine bivalves, with particular emphasis on Aeromonas spp., Vibrio spp., Salmonella spp., and Escherichia coli. High resistance rates were observed for several antibiotic classes, including carboxypenicillins, glycopeptides, and first/second generation cephalosporins.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review and meta-analysis of literature on antimicrobial resistance in marine bivalves.

full_output.paper_title: Cluster analysis and geospatial mapping of antibiotic resistant Escherichia coli O157 in southwest Nigerian communities.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies high levels of antibiotic resistance in Escherichia coli O157 strains from human, water, and food animal sources in southwest Nigeria, highlighting the spread and relatedness of these resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed antibiotic resistance patterns, conducted PCR for stx genes, and used geospatial mapping to evaluate the spread of resistant Escherichia coli O157 strains.

full_output.paper_title: Prenylated phenolics from Morus alba against MRSA infections as a strategy for wound healing.

full_output.sample_size: 12 natural compounds tested against 5 MRSA and 3 MSSA strains.

full_output.paper_title: Production of extended-spectrum beta-lactamases in Escherichia coli isolated from poultry in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of ESBL-producing E. coli isolates in poultry farms in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, with the blaSHV, blaTEM, and blaCTX-M genes being the primary resistance determinants.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid Phenotypic Convergence towards Collateral Sensitivity in Clinical Isolates of Pseudomonas aeruginosa Presenting Different Genomic Backgrounds.

full_output.paper_title: A Novel Biosynthetic Gene Cluster Across the Pantoea Species Complex Is Important for Pathogenicity in Onion.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the Halophos gene cluster, which includes the pepM gene, as crucial for onion pathogenicity in Pantoea species. Deletion of pepM significantly reduces pathogenicity, indicating its vital role in the biosynthesis of a phosphonate compound that causes onion tissue necrosis.
full_output.methodology: Genome analysis, gene deletion, complementation experiments, and pathogenicity assays were conducted to evaluate the role of the Halophos gene cluster and pepM in onion pathogenicity.
full_output.sample_size: Multiple strains of Pantoea species were analyzed.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla OXA-23, bla OXA-48, bla OXA-51, bla OXA-58, bla NDM-5, armA, qnrB, and aac(6′)-Ib-cr as the primary resistance genes in carbapenemase-producing Gram-negative bacteria in Gabon.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex PCR and sequencing were used to identify resistance genes in clinical and fecal samples.

full_output.paper_title: New insights into the antibacterial mode of action of quercetin against uropathogen Serratia marcescens in-vivo and in-vitro.
full_output.key_findings: Quercetin exhibits antibacterial activity against Serratia marcescens by inhibiting biofilm formation, extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) production, prodigiosin synthesis, and swarming motility. It also reduces the metabolic activity of planktonic cells and affects the expression of virulence-related genes.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized MIC determination, biofilm assays, MTT reduction, EPS quantification, prodigiosin measurement, swarming motility assessment, SEM, CLSM, and qPCR to evaluate the effects of quercetin on S. marcescens.

full_output.paper_title: Risk factors and mortality of carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae bloodstream infection in a tertiary-care hospital in China: an eight-year retrospective study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies hematologic malignancy and ICU-acquired infection as independent risk factors for carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae bloodstream infection (CRKP-BSI). It also highlights the significance of adequate empirical antibiotic therapy and high-dose carbapenem combination therapy in reducing mortality.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of clinical data from a tertiary-care hospital in China, focusing on risk factors and mortality associated with CRKP-BSI.

full_output.paper_title: Risk factors for colonization by carbapenemase-producing bacteria in Spanish long-term care facilities: a multicentre point-prevalence study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high prevalence of colonization by carbapenemase-producing bacteria (CPB) in Spanish long-term care facilities, highlighting risk factors such as male sex, high health requirement, and prior hospitalization. mcr-1.genetic_context: The mcr-1 sequence of all E. coli genomes was 100% identical to the mcr-1 sequence from the Resfinder database. The exploration of the genetic context of mcr-1 allowed us to identify three different types of mcr-1 -containing cassettes suggesting a diverse genetic context of mcr-1 -harboring E. coli in the farms of Lima ( Figure 3 ). Two different context structures were identified in chicken farms. The IS Apl1–mcr1–pap2– IS Apl1 was identified in the AV4P5C isolate, which belongs to ST48. This cassette shows a structure called Tn6330 inserted into an IncHI1A:IncHI1B hybrid plasmid. Tn6330 is a composite transposon that improves the transmission of the mcr-1 gene [ 35 ]. The second structure shows the nikB–mcr1–pap2 composition that has lost IS Apl1 both upstream and downstream. This structure was found within IncI2 plasmids in the AV4P2D, AV5P5C, AV5P3A and AV8P7A isolates ( Figure 3 ).

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mcr-1-harboring E. coli isolates in chicken and pig farms in Lima, Peru, highlighting the presence of multiple antibiotic resistance genes, including bla CTX-M-55, and diverse plasmid types such as IncI2 and IncHI1A:IncHI1B.

full_output.paper_title: Bacterial Communities and Antibiotic Resistance of Potential Pathogens Involved in Food Safety and Public Health in Fish and Water of Lake Karla, Thessaly, Greece.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Serratia fonticola, Aeromonas salmonicida, and Aeromonas veronii as the most prevalent bacteria in water and fish samples from Lake Karla, with notable resistance to tetracycline, cefoxitin, cefazolin, ampicillin, and penicillin.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic resistance testing using disc diffusion assay and MALDI-TOF MS for bacterial identification.

full_output.paper_title: Genomics Analysis to Identify Multiple Genetic Determinants That Drive the Global Transmission of the Pandemic ST95 Lineage of Extraintestinal Pathogenic Escherichia coli (ExPEC).
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple genetic determinants driving the global transmission of the pandemic ST95 lineage of ExPEC, including various resistance genes such as blaTEM-1, sul2, dfrA, aph(3'')-I, aph(6)-I, tet(A), aadA, ere(A), erm(B), mph(A), and mcr-1.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to characterize the ST95 pan-genome, identify resistance genes, and analyze plasmid replicons and virulence factors.

full_output.paper_title: A Familiar Outbreak of Monophasic Salmonella serovar Typhimurium (ST34) Involving Three Dogs and Their Owner's Children.

organisms_tested_in: Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica serovar Typhimurium
sul2.validation_method: whole-genome sequencing and AMR gene detection

full_output.key_findings: The study identified AMR genes sul2, tetB, and blaTEM-1B in a monophasic Salmonella Typhimurium ST34 outbreak involving humans and dogs.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial resistance gene detection.

full_output.paper_title: Characteristics of Staphylococcus aureus Isolated from Patients in Busia County Referral Hospital, Kenya.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified S. aureus isolates carrying genes conferring resistance to penicillin-G, trimethoprim, tetracycline, erythromycin, gentamicin, and other antibiotics. Key resistance genes included blaZ, tetK, tetM, dfrG, ermA, ermC, aacA-aphD, aad9, and mecA.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR, and genomic analyses were used to identify resistance genes and virulence factors in S. aureus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Cross-Over Pathogenic Bacteria Detected in Infected Tomatoes (Solanum lycopersicum L.) and Peppers (Capsicum annuum L.) in Bulgaria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several bacterial species from infected tomato and pepper plants, including opportunistic human pathogens such as Leclercia adecarboxylata, Pseudomonas vulneris, Enterobacter species, and Acinetobacter calcoaceticus. While antibiotic resistance was observed, no specific resistance genes were detected in the isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study involved isolation and phenotypic characterization of bacterial strains from infected plant samples, followed by molecular detection of resistance genes using PCR.

full_output.paper_title: Cefiderocol against Multi-Drug and Extensively Drug-Resistant Escherichia coli: An In Vitro Study in Poland.
full_output.key_findings: Cefiderocol shows high in vitro susceptibility against multidrug-resistant (MDR) and extensively drug-resistant (XDR) E. coli isolates, including those producing ESBLs and carbapenemases such as VIM and NDM.
full_output.methodology: Disk diffusion and MIC test strip methods were used to assess susceptibility of E. coli isolates to cefiderocol.

full_output.paper_title: Multidrug-Resistant Gram-Negative Bacteria Contaminating Raw Meat Sold in Accra, Ghana.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that raw meat samples in Accra, Ghana, were contaminated with multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria, including Escherichia coli, Aeromonas hydrophila, Vibrio cholerae, and Klebsiella pneumoniae. The prevalence of MDR bacteria was 14.9%, and 2% of the isolates were extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) producers.
full_output.methodology: The study involved collecting 270 meat samples and analyzing them for bacterial contamination and antimicrobial resistance through susceptibility testing and identification techniques.

full_output.paper_title: Syphilis as Re-Emerging Disease, Antibiotic Resistance, and Vulnerable Population: Global Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the A2058G and A2059G mutations in the 23S rRNA gene of Treponema pallidum, which confer resistance to macrolides. These mutations show an increasing prevalence over time, particularly in certain geographic regions and populations.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review and meta-analysis of studies on molecular detection of syphilis and antibiotic resistance mutations.

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the potential of the CRISPR-Cas system as a tool to combat drug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria, focusing on its application in diagnosis and treatment. It highlights the challenges posed by antimicrobial resistance and explores alternative strategies to address this issue.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews existing literature and discusses the mechanisms of antibiotic resistance in Gram-negative bacteria, as well as the potential of CRISPR-Cas technology in overcoming these challenges.

full_output.paper_title: Assessing Clinical Potential of Old Antibiotics against Severe Infections by Multi-Drug-Resistant Gram-Negative Bacteria Using In Silico Modelling.
full_output.key_findings: The review evaluates the in vitro activity and potential clinical efficacy of old antibiotics against multidrug-resistant (MDR) gram-negative bacteria using in silico modeling. It highlights the potential of polymyxin B, temocillin, fosfomycin, and mecillinam against specific MDR pathogens.
full_output.methodology: The study uses in silico modeling and Monte Carlo simulations to analyze the pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) profiles of old antibiotics against MDR gram-negative bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: A Bioluminescence-Based Ex Vivo Burn Wound Model for Real-Time Assessment of Novel Phage-Inspired Enzybiotics.

chloramphenicol acetyltransferase.validation_method: experimental validation through plasmid construction and verification via PCR

full_output.key_findings: The study presents a bioluminescence-based ex vivo burn wound model using A. baumannii NCTC13423 tagged with the luxCDABE operon. It characterizes the aacC1 gene for gentamycin resistance and the chloramphenicol acetyltransferase gene for chloramphenicol resistance.
full_output.methodology: Plasmid construction, PCR verification, and bioluminescence monitoring were used to validate the resistance genes and the reporter system.

full_output.paper_title: Cationic Surfactants Based on Arginine-Phenylalanine and Arginine-Tryptophan: Synthesis, Aggregation Behavior, Antimicrobial Activity, and Biodegradation.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis and evaluation of amino acid-based cationic surfactants with antimicrobial activity against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. The surfactants showed varying levels of antimicrobial effectiveness depending on their structural characteristics.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of surfactants, determination of critical micelle concentration, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and biodegradability assessment.

full_output.paper_title: A Thermosensitive, Chitosan-Based Hydrogel as Delivery System for Antibacterial Liposomes to Surgical Site Infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes the development of a thermosensitive chitosan-based hydrogel (CS-βGP) incorporating liposomes of Cu(DDC)2 and Cu2+ for treating surgical site infections. The lipogel effectively prevented biofilm formation and killed methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and Staphylococcus epidermidis.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the preparation and characterization of liposomes, lyophilization, rheological measurements, and evaluation of antibiofilm activity against S. aureus and S. epidermidis.

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the development of technologies to prevent, diagnose, and manage antimicrobial resistance in healthcare-associated infections, focusing on rapid diagnostics and innovative therapeutic approaches.
full_output.methodology: The paper provides an overview of current and emerging technologies for detecting and managing antimicrobial resistance, including sequencing, MALDI-TOF MS, and spectroscopy-based methods.

full_output.paper_title: In Vitro and Pre-Clinical Evaluation of Locally Isolated Phages, vB_Pae_SMP1 and vB_Pae_SMP5, Formulated as Hydrogels against Carbapenem-Resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates carrying bla KPC, bla NDM, bla VIM, and bla OXA-48 genes, which confer resistance to imipenem and meropenem. Two phages, vB_Pae_SMP1 and vB_Pae_SMP5, were isolated and evaluated for their efficacy against these resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of carbapenemase genes, phage isolation, and in vitro/in vivo evaluation of phage activity against CRPA isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Chimeric Peptidoglycan Hydrolases Kill Staphylococcal Mastitis Isolates in Raw Milk and within Bovine Mammary Gland Epithelial Cells.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several chimeric peptidoglycan hydrolases (PGHs) with high staphylolytic activity against Staphylococcus aureus in raw milk and within bovine mammary gland epithelial cells. These PGHs include LST, M23LST(L)_SH3b2638, ALE-1, CHAPGH15_SH3bAle1, CHAPK_SH3bLST_H, and CHAPH5_LST_H, which effectively reduce bacterial loads and show synergistic activity when combined.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized time-kill assays, minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC) determinations, and intracellular activity assays to evaluate the staphylolytic activity of selected PGHs against S. aureus in various environments, including raw milk and bovine mammary alveolar cells.

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the use of essential oils and their components as potential antimicrobial agents against ESKAPE pathogens, focusing on their anti-biofilm and antimicrobial activities.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews the literature on the antimicrobial and anti-biofilm effects of essential oils and their components against ESKAPE pathogens.

full_output.paper_title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of integrated studies on antimicrobial resistance in Vietnam, with a focus on Enterobacteriaceae, from a One Health perspective.
full_output.key_findings: This study provides a comprehensive overview of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in Enterobacteriaceae, particularly E. coli and non-typhoidal Salmonella (NTS), across humans, animals, and the environment in Vietnam. High resistance levels were observed against quinolones, third-generation cephalosporins, penicillins, and aminoglycosides.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 89 studies on AMR in Enterobacteriaceae from Vietnam.

full_output.paper_title: Sepsis and survival in critically ill calves: Risk factors and antimicrobial use.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Escherichia coli as the most frequently isolated bacterium from blood cultures of critically ill calves, with 90.9% of isolates showing multidrug resistance. Other bacteria included Staphylococcus spp., Salmonella spp., and various Enterobacteriaceae, many of which exhibited high levels of antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective cohort study analyzing data from 230 critically ill calves, including blood culture results and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Biogenic nanosilver-fabricated endotracheal tube to prevent microbial colonization in a veterinary hospital.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that silver nanoparticles (AgNPs)-coated endotracheal tubes exhibit potent antimicrobial activity against a wide range of pathogens, including multidrug-resistant clinical isolates, without cytotoxic effects on mammalian cells.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a combination of in vitro antimicrobial assays, biofilm formation tests, and in vivo porcine models to evaluate the efficacy and safety of AgNPs-coated endotracheal tubes.

full_output.paper_title: Combating Escherichia coli O157:H7 with Functionalized Chickpea-Derived Antimicrobial Peptides.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents functionalized chickpea-derived antimicrobial peptides (FCLAPs) with potent antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli O157:H7, showing a dual-targeting mechanism involving lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and peptidoglycan (PGN) layers.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized in vitro and in vivo assays, including MIC determination, time-kill curves, membrane permeability assessments, and multi-omics profiling to evaluate the antibacterial mechanisms of FCLAPs.

full_output.paper_title: Structural Determinants of Indole-2-carboxamides: Identification of Lead Acetamides with Pan Antimycobacterial Activity.

full_output.methodology: Synthesis of acetamide derivatives, antimycobacterial activity testing, and structural analysis of MmpL3 binding.

full_output.paper_title: Paratype: a genotyping tool for Salmonella Paratyphi A reveals its global genomic diversity.

full_output.methodology: Fluorescence-coupled synthetic mutations and time-resolved microscopy were used to track evolutionary rescue dynamics in yeast colonies.

full_output.paper_title: Hydrogels with intrinsic antibacterial activity prepared from naphthyl anthranilamide (NaA) capped peptide mimics.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents the development of NaA-capped cationic hydrogels with intrinsic antibacterial activity against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, demonstrating significant bacterial reduction without cytotoxicity.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of NaA-capped cationic peptide mimics, evaluation of hydrogel formation, and assessment of antibacterial activity through various experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Preferred β-lactone synthesis can explain high rate of false-negative results in the detection of OXA-48-like carbapenemases.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies OXA-48-like carbapenemases (blaOXA-48, blaOXA-181, blaOXA-232, blaOXA-244) as responsible for carbapenem resistance through β-lactone formation, which can lead to false-negative results in traditional detection methods.
full_output.methodology: MALDI-TOF MS, LC–MS, and susceptibility testing were used to analyze carbapenemase activity and β-lactone formation in OXA-48-like-producing Enterobacterales.

full_output.paper_title: Genotypic characterization and clonal relatedness of metallo-β-lactamase-producing non-fermentative gram negative bacteria in the first 5 years of their circulation in Paraguay (2011-2015).
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaVIM-2, blaNDM-1, and blaIMP-18 as the主要 metallo-β-lactamase genes in non-fermentative gram-negative bacteria in Paraguay, highlighting their prevalence and clonal spread.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and pulsed-field gel electrophoresis (PFGE) were used for genotypic characterization and clonal relatedness analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of pre-treated healthcare wastes during COVID-19 pandemic reveals pathogenic microbiota, antibiotics residues, and antibiotic resistance genes against beta-lactams.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaTEM-1 and penP genes in pre-treated healthcare waste samples, which confer resistance to beta-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: AMPlicon sequencing and UPLC-QTOF-MS analysis were used to profile microbial communities and detect antibiotic compounds, while ARGs-OAP and KEGG annotation were used for ARG detection and functional analysis.
full_output.sample_size: 10 bags of microwaved pre-treated HCW samples

full_output.paper_title: Precursor-derived in-water peracetic acid impacts on broiler performance, gut microbiota, and antimicrobial resistance genes.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the impact of in-water peracetic acid on broiler performance, gut microbiota, and antimicrobial resistance genes. It found that PAA treatment affected bacterial concentration in the crop and altered the abundance of certain AMR genes, including aadA, tetQ, vanC, and mecA.
full_output.methodology: Relative qPCR quantification was used to analyze the abundance of six AMR genes (aadA, tetQ, vanC, mecA, tetW, vanA) in the crop of broilers treated with varying levels of peracetic acid.

full_output.paper_title: ADMET profiling and molecular docking of potential antimicrobial peptides previously isolated from African catfish, Clarias gariepinus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified two antimicrobial peptides, ACAP-IV and ACAP-V, from African catfish with promising ADMET profiles and antibacterial activity against E. coli and S. aureus.
full_output.methodology: In silico ADMET profiling, molecular docking, and in vitro antibacterial activity testing.

full_output.paper_title: Recent developments on UDP-N-acetylmuramoyl-L-alanine-D-glutamate ligase (Mur D) enzyme for antimicrobial drug development: An emphasis on in-silico approaches.
full_output.key_findings: This review discusses the role of UDP-N-acetylmuramoyl-L-alanine-D-glutamate ligase (MurD) as a target for antimicrobial drug development, focusing on structural and functional aspects, inhibitors, and in-silico approaches.
full_output.methodology: Review of literature on MurD enzyme, structural analyses, and computational methods for inhibitor design.

full_output.methodology: The study utilized whole-genome sequencing data from over 180,000 bacterial genomes to construct the ggMOB network, analyzing conjugative features and their association with AMR genes.

full_output.paper_title: Modern knowledge-scape possess petite influence on the factual persistence of resistance determinants (ARGs/MGEs): A map and assessment of discharged wastewater and water bodies.
full_output.key_findings: This study provides a bibliometric assessment of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) and mobile genetic elements (MGEs) in wastewater and water bodies, highlighting the lack of effective strategies for their removal and the need for research-based approaches.
full_output.methodology: The study used a bibliometric analysis of 1301 articles retrieved from the Web of Science, focusing on the annual growth rate, citation trends, and research contributions related to ARGs and MGEs in water systems.

full_output.paper_title: Inhaled Bacteriophage Therapy for Multi-Drug Resistant Achromobacter.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes the use of two lytic phages, Achr-1 and Achr-2, for treating multidrug-resistant Achromobacter infections in a cystic fibrosis patient. The phages showed effectiveness in reducing bacterial load and stabilizing respiratory status, with some evidence of trade-offs including increased antibiotic sensitivity in resistant mutants.
full_output.methodology: Phage characterization, in vitro assays, and clinical case report.

full_output.paper_title: Drug-Resistant Aerobic Bacterial Pathogens in Patients with Crocodile Bite Wounds Attending at Arba Minch General Hospital, Southern Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple drug-resistant aerobic bacterial pathogens in crocodile bite wounds, with a high prevalence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) isolates. Key findings include high resistance rates to various antibiotics among Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Citrobacter spp., coagulase-negative Staphylococci (CoNS), and Enterococcus faecalis.
full_output.methodology: The study involved a hospital-based cross-sectional analysis of bacterial isolates from crocodile bite wounds, utilizing microbiological culture techniques and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Designing double-site lipidated peptide amphiphiles as potent antimicrobial biomaterials to combat multidrug-resistant bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a novel double-site lipidated peptide amphiphile, WL-C6, which exhibits potent antimicrobial activity against multidrug-resistant bacteria without significant toxicity towards mammalian cells.
full_output.methodology: The study involved designing and synthesizing lipidated peptides, evaluating their antimicrobial activity through MIC measurements, assessing hemolysis and cytotoxicity, and investigating their stability and bactericidal kinetics.

full_output.paper_title: Surveillance of osteoarticular infections caused by Staphylococcus aureus in a paediatric hospital in Mexico City.

full_output.paper_title: β-Lactamase Suppression as a Strategy to Target Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus: Proof of Concept.

full_output.methodology: The study utilized MIC assays, nitrocefin assays, and structural activity studies to evaluate the effects of P2As on penicillin G potency against MRSA strains.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular genetic testing does not improve the detection of fluoroquinolone resistance before transrectal prostate biopsy.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and antimicrobial resistance patterns of Enterococcus species isolated from laying hens in Lusaka and Copperbelt provinces of Zambia: a call for AMR surveillance in the poultry sector.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a high prevalence of antimicrobial-resistant Enterococcus species in laying hens in Zambia, with high resistance to tetracycline, erythromycin, and quinupristin/dalfopristin, and moderate resistance to other antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method and molecular identification of Enterococcus species.

full_output.paper_title: A systematic scoping review of faropenem and other oral penems: treatment of Enterobacterales infections, development of resistance and cross-resistance to carbapenems.
full_output.key_findings: The review highlights the limited evidence on faropenem resistance and cross-resistance to carbapenems among Enterobacterales, noting some potential bacterial resistance to faropenem and preliminary in vitro evidence suggesting faropenem resistance might foster cross-resistance to carbapenems.
full_output.methodology: Systematic scoping review of literature on faropenem and other oral penems, including analysis of in vitro studies and clinical trials.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic and Phenotypic Characteristics of Carbapenem-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae Isolates from a Tertiary Hospital in Beijing.

full_output.paper_title: CRISPR/Cas9 targeting liposomes knocked down multidrug resistance proteins in brain endothelial cells as a model to predict potential pharmacoresistance.

full_output.paper_title: Genotypic and phenotypic diversity of Prototheca spp. recovered from bovine mastitis in terms of antimicrobial resistance and biofilm formation ability.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that Prototheca bovis isolates from bovine mastitis exhibited varying levels of biofilm production and resistance to various antimicrobial drugs. Gentamicin and colistin showed the highest sensitivity among the tested antimicrobials.

full_output.paper_title: MRSA Isolates from Patients with Persistent Bacteremia Generate Nonstable Small Colony Variants In Vitro within Macrophages and Endothelial Cells during Prolonged Vancomycin Exposure.

full_output.methodology: The study uses macrophage and endothelial cell infection models, gentamicin protection assays, fluorescence-based proliferation assays, and SCV quantification to analyze the formation of nsSCVs in MRSA isolates under vancomycin exposure.

full_output.paper_title: Discovery and Characterization of Polymyxin-Resistance Genes pmrE and pmrF from Sediment and Seawater Microbiome.

full_output.methodology: Bioinformatics analysis, heterologous expression, biochemical characterization, and MIC assays.

full_output.paper_title: Attachment of the RNA degradosome to the bacterial inner cytoplasmic membrane prevents wasteful degradation of rRNA in ribosome assembly intermediates.

full_output.paper_title: The Myxobacterial Antibiotic Myxovalargin: Biosynthesis, Structural Revision, Total Synthesis, and Molecular Characterization of Ribosomal Inhibition.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance profile of Escherichia coli isolated from poultry litter.

full_output.paper_title: Nigericin is effective against multidrug resistant gram-positive bacteria, persisters, and biofilms.
full_output.key_findings: Nigericin shows potent bactericidal activity against multidrug-resistant Gram-positive bacteria, including MRSA and VRE, and is effective against persisters and biofilms with low resistance development. full_output.paper_title: Evidence of Sharing of Carbapenem-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae Strains Between Intensive Care Unit Patients and the Environment.

full_output.paper_title: Occurrence and plasmid profiles of multidrug-resistant Enterobacteriaceae isolated from hawked soymilk samples in the Polytechnic of Ibadan Community, Nigeria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multidrug-resistant Enterobacteriaceae in hawked soymilk samples, including Citrobacter spp., Klebsiella spp., Escherichia coli, Shigella spp., and Proteus spp., which exhibited resistance to various antibiotics such as ertapenem, gentamicin, aztreonam, amoxicillin-clavulanate, ciprofloxacin, ceftazidime, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, and cefepime.

full_output.paper_title: Dissemination and characteristics of high-level erythromycin-resistant Enterococcus faecalis from bulk tank milk of dairy companies in Korea.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic resistance and siderophores production by clinical Escherichia coli strains.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that 31 out of 32 E. coli strains were extensively drug-resistant (XDR) and one was pan-drug-resistant (PDR). Siderophore production was observed in 23 strains, with E. coli strains 21 and 49 being the most potent producers. Plasmid-cured strains showed susceptibility to all antibiotics, while plasmid-transformed strains exhibited resistance to certain antibiotic classes.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing using the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method, siderophore production assessed via CAS agar and liquid medium, and plasmid curing experiments.

full_output.paper_title: A scoping review of the distribution and frequency of extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Enterobacteriaceae in shrimp and salmon.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies various extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL) genes, including bla CTX-M-1, bla CTX-M-15, bla CTX-M-9, bla TEM, bla SHV, and bla CTX-M-55, in Enterobacteriaceae isolated from shrimp and salmon. These genes confer resistance to multiple β-lactam antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of 2-Aryl-Quinolone Inhibitors of Cytochrome bd and Chemical Validation of Combination Strategies for Respiratory Inhibitors against Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

full_output.paper_title: The impact of agarose immobilization on the activity of lytic Pseudomonas aeruginosa phages combined with chemicals.

full_output.paper_title: Plasmid-Encoded Traits Vary across Environments.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed plasmid sequences from various environments and found that plasmid accessory traits, including resistance genes, carbon utilization genes, and nitrogen-cycling genes, vary significantly across environments. Resistance genes were more prevalent in human and animal environments, while nitrogen-cycling and carbohydrate degradation genes were more common in plant, soil, and marine environments.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed 9,725 unique plasmid sequences from a public database, focusing on their accessory traits and comparing them across different environments.

full_output.methodology: The study utilized in vitro experiments, including cellular uptake studies, drug release analysis, and antibacterial efficacy assessments, to evaluate the performance of rifampicin-loaded ILH microparticles.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization of antimicrobial resistance related genes in E. coli, Salmonella and Klebsiella isolates from broilers in the West Region of Cameroon.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified plasmid-mediated resistance genes for ESBL, quinolone, and aminoglycoside resistance in Enterobacteriaceae isolates from broilers in Cameroon. These genes included blaTEM, blaTEM-1, blaTEM-2, blaCTX-M, blaSHV-1, blaKPC, qnrA, qnrB, qnrS, qepA, aac(6')-IB-CR, aac(6')-IB, aph(3')-IA, and ant(2')-IA. The presence of these genes was not always correlated with phenotypic resistance, highlighting the need for more comprehensive methods to detect resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR and phenotypic susceptibility testing were used to detect plasmid-borne resistance genes in Enterobacteriaceae isolates.

full_output.methodology: The research involved designing a synthetic macrocyclic β-hairpin peptide library, screening for antibacterial activity using SLAY, and characterizing the peptides through biochemical and structural analyses.

full_output.key_findings: The study establishes mouse primary epidermal organoids (mPEOs) as a model for USA300 infection and evaluates drug testing methods. Vancomycin was shown to restore cell viability and inhibit bacterial internalization in a concentration-dependent manner.
full_output.methodology: The study used mPEOs to model USA300 infection and tested drug efficacy using various methods, including cell viability assays and immunofluorescence staining.

full_output.paper_title: Hybrid of Metapenaeus dobsoni lectin and platinum nanoparticles exert antimicrobial and immunostimulatory effects to reduce bacterial bioburden in infected Nile tilapia.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that the Pt-lec hybrid, composed of Metapenaeus dobsoni lectin (Md-Lec) and platinum nanoparticles (PtNPs), exhibits antimicrobial activity against fish pathogens such as Aeromonas hydrophila, Enterococcus fecalis, and Streptococcus iniae. It reduces bacterial bioburden in infected Nile tilapia and enhances the expression of immune-related genes (LEC, Myd88, and COX-2).
full_output.methodology: The study utilized resazurin microtiter assay (REMA) to determine MIC, fluorescence quenching, membrane permeability assays, scanning electron microscopy, and lipid peroxidation assays to evaluate the antimicrobial mechanism of Pt-lec. In vivo studies were conducted on Nile tilapia to assess therapeutic efficacy.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified antibiotic resistance patterns in binary toxin-positive Clostridioides difficile isolates, noting that ST1 strains exhibited higher resistance to moxifloxacin, clindamycin, and rifaximin. Metronidazole resistance was also observed in some isolates.
full_output.methodology: Multi-locus sequence typing and antibiotic susceptibility testing were performed on 58 binary toxin-positive C. difficile isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Expanded catalogue of metagenome-assembled genomes reveals resistome characteristics and athletic performance-associated microbes in horse.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a diverse array of antibiotic resistance genes (ARG) in the horse gut microbiome, highlighting the widespread use of antibiotics in horse management. The resistome characteristics were analyzed alongside the identification of microbes associated with athletic performance.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput metagenomic sequencing and bioinformatic analysis were used to assemble metagenome-assembled genomes (MAG) and identify antibiotic resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Genome-Wide Identification of Fluoroquinolone-Stabilized Gyrase Cleavage Sites in Starving E. coli
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies genome-wide fluoroquinolone-stabilized DNA gyrase cleavage sites and shows that the distribution of these sites correlates with bacterial persistence. It highlights the importance of DNA gyrase cleavage strength in determining persister levels.
full_output.methodology: The study used GCS-seq, qPCR, and bioinformatic analysis to map DNA gyrase cleavage sites and assess their correlation with bacterial persistence.

full_output.paper_title: Bacteriology of community-acquired pneumonia, antimicrobial susceptibility pattern and associated risk factors among HIV patients, Northeast Ethiopia: cross-sectional study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high rates of multidrug resistance among bacterial isolates from HIV patients with community-acquired pneumonia in Northeast Ethiopia, highlighting the need for routine antimicrobial susceptibility testing.
full_output.methodology: Cross-sectional study involving sputum sample collection, bacterial isolation, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Microbial spectrum and drug resistance of pathogens cultured from gallbladder bile specimens of patients with cholelithiasis: A single-center retrospective study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae as the most frequent gram-negative bacteria in bile cultures, along with Enterococcus spp. as gram-positive bacteria. E. coli showed high resistance to cephalosporins and penicillins, but was generally susceptible to carbapenems. K. pneumoniae exhibited a similar resistance pattern to E. coli. Enterococcus spp. were mostly sensitive to glycopeptides and penicillin, except for some E. faecium strains.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of bile cultures and antibiotic susceptibility testing of patients with cholelithiasis.

full_output.paper_title: Dual Action of Eeyarestatin 24 on Sec-Dependent Protein Secretion and Bacterial DNA.

full_output.paper_title: Maternal colonization with group B Streptococcus and antibiotic resistance in China: systematic review and meta-analyses.

full_output.paper_title: In vivo pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic evaluation of cefepime/taniborbactam combination against cefepime-non-susceptible Enterobacterales and Pseudomonas aeruginosa in a murine pneumonia model.

full_output.methodology: High-throughput screening and acetylation activity assays were used to identify and characterize Eis inhibitors.

full_output.paper_title: Impact of COVID-19 pandemic on multidrug resistant gram positive and gram negative pathogens: A systematic review.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that the COVID-19 pandemic had varying effects on the rates of multidrug-resistant gram-positive and gram-negative pathogens. It reported increases in MRSA, CRAB, and CRE infections, while decreases were noted in ESBL-producing Enterobacteriaceae and CRPA. The findings highlight the complex relationship between the pandemic and antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review of studies published from the start of the COVID-19 pandemic to July 2022, focusing on the impact of the pandemic on multidrug-resistant pathogens.

full_output.paper_title: DNase I and chitosan enhance efficacy of ceftazidime to eradicate Burkholderia pseudomallei biofilm cells.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that DNase I enhances the efficacy of ceftazidime (CAZ) against Burkholderia pseudomallei biofilm cells by degrading extracellular DNA (eDNA), thereby reducing biofilm formation and increasing susceptibility to CAZ. full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro experiments involving biofilm formation, crystal violet staining, confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM), and bacterial enumeration techniques to evaluate the effects of DNase I and CS/CAZ on B. pseudomallei biofilms.

full_output.paper_title: Local characteristics of molecular epidemiolgy of Acinetobacter baumannii in Jilin province (northeast China).

Carbapenem resistance was prevalent, with over 94% of isolates resistant to at least one carbapenem. Certain STs were associated with carbapenem resistance, indicating the role of resistance in the spread of these strains.
full_output.methodology: MLST analysis, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and phylogenetic analysis were conducted to characterize the molecular epidemiology of A. baumannii isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified various antimicrobial resistance genes, including beta-lactamases such as bla TEM-1, bla CTX-M-2, bla KPC-2, bla OXA-726, imiH, bla OXA-18, and bla TOHO-1, as well as the mcr-3 gene for colistin resistance in Aeromonas hydrophila strain 34SFC-3. full_output.paper_title: Clostridioides difficile in South American Camelids in Germany: First Insights into Molecular and Genetic Characteristics and Antimicrobial Resistance.

full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and molecular characterization techniques were employed to identify AMR genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Comparison of Lateral Flow Immunochromatography and Phenotypic Assays to PCR for the Detection of Carbapenemase-Producing Gram-Negative Bacteria, a Multicenter Experience in Mexico.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes various carbapenemase genes, including bla_NDM-1, bla_NDM-5, bla_KPC-2, bla_KPC3, bla_OXA-181, bla_OXA-232, bla_VIM-2, bla_IMP-15, bla_IMP-75, and bla_IMP-62, in carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales and Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from Mexico.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and phenotypic assays were used to detect and characterize carbapenemase-producing bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Enhancing Antibiotics Efficacy by Combination of Kuraridin and Epicatechin Gallate with Antimicrobials against Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that the combination of ECG and kuraridin enhances the antibacterial activities of gentamicin, fusidic acid, and vancomycin against MRSA in vitro. It also shows that ECG and kuraridin are non-cytotoxic and have anti-inflammatory properties.
full_output.methodology: The study used checkerboard and time-kill assays to evaluate the synergy between ECG, kuraridin, and antibiotics against MRSA strains. It also assessed the anti-inflammatory effects of ECG and kuraridin on human PBMCs and tested the in vivo efficacy in a murine pneumonia model.

full_output.paper_title: First Report of IMI-2-Producing Enterobacter bugandensis and CTX-M-55-Producing Escherichia coli isolated from Healthy Volunteers in Tunisia.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first detection of IMI-2-producing Enterobacter bugandensis and CTX-M-55-producing Escherichia coli in healthy volunteers in Tunisia, highlighting the presence of extended-spectrum beta-lactamases and carbapenemases in the fecal microbiota of healthy individuals.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, whole-genome-sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize the resistance genes and mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of the Efficiency of Random and Diblock Methacrylate-Based Amphiphilic Cationic Polymers against Major Bacterial Pathogens Associated with Cystic Fibrosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates methacrylate-based cationic copolymers for their antibacterial efficiency against major cystic fibrosis pathogens, identifying four copolymers with potent activity and low toxicity.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial activity was assessed via MIC determination, cytotoxicity was evaluated using BEAS-2B cells, and mechanisms of action were studied through membrane permeabilization and lipid insertion assays.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiofilm and Anti-Quorum-Sensing Activities of Novel Pyrazole and Pyrazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidine Derivatives as Carbonic Anhydrase I and II Inhibitors: Design, Synthesis, Radiosterilization, and Molecular Docking Studies.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several pyrazole and pyrazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidine derivatives with significant antibacterial, antibiofilm, and anti-quorum-sensing activities. These compounds show potent inhibition of human carbonic anhydrase I and II isoforms.
full_output.methodology: The study involves the synthesis of novel pyrazole and pyrazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidine derivatives, assessment of their antibacterial and antibiofilm activities, and evaluation of their inhibitory effects on carbonic anhydrase enzymes.

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the potential of repurposing antidepressants and phenothiazine antipsychotics as efflux pump inhibitors in both cancer and infectious diseases, highlighting their ability to modulate efflux pump activity and enhance the effectiveness of antimicrobial and anticancer agents.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews existing literature on the antibacterial and anticancer effects of antidepressants and antipsychotics, focusing on their mechanisms of action, particularly their impact on efflux pumps.

full_output.paper_title: Microbial Resistance to Antibiotics and Biofilm Formation of Bacterial Isolates from Different Carp Species and Risk Assessment for Public Health.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that bacterial isolates from different carp species exhibited resistance to multiple antibiotics, with biofilm formation contributing to increased multidrug resistance. Antibiotic residues were detected in fish samples, highlighting potential public health risks.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed bacterial isolates from carp fish samples, assessed antibiotic resistance using the Kirby-Bauer method, and evaluated antibiotic residues through LC-MS/MS analysis.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that 15.38% of H. pylori isolates were resistant to clarithromycin, highlighting the importance of antibiotic susceptibility testing in guiding treatment for pediatric H. pylori infections.

full_output.paper_title: Characteristics of tet(X4)-Producing Escherichia coli in Chicken and Pig Farms in Hunan Province, China.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of Carbapenemase and Extended-Spectrum β-Lactamase Producing Enterobacteriaceae: A Cross-Sectional Study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the prevalence of carbapenemase (KPC, NDM, OXA-48) and extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) producing Enterobacteriaceae, highlighting the high levels of resistance to carbapenems and third-generation cephalosporins.
full_output.methodology: The study employed a cross-sectional design with microbiological analysis, including disk diffusion, carbapenem inhibition tests, and multiplex real-time PCR for gene detection.

full_output.key_findings: The study differentiated Escherichia fergusonii and Escherichia coli using adk gene phylogenetic analysis and found high rates of antimicrobial resistance, particularly to erythromycin, ampicillin, ciprofloxacin, and third-generation cephalosporins, with a significant proportion of isolates producing extended-spectrum beta-lactamases (ESBLs).

full_output.methodology: Microtiter plate assay for biofilm quantification and statistical analysis of gene associations.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Characterization of Community- and Hospital- Acquired Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus Isolates during COVID-19 Pandemic.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterized 12 biofilm-associated adhesion genes in MRSA isolates, highlighting their role in biofilm formation and resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Relationship between Penicillin-Binding Proteins Alterations and β-Lactams Non-Susceptibility of Diseased Pig-Isolated Streptococcus suis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple mutations in penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs) that are associated with β-lactam non-susceptibility in Streptococcus suis isolates from diseased pigs. Key mutations include P409T in PBP1a, T584A and H588Y in PBP2a, T625R in PBP2b, and M341I in PBP2x, which contribute to resistance against penicillin, ampicillin, amoxicillin/clavulanic acid, and other β-lactams.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze mutations in PBPs and their association with β-lactam resistance in S. suis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Susceptibility and Molecular Features of Colonizing Isolates of Pseudomonas aeruginosa and the Report of a Novel Sequence Type (ST) 3910 from Thailand.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antimicrobial resistance genes in Pseudomonas aeruginosa colonizing isolates, including bla OXA-50, aph(3′)-IIb, fosA, bla PAO, catB7, and crpP, which confer resistance to beta-lactam, aminoglycoside, fosfomycin, chloramphenicol, and ciprofloxacin. A novel sequence type ST-3910 was also reported.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several β-lactamase genes (bla CTX-M, bla TEM, bla OXA-1) and integron-related genes (intl1, merA, merC) associated with multidrug resistance in ESBL-producing E. coli isolates from the UK.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the effect of glycosylation of ultrashort cationic lipopeptides (USCLs) on their antimicrobial activity, cytotoxicity, and hemolytic activity. Glycosylation did not consistently enhance antimicrobial activity or reduce cytotoxicity, but certain glycosylated derivatives showed improved activity against specific pathogens.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of lipopeptides, antimicrobial activity testing via broth microdilution, biofilm activity assessment, hemolysis assay, and cytotoxicity evaluation using MTT assay.

full_output.key_findings: An rpoB mutation associated with rifampin resistance was detected in 53% of biofilms from artificial urinary sphincter devices.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic and Genomic Insights into Biofilm Formation in Antibiotic-Resistant Clinical Coagulase-Negative Staphylococcus Species from South Africa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several genes associated with biofilm formation and adherence in coagulase-negative staphylococci, including icaA, icaB, icaC, atl, ebp, ebh, clfA, sdrC, sdrG, sdrH, sdrE, ebpC, pavA, flmH, and IS256. These genes were detected through whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify genes associated with biofilm formation and adherence in coagulase-negative staphylococci.

full_output.paper_title: Fast Track Diagnostic Tools for Clinical Management of Sepsis: Paradigm Shift from Conventional to Advanced Methods.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the evolution of diagnostic tools for sepsis, emphasizing the transition from conventional methods to advanced technologies. It highlights the limitations of traditional culture-based methods and explores modern molecular techniques like PCR, real-time PCR, SERS, and MALDI-TOF for faster and more accurate pathogen and AMR detection.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews existing literature on conventional and modern diagnostic methods for sepsis, focusing on their efficacy, limitations, and applications in detecting pathogens and antimicrobial resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of Multidrug-Resistant Bacteria (Enteropathogens) Recovered from a Blend of Pig Manure and Pinewood Saw Dust during Anaerobic Co-Digestion in a Steel Biodigester.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multidrug-resistant bacteria in a mixture of pig manure and pine wood saw dust, highlighting resistance to erythromycin, sulfamethoxazole, amoxicillin, tetracycline, and cefotaxime. High multiple antibiotic resistance (MAR) indices were observed, indicating resistance to multiple antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study used the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method to assess antibiotic susceptibility of bacterial isolates from pig manure and pine wood saw dust samples.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis and Antibacterial Evaluation of Ciprofloxacin Congeners with Spirocyclic Amine Periphery.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis and antibacterial evaluation of novel ciprofloxacin congeners with spirocyclic amine peripheries. These compounds exhibited varying degrees of antibacterial activity against the ESKAPE pathogens, with some showing potent activity against several of these bacteria, though none were active against Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: The compounds were synthesized and evaluated for antibacterial activity using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method and minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) testing.

full_output.paper_title: Optimized Antimicrobial Peptide Jelleine-I Derivative Br-J-I Inhibits Fusobacterium Nucleatum to Suppress Colorectal Cancer Progression.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Br-J-I as an optimized antimicrobial peptide derivative with potent antibacterial activity against Fusobacterium nucleatum (Fn), effectively inhibiting Fn-induced tumor promotion and inflammation in colorectal cancer (CRC).
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antibacterial activity of Br-J-I against Fn using MIC and MBC assays, assessed membrane disruption via NPN and PI fluorescence, and examined the impact of Br-J-I on CRC tumor growth and inflammation in vivo.

full_output.key_findings: The study describes the synthesis and biological evaluation of new semisynthetic penicillins incorporating 5-mercapto-1,2,4-triazole derivatives, showing antibacterial activity similar to amoxicillin.
full_output.methodology: Chemical synthesis, structural characterization via spectroscopy, and biological activity testing including MIC determination and toxicity assessment.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in metagenomic assemblies from apical periodontal infections, highlighting the presence of multidrug resistance mechanisms in Enterobacter and Pseudomonas species.

full_output.paper_title: Farming Practice Influences Antimicrobial Resistance Burden of Non-Aureus Staphylococci in Pig Husbandries.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that organic and alternative pig farming practices are associated with reduced antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in non-aureus staphylococci (NAS) compared to conventional farming. Specific AMR genes such as mecA, blaZ, blaPC1, and others were more prevalent in conventional farms, while organic farms showed lower levels of AMR genes for aminoglycosides, phenicols, and tetracyclines.
full_output.methodology: Genomic screening and phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze AMR genes and resistance profiles in NAS isolates from different farming practices.

The strains exhibited resistance to multiple antibiotics, including beta-lactams and nitrofurantoin.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR for identifying E. coli strains, antibiotic susceptibility testing via the Kirby-Bauer method, and detection of virulence genes through PCR. Biofilm formation was quantified using microtiter plates.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterized PVL-positive MRSA isolates in Northern Bavaria, Germany, from 2009 to 2016, identifying dominant clonal complexes (CC8, CC30, CC80) and highlighting their resistance profiles, particularly to erythromycin and clindamycin, while noting sensitivity to vancomycin and linezolid.
full_output.methodology: The study used MALDI-TOF MS for identification, PCR for detecting mecA and PVL genes, and antibiotic susceptibility testing via VITEK 2 or disk diffusion.

full_output.paper_title: Hybrid Genomic Analysis of Salmonella enterica Serovar Enteritidis SE3 Isolated from Polluted Soil in Brazil.

It also noted the presence of multidrug-resistant strains, particularly among gram-negative aerobic bacilli.
full_output.methodology: The study employed a prospective observational design with standardized diagnostic protocols, including culture techniques, molecular identification, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) using EUCAST breakpoints.

full_output.paper_title: Staphylococcus aureus and MRSA in Livestock: Antimicrobial Resistance and Genetic Lineages.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the presence of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) in livestock, identifying specific clonal lineages and resistance genes such as mecA and mecC. It highlights the diversity of MRSA clones and their association with multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed S. aureus isolates from various livestock species, detecting resistance genes and clonal lineages through molecular techniques.

full_output.methodology: Molecular detection of antimicrobial resistance genes and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were performed.

full_output.paper_title: Conjugative RP4 Plasmid-Mediated Transfer of Antibiotic Resistance Genes to Commensal and Multidrug-Resistant Enteric Bacteria In Vitro.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the transfer of the RP4 plasmid, which contains the beta-lactamase gene bla, to various enteric bacteria, highlighting the potential for horizontal gene transfer of antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: In vitro conjugation experiments, antibiotic resistance profiling, and molecular techniques such as colony PCR and fluorescence microscopy were used to assess plasmid transfer and resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Susceptibility and Virulence of Enterobacteriaceae Isolated from Urinary Tract Infections in Benin.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various Enterobacteriaceae species, including E. coli, S. marcescens, and K. ornithinolytica, with high resistance rates to antibiotics such as erythromycin, cefixime, and ampicillin. Additionally, 40% of the strains were biofilm-forming, and 6% were ESBL-producing. Virulence genes such as Sfa, IronB, iucD, and Cnf were prevalent among the isolates.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, ESBL detection, biofilm formation assessment, and molecular detection of virulence genes via PCR were performed.

full_output.paper_title: Fighting Antibiotic Resistance: New Pyrimidine-Clubbed Benzimidazole Derivatives as Potential DHFR Inhibitors.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the design and development of pyrimidine-clubbed benzimidazole derivatives as potential DHFR inhibitors. Compounds 27, 29, 30, 33, 37, 38, and 41 were synthesized and tested for their antibacterial and antifungal activities. These compounds showed significant inhibition of DHFR, suggesting their potential as antimicrobial agents.
full_output.methodology: The compounds were designed using ADMET and drug-likeness calculations, followed by molecular docking studies. Synthesis was performed using a modified Biginelli reaction, and biological evaluation was conducted using the broth dilution method.

full_output.paper_title: Napyradiomycin A4 and Its Relate Compounds, a New Anti-PRV Agent and Their Antibacterial Activities, from Streptomyces kebangsaanensis WS-68302.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified napyradiomycin A4 (1) and A80915H (2) as new compounds with antiviral activity against PRV and antibacterial activity against various bacteria, including Streptococcus suis and Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae.
full_output.methodology: The compounds were isolated from Streptomyces kebangsaanensis WS-68302 through fermentation and purification techniques, followed by evaluation of their antiviral and antibacterial activities using in vitro assays.

full_output.paper_title: Anti-Struvite, Antimicrobial, and Anti-Inflammatory Activities of Aqueous and Ethanolic Extracts of Saussurea costus (Falc) Lipsch Asteraceae.
full_output.key_findings: The ethanolic extract of Saussurea costus showed significant anti-struvite activity, inhibiting struvite crystallization by 87.45%. It also exhibited antimicrobial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Klebsiella pneumoniae, with MIC values of 50 mg/mL and 200 mg/mL, respectively. Additionally, the ethanolic extract demonstrated anti-inflammatory effects in vivo.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the anti-struvite, antimicrobial, and anti-inflammatory activities of aqueous and ethanolic extracts of Saussurea costus using in vitro crystallization assays, disk diffusion, MIC/MBC tests, and an in vivo carrageenan-induced edema test in rats.

full_output.paper_title: Cinnamomum sp. and Pelargonium odoratissimum as the Main Contributors to the Antibacterial Activity of the Medicinal Drink Horchata: A Study Based on the Antibacterial and Chemical Analysis of 21 Plants.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Cinnamomum sp. and Pelargonium odoratissimum as the plants with the strongest antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and MRSA, with Cinnamomum sp. showing a MIC of 250 µg/mL and P. odoratissimum showing a MIC of 500 µg/mL. The active compounds in these plants were identified through HPLC-DAD-MS/MS analysis.
full_output.methodology: The antibacterial activity of 21 plant extracts was evaluated using well diffusion and microdilution assays. HPLC-DAD-MS/MS was used to identify the chemical compounds in the extracts.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial and Biofilm-Preventing Activity of l-Borneol Possessing 2(5H)-Furanone Derivative F131 against S. aureus—C. albicans Mixed Cultures.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic Resistance and Biofilm Formation in Enterococcus spp. Isolated from Urinary Tract Infections.
