The presence of biofilm-related genes esp, ebpA, and ebpB was confirmed in all isolates.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing, biofilm formation assessment via Congo red agar and microtiter plate methods, and PCR detection of biofilm-related genes.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance and Genetic Diversity of Pseudomonas aeruginosa Strains Isolated from Equine and Other Veterinary Samples.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in Pseudomonas aeruginosa strains isolated from equine and other veterinary samples, including beta-lactamases, aminoglycoside modifying enzymes, quinolone resistance genes, sulfonamide resistance genes, phenicol resistance genes, tetracycline resistance genes, and efflux pumps. Additionally, genes conferring resistance to quaternary ammonium compounds were detected.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were conducted on 41 P. aeruginosa strains.

full_output.methodology: The study conducted antimicrobial susceptibility testing and risk assessment modeling to evaluate the presence and impact of antimicrobial-resistant Vibrio parahaemolyticus in grey mullets.

full_output.paper_title: Klebsiella pneumoniae carrying multiple alleles of antigen 43-encoding gene of Escherichia coli associated with biofilm formation.

full_output.paper_title: Genome-wide screen in human plasma identifies multifaceted complement evasion of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified srgA, purD, and bioB as key genes involved in Pseudomonas aeruginosa's ability to survive in human plasma by modulating complement evasion and metabolic pathways.
full_output.methodology: Genome-wide transposon sequencing (Tn-seq) and survival assays in human plasma.

full_output.paper_title: Switching from membrane disrupting to membrane crossing, an effective strategy in designing antibacterial polypeptide.

full_output.methodology: Synthesis and evaluation of poly-beta-peptides for antibacterial activity and toxicity.

full_output.paper_title: Exploiting a conjugative endogenous CRISPR-Cas3 system to tackle multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the successful use of a native CRISPR-Cas3 system to cure IncFII plasmids carrying blaKPC genes in multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae, significantly reducing plasmid carriage and antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: CRISPR-Cas3 system engineering, conjugation assays, plasmid curing, and in vivo evaluation in Galleria mellonella.

full_output.paper_title: Genome sequencing and comparative genomic analysis of bovine mastitis-associated Staphylococcus aureus strains from India.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 17 antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes among 41 bovine mastitis-associated Staphylococcus aureus strains from India, including genes such as arlR, mepR, norA, mgrA, lmrS, fosB, murA, GlpT, arlS, dfrG, blaZ, gyrA, parC, mepA, tet(K), TEM-116, and TEM181. All the strains were methicillin-susceptible S. aureus (MSSA).
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and comparative genomic analysis were conducted to identify AMR genes and virulence factors in the strains.

full_output.paper_title: Integrated surveillance of extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Salmonella and Escherichia coli from humans and animal species raised for human consumption in Canada from 2012 to 2017.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various ESBL genes, including bla TEM, bla SHV, bla CTX-M, bla OXA, and bla CMY-2, in ESBL-producing E. coli and Salmonella isolates from agrifood and human sources in Canada. These genes were found to confer resistance to beta-lactam antibiotics such as ceftiofur and ceftriaxone.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized PCR and whole genome sequencing (WGS) to detect and characterize ESBL genes in E. coli and Salmonella isolates from various sources in Canada.

full_output.paper_title: A Cross-Validated Feature Selection (CVFS) approach for extracting the most parsimonious feature sets and discovering potential antimicrobial resistance (AMR) biomarkers.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a Cross-Validated Feature Selection (CVFS) approach for identifying the most parsimonious gene sets for predicting antimicrobial resistance (AMR) from bacterial pan-genomes. The CVFS approach was able to extract both known and novel AMR genes, demonstrating its effectiveness in selecting relevant features for AMR prediction.
full_output.methodology: The CVFS approach involved splitting pan-genome datasets into sub-parts, performing feature selection, and intersecting features to identify the most representative gene sets for AMR prediction.
full_output.sample_size: 4216 Escherichia coli genomes and 7712 Salmonella enterica genomes

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the presence of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in bivalve molluscs, highlighting the spread of resistance to various antibiotics such as colistin, beta-lactams, fluoroquinolones, and tetracyclines. full_output.paper_title: Computational protein design repurposed to explore enzyme vitality and help predict antibiotic resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study utilized computational protein design to predict resistance mutations in dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) by analyzing enzyme vitality, focusing on changes in inhibitor and substrate binding. Several mutations were identified that could potentially confer resistance through alterations in binding affinities.
full_output.methodology: The research employed Monte Carlo simulations and adaptive landscape flattening to explore mutation spaces and predict resistance mechanisms in DHFR, focusing on vitality changes related to substrate and inhibitor binding.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular epidemiology, drug resistance, and virulence gene analysis of Streptococcus agalactiae isolates from dairy goats in backyard farms in China.

It highlights the importance of understanding MRSA transmission and pathophysiology in both human and animal populations.

full_output.paper_title: Ampicillinase C Beta-lactamase Producers among Isolates of Enterobacteriaceae in a Tertiary Care Centre: A Descriptive Cross-sectional Study.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that 10.19% of Enterobacteriaceae isolates were AmpC beta-lactamase producers, which showed resistance to fluoroquinolones and cotrimoxazole but were generally susceptible to carbapenems like meropenem.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic detection of AmpC beta-lactamase producers using cefoxitin-cloxacillin double-disc synergy test and antibiotic susceptibility testing via Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Pseudomonas aeruginosa Isolates among Clinical Samples showing Growth in a Tertiary Care Centre: A Descriptive Cross-sectional Study.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that 6.48% of clinical samples contained Pseudomonas aeruginosa, with 8.82% of these isolates being metallo-beta-lactamase (MBL)-positive. MBL-producing strains exhibited multidrug resistance and reduced susceptibility to several antibiotics, including imipenem, ceftazidime, and gentamicin.
full_output.methodology: The study used standard microbiological techniques for identification and the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method for antibiotic susceptibility testing. MBL production was detected using the Imipenem-EDTA combined disk method and Double disk synergy test.

full_output.paper_title: Occurrence and antimicrobial resistance pattern of E. coli O157:H7 isolated from foods of Bovine origin in Dessie and Kombolcha towns, Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: All E. coli O157:H7 isolates were resistant to Penicillin G, Vancomycin, and Oxacillin, while being susceptible to Ampicillin, Sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim, and Norfloxacin. Multidrug resistance was observed among all isolates.
full_output.methodology: Agar disk diffusion method was used to evaluate antimicrobial susceptibility of E. coli O157:H7 isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis and Testing of Analogs of the Tuberculosis Drug Candidate SQ109 against Bacteria and Protozoa: Identification of Lead Compounds against Mycobacterium abscessus and Malaria Parasites.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified SQ109 analogs with improved activity against Mycobacterium abscessus, bacteria lacking MmpL3, and malaria parasites. Some analogs showed enhanced potency compared to SQ109, particularly against P. falciparum. The research also explored the binding of these compounds to MmpL3 and their effects on lipid membranes.
full_output.methodology: The study synthesized 19 SQ109 analogs and tested their activity against various bacteria and protozoa using MIC and IC50 assays. Surface plasmon resonance and differential scanning calorimetry were used to analyze MmpL3 binding and membrane interactions.

full_output.paper_title: Development of a Peptide-Based Nanocarrier for Controlled Release of Vancomycin Against MRSA
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a peptide-based nanocarrier (ECnVs) for controlled release of vancomycin against MRSA, demonstrating improved antibacterial effects through sustained release and matrix retention.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the physical properties, vancomycin release kinetics, and antibacterial effects of ECnVs in collagen and co-gel matrices.

full_output.paper_title: Virulence and antibiotic-resistance genes in Enterococcus faecalis associated with streptococcosis disease in fish.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various antibiotic-resistance genes in three strains of Enterococcus faecalis associated with streptococcosis in fish, including genes conferring resistance to tetracycline, macrolide-lincosamide-streptogramin, and vancomycin.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis and sequencing of three E. faecalis strains isolated from fish with streptococcosis.

full_output.key_findings: The study introduces BacDrop, a droplet-based single-cell RNA-seq technology for bacteria, revealing heterogeneous cellular states in Klebsiella pneumoniae under antibiotic stress. It highlights the role of mobile genetic elements (MGEs) and specific gene expressions, such as cspD, in antibiotic resistance and persistence.
full_output.methodology: BacDrop was developed using droplet-based microfluidics and validated through single-cell RNA-seq analysis, comparing transcriptional responses under different antibiotic treatments.

full_output.paper_title: Analysis of microbial keratitis incidence, isolates and in-vitro antimicrobial susceptibility in the East of England: a 6-year study.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports on the incidence, microbiological profile, and in vitro antimicrobial susceptibility of microbial keratitis (MK) in the East of England over a 6-year period. It identifies a significant rising trend of ceftriaxone resistance among gram-negative organisms.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of corneal scrapes from patients diagnosed with MK, including antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid emergence of extensively drug-resistant Shigella sonnei in France.

mutations_found.validated_by: analysis of the AMR genes and structures in XDR S. sonnei isolates
analysis of the AMR genes and structures in XDR S. sonnei isolates

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple AMR genes and mutations contributing to the emergence of extensively drug-resistant Shigella sonnei in France, including bla CTX-M-3, bla CTX-M-15, bla CTX-M-27, bla CTX-M-55, bla CTX-M-134, mphA, ermB, and qnr, along with chromosomal mutations in gyrA and parC.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis and antimicrobial susceptibility testing of 164 XDR S. sonnei isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Risk factors and molecular epidemiology of fecal carriage of carbapenem resistant Enterobacteriaceae in patients with liver disease.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla KPC-2 and bla NDM as the primary carbapenemase genes in CRE strains, with bla KPC-2 being the most prevalent. Additionally, the polymyxin resistance gene mcr-1 was detected in some E. coli strains.
full_output.methodology: PCR and DNA sequencing were used to characterize carbapenemase and polymyxin resistance genes in CRE isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Role of peptidoglycan recycling enzymes AmpD and AnmK in Acinetobacter baumannii virulence features.

AmpD.notes: The Δ ampD ::Kan mutant shows increased susceptibility to fosfomycin.

AnmK.notes: The Δ anmK ::Kan mutant shows increased susceptibility to fosfomycin.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that the peptidoglycan recycling enzymes AmpD and AnmK contribute to intrinsic fosfomycin resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii. Deletion of these genes leads to increased susceptibility to fosfomycin and affects various virulence traits such as biofilm formation and twitching motility.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized genetic mutants (Δ ampD ::Kan and Δ anmK ::Kan) and their complemented strains to investigate the role of AmpD and AnmK in A. baumannii virulence and resistance. Techniques included transmission electron microscopy, cell permeability assays, growth curve analysis, competition indices, and minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) testing.

full_output.paper_title: Development of a novel loop-mediated isothermal amplification assay for ß-lactamase gene identification using clinical isolates of Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed LAMP assays for four β-lactamase genes (bla KPC, bla NDM-1, bla IMP-1 group, and bla VIM) and validated their specificity and sensitivity using clinical isolates of Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.methodology: LAMP assays were developed and validated using clinical isolates and reference strains, with comparisons to PCR for sensitivity and specificity.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiology, antimicrobial resistance, and mortality risk factors of carbapenem resistant gram-negative bacteria in hematopoietic stem cell transplantation recipients.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the high prevalence and mortality rate of carbapenem-resistant gram-negative bacteria (CRGNB) infections in hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) recipients. It identifies several risk factors associated with mortality, including prolonged time from diagnosis to transplantation, septic shock, low platelet count, and elevated bilirubin levels.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective case-control study analyzing clinical data from HSCT recipients with CRGNB infections, including assessment of antimicrobial resistance patterns and risk factors for mortality.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular insights into novel environmental strains of Klebsiella quasipneumoniae harboring different antimicrobial-resistance genes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antimicrobial resistance genes in novel environmental strains of Klebsiella quasipneumoniae, including fosA, bla OKP, oqxB, oqxA, bla SHV−1, bla OXA−1, aac(6')-Ib-cr, catB, and aph(3”)-Ia, which confer resistance to various antibiotics such as fosfomycin, beta-lactams, aminoglycosides, and chloramphenicol.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to characterize the antimicrobial resistance genes and virulence factors in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: The gut metagenome harbors metabolic and antibiotic resistance signatures of moderate-to-severe asthma.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified an increased richness of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in the gut microbiota of individuals with moderate-to-severe asthma, with ermF being a notable macrolide resistance marker co-occurring with the Bacteroides fragilis toxin.
full_output.methodology: Whole metagenomic shotgun sequencing of fecal samples followed by functional annotation and differential abundance analysis.

full_output.paper_title: The QseB response regulator imparts tolerance to positively charged antibiotics by controlling metabolism and minor changes to LPS.

qseB.notes: Deletion of qseB leads to increased susceptibility to polymyxin B.
qseB.source: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
qseB.evidence_note: The paper states that deletion of qseB leads to increased susceptibility to polymyxin B, and that QseB is involved in mediating resistance to positively charged antibiotics.

full_output.key_findings: QseB, a transcription factor, mediates resistance to positively charged antibiotics by controlling metabolism and LPS modifications. Deletion of qseB increases susceptibility to polymyxin B.
full_output.methodology: Survival assays, metabolite measurements, RNA sequencing, and ChIP-on-chip experiments were used to analyze the role of QseB in antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: A novel strategy to characterize the pattern of β-lactam antibiotic-induced drug resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the β-lactamase expression patterns in Acinetobacter baumannii in response to different β-lactam antibiotics, identifying variations in the expression of AmpC and OXA β-lactamases.
full_output.methodology: Label-free LC-MS-based quantitative proteomics to analyze β-lactamase expression in response to various β-lactam antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of macrolide-lincosamide-streptogramin resistant lactic acid bacteria isolated from food samples.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the presence of MLS resistance genes ermB, mefA/E, msrA/B, and msrC in lactic acid bacteria isolated from food samples, highlighting the prevalence of macrolide-lincosamide-streptogramin resistance in LAB.
full_output.methodology: PCR, gene expression analysis, and MIC testing were used to characterize MLS resistance genes in lactic acid bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Editorial: Resistance to third-generation tetracyclines

tet(X4).evidence_note: Mutations reported in this review paper are sourced from cited studies. Original experimental data is in the referenced publications.

full_output.key_findings: The editorial discusses the emergence and spread of plasmid-encoded tet(X4) genes, which confer resistance to third-generation tetracyclines, particularly in Escherichia coli, Enterobacterales, and Acinetobacter spp.
full_output.methodology: Literature review and analysis of plasmid-mediated resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: β-LacFamPred: An online tool for prediction and classification of β-lactamase class, subclass, and family.
full_output.key_findings: The paper presents β-LacFamPred, a machine learning-based tool for predicting and classifying β-lactamase (BL) families. It uses hidden Markov models (HMMs) trained on a comprehensive dataset of BL sequences to accurately predict BL classes, subclasses, and families.
full_output.methodology: The paper describes the development of β-LacFamPred using HMMs trained on a dataset of BL sequences from multiple sources, including CBMAR, BLDB, CARD, UniProtKB, and NCBI NR. The tool was validated using independent datasets and compared with existing methods.

full_output.paper_title: Analysis of drug resistance among difficult-to-treat tuberculosis patients in Ghana identifies several pre-XDR TB cases.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several pre-XDR TB cases in Ghana, highlighting the presence of mutations in katG, rpoB, gyrA, rrs, and eis genes associated with resistance to isoniazid, rifampicin, fluoroquinolones, and aminoglycosides.
full_output.methodology: Genotyping using MTBDR plus and MTBDR sl assays to detect drug resistance mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates from sputum samples.

full_output.paper_title: Gossypol acetate: A natural polyphenol derivative with antimicrobial activities against the essential cell division protein FtsZ.

ftsZ.mechanism: inhibits GTPase activity and stabilizes polymerization
ftsZ.validation_method: in vitro GTPase assay, light scattering assay, ITC

full_output.key_findings: Gossypol acetate (S2303) exhibits antimicrobial activity against Gram-positive bacteria such as Bacillus subtilis and Staphylococcus aureus, and against Gram-negative bacteria when the outer membrane is permeabilized. It targets the essential cell division protein FtsZ, inhibiting its GTPase activity and disrupting Z-ring formation, leading to cell division defects.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial activity assays, time-kill assays, phase-contrast microscopy, GTPase activity assays, isothermal titration calorimetry, and molecular docking studies were used to evaluate the effects of S2303 on FtsZ and bacterial cell division.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial mechanism of semi-bionic extracts of three traditional medicinal plants-Rheum palmatum L., Scutellaria baicalensis Georgi, and Houttuynia cordata Thunb-That can be used as antibiotic alternatives.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that SEDQS significantly inhibited the growth of S. enteritidis, destroyed the cell membrane structure, and reduced the expression of several virulence genes.
full_output.methodology: The study used microwell-plate method to determine MIC, and various biochemical assays to analyze the effect of SEDQS on bacterial growth, metabolism, and virulence gene expression.

full_output.paper_title: Resistance and Molecular Characteristics of Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus and Heterogeneous Vancomycin-Intermediate Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the mecA gene as a key factor in methicillin resistance among Staphylococcus aureus strains, with specific molecular types like ST59-t437-agr I-IVa and ST72-t2431-agr I-IVF showing high resistance to erythromycin and clindamycin.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing, spa typing, agr typing, MLST, and SCC mec typing were performed to analyze the molecular characteristics and resistance profiles of S. aureus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: C25-modified rifamycin derivatives with improved activity against Mycobacterium abscessus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Arr Mab as a key enzyme responsible for rifampicin resistance in Mycobacterium abscessus. It shows that 5j, a C25-modified rifamycin derivative, is not modified by Arr Mab, leading to improved antimicrobial activity against M. abscessus.
full_output.methodology: Enzymatic activity assays, thermal denaturation assays, and MIC testing were used to evaluate the resistance mechanisms and efficacy of rifamycin derivatives.

full_output.paper_title: Functional Diversity of Gram-Negative Permeability Barriers Reflected in Antibacterial Activities and Intracellular Accumulation of Antibiotics.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the permeability barriers of three Gram-negative pathogens, E. coli, P. aeruginosa, and A. baumannii, focusing on the roles of the outer membrane (OM) and active efflux pumps in antibiotic resistance. It highlighted species-specific differences in antibiotic permeation and resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized SPE-MS to measure intracellular accumulation of antibiotics and compared antibacterial activities across different strains with altered permeability barriers.

full_output.paper_title: PorinPredict: In Silico Identification of OprD Loss from WGS Data for Improved Genotype-Phenotype Predictions of P. aeruginosa Carbapenem Resistance.

OprD.notes: Missense mutations in nonsusceptible isolates affected residue R154 (corresponding to R131 when excluding the 23-amino-acid signal sequence), a critical site known to determine pore width (15); H288 and S403, which are both conserved across different members of the OprD family (15); multiple sites in β-strands (S278, Q340, L359) replaced by proline, which disrupts secondary structures; and G316, which forms a hydrogen bond to R391 (R393 in L8 12 ), part of the characteristic basic ladder in the OprD pore constriction (15) (Table 2).

full_output.paper_title: Biochemical Insights into Imipenem Collateral Susceptibility Driven by ampC Mutations Conferring Ceftolozane/Tazobactam Resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

ampC.mechanism: confers resistance to ceftolozane/tazobactam via structural modifications

ampC.notes: Mutations in the Ω-loop of ampC lead to increased resistance to ceftolozane/tazobactam and decreased resistance to imipenem.

full_output.key_findings: Mutations in the ampC gene of Pseudomonas aeruginosa enhance resistance to ceftolozane/tazobactam but reduce resistance to imipenem, leading to collateral susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: Enzyme kinetic analysis and structural modeling of AmpC mutants.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports that Leptotrichia species are rarely encountered but significant causes of bloodstream infections in neutropenic patients. It highlights high resistance rates to moxifloxacin and decreasing susceptibility to metronidazole.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of Leptotrichia bacteremia cases and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Bacterial drug-resistance and viability phenotyping upon disinfectant exposure revealed by single-nucleotide resolved-allele specific isothermal RNA amplification.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed the AlleRNA assay to detect quinolone resistance in Salmonella enterica by identifying mutations in the gyrA gene, which is critical for quinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: The AlleRNA assay combines NASBA and CRISPR-Cas13a to detect single nucleotide polymorphisms in gyrA mRNA, enabling the identification of quinolone-resistant Salmonella enterica.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several AMR genes, including beta-lactamases, aminoglycoside modifying enzymes, tetracycline resistance genes, quinolone resistance genes, macrolide resistance genes, and others, which are associated with differences in gut microbiome composition between CSD and VD infants.
full_output.methodology: High-resolution metagenomic analyses of gut microbiomes from infants born by vaginal delivery (VD) or caesarean section (CSD).

full_output.key_findings: The study identified Staphylococcus spp. as the most prevalent bacteria on the ocular surfaces of fighting bulls in Thailand, with some isolates showing multidrug resistance. full_output.methodology: Bacterial isolation, identification via MALDI-TOF MS, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing using agar disk diffusion.

full_output.paper_title: Extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli from pork in Muang district, Chiang Mai Province, Thailand.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified ESBL-producing E. coli in pork from various market types in Thailand, with a high prevalence of bla CTX-M, bla CTX-M-1, and bla TEM genes. These isolates exhibited multidrug resistance, particularly to beta-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex PCR and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to detect ESBL-producing E. coli and characterize their resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Phylogenetic analysis and antibiotic resistance of Escherichia coli isolated from wild and domestic animals at an agricultural land interface area of Salaphra wildlife sanctuary, Thailand.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in E. coli isolates from wild and domestic animals in Thailand, including blaTEM, blaSHV, blaCMY-2, aac(3)-IV, aadA, tetA, tetB, qnrA, sul3, dfrA1, dfrA5, and dfrA7, which conferred resistance to various antibiotics such as ampicillin, gentamicin, tetracycline, ciprofloxacin, and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole.
full_output.methodology: PCR and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to identify AMR genes and their corresponding resistance phenotypes in E. coli isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple plasmid-borne and chromosomal resistance genes in extensively drug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii isolates, highlighting the role of conjugative plasmids in the dissemination of resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Transiently silent acquired antimicrobial resistance: an emerging challenge in susceptibility testing.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the phenomenon of transiently silent acquired antimicrobial resistance (tsaAMR), where resistance genes are present but not expressed, and can be reactivated under certain conditions. It highlights the molecular mechanisms behind this, including mutations, IS insertions, and copy number variations.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews existing literature and case studies on tsaAMR, focusing on molecular mechanisms and clinical implications.

full_output.paper_title: New Delhi Metallo-Beta-Lactamase (NDM)-5 in Uropathogenic Klebsiella pneumoniae in a Tertiary Care Hospital in Jamaica.

full_output.paper_title: Recombinant Reporter Phage rTUN1::nLuc Enables Rapid Detection and Real-Time Antibiotic Susceptibility Testing of Klebsiella pneumoniae K64 Strains.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial peptides against polymyxin-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae: a patent review.
full_output.key_findings: The review highlights the development of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) targeting polymyxin-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae, emphasizing the need for new therapeutic approaches due to rising resistance levels.
full_output.methodology: A patent review analysis was conducted to assess innovations in antimicrobial peptides against polymyxin-resistant K. pneumoniae.

full_output.paper_title: CID12261165, a flavonoid compound as antibacterial agents against quinolone-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic and genotypic detection of resistance mechanisms in carbapenem-resistant gram-negative bacteria isolated from Egyptian ICU patients with first emergence of NDM-1 producing Klebsiella oxytoca.

full_output.paper_title: First report of SPM metallo-β-lactamases producing Acinetobacter baumannii isolates in Morocco.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first detection of SPM metallo-β-lactamase-producing Acinetobacter baumannii isolates in Morocco, along with the prevalence of various carbapenemase genes such as OXA-23, OXA-51, OXA-58, VIM, GIM, SIM, IMP, NDM, and SPM.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used for molecular characterization of carbapenemase genes in A. baumannii isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Bacteriological characteristics of hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae rmpA gene (hvKp-rmpA)-harboring strains in the south of Iran.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla SHV and bla CTX-M as prevalent ESBL genes in cKp isolates, while hvKp- rmpA + strains exhibited lower antibiotic resistance compared to cKp isolates. Additionally, bla NDM was detected in 7.8% of cKp isolates.
full_output.methodology: PCR, antibiotic susceptibility testing, and analysis of clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Screening and Drug Resistance Analysis of Non-Tuberculous Mycobacteria in Patients with Suspected Pulmonary Tuberculosis on the Hainan Island, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the prevalence and resistance characteristics of non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) in patients with suspected pulmonary tuberculosis on Hainan Island, China. It found that NTM infections were common, with M. avium complex (MAC) and M. abscessus complex (MABC) being the most frequently detected species. The study also highlighted the resistance profiles of these NTM species to various antibiotics, indicating that amikacin and clarithromycin were generally effective, while resistance to other antibiotics was prevalent.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the collection and analysis of respiratory specimens from 3025 patients with suspected tuberculosis. NTM species were identified using DNA chip technology and gene sequencing, and drug resistance was assessed through antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the micro broth dilution method.

full_output.paper_title: Menthone Exerts its Antimicrobial Activity Against Methicillin Resistant Staphylococcus aureus by Affecting Cell Membrane Properties and Lipid Profile.
full_output.key_findings: Menthone exhibits antimicrobial activity against MRSA, affecting cell membrane properties and lipid profile, leading to membrane potential depolarization and disruption of membrane integrity.
full_output.methodology: Integrated microbiology and lipidomics approach, including lipid profiling via UHPLC-QE-MS, membrane potential analysis, and molecular docking.

full_output.paper_title: Growth Arrest of Staphylococcus aureus Induces Daptomycin Tolerance via Cell Wall Remodelling.
full_output.key_findings: Growth arrest of Staphylococcus aureus leads to daptomycin tolerance through cell wall remodelling, involving increased peptidoglycan and wall teichoic acid (WTA) production, but not through membrane changes.
full_output.methodology: Experiments involving growth arrest with tetracycline, daptomycin exposure, and analysis of cell wall components.

full_output.paper_title: Tracking the Emergence and Dissemination of a bla(NDM-23) Gene in a Multidrug Resistance Plasmid of Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the emergence of a novel bla(NDM-23) allele in a multidrug resistance plasmid of Klebsiella pneumoniae, highlighting its dissemination through a ST437 clone in Spanish hospitals.

full_output.methodology: Negative-ion matrix-assisted laser desorption ionization–time of flight (MALDI-TOF) mass spectrometry, phagocytosis assays, and cytokine production analysis.

full_output.methodology: Genome-based k-mers approach for molecular characterization including antimicrobial resistance genes, virulence factors, MLST, serotypes, and plasmid types.

full_output.paper_title: Virulence genes and antimicrobial resistance in Enterococcus strains isolated from dogs and cats in Northeast China.

full_output.paper_title: Impact of short chain fatty acids (SCFAs) on antimicrobial activity of new β-lactam/β-lactamase inhibitor combinations and on virulence of Escherichia coli isolates.
full_output.key_findings: Short chain fatty acids (SCFAs) enhanced the susceptibility of E. coli isolates to β-lactam/β-lactamase inhibitor combinations and downregulated the expression of virulence genes.
full_output.methodology: Determination of MICs of SCFAs and β-lactam/β-lactamase inhibitor combinations, qRT-PCR for virulence gene expression, and assessment of bacterial growth and biofilm formation.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical Evaluation of Meropenem-Vaborbactam Combination for the Treatment of Urinary Tract Infection: Evidence to Date.
full_output.key_findings: Meropenem-vaborbactam shows effective activity against carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales, particularly those producing KPC enzymes, demonstrating improved clinical and microbiological outcomes in complicated urinary tract infections.
full_output.methodology: Phase 3 clinical trials evaluating the efficacy and safety of meropenem-vaborbactam in treating complicated urinary tract infections and acute pyelonephritis.

full_output.paper_title: Drug Resistance of Mycobacterium tuberculosis Based on Whole-Genome Sequencing in the Yi Ethnic Group, Sichuan Province, China.

full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing was used to analyze drug resistance mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis strains.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic insights of mcr-1 harboring Escherichia coli by geographical region and a One-Health perspective.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes various mcr-1 variants and other antibiotic resistance genes in Escherichia coli isolates from diverse geographical regions, emphasizing the prevalence of multidrug resistance and the role of plasmids in the spread of resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify and characterize antibiotic resistance genes and plasmid content in mcr-1 harboring E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Predominance of High-Level Tetracycline-Resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae in Kenya: Implications for Global Implementation of Doxycycline Postexposure Prophylaxis for Prevention of Sexually Transmitted Infections.
full_output.key_findings: High-level tetracycline resistance in Neisseria gonorrhoeae, mediated by the tet(M) gene, was prevalent among Kenyan women, potentially affecting the efficacy of doxycycline post-exposure prophylaxis.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of the tet(M) gene in archived Neisseria gonorrhoeae samples.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes a series of gold(III) complexes with antibacterial and antibiofilm properties, highlighting their effectiveness against various bacterial strains, including Gram-positive and Gram-negative species.
full_output.methodology: The paper describes the synthesis, characterization, and biological evaluation of gold(III) complexes, including antimicrobial testing and electrochemical analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Metagenomic Analysis of the Abundance and Composition of Antibiotic Resistance Genes in Hospital Wastewater in Benin, Burkina Faso, and Finland.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antibiotic resistance genes in hospital wastewater samples from Benin, Burkina Faso, and Finland, including carbapenemase genes like blaGES, blaOXA-5-like, and blaOXA-10-like, as well as genes conferring resistance to tetracyclines, fluoroquinolones, and macrolides. Notably, mcr-5 was widely detected in samples from all three countries.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic sequencing was used to analyze the abundance and composition of antibiotic resistance genes in hospital wastewater samples.

full_output.paper_title: Colloidal silver against macrophage infections and biofilms of atypical mycobacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the antimycobacterial activity of green synthesized colloidal silver (GSCS) against M. abscessus and MAIC clinical isolates in planktonic and biofilm forms as well as mycobacteria internalized within macrophages.

full_output.methodology: The research involved engineering a P4 cosmid system with CRISPR-Cas9 components and evaluating its efficacy in delivering antimicrobial effects through transduction experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Airborne antibiotic resistome and human health risk in railway stations during COVID-19 pandemic.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified an increase in airborne antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) during the COVID-19 pandemic, particularly those conferring resistance to macrolides, lincosamides, streptogramin B, chloramphenicol, beta-lactams, and fosfomycin. full_output.key_findings: The XDR-LFC assay was evaluated for the molecular detection of drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, identifying several resistance-conferring mutations in genes such as katG, inhA, ahpC, rpoB, gyrA, rrs, and eis.
full_output.methodology: The XDR-LFC assay was used to detect resistance-conferring mutations in M. tuberculosis, with results validated through phenotypic drug susceptibility testing (pDST) and whole-genome sequencing (WGS).

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of Oral Tebipenem as a Step-Down Therapy following Intravenous Ertapenem against Extended-Spectrum β-Lactamase-Producing Escherichia coli in a Hollow-Fiber In Vitro Infection Model.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated tebipenem as a step-down therapy from ertapenem for treating extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing E. coli. It identified several resistance mechanisms, including β-lactamases (CTX-M-15, OXA1, OXA30, CMY-2, TEM-1) and efflux pumps (AcrAB-TolC) and porins (OmpC), which conferred resistance to various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: In vitro hollow-fiber infection model and MIC testing.

full_output.paper_title: Seven Years of Culture Collection of Neisseria gonorrhoeae: Antimicrobial Resistance and Molecular Epidemiology.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed antimicrobial resistance in Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates from Italy over seven years, identifying increases in azithromycin and ciprofloxacin resistance, while cefixime resistance remained stable. It also highlighted the molecular epidemiology of the isolates, noting the predominance of certain sequence types and genogroups.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, NG-MAST, and comparative genomic analysis were used to assess resistance and genetic diversity.

full_output.paper_title: High occurrence of Enterococcus faecalis, Enterococcus faecium, and Vagococcus lutrae harbouring oxazolidinone resistance genes in raw meat-based diets for companion animals - a public health issue, Switzerland, September 2018 to May 2020.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of oxazolidinone resistance genes optrA, poxtA, and cfr in Enterococcus faecalis, Enterococcus faecium, and Vagococcus lutrae isolates from raw meat-based diets for companion animals in Switzerland. These genes confer resistance to oxazolidinones, highlighting a public health concern regarding the potential spread of resistant bacteria from pets to humans.
full_output.methodology: PCR, whole genome sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize the resistance genes and their associated resistance profiles.

full_output.paper_title: Bacteria and antimicrobial resistance profile during the composting process of wastes from animal production.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of antimicrobial resistance in bacteria isolated from animal waste during composting, particularly in Enterobacteriaceae, Morganellaceae, Pseudomonadaceae, and Moraxellaceae families. full_output.methodology: Bacterial strains were isolated from animal waste and identified using MALDI-TOF. Antimicrobial resistance was assessed via disk diffusion tests.

full_output.paper_title: Gold(I) selenium N-heterocyclic carbene complexes as potent antibacterial agents against multidrug-resistant gram-negative bacteria via inhibiting thioredoxin reductase.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the inhibition of thioredoxin reductase (TrxR) by gold(I) selenium N-heterocyclic carbene complexes H7 and H8 as a key mechanism against multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several AMR genes, including aadA, aacC1, emrE, and ant1, which are upregulated in co-cultures of A. baumannii and K. pneumoniae, contributing to increased resistance to antibiotics such as streptomycin and gentamicin.

full_output.paper_title: Metagenome-assembled genomes indicate that antimicrobial resistance genes are highly prevalent among urban bacteria and multidrug and glycopeptide resistances are ubiquitous in most taxa.

The research highlights the ubiquity of these resistance mechanisms across various bacterial taxa in urban environments.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) from urban metagenomes to analyze the prevalence and distribution of antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) using computational tools like DeepARG-LS and PlasFlow.

full_output.paper_title: The fate of sulfonamide resistance genes and anthropogenic pollution marker intI1 after discharge of wastewater into a pristine river stream.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of extended spectrum beta lactamase and molecular detection of blaTEM, blaSHV and blaCTX-M genotypes among Gram negative bacilli isolates from pediatric patient population in Gaza strip.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaTEM, blaSHV, and blaCTX-M genes as the primary contributors to extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) resistance in Gram-negative bacilli from pediatric patients in Gaza strip. These genes were prevalent among various bacterial species, with blaCTX-M being the most dominant.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic detection of ESBLs using double disk synergy and CHROMagar methods, along with molecular characterization via PCR targeting blaTEM, blaSHV, and blaCTX-M genes.

full_output.paper_title: Fructose promotes ampicillin killing of antibiotic-resistant Streptococcus agalactiae.

rodA.encodes: shape, elongation, division and sporulation family glycotransferase

acm.notes: five mutations including point mutation and frameshift mutation

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in rodA, acm, and pBp2× in ampicillin-resistant Streptococcus agalactiae (AR-GBS) and shows that fructose enhances ampicillin efficacy by reactivating glycolysis and increasing penicillin-binding protein expression.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, metabolomic analysis, qRT-PCR, and enzyme activity assays were used to characterize mutations and mechanisms of ampicillin resistance in AR-GBS.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic and phenotypic profiling of Staphylococcus aureus isolates from bovine mastitis for antibiotic resistance and intestinal infectivity.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in Staphylococcus aureus isolates from bovine mastitis, including genes encoding tetracycline efflux pumps (tetK, tetM, tet38), aminoglycoside modifying enzymes (aac3, aph3', aac6'), lincomycin resistance (lnuA), beta-lactam resistance (blaI, blaR, blaZ, mecA), and multidrug efflux pumps (norA, norB, lmrS, mepA, mepB, mepR, arlR, arlS, mgrA, rlmH, fosB).
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to identify AMR genes and their resistance profiles in S. aureus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic determinants of macrolide and tetracycline resistance in penicillin non-susceptible Streptococcus pneumoniae isolates from people living with HIV in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania.

erm(B).validation_method: whole genome sequencing and MIC testing

mef(A).validation_method: whole genome sequencing and MIC testing

tet(M).validation_method: whole genome sequencing and MIC testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identified erm(B) and mef(A)-msr(D) as common genes conferring resistance to macrolides and clindamycin, while tet(M) was responsible for tetracycline resistance in penicillin non-susceptible Streptococcus pneumoniae isolates from HIV patients in Tanzania.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify resistance genes and mechanisms in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical Evaluation of Metagenomic Next-Generation Sequencing for the detection of pathogens in BALF in severe community acquired pneumonia.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the effectiveness of metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) in detecting pathogens in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) of children with severe community-acquired pneumonia (SCAP). mNGS showed higher detection rates for Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, and fungi compared to conventional technology (CT). However, mNGS had a lower detection rate for Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MP) compared to CT.
full_output.methodology: The study used mNGS and conventional technology (CT) to analyze BALF samples from 84 children with SCAP. mNGS involved sample processing, nucleic acid extraction, library construction, and sequencing, while CT included culture, PCR, and antigen detection.

full_output.paper_title: Evidence of structural rearrangements in ESBL-positive pESI(like) megaplasmids of S.Infantis.

organisms_tested_in: Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica serovar Infantis
Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica serovar Infantis
Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica serovar Infantis
Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica serovar Infantis
Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica serovar Infantis

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the structural rearrangements in ESBL-positive pESI(like) megaplasmids of S. Infantis, identifying genes such as blaCTX-M-1, blaCTX-M-65, dfr1, sul1, qacΔE1, and aadA1 that confer resistance to various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Long-read sequencing using Oxford Nanopore Technology and hybrid assembly with Illumina data.

full_output.paper_title: Unraveling topoisomerase IA gate dynamics in presence of PPEF and its preclinical evaluation against multidrug-resistant pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: PPEF and BPVF demonstrate potent antibacterial activity against multidrug-resistant pathogens, including MRSA, VRSA, and ESBL-producing bacteria, by inhibiting bacterial TopoIA and TopoIII enzymes.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized computational modeling, molecular dynamics simulations, and in vitro antibacterial assays to evaluate the efficacy of PPEF and BPVF against multidrug-resistant pathogens.

full_output.paper_title: Influence of class 2 integron integrase concentration on gene cassette insertion and excision in vivo.

intI2.validation_method: quantitative real-time PCR and western blotting

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that the concentration of class 2 integron integrase (IntI2) influences the frequency of gene cassette insertion and excision in vivo.
full_output.methodology: Construction of plasmids with varying intI2 expression levels, quantitative real-time PCR, and western blotting.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterizations of antibiotic resistance, biofilm formation, and virulence determinants of Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolated from burn wound infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla TEM, bla VIM, and bla CTX-M as the most common beta-lactamase genes in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from burn wounds, contributing to resistance against multiple antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: PCR assay and disc diffusion method were used to detect beta-lactamase genes and antibiotic resistance patterns.

full_output.paper_title: Analytical Performance and Potential Clinical Utility of EUCAST Rapid Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing in Blood Cultures after Four Hours of Incubation.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the analytical performance of EUCAST RAST for determining antimicrobial susceptibility in E. coli and K. pneumoniae complex isolates after four hours of incubation, demonstrating high accuracy and clinical relevance for guiding antibiotic treatment decisions.
full_output.methodology: The study compares EUCAST RAST results with standard disk diffusion methods, analyzes susceptibility testing data, and evaluates the impact of RAST on empirical antibiotic treatment and ESBL detection.
full_output.sample_size: 530 E. coli and 112 K. pneumoniae complex strains

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies small-molecule inhibitors of the Salmonella FraB deglycase, which is essential for the catabolism of fructose-asparagine. These inhibitors show fra-dependent growth inhibition of Salmonella, suggesting potential for targeted antibacterial therapies.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput screening of small molecules using a live-cell assay to identify inhibitors of FraB, followed by enzymatic validation and kinetic analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of a Tigecycline-Resistant and blaCTX-M-Bearing Klebsiella pneumoniae Strain from a Peacock in a Chinese Zoo.

blaCTX-M-3.evidence_note: The paper states that strain LYS105A harbored the blaCTX-M-3 gene and exhibited resistance to amoxicillin, cefotaxime, gentamicin, oxytetracycline, doxycycline, tigecycline, florfenicol, and enrofloxacin.

aac(6')-Ib-cr5.genetic_context: aac(6′)-Ib-cr5 is located in a novel mobile composite transposon, Tn 7131
aac(6')-Ib-cr5.evidence_note: The paper mentions that aac(6′)-Ib-cr5 is part of the resistance genes in plasmid pLYS105A-2.

qnrB91.genetic_context: located in a novel mobile composite transposon, Tn 7131
qnrB91.evidence_note: qnrB91 is located in a novel mobile composite transposon, Tn 7131, which facilitates horizontal transfer.

phoP.notes: mutations in phoP lead to increased expression of phoPQ contributing to colistin resistance
phoP.evidence_note: The paper states that mutations in phoP lead to increased expression of phoPQ, which contributes to colistin resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified a multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae strain, LYS105A, from a peacock in a Chinese zoo, carrying blaCTX-M-3, aac(6')-Ib-cr5, and qnrB91 genes, which confer resistance to beta-lactams, aminoglycosides, and fluoroquinolones, respectively. Additionally, mutations in phoP were linked to colistin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and RT-qPCR were used to identify and characterize the resistance genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Whole-genome-based characterization of Campylobacter jejuni from human patients with gastroenteritis collected over an 18 year period reveals increasing prevalence of antimicrobial resistance.

aph(3')-III.genetic_context: carrying several resistance genes, including aph(3')-III , satA and aad (6), and flanked by insertion sequence elements

aad(6).genetic_context: carrying several resistance genes, including aph(3')-III , satA and aad (6), and flanked by insertion sequence elements

gyrA.notes: T86I is the most prevalent mutation in quinolone-resistant isolates

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies increasing prevalence of antimicrobial resistance in Campylobacter jejuni isolates, with quinolone resistance primarily due to gyrA mutations and tetracycline resistance mainly attributed to the tet(O) gene. A novel chromosomal cassette carrying aph(3')-III, satA, and aad(6) was also detected.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing of 340 C. jejuni isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Cyclic AMP is a critical mediator of intrinsic drug resistance and fatty acid metabolism in M. tuberculosis.

mutations_found.origin: spontaneous suppressors of Δ rv3645 oleic acid sensitivity

full_output.key_findings: The essential adenylate cyclase Rv3645 contributes to intrinsic drug resistance in Mtb H37Rv. Loss-of-function of the atypical cAMP phosphodiesterase Rv1339 rescues fatty acid and drug sensitivity phenotypes of the Δ rv3645 strain.
full_output.methodology: CRISPRi screening, gene knockout, and biochemical assays were used to validate the roles of rv3645 and rv1339 in drug resistance and fatty acid metabolism.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial activity of ceftibuten-avibactam against a global collection of Enterobacterales from patients with urinary tract infections (2021).
full_output.key_findings: Ceftibuten-avibactam showed high in vitro activity against a large collection of Enterobacterales causing urinary tract infections, including those with extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) and carbapenem-resistant phenotypes.
full_output.methodology: In vitro susceptibility testing using CLSI broth microdilution method.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic and enzymatic characterization of two novel bla(NDM-36, -37) variants in Escherichia coli strains.

blaNDM-36.validation_method: expression in E. coli DH5α and MIC testing
blaNDM-36.genetic_context: bla NDM-36 and bla NDM-37 were located in an ΔTn 125 -like region with the structure of 'tnpA-IS5-bla NDM-37-ble MBL-trpF-tat', containing Tn 3 family transposase IS 3000 upstream and IS 1380 family transposase ISEcp1 downstream
blaNDM-36.evidence_note: The bla NDM-36 and bla NDM-37 genes were cloned and expressed in E. coli DH5α, and their resistance profiles were determined through MIC testing.

blaNDM-37.validation_method: expression in E. coli DH5α and MIC testing
blaNDM-37.genetic_context: bla NDM-37 was carried by pJNQH497-1 which belongs to IncHI2-type plasmid. bla NDM-36 was carried by pJNQH498-1 which also belongs to IncHI2-type plasmid
blaNDM-37.evidence_note: The paper states that bla NDM-36 and bla NDM-37 were identified in E. coli strains and that their expression in E. coli DH5α conferred resistance to most β-lactams except aztreonam and ATM/AVI.

full_output.key_findings: Two novel NDM variants, NDM-36 and NDM-37, were identified in E. coli strains from a patient with a refractory UTI. Both variants confer resistance to multiple beta-lactams, with distinct kinetic properties.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, cloning, expression in E. coli, and kinetic analysis of NDM enzymes.

full_output.paper_title: Frequency and diversity of carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales recovered from untreated wastewater impacted by selective media containing cefotaxime and meropenem in Ohio, USA.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla KPC and bla NDM genes as the primary carbapenemase resistance mechanisms in Enterobacterales isolated from untreated wastewater in Ohio, USA.
full_output.methodology: PCR, Carba-NP test, and selective enrichment media.

full_output.paper_title: Mitoxantrone targets both host and bacteria to overcome vancomycin resistance in Enterococcus faecalis.

dead/deah.notes: Mutation in DEAD/DEAH box helicase confers methotrexate resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a mutation in a DEAD/DEAH box helicase gene (EF_RS05155) that confers resistance to mitoxantrone (MTX) in Enterococcus faecalis V583. This mutation (G389R) was found to reduce the effectiveness of MTX by preventing ROS and DNA damage.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, mutant selection, genetic complementation, and functional analysis of MTX resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular surveillance reveals widespread colonisation by carbapenemase and extended spectrum beta-lactamase producing organisms in neonatal units in Kenya and Nigeria.

blaNDM.evidence_note: The paper states that bla NDM was the most prevalent carbapenemase in both Ibadan and Kisumu NNUs.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla NDM as the most prevalent carbapenemase gene and CTX-M-1 as the dominant ESBL gene in neonatal units in Kenya and Nigeria.
full_output.methodology: qPCR assay for detection of AMR genes in stool and rectal swab samples.

full_output.paper_title: Risk Factors of Clonally Related, Multi, and Extensively Drug-Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii in Severely Ill COVID-19 Patients.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high incidence of clonally related, multi-drug-resistant (MDR), and extensively drug-resistant (XDR) Acinetobacter baumannii in severely ill COVID-19 patients, highlighting the challenges in treating these infections due to widespread antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used microbiological cultures, VITEK 2 system, real-time PCR, and ERIC-PCR for molecular typing, along with antimicrobial susceptibility testing against 33 antibiotics.
full_output.sample_size: 50 severely ill patients and 60 environmental samples

full_output.paper_title: Detection of Pathogens and Antimicrobial Resistance Genes in Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia by Metagenomic Next-Generation Sequencing Approach.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a rapid nanopore-based mNGS diagnostic assay for detecting VAP pathogens and antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs). It identified OXA, a β-lactamase gene, as the most prevalent ARG associated with resistance to penicillin and cephalosporin.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) was used to detect pathogens and ARGs in endotracheal aspirate samples from patients with ventilator-associated pneumonia.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Epidemiology of Staphylococcus aureus in a Tertiary Hospital in Anhui, China: ST59 Remains a Serious Threat.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified ST59 as a highly prevalent and virulent clone of Staphylococcus aureus in Anhui, China, with high resistance to oxacillin and strong hemolytic capacity.
full_output.methodology: MLST typing, antibiotic susceptibility testing, and hemolysis assays were conducted to analyze the molecular characteristics and resistance profiles of S. aureus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence, antimicrobial resistance pattern, and associated factors of Salmonella and Shigella among under five diarrheic children attending public health facilities in Debre Markos town, Northwest Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a high prevalence of Salmonella and Shigella among under-five children in Debre Markos town, with a significant rate of multidrug resistance. Key factors associated with the prevalence included low parental education, presence of multiple under-five children in the family, unimproved water sources, and poor hygiene practices.
full_output.methodology: The study used a cross-sectional design with stool sample collection and antimicrobial susceptibility testing via the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: High-Throughput Mutagenesis Reveals a Role for Antimicrobial Resistance- and Virulence-Associated Mobile Genetic Elements in Staphylococcus aureus Host Adaptation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies SAPIG0966 and SAPIG1525 as genes important for Staphylococcus aureus CC398 survival in porcine blood, with SAPIG0966 located on the Tn 916 transposon carrying a tetracycline resistance gene.
full_output.methodology: Transposon mutagenesis and TraDIS analysis were used to identify genes essential for S. aureus survival in human and porcine blood.

full_output.paper_title: Outbreak of colistin resistant, carbapenemase (bla (NDM), bla (OXA-232)) producing Klebsiella pneumoniae causing blood stream infection among neonates at a tertiary care hospital in India.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes an outbreak of colistin-resistant, carbapenemase-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae in a neonatal intensive care unit, highlighting the presence of bla NDM-1, bla NDM-5, and bla OXA-232 genes, along with other beta-lactamase genes, contributing to multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: Polymerase chain reaction and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify resistance genes and determine susceptibility profiles.

full_output.paper_title: Usefulness of EUCAST rapid antibiotic susceptibility breakpoints and screening cut-off values directly from blood cultures for the inference of β-lactam resistance mechanisms in Enterobacterales.

CTX-M.validation_method: phenotypic analysis and disc diffusion testing

SHV.validation_method: phenotypic analysis and disc diffusion testing

KPC.validation_method: phenotypic analysis and disc diffusion testing

VIM.validation_method: phenotypic analysis and disc diffusion testing

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the effectiveness of EUCAST rapid AST (RAST) disc diffusion breakpoints and screening cut-off values (sRAST) for detecting β-lactam resistance mechanisms in Enterobacterales. It identified several β-lactamases, including CTX-M, SHV, OXA-48, KPC, and VIM, which confer resistance to various β-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic analysis, disc diffusion testing, and evaluation of EUCAST RAST and sRAST breakpoints for detecting β-lactam resistance mechanisms in Enterobacterales.

full_output.paper_title: The under investigated facet of the COVID-19 pandemic: Molecular analysis of secondary bacterial infections at a COVID dedicated intensive care unit within a tertiary care center in Lebanon.

parC.notes: detected in 6 E. coli isolates

gyrA.notes: detected in 6 E. coli isolates

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple AMR genes including bla CTX-M-15, bla TEM-1 B, bla SHV-26, bla CMY-145, bla OXA-1, bla NDM-5, bla NDM-7, aph(3")-Ib, aac(6')-Ib-cr, aadA, FosA, FosA3, FosA6, mcr-1.26, acrAB-TolC, and MexAB-OprM in Gram-negative isolates from COVID-19 patients. These genes conferred resistance to various antibiotics such as carbapenems, cephalosporins, fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, fosfomycin, and colistin.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify AMR genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: CRISPR/Cas-based nucleic acid diagnostics for pathogens
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses various CRISPR/Cas-based nucleic acid diagnostic methods for detecting pathogens, including viruses, bacteria, and fungi. It highlights the development of assays for SARS-CoV-2 variants, drug-resistant bacteria, and fungal infections, emphasizing the importance of sensitivity, specificity, and point-of-care (POCT) applications.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews CRISPR/Cas-based diagnostic techniques, including RT-PCR, RPA, LAMP, and CRISPR reporting, for the detection of various pathogens.

full_output.paper_title: ST7 Becomes One of the Most Common Staphylococcus aureus Clones After the COVID-19 Epidemic in the City of Wuhan, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that ST7 became the second dominant clone of Staphylococcus aureus in Wuhan after the COVID-19 pandemic, with an increased prevalence of virulence genes and SCCmec elements. The MRSA proportion in ST7-t091 increased from 19.1% to 50% post-pandemic.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed 619 S. aureus isolates using molecular typing (MLST, spa, SCCmec), PCR for virulence genes, and antibiotic susceptibility testing via VITEK system.

full_output.paper_title: oprL Gene Sequencing, Resistance Patterns, Virulence Genes, Quorum Sensing and Antibiotic Resistance Genes of XDR Pseudomonas aeruginosa Isolated from Broiler Chickens.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified XDR P. aeruginosa strains from broiler chickens in Egypt, which harbor multiple antibiotic resistance genes including bla TEM, bla CTX-M, bla OXA-1, aad A1, tet A, and sul 1. These strains showed resistance to multiple antimicrobial classes.
full_output.methodology: PCR screening and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify resistance genes and determine resistance patterns.

full_output.paper_title: Advances in the preclinical characterization of the antimicrobial peptide AS-48.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the antimicrobial peptide AS-48, highlighting its effectiveness against various pathogens, including multidrug-resistant bacteria and parasites, through mechanisms involving membrane disruption and intracellular targeting. It also identifies the immunity protein (As-48D1) and ABC transporter (As-48EFGH) as key resistance mechanisms in AS-48-producing strains.
full_output.methodology: In vitro assays, genetic analysis, and evaluation of antimicrobial activity against various pathogens.

full_output.paper_title: Advantages of long- and short-reads sequencing for the hybrid investigation of the Mycobacterium tuberculosis genome.
full_output.key_findings: The study compares the performance of short-reads (SRS), long-reads (LRS), and hybrid-reads (HYBR) sequencing approaches for analyzing the Mycobacterium tuberculosis genome, focusing on genome coverage, variant calling, drug resistance detection, and de novo assembly. HYBR showed superior performance in genome coverage and variant calling, particularly in repetitive regions like PE/PPE genes.
full_output.methodology: The study used 13 MTB clinical isolates sequenced with SRS and LRS, with HYBR created by correcting long reads with short reads. Analysis involved genome coverage estimation, variant calling, drug resistance detection, and de novo assembly using various tools.

poxtA.mechanism: resistance to phenicols, oxazolidinones, and tetracyclines

blaTEM-116.evidence_note: The paper mentions that the blaTEM-116 gene confers resistance to penicillins, three generations of cephalosporins, and aztreonam.

ermX.mechanism: resistance to macrolides, lincosamides, and streptogramins

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several AMR genes in probiotic bacteria, including strA, strB, sul1, sul2, aac(6')-aph(2'), aph(3')-II, tetM, poxtA, aph(3')-IIb, rpoB, tet(W/N/W), TEM-116, aadK, lmrD, ermX, and vanG, which confer resistance to various antibiotics such as streptomycin, sulfonamides, aminoglycosides, tetracycline, phenicols, oxazolidinones, beta-lactams, lincosamides, macrolides, and vancomycin.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic testing, metagenomic analysis, and genomic analysis were used to identify and validate AMR genes in probiotic bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of Tigecycline Utilization and Trends in Antibacterial Resistance from 2018 to 2021 in a Comprehensive Teaching Hospital in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that Acinetobacter baumannii showed high resistance rates to several antibiotics, including tigecycline, and highlighted the increasing resistance to tigecycline despite a decrease in its detection rate.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of tigecycline usage and antimicrobial resistance trends in a comprehensive teaching hospital in China.

full_output.paper_title: New insights on tuberculosis transmission dynamics and drug susceptibility profiles among the prison population in Southern Brazil based on whole-genome sequencing.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified six M. tuberculosis isolates with drug resistance, including resistance to rifampicin, isoniazid, fluoroquinolones, and streptomycin, using whole-genome sequencing.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and phenotypic drug susceptibility testing were used to analyze drug resistance profiles in M. tuberculosis isolates from prisoners in Brazil.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of toxin-antitoxin genes, antibiotic resistance, and virulence genes in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates.

RelBE.mechanism: regulation of biofilm formation and virulence

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of RelBE and HigBA toxin-antitoxin genes, as well as ExoS and ToxA virulence genes, in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates. It found a significant correlation between RelBE gene expression and imipenem/meropenem sensitivity, and between HigBA gene expression and amikacin sensitivity. Additionally, a significant correlation was observed between RelBE and ExoS gene expression, suggesting a link between toxin-antitoxin genes and bacterial virulence.
full_output.methodology: Real-time PCR was used to detect the presence and transcription levels of toxin-antitoxin and virulence genes in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates.

full_output.paper_title: A Systematic Review of Culture-Based Methods for Monitoring Antibiotic-Resistant Acinetobacter, Aeromonas, and Pseudomonas as Environmentally Relevant Pathogens in Wastewater and Surface Water.
full_output.key_findings: This review highlights the challenges and methods for monitoring antibiotic-resistant Acinetobacter, Aeromonas, and Pseudomonas in wastewater and surface water environments. It discusses the importance of these bacteria as potential reservoirs of antibiotic resistance genes and the need for standardized culture-based methods to effectively monitor their presence and resistance profiles.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review of peer-reviewed literature focusing on culture-based methods for isolating and characterizing antibiotic-resistant Acinetobacter, Aeromonas, and Pseudomonas from wastewater and surface water.

full_output.paper_title: Association of Proton Pump Inhibitor Use With Risk of Acquiring Drug-Resistant Enterobacterales.
full_output.key_findings: Proton pump inhibitor (PPI) use was associated with an increased risk of acquiring extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)- or carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales in hospitalized patients.
full_output.methodology: Case-control study analyzing the association between PPI use and the risk of acquiring drug-resistant Enterobacterales.

full_output.paper_title: Enrichment of antibiotic resistant genes and pathogens in face masks from coastal environments.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 64 antibiotic-resistance genes (ARGs) and 12 mobile gene elements (MGEs) in the plastisphere of face masks, with significant enrichments in tetracycline, multidrug, macrolide-lincosamide-streptogramin B (MLSB), and phenicol-resistant genes compared to sediments.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput quantitative PCR (HT-qPCR) and Illumina sequencing were used to analyze the ARG and MGE profiles in face masks and sediments.

full_output.paper_title: Oxidative stress induced by Etoposide anti-cancer chemotherapy drives the emergence of tumor-associated bacteria resistance to fluoroquinolones.

gyrA.notes: Mutations in the gyrA gene were identified in EICR isolates, contributing to ciprofloxacin resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that prolonged exposure to Etoposide leads to the emergence of ciprofloxacin-resistant P. aeruginosa through mutations in the gyrA gene, which encodes DNA gyrase subunit A.
full_output.methodology: Experimental evolution assay, genomic sequencing, and MIC analysis were used to identify and validate the mutations in the gyrA gene.

full_output.paper_title: Phytochemicals and quaternary phosphonium ionic liquids: Connecting the dots to develop a new class of antimicrobial agents.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the antimicrobial activity of phytochemical-based triphenylphosphonium (TPP + ) conjugates against various Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria and fungi, highlighting their potential as new antimicrobial agents.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis of TPP + conjugates, antimicrobial screening, and evaluation of their mechanism of action.

full_output.paper_title: An optogenetic toolkit for light-inducible antibiotic resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents an optogenetic toolkit enabling light-inducible antibiotic resistance in Escherichia coli, utilizing genes such as bla, knt, cat, and tetA, which confer resistance to carbenicillin, kanamycin, chloramphenicol, and tetracycline, respectively.
full_output.methodology: The study uses light-inducible Cre recombinase OptoCreVvd2 to control the expression of antibiotic resistance genes, followed by MIC testing to validate resistance.

full_output.paper_title: First report of Staphylococcus pseudintermedius ST71-SCCmec III and ST45-ΨSCCmec(57395) from canine pyoderma in Argentina.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first identification of Staphylococcus pseudintermedius ST71-SCCmec III and ST45-ΨSCCmec 57395 in Argentina, highlighting the global spread of these multidrug-resistant clones.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis for MLST and SCC mec typing.

full_output.key_findings: The study discusses the impact of antimicrobial and heavy metal usage on the antimicrobial resistance profiles of pigs, highlighting the positive association between antimicrobial use (AMU) and heavy metal use (HMU) with antimicrobial resistance (AMR). It also identifies the co-location of antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) with mobile genetic elements (MGEs) and the influence of the microbiome and virome on AMR development.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a systematic literature review approach, analyzing data from 28 research studies that employed metagenomics, 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing, and quantitative PCR (qPCR) to investigate the relationship between AMU/HMU and AMR in pigs.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of Antimicrobial Resistance and Clonal Relationship in ESBL/AmpC-Producing Proteus mirabilis Isolated from Meat Products and Community-Acquired Urinary Tract Infection (UTI-CA) in Southern Brazil.

These genes were associated with resistance to various antimicrobial classes, emphasizing the role of meat as a potential source of multidrug-resistant P. mirabilis.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR-based detection of resistance genes, and molecular typing using PFGE were employed to analyze the AMR profiles of P. mirabilis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: The Pork Food Chain as a Route of Transmission of Antimicrobial Resistant Escherichia coli: A Farm-to-Fork Perspective.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in Escherichia coli isolates from various stages of the pork food chain, highlighting the prevalence of resistance to sulfamethoxazole (SXT), tobramycin (TOB), and gentamicin (GEN). Multidrug-resistant (MDR) profiles were frequently observed in fecal isolates, with some resistance patterns detected in carcasses but none in pork meat products.

full_output.paper_title: Genotypic Characteristics and Antimicrobial Resistance of Escherichia coli ST141 Clonal Group.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and Characterization of Beta-Lactam and Carbapenem-Resistant Bacteria Isolated from Organic Fresh Produce Retailed in Eastern Spain.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that the combination of LL-37 and polymyxin B (PMB) shows strong synergy against both planktonic and biofilm cells of E. coli and P. aeruginosa, with significant anti-biofilm activity and in vivo efficacy.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth microdilution, checkerboard assays, biofilm inhibition and eradication experiments, and in vivo Galleria mellonella models to evaluate the synergistic effects of LL-37 and PMB.

full_output.methodology: Transcriptional analysis via qRT-PCR and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.methodology: PCR, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and multilocus sequence typing were used to analyze resistance genes and genetic correlations.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance and Virulence Genes of Streptococcus Agalactiae Isolated from Mastitis Milk Samples in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in multidrug-resistant Streptococcus agalactiae isolates from bovine mastitis milk samples in China, including ermB, ermA, lnuA, tetM, tetK, tetS, and tetO. These genes conferred resistance to macrolides, lincosamides, and tetracyclines.
full_output.methodology: PCR and broth microdilution method were used to detect AMR and virulence genes in S. agalactiae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Analysis of Efflux Pump System and Other Drug Resistance Related Gene Mutations in Tigecycline-Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in the efflux pump regulator genes adeR and adeS, as well as in the drug resistance-related genes plsC and trm, which contribute to tigecycline resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii. Specifically, mutations in adeR (Gly232Ala) and adeS (Ala97Thr, Leu105Phe, Leu172Pro, Arg195Gln, Gln203Leu, Tyr303Phe, Lys315Asn, Gly319Ser) were found to be associated with increased tigecycline resistance. Additionally, mutations in plsC (CAA592AAA, TAA925AAA) and trm (Insert29A, Deletion51A, Deletion267A) were also linked to tigecycline resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized fluorescence quantitative PCR, broth microdilution testing, efflux pump inhibition experiments, and PCR sequencing to analyze gene expression and mutations in tigecycline-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii strains.

full_output.paper_title: Five copper homeostasis gene clusters encode the Cu-efflux resistome of the highly copper-tolerant Methylorubrum extorquens AM1.

Aztreonam-avibactam showed potent activity against these isolates, including MBL producers and those resistant to other beta-lactamase inhibitors.
