full_output.paper_title: In vitro digestion of ESC-resistant Escherichia coli from poultry meat and evaluation of human health risk.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla CMY-2 as a gene responsible for extended-spectrum cephalosporin resistance in E. coli isolates from poultry meat. The gene was shown to be transferable via conjugation and confirmed through PCR analysis.
full_output.methodology: The study used an in vitro digestion model to assess the survival and conjugation abilities of ESC-resistant E. coli isolates, along with PCR analysis to confirm the presence of the bla CMY-2 gene.

full_output.paper_title: Novel copper-containing ferrite nanoparticles exert lethality to MRSA by disrupting MRSA cell membrane permeability, depleting intracellular iron ions, and upregulating ROS levels.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Cu@Fe NPs as a novel antibacterial agent with potent activity against MRSA, demonstrating effectiveness in disrupting cell membrane permeability, depleting intracellular iron ions, and upregulating ROS levels.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized in vitro and in vivo experiments, including MIC determination, time-kill assays, SEM, and fluorescence microscopy, to assess the antibacterial activity of Cu@Fe NPs against MRSA.

full_output.paper_title: Dynamic state of plasmid genomic architectures resulting from XerC/D-mediated site-specific recombination in Acinetobacter baumannii Rep_3 superfamily resistance plasmids carrying bla(OXA-58) - and TnaphA6-resistance modules.

full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, PCR, and plasmid analysis were used to investigate the role of XerC/D-mediated recombination in plasmid architecture and resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: COF-Based Single Atom Catalysts Induce Bacterial Ferroptosis-Like Death for Effective Anti-Infective Therapy
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that COF-based single atom catalysts (SACs) induce bacterial ferroptosis-like death, effectively killing MRSA and reducing biofilm formation. The SACs, sp2c-COF-Ir-ppy2 and sp2c-COF-Ru-bpy2, generate reactive oxygen species (ROS) and lipid peroxidation (LPO), disrupting bacterial membranes and metabolic processes.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro and in vivo experiments, including CFU counting, SEM, TEM, flow cytometry, and transcriptomic analysis, to evaluate the antibacterial effects of COF-based SACs.

These isolates carried multiple resistance genes, including bla CTX-M-55, bla TEM-1B, aac(3)-IId, aadA17, rmtB, tet(A), floR, lnu(F), arr-2, qnrS1, sul1, mph(A), and fosA3, and mutations in gyrA (S83F, D87N) and parC (S80I), leading to resistance against several antimicrobial agents.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify resistance genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: The Colorectal Cancer Gut Environment Regulates Activity of the Microbiome and Promotes the Multidrug Resistant Phenotype of ESKAPE and Other Pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies various antibiotic resistance genes in the gut microbiota of colorectal cancer (CRC) patients, highlighting the upregulation of resistance determinants in CRC compared to controls. Key genes include cls, bla2, mdtO, phoP, eptB, catA, bla CMY, nfsA, marA, and gadX, which confer resistance to multiple antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Metatranscriptomic and 16S rRNA gene sequencing were used to analyze the gut microbiota of CRC and control patients, along with qRT-PCR to validate the expression of selected antibiotic resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Cefiderocol, a Siderophore Cephalosporin, as a Treatment Option for Infections Caused by Carbapenem-Resistant Enterobacterales.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses cefiderocol, a siderophore cephalosporin with potent in vitro activity against carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE), including those with various carbapenemase mechanisms. full_output.paper_title: Multidrug resistant Klebsiella Pneumoniae reservoir and their capsular resistance genes in cow farms of district Peshawar, Pakistan.

full_output.key_findings: This review discusses the ecological and health risks associated with antimicrobial contamination and resistance, highlighting the role of environmental factors in the spread of antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) and antimicrobial-resistant bacteria (ARB).
full_output.methodology: This is a review paper summarizing current knowledge on antimicrobial resistance in the environment.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative Analysis of Transcriptomic Response of Escherichia coli K-12 MG1655 to Nine Representative Classes of Antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Distribution pattern of antibiotic resistance genes in Escherichia coli isolated from colibacillosis cases in broiler farms of Egypt.

The research constructed a risk prediction model for drug-resistant bacterial infections based on clinical and demographic factors.

full_output.paper_title: A novel lytic bacteriophage against colistin-resistant Escherichia coli isolated from different animals.

full_output.paper_title: The ComRS-SigX pathway regulates natural transformation in Streptococcus ferus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the ComRS system in Streptococcus ferus, including comR, comR2, sigX, and sigX2, which are essential for natural transformation. The system is activated by XIP peptides, and the genes are necessary for competence induction.
full_output.methodology: Protein BLAST, promoter analysis, and transformation experiments were used to identify and characterize the ComRS system in S. ferus.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Epidemiology of Community-Acquired Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus and Clinical Characteristics of Different Sites of Infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the molecular types, virulence factors, and antimicrobial resistance of CA-MRSA strains, highlighting the predominance of ST59-t437-IV and the varying susceptibility profiles of CA-MRSA infections based on the site of infection.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized molecular typing techniques, PCR, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing to analyze CA-MRSA strains.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies risk factors for multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacterial infections in ICU patients, including the number of bacteria, multiple invasive procedures, length of stay, and hemoglobin levels. It also highlights the prevalence of MDR pathogens such as Klebsiella pneumoniae, Acinetobacter baumannii, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of ICU patient data, including microbiological cultures and clinical outcomes, with statistical modeling to identify risk factors for MDR infections.

full_output.paper_title: MGIT-seq for the Identification of Nontuberculous Mycobacteria and Drug Resistance: a Prospective Study.

rrs.validation_method: sequencing and drug susceptibility testing

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrated the effectiveness of MGIT-seq for identifying nontuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) and predicting drug resistance, particularly for macrolides and amikacin. Key findings include the identification of specific mutations in rrl, erm (41), and rrs genes associated with resistance.
full_output.methodology: Direct MGIT sequencing combined with computational analysis for species identification and drug resistance prediction.

full_output.paper_title: Development of Modernized Acinetobacter baumannii Susceptibility Test Interpretive Criteria for Recommended Antimicrobial Agents Using Pharmacometric Approaches.
full_output.key_findings: The study aimed to modernize susceptibility test interpretive criteria (STIC) for Acinetobacter baumannii using pharmacometric approaches. It evaluated four antimicrobial agents (amikacin, ceftazidime, ciprofloxacin, and minocycline) and proposed updated susceptible breakpoints based on PK/PD target attainment analyses.
full_output.methodology: The research combined in vitro surveillance data, preclinical murine infection models, population pharmacokinetics, and pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) target attainment analyses to assess STIC for A. baumannii.

full_output.key_findings: The study reveals a global increase in the abundance of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in conjugative plasmids, highlighting the role of plasmids in the spread of resistance. The abundance of ARGs in plasmids increased tenfold from 2000 to 2020, with a more pronounced rise in low-to-middle income countries. The study also identifies high sequence similarities between clinical and environmental plasmids, suggesting potential transmission of ARGs across ecological boundaries.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed 27,938 fully sequenced plasmids from the NCBI RefSeq database, classified them into conjugative, mobilizable, and nonmobilizable types, and assessed ARG abundance using bioinformatics tools and statistical analyses.

full_output.paper_title: Pharmacokinetic-Pharmacodynamic Target Attainment Analyses Evaluating Omadacycline Dosing Regimens for the Treatment of Patients with Community-Acquired Bacterial Pneumonia Arising from Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated omadacycline's effectiveness against Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae through pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK-PD) target attainment analyses, showing high probabilities of achieving therapeutic targets across various MIC values.
full_output.methodology: Nonclinical PK-PD target attainment analyses using in vitro surveillance data and population pharmacokinetic models.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of Efflux Substrates Using a Riboswitch-Based Reporter in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a riboswitch-based reporter system in Pseudomonas aeruginosa that detects folate pathway inhibitors and distinguishes compounds that are substrates for efflux systems from those that are retained inside the cell.
full_output.methodology: The study uses a riboswitch-based reporter system combined with efflux-deficient and efflux-proficient strains to screen for compounds affecting the folate pathway and efflux mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Efficacy of Zidovudine-Amikacin Combination Therapy In Vitro and in a Rat Tissue Cage Infection Model against Amikacin-Resistant, Multidrug-Resistant Enterobacteriales.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the aac(6')-Ib, armA, rmtB, and rmtC genes as responsible for amikacin resistance in 53 amikacin-resistant MDR Enterobacteriales isolates. The zidovudine-amikacin combination showed significant synergistic effects against these isolates in vitro and in vivo.
full_output.methodology: PCR, susceptibility testing, checkerboard assays, time-kill experiments, Galleria mellonella model, and rat tissue cage infection model.

full_output.paper_title: Identification and Characterization of OXA-232-Producing Sequence Type 231 Multidrug Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae Strains Causing Bloodstream Infections in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies OXA-232-producing multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae ST231 strains in China, highlighting their resistance to carbapenems and other antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and phylogenetic analysis were used to characterize the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: The Significance of Epidemic Plasmids in the Success of Multidrug-Resistant Drug Pandemic Extraintestinal Pathogenic Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the significant role of epidemic IncF plasmids in the success of multidrug-resistant extraintestinal pathogenic Escherichia coli (ExPEC) clones such as ST131 and ST410. These plasmids contain various antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes, including bla CTX-M-14, bla CTX-M-15, bla CTX-M-27, bla NDM-5, and others, contributing to resistance against multiple antibiotic classes.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis of plasmids and their association with AMR genes in ExPEC clones.

full_output.paper_title: Modulation of MRSA virulence gene expression by the wall teichoic acid enzyme TarO.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that inhibition of TarO, a wall teichoic acid (WTA) biosynthesis enzyme, reduces the expression of virulence genes such as psmα, psmβ, and spa in CA-MRSA strain USA300 LAC. This effect is mediated through the activation of the VraRS two-component system, which represses the agr quorum sensing system.
full_output.methodology: The study used genetic and chemical approaches, including qRT-PCR, Western blotting, and reporter assays, to investigate the role of TarO in regulating virulence gene expression in S. aureus.

full_output.paper_title: Cooperative antibiotic resistance facilitates horizontal gene transfer.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial potential of myricetin-coated zinc oxide nanocomposite against drug-resistant Clostridium perfringens.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the antimicrobial potential of myricetin (MYR)-coated zinc oxide (ZnO) nanocomposite against drug-resistant Clostridium perfringens. It found that all tested C. perfringens isolates were susceptible to MYR-loaded ZnO/PVA with minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) ranging from 0.125 to 2 µg/mL. Additionally, the MYR-based nanocomposite effectively reduced the hemolytic activity of C. perfringens isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study conducted antimicrobial susceptibility testing, agar well diffusion assay, time-kill kinetics, and transcriptional analysis to evaluate the efficacy of MYR, ZnO, ZnO/PVA, and ZnO/PVA/MYR nanocomposites against C. perfringens isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Biofilm formation of two genetically diverse Staphylococcus aureus isolates under beta-lactam antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Stimulating Transcription in Antibiotic-Tolerant Escherichia coli Sensitizes It to Fluoroquinolone and Nonfluoroquinolone Topoisomerase Inhibitors.

full_output.paper_title: Structural Basis for Binding of Neutralizing Antibodies to Clostridioides difficile Binary Toxin.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the activity of imipenem/relebactam against Enterobacterales and Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates in Spain from 2016 to 2020, showing high susceptibility rates, particularly against Class A carbapenemases.

full_output.paper_title: The risk of pig and chicken farming for carriage and transmission of Escherichia coli containing extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) and mobile colistin resistance (mcr) genes in Thailand.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of Ancylostoma caninum parasites with the benzimidazole resistance F167Y polymorphism in the US dog population.

full_output.paper_title: Phylogroup-specific variation shapes the clustering of antimicrobial resistance genes and defence systems across regions of genome plasticity in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis involving the generation of new genome assemblies for 18 strains of the mPact panel, combined with publicly available genomes, to explore variations in AMR genes, defence systems, and virulence genes across different phylogroups.

full_output.paper_title: The potential to produce tropodithietic acid by Phaeobacter inhibens affects the assembly of microbial biofilm communities in natural seawater.

full_output.methodology: The study used a semi-natural marine model system to examine the impact of TDA-producing and non-TDA-producing strains of Phaeobacter inhibens on microbial community assembly, employing qPCR, amplicon sequencing, and network analysis.

full_output.paper_title: High prevalence of extensively drug resistant and extended spectrum beta lactamases (ESBLs) producing uropathogenic Escherichia coli isolated from Faisalabad, Pakistan.

full_output.methodology: Environmental sampling and PCR detection of the blaVIM gene in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from sink drains and surrounding areas.

full_output.paper_title: Enterobacterales plasmid sharing amongst human bloodstream infections, livestock, wastewater, and waterway niches in Oxfordshire, UK.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies various AMR genes, including bla TEM-1, aph(3'')-Ib, aph(6)-Id, dfrA5, sul2, and robA, which are associated with plasmids shared among human bloodstream infections, livestock, wastewater, and waterways in Oxfordshire, UK.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed plasmid sharing among Enterobacterales isolates from human bloodstream infections, livestock, and wastewater using whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics tools.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies high rates of antibiotic resistance among uropathogenic E. coli isolates, particularly to Bactrim, tetracycline, and ampicillin-sulbactam, highlighting the need for improved antibiotic stewardship in the region.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of bacterial isolates using Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method for antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Risk factors for third-generation cephalosporin-resistant and extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli carriage in domestic animals of semirural parishes east of Quito, Ecuador.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified risk factors for the carriage of third-generation cephalosporin-resistant (CR) and extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Escherichia coli in domestic animals in semirural parishes east of Quito, Ecuador. CR and ESBL-producing E. coli were detected in 56% and 10% of fecal samples, respectively. Factors associated with increased odds of CR E. coli carriage included proximity to commercial food animal facilities and poultry odor exposure. ESBL-producing E. coli carriage was linked to recent antimicrobial use and purchasing antimicrobials from pet food stores.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed 1195 fecal samples from domestic animals in 304 households using antimicrobial susceptibility testing and multivariable regression analyses to assess risk factors for CR and ESBL-producing E. coli carriage.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated antibiotic susceptibility patterns of bacteria isolated from Livingstone Central Hospital, revealing high resistance rates to several antibiotics, including ampicillin, oxacillin, and penicillin, with implications for antimicrobial resistance trends in the region.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of bacterial isolates from clinical specimens using Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Methicillin resistance Staphylococcus aureus nasal carriage and its associated factors among HIV patients attending art clinic at Dessie comprehensive specialized hospital, Dessie, North East Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a high rate of nasal carriage of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) among HIV patients, with 28.2% being MRSA carriers. MRSA showed resistance to tetracycline (53.4%), erythromycin (84.5%), and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (86.2%).
full_output.methodology: Cross-sectional study involving 206 HIV patients, with nasal specimens cultured and tested for antimicrobial susceptibility using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Smartphone-operated affordable PCR thermal cycler for the detection of antimicrobial resistant bacterial genes.

full_output.methodology: Development and evaluation of a custom-built PCR thermal cycler using a smartphone application for temperature and time control, along with PCR amplification and gel electrophoresis for gene detection.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic and genotypic antibiotic susceptibility profiles of Gram-negative bacteria isolated from bloodstream infections at a referral hospital, Lusaka, Zambia.

full_output.methodology: The study used metagenomic data analysis to identify and quantify the presence of origin species and their associated MISE in various environments.

full_output.methodology: The paper is a review article summarizing existing literature on the virulence factors and mechanisms of A. baumannii.

full_output.paper_title: The Phospholipase A1 Activity of Glycerol Ester Hydrolase (Geh) Is Responsible for Extracellular 2-12(S)-Methyltetradecanoyl-Lysophosphatidylglycerol Production in Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the glycerol ester hydrolase (Geh) as the gene responsible for the extracellular production of 2-12(S)-methyltetradecanoyl-lysophosphatidylglycerol (a15-LPG) in Staphylococcus aureus. Geh exhibits phospholipase A1 activity, specifically hydrolyzing the 1-position acyl chain of phosphatidylglycerol (PG), leading to the formation of a15-LPG. This activity was validated through genetic knockout and complementation experiments, as well as enzymatic assays.
full_output.methodology: Genetic knockout and complementation experiments, enzymatic assays, and lipid analysis via LC-MS/MS were used to validate the role of Geh in a15-LPG production.

full_output.paper_title: Is nanomaterial- and vancomycin-loaded polymer coating effective at preventing methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus growth on titanium disks? An in vitro study.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the effectiveness of vancomycin-loaded Resomer® coating in preventing methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) biofilm growth on titanium disks. High- and low-dose vancomycin-loaded coatings showed significant biofilm reduction, indicating potential for preventing MRSA infections in orthopedic implants.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro assays including MIC and MBIC determinations, SEM for biofilm visualization, and XTT reduction assays to evaluate the antibiofilm efficacy of vancomycin-loaded coatings on titanium disks.

full_output.paper_title: Crosstalk between Pseudomonas aeruginosa antibiotic resistance and virulence mediated by phenylethylamine.
full_output.key_findings: Phenylethylamine induces the expression of the MexCD-OprJ efflux pump in Pseudomonas aeruginosa without increasing antibiotic resistance. It acts as both an inducer and a substrate of the efflux pump, reducing virulence-related traits such as pyocyanin production and swarming motility.
full_output.methodology: RT-qPCR, luminescence biosensors, MIC testing, and growth assays.

full_output.paper_title: Longitudinal temperature measurement can determine humane endpoints in BALB/c mouse models of ESKAPEE infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates temperature as an objective measure to determine humane endpoints in BALB/c mouse models of ESKAPEE infection, showing that internal temperature significantly predicts mortality.
full_output.methodology: The study uses BALB/c mice infected with ESKAPEE pathogens and monitors internal and external temperatures, along with clinical scores and weight loss, to assess mortality predictors.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation, identification, molecular typing, and drug resistance of Escherichia coli from infected cattle and sheep in Xinjiang, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antibiotic resistance genes in E. coli isolates from cattle and sheep in Xinjiang, China, including aadB, aacC2, aph(3')-Ia, aadA1, blaTEM, blaSHV, blaCTX-M, tet(A), tet(B), tet(C), qnrA, oqxAB, aac(6')-Ib, sul1, sul2, and sul3. High levels of multidrug resistance were observed, particularly against streptomycin, gentamicin, and sulfamethoxazole.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR detection and antimicrobial susceptibility testing to identify antibiotic resistance genes and assess drug resistance profiles in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Characteristics of Extended-Spectrum β-Lactamase Producing Enterobacterales Isolated from Dogs and Cats, 2011-2021.

blaCTX-M-15.evidence_note: Bla CTX-M-15 was the most common ESBL gene identified, present in 13/22 (59%) isolate genomes.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla CTX-M-15 as the most common ESBL gene in Enterobacterales isolates from dogs and cats, highlighting the prevalence of multidrug-resistant infections and the importance of alternative antibiotics like piperacillin-tazobactam and amikacin.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize ESBL-producing Enterobacterales isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical characteristics, risk factors and outcomes of Klebsiella pneumoniae pneumonia developing secondary Klebsiella pneumoniae bloodstream infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several risk factors for Klebsiella pneumoniae (KP) pneumonia progressing to secondary KP bloodstream infection (KP-BSI), including male sex, immunosuppression, high APACHE II score, elevated serum procalcitonin (PCT), prolonged ICU stay before pneumonia, mechanical ventilation, ESBL-producing KP, and inappropriate antibacterial therapy. ESBL-positive KP was more prevalent in KP-pneumonia/KP-BSI cases and was associated with reduced susceptibility to certain antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective observational study analyzing clinical data from patients with KP pneumonia and KP-BSI.

full_output.paper_title: Gram-negative bacteria resist antimicrobial agents by a DzrR-mediated envelope stress response.

dzrR.validation_method: mutant analysis, complementation, MIC assay, EMSA, DNase I footprinting

desAB.validation_method: mutant analysis, reporter gene assays, and EMSAs

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies DzrR as a key regulator of zeamine resistance in Dickeya oryzae EC1, demonstrating its role in activating the RND efflux pump desAB. DzrR homologs in Ralstonia and Burkholderia species also show similar functionality, indicating a conserved envelope stress response mechanism.
full_output.methodology: Transposon mutagenesis, RT-qPCR, EMSA, DNase I footprinting, MIC assays, and phylogenetic analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Environmental contamination across multiple hospital departments with multidrug-resistant bacteria pose an elevated risk of healthcare-associated infections in Kenyan hospitals.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multidrug-resistant (MDR) ESKAPEE pathogens, including Acinetobacter baumannii, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Enterobacter species, and others, contaminating high-touch surfaces in Kenyan hospitals, highlighting the risk of healthcare-associated infections.
full_output.methodology: Systematic sampling and bacteriological culture methods were used to identify and characterize MDR ESKAPEE pathogens from high-touch surfaces in five Kenyan hospitals.

full_output.paper_title: Low-Level Tetracycline Resistance Gene tet(O)_3 in Campylobacter jejuni.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel low-level tetracycline resistance gene, tet(O)_3, in two Campylobacter jejuni isolates from chicken meat. This gene is highly responsive to low tetracycline concentrations and shows similarity to a tet(O) gene in Streptococcus pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: PCR, Sanger sequencing, WGS, RT-PCR, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize the gene and its resistance profile.
full_output.sample_size: Three C. jejuni isolates (FC77, FC88, GC119)

full_output.paper_title: Recent Trends of Antibiotic Resistance in Staphylococcus aureus Causing Clinical Mastitis in Dairy Herds in Abruzzo and Molise Regions, Italy.

blaZ.evidence_note: The blaZ gene was found in 59.2% of 2021 isolates and in 48.1% of 2022 isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaZ and mecA genes as prevalent in S. aureus isolates from clinical mastitis cases in Italy, with blaZ being associated with cefoxitin resistance. Additionally, other resistance genes including aph3, ant6, ermC/T, and mph were detected, contributing to resistance against various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic resistance testing and qPCR were used to detect antibiotic resistance genes in S. aureus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Analysis of Antimicrobial Resistance Genes (ARGs) in Enterobacterales and A. baumannii Clinical Strains Colonizing a Single Italian Patient.

full_output.methodology: The study involved antimicrobial susceptibility testing, molecular detection of resistance genes, and data collection from various sectors including human, poultry, and aquaculture.

full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the high prevalence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacterial pathogens in adult and pediatric ICUs, particularly Gram-negative Enterobacterales and non-fermenters, which exhibited resistance to multiple antibiotic classes including beta-lactams, fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, and carbapenems.

full_output.paper_title: Production of Silver Nano-Inks and Surface Coatings for Anti-Microbial Food Packaging and Its Ecological Impact.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed silver nano-inks and surface coatings for anti-bacterial food packaging, demonstrating strong antibacterial activity against E. coli. The silver nanoparticles produced via laser ablation synthesis in solution (LASiS) and ultrasonic spray pyrolysis (USP) showed effective bacterial inhibition, with LASiS under recirculation mode yielding the smallest nanoparticle size and highest antibacterial efficacy.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized laser ablation synthesis in solution (LASiS) and ultrasonic spray pyrolysis (USP) to produce silver nanoparticles, characterized their physicochemical properties, and evaluated their antibacterial activity against E. coli using agar disc diffusion and immersion assays.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance and Genomic Characterization of Salmonella Infantis from Different Sources.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the antimicrobial resistance of Salmonella Infantis strains from various sources, revealing high resistance rates against fluoroquinolones, ampicillin, and tetracycline. Multidrug-resistant (MDR) strains were prevalent, highlighting the need for stricter antimicrobial controls in veterinary medicine.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed 185 S. Infantis strains using MIC testing, MLVA, and serotyping to assess antimicrobial resistance and genetic diversity.

full_output.paper_title: Influence of Lipidation Pattern of the KR12 Fragment of Peptide LL-37 on Its Antibacterial and Hemolytic Activities.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the effects of lipidation patterns on the antibacterial and hemolytic activities of KR12-NH2 peptide fragments. It identified that lipidation at the N-terminal lysine side chain significantly influenced the activity and selectivity of the peptides against various bacterial strains, particularly showing higher selectivity against S. aureus.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (ESI-MS), circular dichroism (CD) spectroscopy, and dynamic light scattering (DLS) to analyze the structural and functional properties of the lipidated KR12-NH2 peptides.

full_output.paper_title: New Bioactive Peptides from the Mediterranean Seagrass Posidonia oceanica (L.) Delile and Their Impact on Antimicrobial Activity and Apoptosis of Human Cancer Cells.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified nine novel peptides from Posidonia oceanica and evaluated their antimicrobial and antibiofilm activities against various bacterial and fungal strains, as well as their cytotoxic effects on HepG2 cancer cells.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the extraction and characterization of peptides from Posidonia oceanica, followed by in vitro testing for antimicrobial and antibiofilm activities, and evaluation of cytotoxic effects on HepG2 cells.

full_output.paper_title: A Comparative Study of the Inhibitory Action of Berberine Derivatives on the Recombinant Protein FtsZ of E. coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the inhibitory action of berberine derivatives on the FtsZ protein of E. coli, identifying compounds that effectively inhibit FtsZ GTPase activity and polymerization, highlighting their potential as novel antibacterial agents.
full_output.methodology: The research involved molecular docking simulations, enzymatic assays, and fluorescence spectroscopy to analyze the interaction and inhibitory effects of berberine derivatives on FtsZ.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization and Comparative Genomic Analysis of Three Virulent E. coli Bacteriophages with the Potential to Reduce Antibiotic-Resistant Bacteria in the Environment.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes three E. coli bacteriophages (BF9, BF15, and BF17) with lytic activity against ESBL/AmpC-producing E. coli. These phages show potential for reducing antibiotic-resistant bacteria in the environment. No genes encoding toxins, antibiotic resistance, or virulence factors were identified in their genomes.
full_output.methodology: Genomic sequencing, comparative genomics, and in vitro bacteriolytic activity assays were performed.

full_output.paper_title: A Novel Strategy to Identify Endolysins with Lytic Activity against Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a novel strategy to identify endolysins with lytic activity against MRSA. A new endolysin, LyJH1892, was successfully developed and characterized, showing potent lytic activity against both methicillin-susceptible and methicillin-resistant S. aureus, as well as coagulase-negative staphylococci.
full_output.methodology: Bioinformatical strategy involving genome retrieval, annotation, selection of endolysin candidates, and experimental validation through overexpression, purification, and lytic activity assessment.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis and Biological Evaluation of Piperazine Hybridized Coumarin Indolylcyanoenones with Antibacterial Potential.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a novel compound, 4-chlorobenzyl derivative 11f, which exhibits potent antibacterial activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa with a low MIC of 1 μg/mL. It disrupts bacterial cell membranes, increases membrane permeability, causes depolarization, and induces oxidative stress and metabolic dysfunction in bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Chemical synthesis, antibacterial activity testing, membrane disruption assays, and molecular docking studies.

full_output.paper_title: A Comparison of the Antibacterial Efficacy of Carbohydrate Lipid-like (Thio)Ether, Sulfone, and Ester Derivatives against Paenibacillus larvae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several carbohydrate lipid-like derivatives with high antibacterial efficacy against Paenibacillus larvae, including dodecyl derivatives with (thio)glycosidic or ether linkages at C-6, which showed MICs ranging from 12.5 μM to 50 μM. These compounds were more effective than traditional antibiotics and larval food components.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antibacterial efficacy of 24 glycolipid mimetics against two P. larvae strains using MIC measurements.

full_output.paper_title: The Novel Chiral 2(5H)-Furanone Sulfones Possessing Terpene Moiety: Synthesis and Biological Activity.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis of chiral 2(5H)-furanone sulfones, with compound 26 showing potent antimicrobial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Bacillus subtilis. Additionally, compound 26 synergizes with aminoglycosides to enhance their efficacy.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of chiral 2(5H)-furanone sulfones, antimicrobial activity testing, and evaluation of synergistic effects with aminoglycosides.

full_output.paper_title: Investigating the Antibacterial Effects of Synthetic Gamma-Lactam Heterocycles on Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus Strains and Assessing the Safety and Effectiveness of Lead Compound MFM514.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the antibacterial effects of synthetic gamma-lactam heterocycles against MRSA and identified MFM514 as a lead compound with good inhibitory activity. MFM514 showed MIC values of 7.8-15.6 µg/mL against MRSA and MSSA isolates and demonstrated a favorable safety profile with a high selectivity index.
full_output.methodology: The study synthesized and tested 32 gamma-lactam derivatives for their antibacterial activity against MRSA and MSSA strains using MIC assays. Cytotoxicity was assessed using the MTT assay, and acute toxicity was evaluated in mice.

full_output.paper_title: Phage Display Technology in Antimicrobial Research: Targeting Virulence Factors, Resistance Proteins, and Essential Bacterial Components
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the use of phage display technology to identify peptides and antibodies targeting bacterial virulence factors, resistance proteins, and essential components, highlighting their potential in combating multidrug-resistant bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Phage display technology was utilized to screen for peptides and antibodies that bind to specific bacterial targets, followed by evaluation of their antibacterial activity and mechanism of action.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies resveratrol as a potential quorum quencher that targets the quorum-sensing system of MRSA, specifically the accessory gene regulator proteins A, B, and C, and the signal transduction protein TRAP.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis and Biological Evaluation of New Schiff Bases Derived from 4-Amino-5-(3-fluorophenyl)-1,2,4-triazole-3-thione.
full_output.key_findings: The study synthesized new Schiff bases derived from 4-amino-5-(3-fluorophenyl)-1,2,4-triazole-3-thione and evaluated their antimicrobial activity. Compounds RO4 and RO12 showed notable antifungal activity against Candida species, while RO9 exhibited antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Staphylococcus epidermidis.
full_output.methodology: Chemical synthesis, antimicrobial activity testing using broth microdilution, and structural characterization via NMR and IR spectroscopy.

full_output.paper_title: Click Triazole as a Linker for Pretargeting Strategies: Synthesis, Docking Investigations, Fluorescence Diagnosis, and Antibacterial Action Studies.
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on designing and synthesizing compounds A1, A2, and A3, along with fluorescent probes T1, T2, T3, and T4, for potential antibacterial applications. The synthesized compounds and probes were capable of forming diagnostic molecules for fluorescence detection of Agrobacterium tumefaciens.
full_output.methodology: The compounds and probes were synthesized and characterized using various spectroscopic techniques. Their antibacterial activity was evaluated using microdilution assays, and their binding to VirB8 was studied through molecular docking.

full_output.paper_title: One-Step Synthesis of Self-Stratification Core-Shell Latex for Antimicrobial Coating.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a one-step synthesis of cationic acrylate-based core-shell latex (CACS latex) with antimicrobial properties. QAS-BN, a quaternary ammonium salt, was incorporated into the latex to provide broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity against bacteria, molds, and viruses.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of CACS latex via emulsion polymerization, characterization of latex properties, and evaluation of antimicrobial activity against various pathogens.

full_output.paper_title: CeO(2) Nanoparticles-Regulated Plasmid Uptake and Bioavailability for Reducing Transformation of Extracellular Antibiotic Resistance Genes.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that CeO2 nanoparticles can regulate the transformation of plasmid-borne antibiotic resistance genes by reducing plasmid availability, inhibiting DNA replication, and down-regulating gene expression related to DNA uptake. floR.genetic_context: In the IncFIB plasmid draft (Figure 3A), two clusters with high densities of mobile elements and resistance genes were found. Cluster A, of approximately 21 kbp (Figure 3B), has a Tn2 family transposon that contains the tetR and tetA genes that confer resistance to tetracyclines and includes a class 1 integron together with a mer operon for mercury resistance. The integron has insertions of the antibiotic resistance genes ant(3′)-Ia, qacEΔ1 and sul1, which confer resistance to aminoglycosides, quaternary ammonium and sulfonamides, respectively. This cluster is suggested to be well conserved as it is present in all Infantis isolates containing the IncFIB plasmid. On the other hand, cluster B (Figure 3C), is 32 kbp in size, and is made up of various mobile elements, mainly of the IS 26 type. These mobile elements carry aminoglycoside resistance genes, such as aph(3′)-Ia, acc(3)-IVa, aph(4)-Ia, as well as fosfomycin resistance genes, fosA3. On the other hand, the presence of a transposon that contains the floR gene, for amphenicol resistance, is characterized by having two passenger genes that correspond to virD2 and a gene from the lysR transcriptional regulator family. This cluster also includes a transposon that is truncated by the insertion of another mobile element, which contains the fosA3 gene. This transposon includes the bla CTX-M-65 gene, an extended-spectrum beta-lactamase, together with the yncD-Cter / ΔiroN gene, involved in the formation of siderophores.
floR.evidence_note: The presence of the floR gene in the IncFIB plasmid of Salmonella Infantis is mentioned, indicating its role in conferring resistance to phenicol antibiotics.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified linezolid resistance mechanisms in MRSA isolates, including mutations in domain V of 23 S rRNA (A2338T, T2504C, G2576T) and genes such as cfr(B), optrA, msrA, mecA, and vanA.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize linezolid resistance mechanisms in MRSA isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Review and analysis of the overlapping threats of carbapenem and polymyxin resistant E. coli and Klebsiella in Africa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies various carbapenem and polymyxin resistance genes in E. coli and Klebsiella isolates across Africa, highlighting the prevalence of bla OXA-48, bla OXA-181, bla NDM-1, bla NDM-5, bla VIM-1, bla VIM-2, bla KPC, bla KPC-2, mcr-1, mgrB, and phoPQ/pmrAB.
full_output.methodology: The study involved a systematic review of literature and data extraction from various sources to analyze carbapenem and polymyxin resistance in E. coli and Klebsiella isolates from African nations.
full_output.sample_size: 1341 reports for carbapenem resistance and 341 reports for polymyxin resistance

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance and Biofilm Formation of Staphylococcus aureus Isolates from Febrile Cases: Findings from a Rural Cohort of Odisha, India
full_output.key_findings: The study found that Staphylococcus aureus isolates from febrile cases in a rural cohort of Odisha, India, exhibited high resistance to penicillin, with many being multidrug resistant. Additionally, 27.4% of the isolates were strong biofilm producers, and they showed sensitivity to linezolid, gentamicin, and tetracycline.
full_output.methodology: The study involved culturing blood samples from febrile patients, identifying S. aureus isolates, determining antibiotic susceptibility via disk diffusion, and assessing biofilm formation using a microplate method.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic Resistance among Fusobacterium, Capnocytophaga, and Leptotrichia Species of the Oral Cavity.

gyrA.notes: A substitution of the nucleic acid G by A was found at position 2,456,868, but it did not result in an amino acid substitution.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified resistance to ciprofloxacin and moxifloxacin in three Leptotrichia isolates, and resistance to moxifloxacin and metronidazole in two F. nucleatum isolates. A mutation in the QRDR of gyrA was found in two Leptotrichia isolates, which may contribute to fluoroquinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the E-test and PCR for resistance gene detection.

full_output.paper_title: Development of LpxH Inhibitors Chelating the Active Site Dimanganese Metal Cluster of LpxH.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the development of sulfonyl piperazine LpxH inhibitors, JH-LPH-45 (8) and JH-LPH-50 (13), which chelate the active site di-manganese cluster of K. pneumoniae LpxH, significantly improving their potency against LpxH.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the design, synthesis, and biochemical evaluation of LpxH inhibitors, along with structural analysis of Kp LpxH complexes with the inhibitors.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic characterization of endemic diarrheagenic Escherichia coli and Escherichia albertii from infants with diarrhea in Vietnam.

qnrS.mechanism: protects DNA gyrase from quinolone action

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antibiotic resistance genes and mutations in DEC and E. albertii strains isolated from infants with diarrhea in Vietnam, highlighting the high prevalence of resistance to ciprofloxacin and ceftriaxone.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis of 61 DEC-like isolates using MiSeq sequencing and bioinformatics tools to identify resistance genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis and Characterization of Silver Nanoparticles Using Medicinal Plant D. uncinatum and Evaluation of Their Antimicrobial, Antioxidant, and Cytotoxic Activities
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial, antioxidant, and cytotoxic activities of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) synthesized using different parts of the medicinal plant D. uncinatum. RS-AgNPs showed the highest antioxidant and antibacterial activities, while S-AgNPs exhibited the highest antifungal activity. The study also found that AgNPs had significant cytotoxic effects against cancer cells.
full_output.methodology: The study used various analytical techniques including FTIR, XRD, TEM, and TG/DTA/DTG to characterize the synthesized AgNPs. Antimicrobial, antioxidant, and cytotoxic activities were evaluated using standard laboratory assays.

full_output.paper_title: Role of AlgC and GalU in the Intrinsic Antibiotic Resistance of Helicobacter pylori.

algC.validation_method: knockout and complementation experiments with MIC testing

full_output.key_findings: AlgC and GalU are crucial for the intrinsic antibiotic resistance of H. pylori by maintaining the lipid A-core structure and reducing membrane permeability. Their knockout increases susceptibility to multiple antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Gene knockout and complementation experiments combined with MIC testing and LPS analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Penicillin Binding Protein Substitutions Cooccur with Fluoroquinolone Resistance in Epidemic Lineages of Multidrug-Resistant Clostridioides difficile.

PBP1.mechanism: Amino acid substitutions in the transpeptidase domain reduce drug affinity
PBP1.validation_method: Phenotyping of isolates with PBP substitutions and wild-type controls

PBP3.mechanism: Amino acid substitutions in the transpeptidase domain reduce drug affinity
PBP3.validation_method: Phenotyping of isolates with PBP substitutions and wild-type controls

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies PBP1 and PBP3 amino acid substitutions that are associated with elevated cephalosporin MICs in multidrug-resistant Clostridioides difficile lineages. These substitutions co-occur with fluoroquinolone resistance and contribute to reduced susceptibility to β-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, phenotyping of isolates with PBP substitutions, and phylogenetic analysis to date substitution acquisition.

full_output.paper_title: A Novel Tool to Identify Bactericidal Compounds against Vulnerable Targets in Drug-Tolerant M. tuberculosis found in Caseum.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a caseum surrogate model to identify compounds with treatment-shortening potential against drug-tolerant M. tuberculosis. The model successfully replicated the nonreplicating state and drug tolerance of Mtb in caseum, enabling the evaluation of bactericidal activity of bedaquiline analogs TBAJ876 and TBAJ587.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a caseum surrogate model generated from THP-1-derived macrophage lysates, inoculated with M. tuberculosis, to evaluate drug susceptibility and bactericidal activity.

full_output.paper_title: Preceding Host History of Conjugative Resistance Plasmids Affects Intra- and Interspecific Transfer Potential from Biofilm.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies large deletions in the Tra2 conjugal transfer region of the RP4 plasmid in K. pneumoniae-evolved plasmids, which affect PRD1 phage infectivity and conjugation efficiency.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing, spot tests, and conjugation assays were used to analyze the genetic changes and their impact on plasmid functionality.

full_output.paper_title: Thymol-Decorated Gold Nanoparticles for Curing Clinical Infections Caused by Bacteria Resistant to Last-Resort Antibiotics.
full_output.key_findings: Thymol-decorated gold nanoparticles (Thymol_Au NPs) showed strong antibacterial activity against multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria, including strains resistant to tigecycline (TGC), colistin (COL), and ceftazidime-avibactam (CZA).
full_output.methodology: Synthesis and characterization of thymol-decorated gold nanoparticles, evaluation of antibacterial activity via broth microdilution, and analysis of bacterial membrane permeability and biofilm disruption.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization and comparative genomic analysis of Acinetobacter baumannii isolated from the community and the hospital: an epidemiological study in Segamat, Malaysia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in hospital isolates of Acinetobacter baumannii, including beta-lactamases (blaADC, blaOXA-51, blaOXA-72, blaOXA-420, blaOXA-23), extended-spectrum beta-lactamases (TEM-12, TEM-116), aminoglycoside-modifying enzymes (APH(3')-Ia, APH(3'')-Ib, APH(6)-Id, ANT(3'')-IIa, armA), sulfonamide resistance gene (sul2), tetracycline resistance gene (tetB), macrolide resistance genes (mphE, msrE), and various efflux pumps (adeABC, deFGH, deIJK, abgQ, mvA, abeM, flor). None of the community isolates were MDR.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify AMR genes and mutations in Acinetobacter baumannii isolates from the community and hospital in Segamat, Malaysia.

full_output.paper_title: Bacterial profile, their antibiotic susceptibility pattern, and associated factors of urinary tract infections in children at Hiwot Fana Specialized University Hospital, Eastern Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high prevalence of bacterial urinary tract infections (UTIs) in children, with E. coli and K. pneumoniae being the most common pathogens. Resistance to multiple antibiotics was widespread, particularly to beta-lactams.
full_output.methodology: The study conducted antimicrobial susceptibility testing on bacterial isolates from urine samples of children with UTIs.

full_output.paper_title: The F-pilus biomechanical adaptability accelerates conjugative dissemination of antimicrobial resistance and biofilm formation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the F-pilus as a structurally resilient and adaptable appendage that enhances conjugative DNA transmission and biofilm formation under hydrodynamic stress, highlighting its role in the dissemination of antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.methodology: Biophysical and molecular dynamics methods, force-extension measurements using optical tweezers, and molecular dynamics simulations were used to analyze the biomechanical properties of the F-pilus.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports a case of prosthetic joint infection caused by an imipenem-resistant Mycobacterium senegalense strain, highlighting the need for accurate identification and antimicrobial susceptibility testing of fast-growing nontuberculous mycobacteria.
full_output.methodology: Microbial identification was performed using MALDI-TOF MS and hsp65 gene sequencing, while antimicrobial susceptibility was determined by MIC according to CLSI guidelines.

full_output.paper_title: Whole genome sequencing to study antimicrobial resistance and RTX virulence genes in equine Actinobacillus isolates.
full_output.key_findings: Two plasmids were identified in an A. equuli strain that conferred resistance to penicillin-ampicillin-amoxicillin and chloramphenicol. The plasmids carried the class A beta-lactamase ROB-1, the aminoglycoside 3-phosphatase APH(3'')-Ib, and the chloramphenicol O-acetyltransferase catIII.
full_output.methodology: Long-read nanopore whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.key_findings: The paper reviews the transmission of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) from mothers to infants, focusing on the impact of factors such as mode of delivery, breastfeeding, and antibiotic exposure. It highlights the presence of various ARGs in the infant gut, including beta-lactamases, tetracycline resistance genes, macrolide resistance genes, and aminoglycoside resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: Literature review and analysis of existing studies on maternal-infant antibiotic resistance gene transmission.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Peptide Cec4 Eradicates Multidrug-Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii in vitro and in vivo.
full_output.key_findings: The antimicrobial peptide Cec4 effectively eradicates multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii in vitro and in vivo by disrupting the bacterial cell membrane, increasing membrane permeability, and inducing reactive oxygen species. Cec4 does not induce stable drug resistance in A. baumannii and exhibits low toxicity in mammalian cells and animals.
full_output.methodology: In vitro and in vivo experiments, including membrane permeability assays, transcriptome analysis, and toxicity assessments in cell cultures and animal models.
full_output.sample_size: 21 clinical isolates of multidrug-resistant A. baumannii

full_output.paper_title: High Frequency of bla(OXA-48like) Producing Klebsiella pneumoniae Isolated from Nosocomial Infection in Azerbaijan, Iran.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaOXA-48-like as the most common carbapenemase gene in CRKP isolates in Azerbaijan, Iran, followed by blaNDM, blaIMP, blaVIM, and blaKPC. Outer membrane porin genes OmpK35 and OmpK36 were also frequently detected.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR, and RAPD-PCR were used to analyze CRKP isolates.

full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to analyze the resistance mechanisms in Escherichia coli.

full_output.paper_title: Minimal Surviving Inoculum in Collective Antibiotic Resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the β-lactamase TEM-1 in Escherichia coli, demonstrating its role in collective antibiotic resistance through enzymatic degradation of β-lactam antibiotics, particularly cefotaxime.

full_output.paper_title: Mutant Prevention Concentration, Frequency of Spontaneous Mutant Selection, and Mutant Selection Window-a New Approach to the In Vitro Determination of the Antimicrobial Potency of Compounds.
full_output.key_findings: The study introduces new parameters for evaluating antimicrobial potency, focusing on mutant prevention concentration (MPC) and mutant selection window (MSW). It compares agar-dilution and broth-dilution methods for determining these parameters and highlights the importance of considering dominant and inferior mutants in resistance management.
full_output.methodology: The study used agar-dilution and broth-dilution methods to determine MPC and MSW values for ciprofloxacin, linezolid, and a novel benzosiloxaborole compound (No37) against Staphylococcus aureus ATCC 29213.

full_output.paper_title: Proteogenomic analysis of Serratia marcescens using computational subtractive genomics approach.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of Vancomycin-resistant enterococci (VRE) in Egypt (2010-2022): a systematic review and meta-analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that VanA and VanB genes are prevalent among VRE in Egypt, with VanA being more common. The pooled prevalence of VRE was 26%, and E. faecalis had a higher prevalence than E. faecium.

full_output.paper_title: High frequency of NDM-1 and OXA-48 carbapenemase genes among Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates in central Iran.

full_output.paper_title: Exploring the epidemiology of mcr genes, genetic context and plasmids in Enterobacteriaceae originating from pigs and humans on farms in Thailand.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that a frameshift mutation in the mvfR gene enhances polymyxin B resistance in P. aeruginosa by upregulating rfaD, which affects LPS biosynthesis and reduces outer membrane permeability. Additionally, pmrB mutations also contribute to polymyxin B resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, complementation experiments, transcriptomic analysis, and outer membrane permeability assays were used to determine the role of mvfR and pmrB mutations in polymyxin B resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Significance of wastewater surveillance in detecting the prevalence of SARS-CoV-2 variants and other respiratory viruses in the community - A multi-site evaluation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes in wastewater samples, including those conferring resistance to macrolides, beta-lactamases, tetracyclines, sulfonamides, glycopeptides, fluoroquinolones, trimethoprim, aminoglycosides, phenicols, and colistin. These findings highlight the potential of wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) as a tool for monitoring AMR in communities.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic analysis and bioinformatics pipelines were used to detect and characterize AMR genes in wastewater samples.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and multidrug-resistant profile of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus pseudintermedius in dogs, cats, and pet owners in Malaysia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus pseudintermedius (MRSP) isolates from dogs, cats, and pet owners in Malaysia. The MRSA isolate was resistant to enrofloxacin, gentamicin, and cefoxitin, while MRSP isolates showed resistance to doxycycline, oxytetracycline, and other antimicrobials. New sequence types (STs) were identified for MRSA (ST789) and MRSP (ST2296, ST2297, ST2298).
full_output.methodology: Molecular epidemiology and antimicrobial profiling were used, including PCR for detection of mecA gene, disk diffusion for antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and multilocus sequence typing (MLST).

full_output.paper_title: Effectiveness of raw bacteriocin produced from lactic acid bacteria on biofilm of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the mecA gene as a key factor in methicillin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus, highlighting its role in conferring resistance to methicillin.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR to detect the mecA gene in Staphylococcus aureus isolates and evaluated the effectiveness of crude bacteriocin from lactic acid bacteria against MRSA biofilms.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance pattern of avian pathogenic Escherichia coli with detection of extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing isolates in broilers in east Algeria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of antimicrobial resistance in avian pathogenic Escherichia coli (APEC) isolates from broilers in east Algeria, including resistance to ampicillin, tetracycline, nalidixic acid, ofloxacin, doxycycline, ciprofloxacin, trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole, and gentamicin. Two isolates were confirmed as extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL)-producing strains.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial resistance was assessed using the disk diffusion method, and ESBL production was confirmed via double-disk tests.

full_output.paper_title: Distribution analysis of tetracycline resistance genes in Escherichia coli isolated from floor surface and effluent of pig slaughterhouses in Banten Province, Indonesia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the distribution of tetracycline resistance genes (tetA, tetB, tetC, tetE, tetM, tetO, and tetX) in Escherichia coli isolates from pig slaughterhouses in Banten Province, Indonesia. The tetO gene was the most dominant in floor surface samples, while tetA was dominant in effluent samples.
full_output.methodology: The study used qPCR to detect tetracycline resistance genes in E. coli isolates from floor surface and effluent samples.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and resistance to antibacterial agents in Salmonella enterica strains isolated from poultry products in Northern Kazakhstan.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in Salmonella enterica strains from poultry products in Northern Kazakhstan, including tetA, tetB, blaTEM, aadA, sul3, catII, and cmlA, which confer resistance to various antibiotics such as tetracycline, beta-lactams, aminoglycosides, sulfonamides, and chloramphenicol.

full_output.paper_title: Association of multilocus sequencing types and antimicrobial resistance profiles of methicillin-resistant Mammaliicoccus sciuri in animals in Southern Thailand.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mecA and blaZ as the primary antimicrobial resistance genes in methicillin-resistant Mammaliicoccus sciuri isolates from Southern Thailand, with no detection of mecC. Multiple multilocus sequence types (MLSTs) were found, highlighting the diversity of resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: PCR, MIC testing, and MLST analysis were used to characterize antimicrobial resistance genes and genetic diversity in M. sciuri isolates.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro activity of sulopenem and comparator agents against Enterobacterales and anaerobic clinical isolates collected during the SENTRY Antimicrobial Surveillance Program.
full_output.key_findings: Sulopenem showed potent in vitro activity against Enterobacterales and anaerobic isolates, including those with resistance mechanisms such as ESBL-phenotype and fluoroquinolone non-susceptibility.

Seven out of eight synthesized GAN-designed peptides showed antibacterial activity, with GAN-pep 3 and GAN-pep 8 exhibiting the most promising results.
full_output.methodology: The study employed a WGAN-GP model trained on known AMPs to generate novel AMP candidates, followed by in vitro evaluation using disc diffusion and MIC assays to assess antibacterial activity.

full_output.paper_title: Preparation of Ciprofloxacin-Based Carbon Dots with High Antibacterial Activity.

full_output.key_findings: This meta-analysis identified high levels of resistance in Staphylococcus aureus to various antibiotics in Nigeria, including penicillin G (82%), cloxacillin (77%), amoxacillin (74%), cefuroxime (69%), ampicillin (68%), erythromycin (47%), chloramphenicol (47%), methicillin (46%), ofloxacin (24%), and rifampicin (24%). full_output.paper_title: The Effects of Antiperspirant Aluminum Chlorohydrate on the Development of Antibiotic Resistance in Staphylococcus epidermidis.

full_output.methodology: This is a review article summarizing existing literature on AMR in poultry production and discussing potential strategies for bacterial control.

full_output.paper_title: MALDI-TOF MS Indirect Beta-Lactamase Detection in Ampicillin-Resistant Haemophilus influenzae.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that MALDI-TOF MS can indirectly detect beta-lactamase-producing Haemophilus influenzae by analyzing ampicillin degradation products, providing a rapid method for identifying resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: MALDI-TOF MS was used to analyze ampicillin degradation products in H. influenzae isolates, comparing results with traditional susceptibility testing methods.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified high prevalence of resistance to tetracycline (67.62%), streptomycin (24.13%), and ampicillin (21.10%) in commensal E. coli isolates from swine at slaughter in the US. Significant increasing trends in resistance to amoxicillin-clavulanic acid, ampicillin, azithromycin, cefoxitin, ceftriaxone, and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole were observed.
full_output.methodology: Analysis of publicly available AMR surveillance data from the National Antimicrobial Resistance Monitoring System (NARMS) using statistical methods including Mann-Kendall test and Poisson regression.

full_output.paper_title: The Isolation and Structure Elucidation of Spirotetronate Lobophorins A, B, and H8 from Streptomyces sp. CB09030 and Their Biosynthetic Gene Cluster.

The glycosyltransferase LobG1 in S. sp. CB09030 has point mutations compared to previously reported LobG1.

full_output.paper_title: The Antibacterial Activity of Rhazya stricta Extracts against Klebsiella pneumoniae Isolated from Some Soil Invertebrates at High Altitudes.

full_output.methodology: PCR detection of genes, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and evaluation of antibacterial and antibiofilm activities of plant extracts.

full_output.paper_title: Hylin-a1: A Host Defense Peptide with Antibacterial Potential against Staphylococcus aureus Multi-Resistant Strains.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the antibacterial activity of the host defense peptide Hylin-a1 against Staphylococcus aureus, demonstrating its effectiveness against multi-resistant strains, including β-lactamase-resistant and methicillin-resistant S. aureus. Hylin-a1 exhibits bacteriostatic and bactericidal effects, reduces bacterial invasion, and modulates the inflammatory response.
full_output.methodology: The study employed in vitro experiments including MTT cytotoxicity assays, MIC and MBC determinations, time-killing assays, invasion assays, biofilm activity assessments, FACScan analysis, SEM imaging, and qPCR to evaluate the antibacterial properties of Hylin-a1.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence, Resistance Patterns and Biofilm Production Ability of Bacterial Uropathogens from Cases of Community-Acquired Urinary Tract Infections in South Italy.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the prevalence of bacterial uropathogens, particularly Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Proteus mirabilis, and their resistance patterns to various antibiotics. It also notes the significant biofilm production ability of these isolates, which contributes to their persistence and resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized Vitek 2 system for bacterial identification and antibiotic susceptibility testing, along with biofilm formation assays using the microtiter plate method.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Characteristics of Methicillin-Resistant and Susceptible Staphylococcus aureus from Pediatric Patients in Eastern China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaZ and mecA genes as major contributors to antimicrobial resistance in Staphylococcus aureus isolates from pediatric patients in eastern China, with blaZ conferring penicillin resistance and mecA responsible for methicillin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and MLST analysis were used to characterize the molecular traits of S. aureus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiological and Clinical Features of Streptococcus dysgalactiae ssp. equisimilis stG62647 and Other emm Types in Germany.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the increasing prevalence of the emm type stG62647 among invasive Streptococcus dysgalactiae ssp. equisimilis infections in Germany, showing a significant rise in its occurrence over the study period. It also notes that stG62647 isolates exhibited lower resistance rates to certain antibiotics compared to other emm types.
full_output.methodology: The study combined national surveillance data with a single-center clinical study to analyze the epidemiological and clinical features of various emm types of Streptococcus dysgalactiae ssp. equisimilis.

full_output.paper_title: Snapshot of Phenotypic and Molecular Virulence and Resistance Profiles in Multidrug-Resistant Strains Isolated in a Tertiary Hospital in Romania.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple beta-lactamase genes (bla CTX-M, bla SHV, bla TEM, bla KPC, bla OXA-48, bla NDM, bla OXA-23, bla OXA-24, bla VIM, and bla IMP) in multidrug-resistant strains of Klebsiella pneumoniae, Acinetobacter baumannii, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Additionally, several virulence genes involved in biofilm formation and tissue destruction were detected.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to detect beta-lactamase and virulence genes in the bacterial strains.

full_output.paper_title: A Novel Generation of Tailored Antimicrobial Drugs Based on Recombinant Multidomain Proteins.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents the development of a new generation of tailored antimicrobial drugs using recombinant multidomain proteins based on Host Defense Peptides (HDPs). Three new antimicrobials, D5L37βD3, D5L37D5L37, and D5LAL37βD3, were designed and evaluated for their antimicrobial activity against various bacterial strains, with D5L37D5L37 showing the most promising results.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the design and production of recombinant multidomain proteins based on HDPs, followed by evaluation of their antimicrobial activity through MIC assays, biofilm eradication tests, and physicochemical characterization.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis of 6″-Modified Kanamycin A Derivatives and Evaluation of Their Antibacterial Properties.

mutations_found.validated_by: susceptibility testing of the native strain

fusA.notes: Mutations in the gene fusA (encoding the EF-G protein) were reported as a novel mechanism of aminoglycoside resistance in the clinical strains of P. aeruginosa.

full_output.key_findings: The study focused on synthesizing 6″-modified kanamycin A derivatives and evaluating their antibacterial properties. It was found that introducing a guanidine residue led to a compound with improved activity against S. aureus. Most of the obtained derivatives were less influenced by the resistant mechanism associated with mutations of the elongation factor G (EF-G) than the parent kanamycin A. Mutations in the gene fusA (encoding the EF-G protein) were reported as a novel mechanism of aminoglycoside resistance in the clinical strains of P. aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis of kanamycin A derivatives, evaluation of their antibacterial activity using MIC assays, and determination of the minimum inhibitory concentration. The study also included susceptibility testing of the native strain and analysis of mutations in the gene fusA.

full_output.paper_title: Recent Advances in Strategies to Combat Bacterial Drug Resistance: Antimicrobial Materials and Drug Delivery Systems.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses various strategies to combat bacterial drug resistance, focusing on antimicrobial materials and drug delivery systems. It highlights the mechanisms of antibiotic resistance and the potential of antimicrobial peptides, enzyme inhibitors, efflux pump inhibitors, metal nanomaterials, cationic polymers, and photo-sensitive materials as innovative solutions.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews existing literature and discusses various strategies for combating bacterial drug resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of Increased Extracellular Vesicle-Mediated Tigecycline Resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies extracellular vesicles (EVs) as mediators of tigecycline (TIG) resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii (AB). TIG-resistant AB produces more EVs, which can transfer TIG resistance to other gram-negative bacteria like E. coli, S. typhimurium, and P. mirabilis, but not to K. pneumoniae or S. aureus. Protein components of TIG-R EVs are critical for resistance transfer.
full_output.methodology: The study used EV isolation, characterization, and transfer experiments to assess TIG resistance mechanisms in AB.

full_output.paper_title: The Lytic Activity of Bacteriophage ZCSE9 against Salmonella enterica and Its Synergistic Effects with Kanamycin.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the lytic bacteriophage ZCSE9, which exhibits broad host range and stability under various environmental conditions. It demonstrates synergistic effects with kanamycin against multiple Salmonella serotypes, reducing the required antibiotic concentration for bacterial inhibition.
full_output.methodology: The study involves phage isolation, characterization, genomic analysis, and evaluation of phage-antibiotic synergy using MIC tests and time-killing curves.

full_output.paper_title: Synergistic effect and antibiofilm activity of the antimicrobial peptide K11 with conventional antibiotics against multidrug-resistant and extensively drug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the antibacterial and antibiofilm activity of the antimicrobial peptide K11 against multidrug-resistant (MDR) and extensively drug-resistant (XDR) Klebsiella pneumoniae. K11 shows synergistic effects with several conventional antibiotics and prevents biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: The study uses broth microdilution, checkerboard assays, and crystal violet staining to evaluate the antimicrobial and antibiofilm activities of K11.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiological and genomic analyses of human isolates of Streptococcus suis between 2005 and 2021 in Shenzhen, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antimicrobial resistance genes in human isolates of Streptococcus suis, including ant(6)-Ia, tet(O), and erm(B), which confer resistance to streptomycin, tetracycline, and erythromycin/clindamycin respectively.

full_output.key_findings: The case report highlights the successful treatment of a multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae infection with carrimycin, suggesting it as an alternative therapy when conventional treatments fail.

bla_VIM.mechanism: metallo-beta-lactamase (MBL) genes tend to be less prevalent than acquired bla OXA carbapenemase genes in A. baumannii. However, many MBL genes have been detected in these species, including bla IMP , bla VIM , bla SIM , and bla NDM , and these genes cause decreased susceptibility to all β-lactam agents, except for monobactam.
bla_VIM.role_in_paper: The SENTRY Antimicrobial Surveillance Program for 2020–2021 included 788 Acinetobacter spp. clinical isolates collected from US hospitals and 943 collected from European countries, including Turkey and Israel. A total of 26.0% (205) and 61.8% (583) of isolates from the United States and Europe were not susceptible to imipenem and/or meropenem. These isolates were sequenced and screened in silico for β-lactamase genes. bla OXA carbapenemase genes prevailed in this collection. All European isolates but 1 each from Israel and Turkey carried bla OXA-23 –like (80.5%), bla OXA-24 –like (16.6%), bla OXA-213 –like (0.3%), or a combination of 2 bla OXA carbapenamases (2.2%) ( Table 1 ). Isolates from US hospitals also showed a similar profile, with bla OXA-23 –like (52.2%) and bla OXA-24 –like (29.3%) as most prevalent, but a higher number of isolates (13.2%) negative for bla OXA carbapenemases. MBL genes were not detected in these isolates, except for 7 (1.2%) isolates carrying bla NDM-1 from Belgium (1), Germany (1), Israel (4), and Turkey (1) and 2 (1.0%) isolates from the United States (data not shown). In addition, all but 1 isolate carrying bla NDM-1 also carried bla OXA-23 (7) or bla OXA-58 (1; data not shown). A small number of isolates showed other β-lactamases, such as 8 isolates with bla CTX-M-115 (and also bla OXA-24 from Turkey), 2 isolates with bla GES-1 (and also bla OXA-23 from Turkey), 1 isolate with bla GES-22 (and also bla OXA-24 from Germany), 4 isolates with bla PER-1 (and also bla OXA-23 from Turkey), 2 isolates with bla PER-7 (and also bla OXA-23 from Turkey), and 4 isolates from the United States with bla SHV-12 and without a bla OXA carbapenemase.
bla_VIM.genetic_context: bla VIM genes were first detected in P. aeruginosa in Italy and France in 1997 [ 95 , 96 ], and since then, many studies have reported the detection of bla VIM variants in Acinetobacter spp., including bla VIM-1 , bla VIM-2 , bla VIM-3 , bla VIM-4 , and bla VIM-11 [ 88 , 93 , 97–101 ]. Similar to bla IMP variants, bla VIM genes were located as a part of integron structures [ 96 ].

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in the ftsI and pbp3 genes that confer reduced susceptibility to sulbactam and sulbactam-durlobactam in Acinetobacter species. These mutations include S390T, V505L, T511A, A326V, S1010R, H370Y, and A578T.
