full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis of AgNPs using chemical reduction, adsorption of AgNPs and AgNO3 onto ESM, and characterization using various analytical techniques. Antimicrobial activity was evaluated using agar well diffusion and MTT assays.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial and Biofilm Production Inhibition Activity of Thymus vulgaris L. Essential Oil against Salmonella spp. Isolates from Reptiles.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in Salmonella spp. isolates from reptiles, including genes encoding multidrug efflux pumps, aminoglycoside resistance, bacitracin resistance, and fosfomycin resistance. Despite the presence of these genes, all isolates were susceptible to tested antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were conducted to identify AMR genes and assess the effectiveness of Thymus vulgaris L. essential oil against Salmonella spp.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence, Serotypes, Antimicrobial Resistance and Biofilm-Forming Ability of Listeria monocytogenes Isolated from Bulk-Tank Bovine Milk in Northern Greece.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that all L. monocytogenes isolates were multidrug resistant, with resistance to penicillin and clindamycin being common features. The isolates carried several virulence genes, including inlA, inlC, inlJ, plcA, hlyA, and iap, but actA was detected in only three isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the isolation and characterization of L. monocytogenes from bovine bulk-tank milk samples, including molecular serotyping, detection of virulence genes, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and assessment of biofilm-forming ability.

full_output.paper_title: Effectiveness of sitafloxacin monotherapy for quinolone-resistant rectal and urogenital Mycoplasma genitalium infections: a prospective cohort study.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antibiotic resistance genes in Enterococcus faecium strain RAOG174, including aac(6'), vanHAX, erm, msr(C), and tet(O), along with mutations in pbp5, parC, and gyrA genes, indicating intrinsic and acquired resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Hybrid genome assembly and in silico prediction tools were used to analyze the resistance genes and mutations in E. faecium RAOG174.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that resistance to clindamycin increased in B. thetaiotaomicron and resistance to ampicillin increased in B. ovatus.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective observational study based on national surveillance data.
full_output.sample_size: 41 949 Bacteroides spp., 40 603 Clostridium spp., 7013 Fusobacterium spp., and 5428 Prevotella spp.

full_output.paper_title: Effectors of the Type VI Secretion System Have the Potential to Be Modified into Antimicrobial Peptides.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Tsap, a T6SS effector from ExPEC RS218, which was modified into three antimicrobial peptides (Tsap-1, Tsap-2, Tsap-3) with potent antibacterial activity against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized genetic manipulation, antimicrobial activity assays, and microscopic techniques to characterize the antimicrobial properties of Tsap-derived peptides.

full_output.paper_title: Dissemination of ArmA- and OXA-23-co-producing Acinetobacter baumannii Global Clone 2 in Switzerland, 2020-2021.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the increasing incidence of Acinetobacter baumannii co-producing OXA-23 and ArmA in Switzerland, primarily due to the dissemination of the high-risk Global Clone 2 (GC-2).
full_output.methodology: PCR, Sanger sequencing, PFGE, and whole-genome sequencing were used to characterize the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Population structure, serotype distribution and antibiotic resistance of Streptococcus pneumoniae causing invasive disease in Victoria, Australia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high diversity among 1288 Streptococcus pneumoniae isolates, with 52 serotypes and 203 sequence types. Penicillin resistance was prevalent, with 20.3% of isolates showing resistance using meningitis breakpoints. Multidrug resistance was observed in 7.8% of isolates, with resistance to beta-lactams, macrolides, and tetracyclines being the most common combination.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze the population structure and antibiotic resistance of S. pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid metagenomic sequencing for diagnosis and antimicrobial sensitivity prediction of canine bacterial infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a rapid, culture-free diagnostics pipeline using metagenomic nanopore sequencing for identifying bacterial pathogens and predicting antibiotic sensitivity in canine infections, achieving up to 95% accuracy for urine samples.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic nanopore sequencing was used for direct analysis of clinical urine and skin samples from dogs, followed by bioinformatics analysis for species identification and antimicrobial resistance prediction.
full_output.sample_size: 35 samples sequenced during the development of the protocol and 8 samples during the real-time processing phase

full_output.paper_title: Dominance of Escherichia coli sequence types ST73, ST95, ST127 and ST131 in Australian urine isolates: a genomic analysis of antimicrobial resistance and virulence linked to F plasmids.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various antimicrobial resistance genes in E. coli isolates from Australian urine samples, including blaCTX-M-15, blaCTX-M-14, blaTEM-28, sul1, sul2, sul3, dfrA17, dfrA5, dfrA1, dfrB4, tetA, tetB, mphA, cmlA1, cmlA5, catB3, sat2, qnrD1, fosA7, aac(3)-IId, aac(3)-IIe, aph(3')-IIa, aph(6)-Id, ant(3'')-IIa, intI1, and intI2. These genes were associated with resistance to various antibiotics such as beta-lactams, sulfonamides, trimethoprim, tetracycline, macrolides, chloramphenicol, streptothricin, quinolones, fosfomycin, and aminoglycosides.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and gene screening were used to identify antimicrobial resistance genes in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: In silico designing and immunoinformatics analysis of a novel peptide vaccine against metallo-beta-lactamase (VIM and IMP) variants.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents an in silico design of a multi-epitope vaccine targeting VIM and IMP metallo-beta-lactamases, focusing on identifying B-cell and T-cell epitopes for potential vaccine development.
full_output.methodology: The research utilized immunoinformatics tools for epitope prediction, molecular docking, and vaccine design, along with computational analyses for stability and immunogenicity.

full_output.paper_title: CHROMAgar™ LIN-R as an efficient screening tool to assess the prevalence of linezolid-resistant enterococci in German hospital patients-a multicentre study approach, 2021-2022.

23S rRNA.notes: associated with linezolid resistance

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic-Loaded Boron Nitride Nanoconjugate with Strong Performance against Planktonic Bacteria and Biofilms.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed antibiotic-loaded boron nitride (BN) nanoconjugates, specifically GPBN, which effectively killed planktonic bacteria and disrupted biofilms of Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli. GPBN showed strong antibacterial activity and prevented biofilm formation on surfaces.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the preparation and characterization of GPBN nanoconjugates, followed by antibacterial and biofilm disruption assays using SEM, live/dead staining, and colony counting.

full_output.key_findings: The study describes the development of heterologous effector phage therapeutics (HEPTs) that produce colicin-like bacteriocins and cell wall hydrolases to enhance bacteriophage efficacy against uropathogens. Specifically, HEPTs expressing colicin E7, klebicin M, and the cell wall hydrolase EC300 were shown to improve the killing of multidrug-resistant bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized phage engineering, bacterial culture, and susceptibility testing to develop and validate HEPTs. Techniques included spot-on-the-lawn assays, turbidity reduction assays, and time kill assays to assess the effectiveness of HEPTs against uropathogens.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic and genotypic characteristics of Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolated from cystic fibrosis patients with chronic infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed 120 P. aeruginosa strains from 10 CF patients, identifying 28 genotypes and highlighting the presence of transmissible clusters (IG1, IG2, IG3) indicating cross-infection risks. It also noted variations in virulence factors and antibiotic resistance patterns among transmissible and non-transmissible strains.
full_output.methodology: The study employed pulsed-field gel electrophoresis (PFGE) for genotyping, phenotypic tests for virulence factors, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: High carriage rate of extended-spectrum β-lactamase Enterobacterales and diarrheagenic Escherichia coli in healthy donor screening for fecal microbiota transplantation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high carriage rate of extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Enterobacterales and diarrheagenic Escherichia coli among healthy donors screened for fecal microbiota transplantation. Key ESBL genes detected include blaCTX-M-79, blaCTX-M-15, blaCMY-2, and blaDHA-1.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing to identify ESBL genes and characterize the resistance profiles of Enterobacterales and diarrheagenic E. coli.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes and mutations in Campylobacter jejuni and C. coli isolates, including blaOXA-193, blaOXA-611, blaOXA-489, tet(O), aadE, aadE-Cc, and mutations in gyrA, rpsL, and rrnL. These genes and mutations confer resistance to beta-lactams, tetracyclines, aminoglycosides, and quinolones.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing analysis using CamPype workflow, including quality control, assembly, and characterization of genomes.

full_output.paper_title: Efficient production of bacterial antibiotics aminoriboflavin and roseoflavin in eukaryotic microorganisms, yeasts.
full_output.key_findings: The study successfully expressed genes involved in the biosynthesis of aminoriboflavin (AF) and roseoflavin (RoF) in yeast strains, leading to the production of these antibiotics. The genes rosB, rosC, and rosA from Streptomyces davaonensis were functionally characterized in yeast, demonstrating their roles in AF and RoF synthesis.
full_output.methodology: Genes were expressed in yeast strains, and their functionality was confirmed through qPCR, HPLC, and mass spectrometry analyses.

full_output.paper_title: Determining effects of nitrate, arginine, and ferrous on antibiotic recalcitrance of clinical strains of Pseudomonas aeruginosa in biofilm-inspired alginate encapsulates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mexY as an efflux pump gene involved in P. aeruginosa antibiotic recalcitrance, showing that its expression increases in response to amikacin and decreases with the addition of ferrous.
full_output.methodology: Real-time PCR was used to analyze the expression of the efflux pump gene mexY in P. aeruginosa strains under different treatment conditions.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation of Sphingomonas paucimobilis from an ocular infection and identification using ribosomal RNA gene: First case report from Iran.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first case of ocular infection caused by Sphingomonas paucimobilis in Iran, highlighting its resistance to aminoglycosides and colistin.
full_output.methodology: Identification via 16S rRNA gene sequencing and antibiogram testing using disk diffusion and microbroth dilution methods.

full_output.paper_title: Conjugation of Vancomycin with a Single Arginine Improves Efficacy against Mycobacteria by More Effective Peptidoglycan Targeting.
full_output.key_findings: The study introduces V-R, a vancomycin-arginine conjugate, which shows improved efficacy against mycobacteria, including M. abscessus, compared to vancomycin. V-R demonstrates better biofilm inhibition and eradication, and synergizes with ethambutol.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the efficacy of V-R and vancomycin through MIC assays, biofilm inhibition, and time-kill kinetics, along with molecular modeling to understand the mechanism of action.

full_output.paper_title: Role of a typical swine liquid manure treatment plant in reducing elements of antibiotic resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified and characterized several antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in swine wastewater treatment plants, including blaTEM, ermB, qnrB, sul1, and tetA, which were found to be present in the raw wastewater and showed significant reductions after anaerobic digestion.
full_output.methodology: Real-time PCR was used to quantify the absolute and relative abundances of ARGs, intI1, and 16S rRNA in swine wastewater samples collected from different stages of the treatment process.
full_output.sample_size: Six sampling campaigns conducted over a period of one year.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial activity of epsilon-poly-l-lysine produced by Stenotrophomonas maltophilia HS4 and Paenibacillus polymyxa HS5, alone and in combination with bacteriophages.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies epsilon-poly-l-lysine (ε-PL) produced by Stenotrophomonas maltophilia HS4 and Paenibacillus polymyxa HS5 as a potent cationic antimicrobial peptide with significant antibacterial activity against various pathogenic and antibiotic-resistant bacteria. The combination of ε-PL with bacteriophages shows enhanced antibacterial effects.
full_output.methodology: Structural and molecular analysis, MIC and MBC determination, and evaluation of antibacterial activity against various bacterial strains.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid-dissolving electrospun nanofibers for intra-vaginal antibiotic or probiotic delivery.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed rapid-dissolving electrospun nanofibers for delivering metronidazole or Lactobacillus acidophilus, demonstrating effective prevention and treatment of Gardnerella infections in a mouse model.
full_output.methodology: Electrospinning of polyethylene oxide fibers, in vitro and in vivo evaluations of metronidazole and L. acidophilus delivery, and assessment of bacterial viability and inhibitory potential.

full_output.paper_title: Propranolol restores susceptibility of XDR Gram-negative pathogens to meropenem and Meropenem combination has been evaluated with either tigecycline or amikacin.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies blaKPC, blaOXA-48, and blaVIM as the主要 carbapenemase genes in XDR CR-GNB isolates, which contribute to resistance against meropenem.
full_output.methodology: PCR and phenotypic testing for carbapenemase genes, MIC determination, and combination therapy experiments.

full_output.paper_title: CPA-Cas12a-based lateral flow strip for portable assay of Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus in clinical sample.

full_output.key_findings: The study presents a CPA-Cas12a-based lateral flow assay for the rapid detection of Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) by targeting the mecA and nuc genes.
full_output.methodology: The CPA-Cas12a lateral flow assay was used to detect the mecA and nuc genes in MRSA.

full_output.key_findings: The study focuses on the synthesis and evaluation of gentamicin congeners, highlighting their antiribosomal and antibacterial activities, and their susceptibility to aminoglycoside modifying enzymes. It identifies the impact of structural variations on their efficacy and resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis of gentamicins C1, C2, and C2a, along with cell-free translation assays and antibacterial inhibition assays to evaluate their activities.

full_output.paper_title: Proteinase K/Retinoic Acid-Loaded Cationic Liposomes as Multifunctional Anti-Acne Therapy to Disorganize Biofilm and Regulate Keratinocyte Proliferation.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents multifunctional liposomes loaded with proteinase K (PK), retinoic acid (RA), and soyaethyl morpholinium ethosulfate (SME) for treating acne by disrupting biofilms and regulating keratinocyte proliferation. The liposomes showed enhanced antimicrobial activity against Cutibacterium acnes, reduced biofilm formation, and regulated keratinocyte behavior without cytotoxicity.
full_output.methodology: The study used physicochemical characterization, antimicrobial activity assays, biofilm disruption tests, and keratinocyte proliferation and migration assays to evaluate the effectiveness of the liposomes.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of atypical pathogenic Aeromonas salmonicida isolated from a diseased Siberian sturgeon (Acipenser baerii).
full_output.key_findings: The study identified seven virulence genes in the Aeromonas salmonicida strain AB001, including pla, ahe2, gcaT, ahpB, aerA, hlyA, and alt, which contribute to its pathogenicity in Siberian sturgeon.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of virulence genes and antibiotic sensitivity testing.

full_output.paper_title: Screening and molecular dynamics simulation of compounds inhibiting MurB enzyme of drug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis: An in-silico approach.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified four compounds (DB12983, DB15688, ZINC084726167, and ZINC254071113) that form stable complexes with the MurB enzyme of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, demonstrating potential as inhibitors.
full_output.methodology: Virtual screening and molecular dynamics simulation were used to identify and analyze potential inhibitors of the MurB enzyme.

full_output.paper_title: Impact of antimicrobial use on abundance of antimicrobial resistance genes in chicken flocks in Vietnam.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) such as mcr-1, arnA, blaCTX-M, blaSHV, erm, and mcr-3 were prevalent in chicken flocks in Vietnam, with variations in abundance across different production stages. The intervention reduced antimicrobial use but had inconsistent effects on ARGs depending on the measurement metric.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput real-time PCR was used to detect 94 ARGs in fecal samples from chicken flocks.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance and Natural Antimicrobials in Food Pathogens
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the mechanisms of antibiotic resistance in foodborne pathogens and highlights the potential of natural antimicrobials as alternatives to conventional antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews existing literature and analyzes data from various studies on antimicrobial resistance and natural antimicrobial compounds.

full_output.paper_title: Environmental concentrations of surfactants as a trigger for climax of horizonal gene transfer of antibiotic resistance.
full_output.key_findings: Surfactants at environmental concentrations facilitate horizontal gene transfer (HGT) of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) via transformation, with a maximum increased transformation frequency of 13.51-22.93-fold. The mechanisms involve increased production of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and enhanced cell membrane permeability.
full_output.methodology: Transformation assays, ROS assessment, cell permeability evaluation, and CLSM observation were used to investigate the effects of surfactants on HGT of ARGs.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of Bacterial Uropathogen and Antimicrobial Resistance Patterns Among Patients with Diabetic and Hypertension Attending Dilla University General Hospital, Dilla, Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high prevalence of bacterial uropathogens, including E. coli, K. pneumoniae, and CoNS, with significant antimicrobial resistance. Multidrug resistance was reported in 62.5% of isolates.
full_output.methodology: Cross-sectional study involving urine sample collection, bacterial isolation, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characteristics and phylogenetic analysis of Clostridium perfringens from different regions in China, from 2013 to 2021.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various AMR genes in Clostridium perfringens isolates from China, including mprF, tetA(P), tetB(P), ErmQ, LnuP, AAC(6′)-Ie-APH(2″)-Ia, ANT(6)-Ib, tet44, and ErmB, which confer resistance to antibiotics such as penicillin, tetracycline, clindamycin, and aminoglycosides.
full_output.methodology: MLST, cgMLST, cgSNP, and ABRicate pipeline on CARD were used for analyzing AMR genes and resistance profiles.

full_output.paper_title: The distribution of fitness effects of plasmid pOXA-48 in clinical enterobacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the fitness effects of the carbapenem resistance plasmid pOXA-48 in 35 clinical enterobacterial isolates. full_output.methodology: The study used a CRISPR-Cas9-based method to cure pOXA-48 from wild-type enterobacteria and conducted competition assays to measure fitness effects.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the genetic diversity of Mycobacterium tuberculosis strains infecting children in Ethiopia and evaluated their drug sensitivity profiles. It found that the Euro-American (EA) lineage was the most prevalent, followed by the East-African-Indian (EAI) and M. Africanum lineages. Drug resistance was low, with 7.8% prevalence of any resistance and 2.6% prevalence of multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB). Mutations in the rpoB and katG genes were associated with resistance to rifampicin and isoniazid, respectively.
full_output.methodology: The study used spoligotyping, RD9-based PCR, and drug susceptibility testing (both phenotypic and genotypic) to analyze Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates from children in Ethiopia.

aadA2.evidence_note: The aadA2 gene was detected in 17 isolates by PCR amplification and is associated with streptomycin resistance in the context of SGI1.

sul1.validation_method: PCR amplification and phenotypic resistance testing
sul1.genetic_context: chromosomally Located Genes In all isolates positive for aadA2 , sul1 and tet (A), with the profiles R6 to R9, these genes were clustered on the chromosome, as part of a ca. 43 kb region, absent in the susceptible isolates as well as in isolates with other resistance profiles. This region, which was identical or nearly identical in all isolates, has features consistent with SGI1 ( Figure 1 A, using LSP 138/08 as a model). Like SGI1, the genomic island of the sequenced isolates was located between the trmE and yidY genes, carried the resistance region towards the yidY end and had a closely related backbone structure. However, the resistance region is remarkably different. Thus, instead of the In104 complex class 1 integron of SGI1, it contained a typical class 1 integron with the intI1 gene, the 1000 bp/ aadA2 variable region and the 3′-conserved segment, where the qacEΔ1 (for resistance to disinfectants) and sul1 genes are located.

full_output.key_findings: The review highlights the prevalence of antimicrobial residues, antibiotic-resistant bacteria (ARB), and antimicrobial-resistant genes (ARGs) in various water matrices in India, emphasizing the significant contribution of pharmaceutical and hospital effluents to the spread of AMR.
full_output.methodology: The study reviewed published literature on the prevalence of antimicrobial residues, ARBs, and ARGs in different water matrices in India.

full_output.paper_title: The bacterial genetic determinants of Escherichia coli capacity to cause bloodstream infections in humans.

dhfrI.validation_method: association with resistance in BSI strains

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several genes associated with the pathogenicity of Escherichia coli, including virulence factors like papG and iucB, and resistance genes like dhfrI. These genes are more prevalent in bloodstream infection (BSI) strains compared to commensal strains.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis of 912 BSI and 370 commensal E. coli isolates using whole-genome sequencing and machine learning models to identify genetic determinants of pathogenicity and resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaKPC and blaNDM genes as the primary mechanisms of carbapenem resistance in carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales (CPE) in Ecuador. The most prevalent KPC variant was KPC-3 in ST512, and no mcr-1 gene was detected.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex PCR, ERIC-PCR, and susceptibility testing were used to characterize carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence, Microbiological Profile, and Risk Factors of Surgical Site Infections in Saudi Patients with Colorectal Cancer.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified E. coli and P. aeruginosa as the most common pathogens causing surgical site infections (SSIs) in patients with colorectal cancer. Three E. coli isolates were producers of extended-spectrum beta-lactamases (ESBLs), and two K. pneumoniae isolates exhibited a multidrug resistance profile.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective cohort study analyzing clinical data and microbiological findings from patients undergoing colorectal cancer surgery.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of multidrug-resistant potential pathogens isolated from milk and some dairy products in Egypt.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various AMR genes in E. coli, S. aureus, and B. cereus isolated from milk and dairy products in Egypt, highlighting the presence of multidrug-resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR and disk diffusion methods to detect AMR genes and assess antimicrobial resistance.

full_output.paper_title: A correlation study between virulence factors and multidrug resistance among clinical isolates of Proteus mirabilis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various virulence factors in Proteus mirabilis isolates, including ureC, zapA, flaA, mrpA, atfA, ucaA, hpmA, and luxS genes, which were detected in a high percentage of isolates. These genes are associated with virulence traits such as biofilm formation, motility, and hemolysis, but no direct correlation was found between these virulence factors and multidrug resistance (MDR) or extensive drug resistance (XDR).
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to detect virulence genes and assess resistance patterns in P. mirabilis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Cluster of Carbapenemase-Producing Carbapenem-Resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa Among Patients in an Adult Intensive Care Unit - Idaho, 2021-2022.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the blaIMP-84 gene, a carbapenemase-producing gene, in carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from two patients and an ICU room sink, highlighting the role of environmental reservoirs in the transmission of multidrug-resistant organisms.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and environmental sampling were used to identify and characterize the blaIMP-84 gene in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Effect of veterinary feed directive rule changes on tetracycline-resistant and erythromycin-resistant bacteria (Salmonella, Escherichia, and Campylobacter) in retail meats in the United States.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that the implementation of the VFD rule changes had a beneficial effect by reducing the occurrence of tetracycline-resistant and erythromycin-resistant bacteria in chicken and ground turkey, while some increases were observed in other meat types.
full_output.methodology: Multivariable mixed effect logistic regression models were used to analyze surveillance data from the National Antimicrobial Resistance Monitoring System (NARMS) in the U.S.

full_output.paper_title: Segregational drift hinders the evolution of antibiotic resistance on polyploid replicons.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that beneficial alleles on polyploid replicons are prone to loss due to segregational drift, highlighting the impact of replicon ploidy on the establishment of antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: Experimental evolution with serial transfers, mathematical modeling, and analysis of allele dynamics.

full_output.paper_title: Peptide barcode of multidrug-resistant strains of Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolated from patients in Thailand.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified nine peptides from specific proteins that showed significant associations with antibiotic resistance in multidrug-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae strains, providing potential biomarkers for resistance detection.
full_output.methodology: The study used MALDI-TOF MS and LC-MS to analyze peptidomes of multidrug-resistant N. gonorrhoeae isolates and identify differentially expressed peptides linked to antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Facially Amphiphilic Bile Acid-Functionalized Antimicrobials: Combating Pathogenic Bacteria, Fungi, and Their Biofilms.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the development of bile acid-based antimicrobials with broad-spectrum activity against bacterial and fungal pathogens, including multidrug-resistant strains, and demonstrates their effectiveness in eradicating biofilms without inducing resistance.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis and evaluation of antimicrobial efficacy, biofilm disruption, and resistance development using MIC assays, biofilm assays, and fluorescence microscopy.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular basis of the pleiotropic effects by the antibiotic amikacin on the ribosome.

A1408G.notes: The A1408G mutation in the 16S rRNA of E. coli ribosomes confers resistance to amikacin.

rrsB.notes: The A1408G mutation in the rrsB gene leads to reduced susceptibility to AMK and KAN.

full_output.key_findings: Amikacin inhibits ribosome function by binding to multiple sites, including the decoding center and the P-site of the 50S subunit, leading to impaired mRNA translocation, peptide release, and ribosome recycling. The A1408G mutation in the 16S rRNA of E. coli ribosomes confers resistance to amikacin.
full_output.methodology: Structural analysis using X-ray crystallography, cryo-EM, and kinetic experiments to determine the effects of amikacin on ribosome function.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic and phenotypic characterization of Acinetobacter colistiniresistens isolated from the feces of a healthy member of the community.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in the Acinetobacter colistiniresistens strain C-214, including blaOXA302, tet39, ANT(3'')-IIc, AAC(6')-Ij, and adeB, which contribute to resistance against beta-lactams, tetracycline, aminoglycosides, and multiple antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and genomic analysis using CARD database to identify AMR genes.

full_output.paper_title: Colistin resistance mutations in phoQ can sensitize Klebsiella pneumoniae to IgM-mediated complement killing.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that mutations in the phoQ gene, specifically WAQRN-97-C deletion and G385S, enhance PhoQ activation, leading to colistin resistance and increased MAC sensitivity in Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptomic analysis, mutational analysis, and MAC-mediated permeabilization assays were used to validate the role of phoQ mutations in colistin resistance and MAC sensitivity.

full_output.paper_title: The identification of two M20B family peptidases required for full virulence in Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies PepT1 and PepT2, two M20B family peptidases, as essential for the full virulence of Staphylococcus aureus, particularly in surviving in human blood and evading phagocytosis by macrophages.
full_output.methodology: Mutant strain construction, survival assays in human blood and macrophages, Western blot analysis, and reporter fusion assays.

full_output.paper_title: Phage resistance formation and fitness costs of hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae mediated by K2 capsule-specific phage and the corresponding mechanisms.

rfaH.mechanism: required for capsule production and phage sensitivity
rfaH.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and gene expression analysis

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies rfaH and galU as essential genes for capsule production and phage sensitivity in hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae, highlighting their role in phage resistance formation.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, gene expression analysis, and phage resistance assays were used to characterize the genes involved in capsule production and phage sensitivity.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiological characteristics of SHV, cmlv, and FosA6-producing carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae based on whole genome sequences in Jiangsu, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) strains, including a novel CR-hvKP strain co-producing KPC-2, NDM-6, SHV-182, SHV-64, and bla CTX-M-122 genes. It also reported the first isolation of a conjugative pHN7A8 plasmid carrying multiple resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, conjugation assays, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze the resistance mechanisms and genetic characteristics of the CRKP isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial and anti-biofilm activities of probiotic Lactobacillus plantarum against Listeria monocytogenes isolated from milk, chicken and pregnant women.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified virulent multidrug-resistant Listeria monocytogenes isolates with strong biofilm-forming abilities in food products in Egypt, highlighting the need for monitoring their prevalence and antimicrobial resistance profiles to improve food safety.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of virulence genes and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.methodology: Review of literature and analysis of genetic mutations in Babesia microti isolates from patients with relapsing infections.

full_output.paper_title: Cutaneous Infection Associated With Myroides odoratimimus Bacteremia in a Diabetic Patient.
full_output.key_findings: The case report identifies multidrug resistance in Myroides odoratimimus, including beta-lactamase genes bla-OXA-347 and bla-OXA-209, tetracycline resistance gene tetX, and chloramphenicol resistance gene cat.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing and microbial identification techniques.

full_output.paper_title: An Overview of Antimicrobial Resistance Profiles of Publicly Available Salmonella Genomes with Sufficient Quality and Metadata.
full_output.key_findings: This study provides an overview of antimicrobial resistance profiles in publicly available Salmonella genomes, identifying common resistance genes such as aac(6')-Iaa, blaTEM-1B, blaCMY-2, blaCTX-M-65, parC[T57S], qnrB19, sul2, mph(A), floR, mcr-1.1, and tet(A).
full_output.methodology: In silico analysis using KmerFinder, SISTR, and ResFinder for species, serovar, and AMR identification.

full_output.paper_title: Identifying Antisense Oligonucleotides to Disrupt Small RNA Regulated Antibiotic Resistance via a Cell-Free Transcription-Translation Platform.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies antisense oligonucleotides targeting the sRNA MicF, which regulates the outer membrane porin OmpF, thereby affecting antibiotic susceptibility in E. coli.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of Antimicrobial Resistance Among the Hydrogen Sulfide Producing Bacteria Isolated on XLD Agar from the Poultry Fecal Samples.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of tetracycline resistance gene tetA and beta-lactamase gene blaTEM in hydrogen sulfide-producing bacteria isolated from poultry fecal samples, indicating the prevalence of multidrug-resistant bacteria in poultry environments.
full_output.methodology: 16S rDNA sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR, and sequencing were used to identify and characterize the resistance genes.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified various AMR genes in E. coli isolates from different organs of sheep, highlighting differences in resistance profiles between organs.
full_output.methodology: PCR and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to detect AMR genes and resistance patterns in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Quinolone resistance and biofilm formation capability of uropathogenic Escherichia coli isolates from an Iranian inpatients' population.

full_output.paper_title: Testing the mutant selection window hypothesis with meropenem: In vitro model study with OXA-48-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the OXA-48 carbapenemase in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates, demonstrating its role in reducing meropenem effectiveness and confirming the applicability of the mutant selection window hypothesis to meropenem.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of carbapenemase production, in vitro pharmacokinetic simulations, and susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Killing of Staphylococcus aureus persisters by a multitarget natural product chrysomycin A.
full_output.key_findings: ChryA targets GlmU and DapD, involved in the biosynthetic pathways for the cell wall peptidoglycan and lysine precursors, leading to inhibition of peptidoglycan precursor biosynthesis and resistance mechanisms involving mutations in glmU and dapD.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, overexpression experiments, and MIC determination.

full_output.paper_title: Correlates of Neisseria gonorrhoeae antimicrobial resistance: cross-sectional results from an open cohort sentinel surveillance network in Québec, Canada, 2016-2019.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified correlates of Neisseria gonorrhoeae antimicrobial resistance to first-line antimicrobials, including azithromycin, cefixime, and ceftriaxone. It found that azithromycin resistance was significantly more likely in individuals who self-reported HIV infection, while increased MIC for cefixime and ceftriaxone were more likely in cases with ≥5 sexual partners.
full_output.methodology: The study conducted cross-sectional analyses of data from an open cohort sentinel surveillance network in Québec, Canada, using generalized estimating equations to assess correlates of antimicrobial resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Efficacy of zinc oxide and copper oxide nanoparticles on virulence genes of avian pathogenic E. coli (APEC) in broilers.
full_output.key_findings: AG-CuNPs effectively reduced the expression of virulence genes (ibeA, hlyA, iss, and papC) in E. coli O17 strain, demonstrating their potential as an alternative to antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: In vitro and in vivo experiments, including PCR, MIC/MBC assays, and real-time qPCR, were used to assess the efficacy of AG-CuNPs against APEC.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first identification of a vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecalis ST21 strain harboring the vanA gene in Brazil, highlighting the role of wastewater treatment plants in the spread of antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatic analysis to identify antimicrobial resistance genes and determine phylogenetic relationships.

full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the gas-phase stability and thermodynamics of chloramphenicol acetyltransferase (Ec CAT I) and its complexes with chloramphenicol (Chl) and a non-hydrolyzable CoA derivative (S-Et-CoA). It reveals that Ec CAT I binds multiple Chl or S-Et-CoA without structural changes and exhibits negative cooperativity in ligand binding.
full_output.methodology: Native ion mobility spectrometry-mass spectrometry (IMS-MS) and molecular dynamics simulations were used to analyze the gas-phase structure and stability of Ec CAT I and its ligand complexes.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several proteins upregulated in Mycobacterium fortuitum biofilm, including those involved in lipid biosynthesis, energy metabolism, and antibiotic resistance, suggesting potential targets for anti-biofilm therapies.
full_output.methodology: Label-free mass spectrometry and bioinformatics analysis were used to compare the proteomes of M. fortuitum planktonic and biofilm cultures.

full_output.paper_title: MtrA modulates Mycobacterium tuberculosis cell division in host microenvironments to mediate intrinsic resistance and drug tolerance.

mtrA.validation_method: CRISPRi knockdown, RNA-seq, and growth assays

full_output.key_findings: MtrA regulates cell division and intrinsic resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis through modulation of peptidoglycan hydrolases and other genes, contributing to drug tolerance.
full_output.methodology: CRISPRi, RNA-seq, Tn-seq, and growth assays were used to investigate MtrA's role in Mtb's response to environmental stresses and drug resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Drug Resistance, Characterization and Phylogenetic Discrepancy of Salmonella enterica Isolates from Distinct Sources.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in Salmonella enterica isolates from clinical and animal sources, including catA1, blaTEM, and tetC, which confer resistance to chloramphenicol, ampicillin, and tetracycline, respectively.
full_output.methodology: PCR screening, sequencing, and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize AMR genes in Salmonella isolates.
full_output.sample_size: 224 isolates (51 clinical and 173 animal product isolates)

full_output.paper_title: Isolation and characterization of a novel mycobacteriophage Kashi-VT1 infecting Mycobacterium species.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes the isolation and characterization of a novel mycobacteriophage Kashi-VT1 (KVT1) that infects Mycobacterium smegmatis and Mycobacterium fortuitum. KVT1 is a cluster K1 temperate phage belonging to the Siphoviridae family, with a genome of 61,010 base pairs and 101 putative open reading frames. The phage exhibits lytic properties and has potential for phage therapy against tuberculosis.
full_output.methodology: The phage was isolated from soil samples, characterized using transmission electron microscopy, and its genome was sequenced and annotated. Functional analysis included restriction digestion, host range determination, and stability tests under various temperatures and pH levels.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization of multidrug resistant Acinetobacter baumannii clinical isolates from Alexandria, Egypt.

full_output.paper_title: Studies on plasmids of multidrug resistant uropathogens isolated from patients with urinary tract infection in a tertiary hospital in Calabar, Nigeria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of SHV, TEM, and CTX-M beta-lactamase genes in multidrug-resistant uropathogens, indicating plasmid-mediated resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance and its relationship with antimicrobial use on Austrian dairy farms.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that commensal E. coli on Austrian dairy farms exhibited resistance to various antibiotics, including tetracyclines, sulfonamides, and penicillins. There was a significant association between antimicrobial use (AMU) and the occurrence of resistance, particularly for penicillins, sulfonamides, and tetracyclines.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed antimicrobial resistance in commensal E. coli from fecal samples collected from dairy cows, pre-weaned, and weaned calves on 51 Austrian dairy farms. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was conducted using broth microdilution, and AMU data were quantified using Defined Daily Doses (DDD vet) and Defined Course Doses (DCD vet).

full_output.paper_title: Effect of dry cow therapy on antimicrobial resistance of mastitis pathogens post-calving.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the impact of dry cow therapy on antimicrobial resistance (AMR) profiles of mastitis pathogens post-calving. It found that dry cow therapy was associated with increased resistance in coagulase-negative Staphylococcus (CNS) isolates to certain antibiotics, including penicillin, cephalothin, and ceftiofur. Additionally, resistance to sulfadimethoxine and tetracycline was observed in various bacterial species.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth microdilution to determine antimicrobial susceptibility of bacterial isolates. It analyzed the effects of dry cow therapy on AMR through parametric survival interval regression models.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance and genotyping of Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolated from the ear canals of dogs in Japan.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of antimicrobial resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from the ear canals of dogs in Japan, with 100% resistance to cefovecin, cefpodoxime, and florfenicol. The isolates showed varying degrees of resistance to fluoroquinolones and aminoglycosides, with some classified as multidrug-resistant (MDR) or extensively drug-resistant (XDR).
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using disk diffusion and MIC methods, and multilocus sequence typing (MLST) was used for genotyping.

full_output.paper_title: Detection and molecular characterization of Actinomyces denticolens causing lymph node abscessation in horses.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Actinomyces denticolens as a cause of submandibular lymph node abscessation in horses and characterizes its genomic features, revealing no known antibiotic resistance genes but four virulence-related genes, including ahpC, which was present in one isolate.
full_output.methodology: Culture, MALDI-TOF MS, MIC testing, and whole genome sequencing were used for identification and characterization of A. denticolens isolates.

full_output.paper_title: The Etiological and Drug Resistance Characteristics of Multidrug-Resistant Pathogens in Patients Requiring Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria (MDR-GNB) as the primary pathogens in ECMO patients, with Acinetobacter baumannii (MDR-AB) and Klebsiella pneumoniae (MDR-KP) showing higher resistance rates to conventional antibiotics compared to other ICU patients. Colistin showed better sensitivity against these MDR-GNB.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective cohort study analyzing clinical and microbiological data from ECMO patients.

full_output.paper_title: Pre-existing heterogeneity facilitates development of heteroresistance upon gene acquisition.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the fosA gene as a key factor in the development of fosfomycin heteroresistance, showing that its presence increases the MIC of a subpopulation beyond the clinical breakpoint, leading to heteroresistance. full_output.methodology: Deletion and complementation experiments, PAP analysis, and whole-genome sequencing were used to analyze the role of fosA in fosfomycin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Metagenomics reveals the abundance and accumulation trend of antibiotic resistance gene profile under long-term no tillage in a rainfed agroecosystem.

full_output.paper_title: Genus-wide genomic characterization of Macrococcus: insights into evolution, population structure, and functional potential.

full_output.paper_title: Stability of Antimicrobials in Peritoneal Dialysis Solutions: A Systematic Review

full_output.paper_title: Structural conservation of antibiotic interaction with ribosomes.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents high-resolution cryo-electron microscopy structures of 17 distinct antibiotics bound to the bacterial ribosome, revealing detailed insights into their binding modes and interactions with the ribosomal components.
full_output.methodology: Cryo-electron microscopy and structural analysis were used to determine the high-resolution structures of antibiotics bound to the ribosome.

full_output.paper_title: Baseline azithromycin resistance in the gut microbiota of preterm born infants.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the presence of macrolide resistance genes in the gut microbiota of preterm infants, with erm(C) and msr(A) being the most common. These genes were found in various bacterial genera, including Staphylococcus and Enterococcus.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative PCR (qPCR) was used to detect the presence of six common macrolide resistance genes in azithromycin-resistant isolates from preterm infants.

full_output.paper_title: Helicobacter pylori in the post-antibiotics era: from virulence factors to new drug targets and therapeutic agents.
full_output.key_findings: The review discusses the challenges of eradicating H. pylori due to rising antibiotic resistance and highlights the need for new therapeutic strategies, including the exploration of alternative drugs, probiotics, and phytomedicine.
full_output.methodology: Review of literature and existing studies on H. pylori virulence factors, resistance mechanisms, and treatment strategies.

full_output.paper_title: Extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing E. coli from retail meat and workers: genetic diversity, virulotyping, pathotyping and the antimicrobial effect of silver nanoparticles.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple AMR genes in ESBL-producing E. coli from retail meat and workers, including bla IMP, bla TEM, bla CTX-M-1, bla VIM, bla NDM, tetA (A), tetA (B), sul, flo R, and mcr-1. These genes conferred resistance to various antibiotics such as β-lactams, tetracycline, sulfonamides, fluoroquinolones, and colistin.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of AMR genes and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence, antimicrobial resistance, and enterotoxin gene profiles of Staphylococcus aureus isolated from mobile phones of the food vendors in Phayao province, Thailand.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of Staphylococcus aureus on mobile phones of food vendors in Phayao province, Thailand, with a focus on antimicrobial resistance and enterotoxin gene profiles. Key findings included the detection of multiple enterotoxin genes (sea, seb, sec, sem, seq) and high levels of antimicrobial resistance, particularly to penicillin, chloramphenicol, and tetracycline. Methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) and vancomycin-resistant S. aureus (VRSA) were also detected.
full_output.methodology: The study involved collecting mobile phone samples from food vendors, identifying S. aureus isolates, and performing antimicrobial susceptibility testing and PCR for enterotoxin genes.

full_output.paper_title: Dihydroartemisinin inhibits plasmid transfer in drug-resistant Escherichia coli via limiting energy supply.
full_output.key_findings: DHA inhibits conjugative transfer of plasmids carrying mcr-1 and bla NDM-5 by impairing energy metabolism and down-regulating conjugation-related genes.
full_output.methodology: Conjugation assays, PCR, RNA sequencing, ATP and PMF measurements, and in vivo experiments in mice.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mecA and blaZ as the primary resistance genes in Staphylococcus aureus isolates from Tamil Nadu and Mizoram, with high prevalence of methicillin-resistant and multidrug-resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing, PCR, and ERIC-PCR for clonal analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Incidence Pattern, Antibiotic Susceptibility Pattern and Associated Risk Factors of Bacterial Uropathogens Among General Population of Pakistan.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that Escherichia coli was the most prevalent uropathogen, showing high resistance to ampicillin. Gram-negative bacteria exhibited significant resistance to multiple antibiotics, highlighting the urgent need for effective antimicrobial stewardship.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed urine samples from 459 participants to determine the prevalence of uropathogens and their antibiotic susceptibility patterns using standard microbiological techniques and the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: A Bacteriophage-Loaded Microparticle Laden Topical Gel for the Treatment of Multidrug-Resistant Biofilm-Mediated Burn Wound Infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes BPKPФ1, a bacteriophage effective against multidrug-resistant K. pneumoniae, demonstrating its lytic activity, host range, and potential for treating biofilm-mediated burn wound infections.
full_output.methodology: Bacteriophage isolation, characterization, and evaluation of antibacterial and antibiofilm efficacy in vitro and in vivo.

full_output.paper_title: Drug resistance prediction for Mycobacterium tuberculosis with reference graphs.

mutations_found.protein_change: Aspartic acid to Glycine at position 94

full_output.key_findings: The study presents DrPRG, a novel software tool for predicting drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis using reference graphs. It identifies several mutations associated with resistance to various antibiotics, including isoniazid, rifampicin, ethambutol, pyrazinamide, and others.
full_output.methodology: The methodology involves constructing a reference graph from a global dataset of M. tuberculosis isolates and evaluating DrPRG's performance against existing tools like Mykrobe and TBProfiler using Illumina and Nanopore sequencing data.

full_output.paper_title: Structural-Activity Relationship-Inspired the Discovery of Saturated Fatty Acids as Novel Colistin Enhancers.

mcr-1.validation_method: Synergistic activity with colistin, reduced MIC, inhibition of biofilm formation

full_output.key_findings: Three saturated fatty acids (SFAs), particularly sodium caprate (SC), enhance the antibacterial activity of colistin against mcr-1-positive bacteria by reducing LPS modification, enhancing membrane permeability, and impairing the efflux pump function.
full_output.methodology: Checkerboard assay, time-killing curves, biofilm formation and eradication experiments, LPS quantification, RT-qPCR, molecular docking, and in vivo animal models.

full_output.paper_title: RVE2, a new regulatory factor in jasmonic acid pathway, orchestrates resistance to Verticillium wilt.

GausRVE2.mechanism: Regulates the jasmonic acid (JA) signaling pathway, which is crucial for resistance to Verticillium wilt.
GausRVE2.validation_method: Overexpression in Arabidopsis and Nicotiana benthamiana, VIGS experiments, and analysis of JA signaling components.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies GausRVE2 as a key regulator in the jasmonic acid (JA) signaling pathway that confers resistance to Verticillium wilt in cotton. Overexpression of GausRVE2 enhances resistance, and its function is linked to the JA signaling pathway.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptome sequencing, VIGS, overexpression in model plants, and analysis of JA signaling components.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic dissection of endemic carbapenem resistance reveals metallo-beta-lactamase dissemination through clonal, plasmid and integron transfer.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies blaIMP-4 as a key factor in carbapenem resistance, highlighting its dissemination through various plasmid types and genetic settings across multiple bacterial species.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and phylogenetic analysis of 270 isolates carrying blaIMP-4.

full_output.paper_title: Repurposing miconazole and tamoxifen for the treatment of Mycobacterium abscessus complex infections through in silico chemogenomics approach.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified miconazole (MCZ) and tamoxifen (TAM) as potential antibacterial agents against Mycobacterium abscessus complex (MABSC) through in silico chemogenomics and experimental validation. MCZ showed bactericidal activity against MABSC in vitro and reduced bacterial load in a murine model of M. massiliense infection.
full_output.methodology: The study used in silico chemogenomics to identify drugs targeting M. abscessus proteins, followed by in vitro and in vivo experimental validation of the most promising candidates.

full_output.paper_title: Bacterial ventriculoperitoneal shunt infections: changing trends in antimicrobial susceptibility, a 7-year retrospective study from Pakistan.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a shift in the causative bacteria of ventriculoperitoneal (VP) shunt infections from Gram-positive to Gram-negative organisms. It highlighted decreasing susceptibility of Gram-negative bacteria to carbapenems and beta-lactam/beta-lactamase inhibitors, suggesting the need for alternative antibiotics like colistin, fosfomycin, ceftazidime/avibactam, ceftolozane/tazobactam, and tigecycline.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of CSF cultures and antimicrobial susceptibility testing results from VP shunt infections over seven years.

full_output.paper_title: UTILITY OF STREM-1 BIOMARKER AND HCP GENE FOR IDENTIFICATION OF ACINETOBACTER BAUMANNII COLONIZATION AND INFECTION IN LUNG.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that the hcp gene was more likely to be present in the infection cohort compared to the colonization group, suggesting its potential utility in distinguishing between A. baumannii infection and colonization.
full_output.methodology: PCR and RT-qPCR were used to detect the presence and expression levels of the hcp gene in A. baumannii clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Serotype replacement and an increase in non-encapsulated isolates among community-acquired infections of Streptococcus pneumoniae during post-vaccine era in Japan.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified serotype 35B and 15A/F as having reduced susceptibility to β-lactams and fluoroquinolones. Additionally, specific mutations in gyrA and parC were associated with levofloxacin resistance in some isolates.
full_output.methodology: PCR, direct sequencing, and broth microdilution for antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial conductive self-healing hydrogel wound dressing with dual dynamic bonds promotes infected wound healing.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a multifunctional hydrogel with self-healing, conductive, and photothermal antibacterial properties for infected wound healing.
full_output.methodology: The hydrogel was synthesized using oxidized sodium alginate-grafted dopamine, carboxymethyl chitosan, Fe3+, and polydopamine-coated poly(thiophene-3-acetic acid).

full_output.paper_title: Isoniazid resistance-conferring mutations are associated with highly variable phenotypic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance and clonality of Staphylococcus aureus causing bacteraemia in children admitted to the Manhiça District Hospital, Mozambique, over two decades.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies various AMR genes in Staphylococcus aureus isolates from children with bacteraemia in Mozambique, including blaZ, mecA, tet(K), tet(L), tet(M), erm(C), msr(A), dfr(G), dfrA(S1), aacA-aphD, and cat pC221. Additionally, mutations in grlA and gyrA were found to confer ciprofloxacin resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize AMR genes and mutations in S. aureus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Effects of synthetic peptide RP557 and its origin, LL-37, on carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the antimicrobial and antibiofilm effects of synthetic peptide RP557 and its origin, LL-37, on carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa (CRPA). Both peptides showed significant inhibition of CRPA growth and biofilm formation, with RP557 demonstrating superior effectiveness. The combination of RP557 or LL-37 with carbapenems significantly increased the susceptibility of CRPA to these antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) assays, biofilm inhibition and removal assays, and quantitative real-time PCR to analyze the effects of RP557 and LL-37 on CRPA.

full_output.paper_title: Serotype distribution and antibiogram of Streptococcus parauberis isolated from fish in South Korea.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified ARGs responsible for resistance to oxytetracycline and erythromycin in S. parauberis isolates, with serotype-dependent distribution of these genes.
full_output.methodology: PCR, disk diffusion testing, and whole-genome sequencing were used to detect and characterize AMR genes in S. parauberis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Preclinical safety and efficacy characterization of an LpxC inhibitor against Gram-negative pathogens.

fabZ.notes: Mutations in fabZ confer resistance to LpxC inhibitors.

full_output.key_findings: LPC-233 is a novel LpxC inhibitor with strong in vitro and in vivo activity against Gram-negative bacteria, including multidrug-resistant strains, and shows no significant cardiovascular toxicity.
full_output.methodology: In vitro and in vivo experiments, including MIC testing, time-kill kinetics, serial passage assays, and pharmacokinetic studies.

full_output.methodology: Genome-wide transposon mutagenesis combined with BarSeq and CRISPRi to identify genes and mutations involved in antibiotic resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the role of Mycobacterium tuberculosis acetyltransferases and protein acetylation modifications in tuberculosis, highlighting their impact on virulence, drug resistance, and host immune response. Specific acetyltransferases such as Rv2170, Rv2215, Rv0262c, and Rv3225c are associated with resistance to isoniazid and aminoglycosides.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews existing literature and discusses the role of acetyltransferases and acetylation in M. tb, focusing on their impact on drug resistance and host immune response.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid bacteriolysis of Staphylococcus aureus by lysin exebacase.
full_output.key_findings: Exebacase, a lysin targeting Staphylococcus aureus, exhibits rapid bactericidal activity, achieving a 3-log 10 reduction in viable cells within 2 hours at 1-2 × MIC. It effectively lyses both methicillin-susceptible and resistant strains, with bacteriolysis confirmed via turbidity reduction, microscopy, and transmission electron microscopy.
full_output.methodology: Time-kill assays, turbidity reduction assays, and microscopy were used to evaluate exebacase's bactericidal activity against various S. aureus strains.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of Proteus mirabilis and associated plasmids isolated from anaerobic dairy cattle manure digesters.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla CTX-M and bla CMY genes in ESC-resistant Proteus mirabilis isolates from dairy manure digesters, highlighting their potential as a reservoir of extended-spectrum cephalosporin resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, whole-genome sequencing, conjugation experiments, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Machine learning and metagenomics reveal shared antimicrobial resistance profiles across multiple chicken farms and abattoirs in China.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of polymyxins resistance among Enterobacterales: evaluation of available methods and proposal of a new rapid and feasible methodology.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates and proposes new rapid methods (RCPE and RCPEm) for detecting polymyxin B resistance among Enterobacterales, showing comparable accuracy to existing methods with shorter incubation times.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated various methods for detecting polymyxin B resistance, including RCPE, RCPEm, PBDE, and RPNP, comparing their performance to the reference broth microdilution method.

full_output.methodology: Systematic review and meta-analysis of studies examining antibiotic resistance mutations in clinical isolates of Mycoplasma and Ureaplasma species.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of the RESIST ACINETO multiplex immunochromatographic assay for detection of OXA-23-like, OXA-40/58-like and NDM carbapenemase production in Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The RESIST ACINETO assay accurately detects OXA-23-like, OXA-40/58-like, and NDM carbapenemases in Acinetobacter baumannii isolates with high sensitivity and specificity.

full_output.paper_title: Spectrum of Virulence Factors in Clinical Isolates of Staphylococcus aureus and Prevalence of SCCmec Types in Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus in a Tertiary Care Center.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several virulence genes in Staphylococcus aureus isolates, including hla, hlb, fnbA, pvl, icaA, sea, seb, sec, clfA, eta, tst, and fnbB. These genes are associated with various pathogenic mechanisms such as cytotoxicity, adhesion, biofilm formation, and toxin production.

full_output.paper_title: Livestock, pets and humans as carriers of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and comparative evaluation of two PCR protocols for detection.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) in various hosts, with a higher incidence in dogs and cattle. The mecA gene was detected using PCR, and the mecA-162 primer showed better sensitivity compared to mecA-310.

full_output.paper_title: Synergistic Interaction of Metallopolymers with Antibiotics Enhances Antimicrobial Activity and Biofilm Disruption
full_output.key_findings: The study explores the use of membrane-active metallopolymers as adjuvants to enhance the efficacy of existing antibiotics against multidrug-resistant (MDR) Gram-negative bacteria, including biofilm disruption and overcoming resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: The research involved synthesizing metallopolymers and assessing their synergistic effects with antibiotics through various assays, including checkerboard experiments, MIC determination, and biofilm disruption analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Novel inhibitors that target bacterial virulence identified via HTS against intra-macrophage survival of Shigella flexneri.

full_output.paper_title: Lung microenvironments harbor Mycobacterium tuberculosis phenotypes with distinct treatment responses.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular detection of multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa of different avian sources with pathogenicity testing and in vitro evaluation of antibacterial efficacy of silver nanoparticles against multidrug-resistant P. aeruginosa.

full_output.paper_title: D-amino Acids Ameliorate Experimental Colitis and Cholangitis by Inhibiting Growth of Proteobacteria: Potential Therapeutic Role in Inflammatory Bowel Disease.

full_output.methodology: The study used in vivo models of colitis and cholangitis, 16S rRNA sequencing, and gene expression analysis to investigate the effects of D-amino acids on gut microbiota and bacterial growth.

full_output.paper_title: Vancomycin-resistant enterococci (VRE) in hospital settings across European borders: a scoping review comparing the epidemiology in the Netherlands and Germany.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative analysis of clinical breakpoints, normalized resistance interpretation and epidemiological cut-offs in interpreting antimicrobial resistance of Escherichia coli isolates originating from poultry in different farm types in Tanzania.
full_output.key_findings: The study compared antimicrobial resistance in Escherichia coli isolates using ECOFFs, CLSI and NRI breakpoints, highlighting the impact of different breakpoints on resistance interpretation and emphasizing the need for standardized breakpoints, especially for microbiological data.
full_output.methodology: Kirby Bauer disc diffusion was used for susceptibility testing, and resistance was interpreted using ECOFFs, CLSI, and NRI breakpoints.

full_output.paper_title: Carbapenem-Resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa Spondylodiscitis Treated with Ceftazidime-Avibactam: A Case Report with Literature Review.
full_output.key_findings: The case report describes the successful treatment of carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa (CRPA) spondylodiscitis with ceftazidime-avibactam (C/A). The patient was resistant to multiple antibiotics but showed significant improvement with C/A therapy.
full_output.methodology: Clinical case report with antimicrobial susceptibility testing and treatment outcome assessment.

full_output.methodology: Plasmid characterization, whole genome sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and bioinformatics analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular epidemiology and genomic characterization of a plasmid-mediated mcr-10 and bla(NDM-1) co-harboring multidrug-resistant Enterobacter asburiae.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports a multidrug-resistant Enterobacter asburiae isolate co-harboring mcr-10 and bla(NDM-1) genes, which confer resistance to colistin and carbapenems, respectively. The mcr-10 gene did not mediate colistin resistance when cloned into E. coli, whereas bla(NDM-1) was successfully transferred and conferred carbapenem resistance.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, conjugation experiments, gene cloning, and whole-genome sequencing were used to characterize the resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Fimbria targeting superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles enhance the antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity of ciprofloxacin against quinolone-resistant E. coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that mannoside-tagged ciprofloxacin-loaded superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (Cip-Man-BSA@PAA@SPION) significantly enhance the antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity of ciprofloxacin against quinolone-resistant E. coli isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the development and characterization of mannoside-conjugated ciprofloxacin-loaded SPIONs, followed by evaluation of their antibacterial and antibiofilm activities against ciprofloxacin-resistant E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Structure-Activity Relationships of the Antimicrobial Peptide Natural Product Apidaecin.
full_output.key_findings: The study focuses on structure-guided modifications of the antimicrobial peptide apidaecin to maintain its antimicrobial activity and interaction with the translation complex. Several amino acid substitutions and modifications were found to preserve the antibacterial activity of this PrAMP, with specific modifications at the C-terminus being well-tolerated.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized structure-guided modifications of apidaecin, followed by antimicrobial activity assays and stop codon readthrough assays to evaluate the effects of various substitutions on the peptide's functionality.

full_output.paper_title: Decreased susceptibility to vancomycin and other mechanisms of resistance to antibiotics in Staphylococcus epidermidis as a therapeutic problem in hospital treatment.

It highlights the presence of heteroresistance to vancomycin in some strains despite the absence of vancomycin resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of resistance genes and phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: The effects of antibiotic use on the dynamics of the microbiome and resistome in pigs.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in porcine fecal microbiota, including aacA-aphD, ermT, lnuB, strB, sul2, tetA, tetM, and blaTEM, which showed increased abundance in antibiotic-treated pigs compared to untreated pigs.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput qPCR was used to analyze the abundance of 82 antibiotic resistance genes in porcine fecal samples.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical Manifestation of Ralstonia mannitolilytica Infection in Pediatric Patients and Epidemiological Investigation of Outbreaks.

blaOXA-443.evidence_note: The paper mentions that OXA-443 and OXA-444 genes were detected in R. mannitolilytica isolates through PCR, and that isolates carrying these genes were resistant to meropenem.

full_output.methodology: PCR detection of OXA-443 and OXA-444 genes in R. mannitolilytica isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Synergistic and Long-Lasting Wound Dressings Promote Multidrug-Resistant Staphylococcus Aureus-Infected Wound Healing.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a novel wound dressing composed of glycyrrhizic acid (GA) and tryptophan-sorbitol carbon quantum dots (WS-CQDs) that exhibits synergistic and long-lasting antibacterial effects against multidrug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA).
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antibacterial activity, sustained-release properties, and biocompatibility of GA/WS-CQDs hydrogels in vitro and in vivo using various microbiological and histological techniques.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified vanA as the gene responsible for vancomycin resistance in VRSA isolates, highlighting the emergence of vancomycin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus in Saudi Arabian hospitals.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the design and engineering of a chimeric glycosyltransferase OleD for the site-specific O-monoglycosylation of 3-hydroxypyridine in nosiheptide, resulting in a derivative (NOS-G) with improved solubility and stability. The engineered enzyme showed enhanced activity, particularly the FG variant, which demonstrated a 70-fold increase in NOS-G production compared to wild-type OleD.
full_output.methodology: Enzyme engineering, site-directed mutagenesis, HPLC, LC-MS, and molecular dynamics simulations were used to characterize the glycosyltransferase activity and optimize the enzyme for improved NOS-G production.

full_output.paper_title: The Microbiome and Antibiotic Resistome in Soil under Biodegradable Composite Carbon Source Amendment.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) including vanR, aac(6')-I, and tetA(48) in soil samples under different dosages of a biodegradable composite carbon source. These genes were found to be prevalent in Actinobacteria and Proteobacteria, and their abundance varied with the application of the composite carbon source.
full_output.methodology: The study employed Illumina MiSeq sequencing and metagenomic analysis to investigate the microbial communities and antibiotic resistome in soil samples treated with varying doses of a biodegradable composite carbon source.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotics promote intestinal growth of carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae by enriching nutrients and depleting microbial metabolites.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that antibiotics promote the growth of carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (CRE) by increasing nutrient availability and decreasing inhibitory microbial metabolites in the gut microbiota.
full_output.methodology: Ex vivo faecal culture experiments, 1H-NMR spectroscopy, and mouse models were used to analyze the effects of antibiotics on gut microbiota composition, nutrient availability, and CRE growth.
full_output.sample_size: 11 healthy human faecal donors, 5 mice per group

full_output.paper_title: Crippling of Klebsiella pneumoniae virulence by metformin, N-acetylcysteine and secnidazole.
full_output.key_findings: Metformin, N-acetylcysteine, and secnidazole inhibit the production of virulence factors in Klebsiella pneumoniae, as evidenced by reduced expression of rmpA, wcaG, fimH-1, mrkD, ureA, and khe genes.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic assays and qRT-PCR were used to evaluate the effect of metformin, NAC, and secnidazole on virulence factor production in K. pneumoniae.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of antibiotic-resistant Gram-negative bacteria having extended-spectrum β-lactamase phenotypes in polluted irrigation-purpose wastewaters from Indian agro-ecosystems.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the prevalence of antibiotic-resistant Gram-negative bacteria with extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL) phenotypes in irrigation-purpose wastewaters from Himachal Pradesh, India. Six isolates were found to be ESBL-positive, including Enterobacter spp., Escherichia coli, Shigella sp., and Citrobacter sp. The ESBL genes detected were bla CTX-M and bla TEM, which confer resistance to various β-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method and phenotypic detection of ESBLs using a confirmatory disk diffusion test.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical features of Streptococcus intermedius infection in children: a case series study.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that Streptococcus intermedius infections in children showed 100% sensitivity to ceftriaxone, levofloxacin, chloramphenicol, vancomycin, and linezolid, 92.6% sensitivity to penicillin, 73.3% resistance to erythromycin, and 76.7% resistance to clindamycin.
full_output.methodology: Susceptibility testing was performed using the disc diffusion method according to the latest version of the American Committee of Clinical and Laboratory Standards guidelines.

full_output.paper_title: Process optimization, antioxidant, antibacterial, and drug adjuvant properties of bioactive keratin microparticles derived from porcupine (Hystrix indica) quills.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the antibacterial properties of bioactive keratin microparticles derived from porcupine quills, showing enhanced antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus when coated with lipids and loaded with erythromycin.
full_output.methodology: The study optimized the extraction and synthesis of keratin microparticles, analyzed their chemical composition using FTIR, and evaluated their antioxidant and antibacterial activities.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro efficacy of humanized regimen of flomoxef against extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: Flomoxef showed good bactericidal effects against ESBL-producing E. coli and K. pneumoniae, even with high MIC values. The study identified several CTX-M types (CTX-M-1, CTX-M-9, CTX-M-14, CTX-M-15, CTX-M-28) and AmpC beta-lactamases (DHA, CMY) as significant contributors to resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, DNA sequencing, broth microdilution, and chemostat model experiments were used to determine susceptibility and characterize resistance mechanisms.
full_output.sample_size: 1274 E. coli isolates and 720 K. pneumoniae isolates

full_output.methodology: smRandom-seq combines random primers for in situ cDNA generation, droplet microfluidics for single-microbe barcoding, and CRISPR-based rRNA depletion for mRNA enrichment.
