full_output.methodology: Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations were performed to evaluate the binding interactions of selected ligands with MbtA.

full_output.paper_title: The Impact of Pseudomonas aeruginosa Infection in Adult Cystic Fibrosis Patients-A Single Polish Centre Study.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that 39.4% of P. aeruginosa isolates exhibited multiple resistances, with notable resistance rates to amikacin (37.8%), ciprofloxacin (36.5%), and ceftazidime (32.4%). Colistin resistance was observed in four strains.
full_output.methodology: Microbiological characterization of 74 P. aeruginosa isolates and evaluation of correlations between bacterial features and clinical parameters in adult Polish CF patients.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical outcomes of intensive care unit patients infected with multidrug-resistant gram-negative bacteria treated with ceftazidime/avibactam and ceftolozane/tazobactam.

full_output.paper_title: The burden of bacterial antimicrobial resistance in the WHO African region in 2019: a cross-country systematic analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Differential responses of the gut microbiome and resistome to antibiotic exposures in infants and adults.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that the gut resistome differs between infants and adults, with E. coli being a major contributor to antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs). Both groups show similar dominant ARGs, but infants exhibit higher ARG abundance. Antibiotic treatment affects both age groups, though its impact lasts longer in adults.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic sequencing of fecal samples from 662 infants and 217 adults to analyze the gut resistome and microbiome.

full_output.paper_title: Activity of Cinnamic Acid Derivatives with 4-Chloro-2-mercaptobenzenesulfonamide Moiety against Clinical HLAR and VRE Enterococcus spp.

The compounds showed potent activity, with MIC values ranging from 2 to 4 µg/mL, and effectively inhibited biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: Antibacterial activity was assessed using the serial dilution method, and biofilm inhibition was evaluated using crystal violet staining.

full_output.paper_title: Shotgun Metagenomics-Guided Prediction Reveals the Metal Tolerance and Antibiotic Resistance of Microbes in Poly-Extreme Environments in the Danakil Depression, Afar Region.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified numerous antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) and metal resistance genes (MRGs) in the metagenomes of Lake Afdera and the Assale salt plain in the Danakil Depression. Key ARGs included beta-lactamases (ACC-1, OXA-58, OXA-363, OXA-212, NDM-17, OXA-134, ACT-29, LRA-19), efflux pumps (emrB, abeM, abeS, mgrA, adeJ, MexC, adeL, adeH), sulfonamide resistance genes (sul1, sul2), tetracycline resistance genes (tet39, tetX, tetK), and others. MRGs included copper resistance genes (copC, copD), cadmium resistance gene (cadD), mercury resistance gene (merA), chromate resistance genes (chrB, chrA), nickel-cobalt-cadmium resistance genes (nccA, nccB), cobalt-zinc-cadmium resistance gene (czcD), arsenic resistance gene (arsO), lead resistance gene (pbrA), and mercury resistance genes (merB, merR, MIR).
full_output.methodology: The study used shotgun metagenomics to analyze the microbial communities in water and salt crust samples from Lake Afdera and the Assale salt plain. ARGs and MRGs were identified using the Comprehensive Antibiotic Resistance Database (CARD) and BacMetScan V.1.0. Functional annotations and taxonomic assignments were performed using BLAST, RAST, and MEGAN4.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the successful bioengineering of yeast to produce recombinant thanatin (rThan), which exhibits antimicrobial activity against a variety of bacteria, including multidrug-resistant strains. rThan was shown to be effective against Enterobacteriaceae and had a mechanism of action involving disruption of the LPS transport system.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the construction of a yeast expression vector for constitutive production of thanatin, followed by purification and evaluation of its antimicrobial activity against various bacterial strains.

full_output.paper_title: In Vitro Microevolution and Co-Selection Assessment of Florfenicol Impact on Escherichia coli Resistance Development.
full_output.key_findings: Florfenicol exposure leads to increased resistance to fluoroquinolones and cephalosporins through mutations in efflux pump genes such as acrB, acrR, emrR, and robA, as well as the presence of resistance genes like ampC, ampH, bacA, and emrB.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis and MIC testing were used to identify resistance genes and mutations in E. coli following florfenicol exposure.

full_output.paper_title: 3-Substituted Coumarins Inhibit NorA and MepA Efflux Pumps of Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies 3-substituted coumarins as inhibitors of the NorA and MepA efflux pumps in Staphylococcus aureus, demonstrating their ability to enhance the efficacy of fluoroquinolones and ethidium bromide by inhibiting efflux pump activity.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized broth microdilution, fluorescence emission assays, molecular docking, and membrane permeability tests to evaluate the inhibitory effects of coumarins on efflux pumps in S. aureus.

full_output.paper_title: Novel Antibacterial Agents SAAP-148 and Halicin Combat Gram-Negative Bacteria Colonizing Catheters.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies SAAP-148 and halicin as effective antibacterial agents against Gram-negative bacteria (GNB) colonizing catheters, demonstrating potent bactericidal activity against multidrug-resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antibacterial, anti-biofilm, and anti-persister activities of SAAP-148 and halicin against GNB strains isolated from catheters using in vitro assays.

full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and in-silico analysis were used to identify antimicrobial resistance genes and mutations in LA-MRSA isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic Profiling of Multidrug-Resistant Swine Escherichia coli and Clonal Relationship to Human Isolates in Peru.

full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, MLST, serotyping, and cgMLST + HierCC clustering were used to characterize the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Exploring the Application Potential of Aquaculture Sewage Treatment of Pseudomonas chengduensis Strain WD211 Based on Its Complete Genome.

full_output.key_findings: Pseudomonas chengduensis strain WD211 exhibits resistance to multiple antibiotics, including beta-lactams, vancomycin, and cationic antimicrobial peptides, and possesses genes associated with antibiotic resistance mechanisms such as efflux pumps. It also shows tolerance to high salt concentrations and a wide pH range, making it suitable for aquaculture sewage treatment.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing and annotation, antibiotic susceptibility testing, and biochemical analyses were performed to assess the strain's capabilities.

full_output.paper_title: Propidium Monoazide-Treated, Cell-Direct, Quantitative PCR for Detecting Viable Chloramphenicol-Resistant Escherichia coli and Corynebacterium glutamicum Cells.

full_output.methodology: qPCR and PMA treatment for viable cell detection.

full_output.paper_title: The Anti-Virulence Activities of the Antihypertensive Drug Propranolol in Light of Its Anti-Quorum Sensing Effects against Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Serratia marcescens.
full_output.key_findings: Propranolol exhibits anti-quorum sensing and anti-virulence effects against Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Serratia marcescens at sub-MIC levels, reducing biofilm formation, motility, and production of virulence factors.
full_output.methodology: Molecular docking, RT-PCR, biofilm inhibition assays, and virulence factor assays were used to evaluate propranolol's effects.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Screening of Carbapenem-Resistant K. pneumoniae (CRKP) Clinical Isolates for Concomitant Occurrence of Beta-Lactam Genes (CTX-M, TEM, and SHV) in the Kingdom of Bahrain.
full_output.key_findings: The study reveals the concomitant carriage of SHV, CTX-M-15, and TEM genes in CRKP isolates, highlighting the significance of detecting these resistance genes for appropriate antibiotic prescription.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and ERIC-PCR for molecular typing.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of Extended-Spectrum Beta-Lactamase Resistance in Uropathogenic Escherichia coli Isolates from Urinary Tract Infection Patients in Al-Baha, Saudi Arabia.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that E. coli ESBL producers were moderately prevalent in community- and hospital-acquired UTIs, particularly among female patients. Effective antibiotics against E. coli ESBL included levofloxacin, colistin, tigecycline, amikacin, meropenem, imipenem, and nitrofurantoin.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective cross-sectional study analyzing urine samples from patients with suspected UTIs.

full_output.paper_title: Contamination of a Water Stream and Water Drainage Reaching Matosinhos Beach by Antibiotic-Resistant Bacteria.

full_output.methodology: Water sampling, phenotypic and genotypic characterization, including PCR for resistance genes.

full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, phylogenomic analysis, antibiotic resistance gene prediction, and cloning experiments were conducted.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of Cronobacter sakazakii and Cronobacter malonaticus Strains Isolated from Powdered Dairy Products Intended for Consumption by Adults and Older Adults.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antibiotic resistance genes in Cronobacter sakazakii and Cronobacter malonaticus strains, including blaCSA-1 and blaCMA-1, which confer resistance to cephalothin, and mcr-9.1, which confers resistance to colistin. These strains also exhibited multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize antibiotic resistance genes in Cronobacter strains.

full_output.methodology: Transcriptome analysis and oxidative stress experiments were conducted to investigate resistance mechanisms in Corynespora cassiicola.

full_output.paper_title: Biofilm Formation by Escherichia coli Isolated from Urinary Tract Infections from Aguascalientes, Mexico.

yfcV.encodes: major subunit of a putative chaperone usher fimbriae

full_output.key_findings: The study identified fimH, papC, and yfcV as genes associated with biofilm formation in E. coli isolates from urinary tract infections. These genes were linked to increased biofilm production and higher resistance to certain antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: PCR, biofilm formation assay, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze the E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: The Benefits of Toxicity: M. smegmatis VapBC TA Module Is Induced by Tetracycline Exposure and Promotes Survival.
full_output.key_findings: The VapC and MazF toxins of M. smegmatis are induced by tetracycline exposure and play roles in stress response and survival. VapC overexpression increases resistance to heat shock, while deletion of vapBC reduces survival under tetracycline treatment.
full_output.methodology: Proteomic profiling, qRT-PCR, and MIC determination were used to analyze the impact of VapC and MazF on M. smegmatis stress responses and antibiotic susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of a Method for Standardized Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing with Mycoplasma hyorhinis Field Isolates.

full_output.methodology: The study used a standardized broth microdilution method with 37 M. hyorhinis field isolates to determine antimicrobial susceptibility and performed whole genome sequencing to identify resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Effect of Zinc Oxide and Copper Sulfate on Antibiotic Resistance Plasmid Transfer in Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: Sub-lethal concentrations of ZnO and CuSO4 significantly enhance plasmid conjugation frequency (PCF) in E. coli, especially for IncL, IncA/C, and IncX3 plasmids, indicating an increased dissemination of antibiotic resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: Plasmid conjugation frequency analysis, ROS detection, and gene expression analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Multiplex Real-Time PCR for the Detection of Tetracycline, Ciprofloxacin, and Erythromycin Resistance Determinants from Human and Foodborne Campylobacter jejuni and Campylobacter coli.

full_output.key_findings: The study developed a multiplex real-time PCR assay to detect tetracycline, ciprofloxacin, and erythromycin resistance determinants in Campylobacter jejuni and Campylobacter coli. The assay successfully detected tet(O), erm(B), GyrA_T86I/V, and A2075G mutations.
full_output.methodology: Real-time PCR assay with specific primers and probes for resistance determinants.

full_output.paper_title: Predominance of Multidrug-Resistant Gram-Negative Bacteria Isolated from Supermarket Retail Seafood in Japan.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple AMR genes, including bla TEM-1, bla CTX-M-like, bla CTX-M-65, aac(6')-Ib, and mcr, in Gram-negative bacteria isolated from retail seafood in Japan, highlighting the prevalence of multidrug-resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize AMR genes in bacterial isolates from seafood samples.

full_output.paper_title: Characteristics, Whole-Genome Sequencing and Pathogenicity Analysis of Escherichia coli from a White Feather Broiler Farm.

full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR, whole-genome sequencing, and biofilm formation assays were used to analyze the E. coli strains.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic Resistance of Bacillus cereus in Plant Foods and Edible Wild Mushrooms in a Province.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in Bacillus cereus strains isolated from plant foods and wild mushrooms, including beta-lactamases (bla, bla2), chloramphenicol resistance gene catA, aminoglycoside resistance gene ant(6), macrolide resistance gene abc-f, fosfomycin resistance gene fosB, lincosamide resistance gene lsa, streptogramin resistance gene vat, glycopeptide resistance genes vanR-A and vanS-Pt, and tetracycline resistance gene tet.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic resistance was tested using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method, and resistance genes were analyzed using the CARD database with BLAST comparisons.

full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, MIC assays, and statistical analysis were used to evaluate the presence and impact of resistance genes on sanitiser resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study found high resistance rates to tetracycline, erythromycin, and tylosin in Enterococcus faecalis and Enterococcus faecium isolates from healthy dogs and cats in South Korea, with notable multidrug resistance patterns.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the sec gene in 19.4% of S. aureus isolates from fresh cheese in Croatia, which was associated with the production of SEC enterotoxin. Only 1.1% of isolates showed resistance to mupirocin.
full_output.methodology: Microbial isolation, PCR, RPLA, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze S. aureus isolates from fresh cheese.

full_output.paper_title: An Outbreak of Vancomycin-Resistant Enterococci in a City Hospital Intensive Care Unit: Molecular Characterization of Resistance.

vanA.mechanism: confers resistance to vancomycin by altering cell wall synthesis
vanA.validation_method: PCR detection of vanA gene in VRE isolates

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the vanA gene as the primary resistance mechanism in vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium (VREfm) isolates during an outbreak in a city hospital ICU. All VREfm isolates carried the vanA gene, and molecular typing revealed 12 distinct genotypes with 88.8% clustering, indicating potential cross-contamination and an ongoing epidemic.
full_output.methodology: PCR and molecular typing techniques (AP-PCR, PFGE) were used to identify vanA gene carriage and assess clonal relationships among VRE isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Activity and Mechanisms of Walnut Green Husk Extract.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the antimicrobial activity of walnut green husk extract (WGHa) against Staphylococcus aureus, Bacillus subtilis, and Escherichia coli, revealing its ability to alter cell membrane permeability, cause cell wall damage, interfere with cellular energy metabolism, compromise RNA integrity, and induce DNA replication stress.
full_output.methodology: The study used antimicrobial activity assays, UHPLC-MS/MS for chemical analysis, and transcriptome sequencing to investigate the mechanisms of action of WGHa.

full_output.paper_title: Structural Analysis and Activity Correlation of Amphiphilic Cyclic Antimicrobial Peptides Derived from the [W(4)R(4)] Scaffold.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the structural and dynamic properties of cyclic peptides derived from the [W4R4] scaffold, focusing on their antimicrobial activity and membrane interactions. Modifications such as adding W, R, or DKP residues affected the peptides' activity, with [W4R5] showing the highest potency against various bacterial strains.
full_output.methodology: Peptide synthesis, in vitro biological testing, and molecular dynamics simulations were used to analyze the structural and membrane-binding properties of the peptides.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotics and Antibiotic Resistance-Mur Ligases as an Antibacterial Target.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the potential of Mur ligases as targets for new antibacterial agents, focusing on their role in peptidoglycan biosynthesis and the development of inhibitors targeting these enzymes.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews the biochemical pathways of peptidoglycan synthesis and analyzes the inhibition of Mur ligases through various chemical approaches.

full_output.paper_title: Rationally Designed Novel Phenyloxazoline Synthase Inhibitors: Chemical Synthesis and Biological Evaluation to Accelerate the Discovery of New Antimycobacterial Antibiotics.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies TSA-5 as a novel inhibitor targeting the phenyloxazoline synthase (MbtB) domain, which shows potent antimycobacterial activity against Mycobacterium aurum and Mycobacterium smegmatis, with potential for intracellular killing and efflux pump inhibition.
full_output.methodology: Chemical synthesis, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and biological evaluation including MIC assays and efflux pump inhibition studies.

full_output.paper_title: Decavanadate-Bearing Guanidine Derivatives Developed as Antimicrobial and Antitumor Species.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis and characterization of decavanadate-bearing guanidine derivatives (compounds 1-4) with antimicrobial and antitumor activities. These compounds showed potent inhibition against various bacterial strains and exhibited high cytotoxicity against cancer cells.
full_output.methodology: The compounds were synthesized and characterized using spectroscopic techniques (FT-IR, UV-Vis, EPR) and X-ray diffraction. Their antibacterial and antitumor activities were evaluated through MIC assays, cytotoxicity tests, and EPR spectroscopy.

full_output.paper_title: Anti-Tuberculosis Potential of OJT008 against Active and Multi-Drug-Resistant Mycobacterium Tuberculosis: In Silico and In Vitro Inhibition of Methionine Aminopeptidase.
full_output.key_findings: OJT008 is a potent inhibitor of MtMetAP1c, showing low micromolar IC50 values against cobalt- and nickel-activated MtMetAP1c and demonstrating efficacy against both active and multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
full_output.methodology: Cloning and overexpression of MtMetAP1c, in vitro enzyme activity assays, molecular docking analysis, and determination of MIC values against Mtb strains.

full_output.paper_title: Gypsum-Related Impact on Antibiotic-Loaded Composite Based on Highly Porous Hydroxyapatite-Advantages and Disadvantages.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the impact of gypsum and gentamicin on hydroxyapatite-based composites for bone tissue regeneration, showing improved antibacterial activity against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria without adverse effects on osteoblasts or mechanical properties.
full_output.methodology: The study characterized composites using FTIR, mechanical testing, and evaluated biocompatibility and antibacterial activity through cell culture and microbial assays.

full_output.paper_title: Depolymerisation of the Klebsiella pneumoniae Capsular Polysaccharide K21 by Klebsiella Phage K5.
full_output.key_findings: Klebsiella phage K5 was isolated and characterized, with two receptor-binding proteins (gp40 and gp41) identified. Only gp41 exhibited polysaccharide depolymerizing activity against capsular polysaccharide type K21.
full_output.methodology: Phage isolation, genome sequencing, protein cloning, expression, and purification, along with biochemical and structural analyses.

full_output.paper_title: Biosynthesis of the Inner Core of Bordetella pertussis Lipopolysaccharides: Effect of Mutations on LPS Structure, Cell Division, and Toll-like Receptor 4 Activation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the eptB gene in B. pertussis, which encodes a PEA transferase responsible for modifying the phosphate on Kdo in the inner core of LPS. Inactivation of eptB leads to reduced TLR4 activation and decreased endotoxicity.
full_output.methodology: Gene inactivation, LC-MS analysis, and TLR4 activation assays were used to characterize the role of eptB in LPS modification and TLR4 signaling.

full_output.paper_title: The Inactivation of the Putative Two-Component System Sensor PA14_27940 Increases the Susceptibility to Several Antibiotics and Reduces the Motility of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

full_output.methodology: Deletion mutant analysis, MIC testing, motility assays, and gene expression analysis.

full_output.paper_title: The Dynamics of OXA-23 β-Lactamase from Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzes the conformational dynamics of OXA-23 β-lactamase from Acinetobacter baumannii, highlighting its structural plasticity and ability to adopt open and closed conformations, which may influence its carbapenemase activity.
full_output.methodology: Molecular dynamics simulations were performed to analyze the conformational changes of OXA-23.

full_output.key_findings: Six new bacteriophages (SAVM01 to SAVM06) were isolated from wastewater treatment plants and characterized for their ability to lyse Staphylococcus clinical isolates from diabetic foot ulcers. These phages showed strong lytic activity against various Staphylococcus species, including methicillin-resistant S. aureus and coagulase-negative staphylococci. Additionally, the phages were effective in disrupting biofilms formed by these bacteria. Mutations in the lexA, recJ, glucosaminidase domain-containing protein, xerC, essG, and splA genes were identified in phage-resistant mutants of S. aureus NSA1385, suggesting potential resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Phages were isolated from wastewater samples and characterized using transmission electron microscopy, whole-genome sequencing, and host range analysis. Phage-resistant mutants were generated and sequenced to identify mutations associated with resistance.

full_output.paper_title: StM171, a Stenotrophomonas maltophilia Bacteriophage That Affects Sensitivity to Antibiotics in Host Bacteria and Their Biofilm Formation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in S. maltophilia strains, including efflux pumps (emrABCRsm, smeABC, smeDEF), beta-lactamases (bla1, bla2), aminoglycoside modifying enzymes (aph(3')-Iic, aph(6)-Smalt), and an RND efflux pump (oqxB9). These genes contribute to resistance against various antibiotics such as fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, beta-lactams, and others.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing and analysis of S. maltophilia strains, along with antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.methodology: PCR and gel electrophoresis were used to detect the presence of bla(CTX-M) and bla(TEM) genes in ESBL-producing E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterisation and antimicrobial resistance of Streptococcus agalactiae isolates from dairy farms in China.

full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and dose-response curve analysis were used to identify genetic mutations and their effects on antibiotic susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Characteristics, Antimicrobial Susceptibility, Biofilm-Forming Ability of Clinically Invasive Staphylococcus aureus Isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified ST59 and ST7 as dominant clones among invasive S. aureus isolates, with ST7 exhibiting strong biofilm-forming ability linked to high icaA expression. MRSA isolates showed higher resistance rates compared to MSSA.

full_output.key_findings: The study describes the design and synthesis of N4-substituted piperazinyl norfloxacin derivatives with broad-spectrum antibacterial activity. The derivatives were found to inhibit DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV, and some exhibited additional effects on bacterial cell wall synthesis.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized in silico, in vitro, and in vivo approaches to evaluate the activity and mechanism of action of the synthesized compounds.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistant Bacteria Monitoring in Raw Seafood Retailed: a Pilot Study Focused on Vibrio and Aeromonas.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the zit B and znt A genes associated with Zn tolerance in E. coli isolates from piglets, highlighting their prevalence in Zn-resistant isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation and characterization of three novel lytic phages against K54 serotype carbapenem-resistant hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: Three novel lytic phages were isolated and characterized against a carbapenem-resistant hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae strain, showing potential as alternatives to conventional antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Development and validation of a rabbit model of Pseudomonas aeruginosa non-ventilated pneumonia for preclinical drug development.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a rabbit model of non-ventilated pneumonia caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa strain 6206, demonstrating its utility for evaluating antibacterial drugs. The model showed acute respiratory distress syndrome features, and humanized dosing regimens of meropenem and tobramycin reduced mortality and bacterial load.
full_output.methodology: The study involved a natural history study, pharmacokinetic studies, and therapeutic randomized controlled trials in rabbits to validate the model and assess antibiotic efficacy.

full_output.paper_title: Polyhexamethylene biguanide promotes adaptive cross-resistance to gentamicin in Escherichia coli biofilms.

full_output.paper_title: Colicins and T6SS-based competition systems enhance enterotoxigenic E. coli (ETEC) competitiveness.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Colicin Ia as a key factor in the competitive ability of ETEC strains, demonstrating that it enables ETEC to outcompete other E. coli strains in vitro. Additionally, the research highlights the role of T6SS in enhancing ETEC competitiveness, especially under conditions involving bile.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, comparative genomics, and in vitro competition assays were used to analyze the role of colicins and T6SS in ETEC competitiveness.

full_output.paper_title: fosA11, a novel chromosomal-encoded fosfomycin resistance gene identified in Providencia rettgeri.

fosA11.validation_method: cloning in E. coli + MIC test
fosA11.genetic_context: The fosA11 gene was located on the chromosome in P. rettgeri W986 (Fig. 5) according to whole-genome sequencing. To understand the genetic context of fosA11, both sides of the flanking regions around fosA11 at approximately 40 kb and closely related fosA-encoding gene regions in five other Providencia strains were analyzed, as shown in Fig. 5. No mobile genetic elements were found in the neighboring regions of fosA. Moreover, the GC content of fosA11 (59.43%) was inconsistent with that of the chromosome (40.23%) in W986. Comparative genomic analysis of the flanking region of fosA11 in W986 and fosA11-carrying fragments in other Providencia species showed that all fosA11 genes were surrounded by two genes encoding hypothetical proteins.
fosA11.evidence_note: The fosA11 gene was identified through whole-genome sequencing and functional characterization. Cloning of fosA11 into E. coli resulted in a significant increase in the MIC with fosfomycin, confirming its role in resistance.

full_output.key_findings: A novel chromosomal-encoded fosfomycin resistance gene, fosA11, was identified in Providencia rettgeri W986. The gene encodes a functional enzyme, FosA11, which effectively inactivates fosfomycin.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, cloning, and MIC testing were used to identify and characterize the fosA11 gene.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that piperacillin/tazobactam resistance in invasive Haemophilus influenzae in Germany is rare, with only 0.3% of strains showing resistance. Mutations in the ftsI gene, encoding penicillin-binding protein 3 (PBP3), were associated with reduced susceptibility to piperacillin/tazobactam.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing, sequencing of ftsI, and molecular characterization of PBP3 mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Resistance to first-line antibiotic therapy among patients with uncomplicated acute cystitis in Melbourne, Australia: prevalence, predictors and clinical impact.

dfrA.validation_method: genomic characterization and phenotypic resistance testing

full_output.key_findings: The study found that 27% of E. coli isolates from patients with uncomplicated acute cystitis in Melbourne, Australia, were resistant to trimethoprim, mediated by the dfrA gene. Resistance to nitrofurantoin was rare.
full_output.methodology: Prospective observational study with genomic characterization and phenotypic susceptibility testing of bacterial isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical, microbiological and genomic characterization of Gram-negative bacteria with dual carbapenemases as identified by rapid molecular testing.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes dual carbapenemase-producing organisms (DCPOs) and identifies various carbapenemase genes including bla NDM, bla OXA-48-like, and bla KPC. These genes were found to confer resistance to carbapenems and were located on distinct plasmids, except for one case where both bla NDM and bla KPC were on a single plasmid.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and molecular testing were used to identify and characterize the carbapenemase genes in DCPO isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Characterizing Neisseria meningitidis in Southern Vietnam between 2012 and 2021: A predominance of the chloramphenicol-resistant ST-1576 lineage.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the chloramphenicol-resistant ST-1576 lineage of Neisseria meningitidis in Southern Vietnam, highlighting the presence of the catP gene encoding chloramphenicol acetyltransferase and mutations in gyrA contributing to ciprofloxacin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing, WGS, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize resistance mechanisms in Neisseria meningitidis isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that N. curviflora methanolic extract exhibits anti-quorum sensing activity by inhibiting the production of virulence factors and biofilm formation in P. aeruginosa. It significantly reduces the expression of pslA and pelA genes, suggesting interference with quorum sensing systems.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the effect of N. curviflora methanolic extract on P. aeruginosa virulence factors and biofilm formation through various assays, including violacein inhibition, pyocyanin production, protease activity, chitinase activity, rhamnolipid production, biofilm formation, swarming motility, aggregation ability, hydrophobicity, and exopolysaccharide production. RT-PCR was used to assess gene expression.

full_output.paper_title: Impact of CRAMP-34 on Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilms and extracellular metabolites.
full_output.key_findings: CRAMP-34 disperses Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilms and increases the susceptibility of dispersed bacteria to colistin and vancomycin. It also delays the development of bacterial resistance to colistin and ciprofloxacin.
full_output.methodology: Metabolomics analysis, biofilm biomass assessment, and antibiotic synergy experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Emerging Challenges in Staphylococcus aureus Bloodstream Infections: Insights from Coagulase Typing, Toxin Genes, and Antibiotic Resistance Patterns.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high rates of multidrug resistance in S. aureus bloodstream infections, with specific toxin genes (tst, pvl, eta, etb) and coagulase types (III, II, VI) showing varied prevalence. All isolates were susceptible to linezolid and teicoplanin.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing via disk diffusion, PCR for toxin gene detection, and coagulase typing via multiplex PCR.

full_output.paper_title: The prevalence of Staphylococcus aureus and the emergence of livestock-associated MRSA CC398 in pig production in eastern China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antibiotic resistance genes in MRSA isolates from pig production in Eastern China, including mecA, blaZ, dfrG, tetM, tetK, tetT, tetL, emr(C), aadD, aadE, aac(6')-aph(2''), norA, lnu(B), fexA, and cfr, highlighting the multidrug-resistant nature of these isolates.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize MRSA isolates from pig farms and slaughterhouses in Eastern China.

full_output.paper_title: Evolution of Staphylococcus aureus infections in Argentina: A nationwide study from 2009 to 2015
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the mupA gene as a determinant of mupirocin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus isolates, with a low prevalence of 0.3% in MRSA isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a prospective observational cross-sectional multicenter study design, analyzing SA clinical isolates collected from hospitals across Argentina in 2015, along with a longitudinal retrospective study from 2009 to 2015.

full_output.paper_title: Resistance to aminoglycoside and quinolone drugs among Klebsiella pneumoniae clinical isolates from northern Jordan.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several aminoglycoside-modifying enzymes and plasmid-mediated quinolone resistance genes in K. pneumoniae isolates from northern Jordan, including aac(6')-Ib, aac(3')-II, ant(3")-I, aph(3')-VI, armA, rmtB, qnrS, qnrB, oqxAB, and aac(6')-Ib-cr. These genes were significantly associated with non-susceptibility to aminoglycosides, quinolones, and beta-lactams.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR, and MLST were used to analyze the resistance genes in K. pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: ABCB1 overexpression through locus amplification represents an actionable target to combat paclitaxel resistance in pancreatic cancer cells.

ABCB1.validation_method: RT-qPCR, Western blot, Hoechst-efflux assay, SRB assay

full_output.key_findings: ABCB1 overexpression through locus amplification was identified as a conserved feature in paclitaxel-resistant PDAC cells, and its inhibition restored paclitaxel sensitivity.
full_output.methodology: RNA-seq, proteomics, RT-qPCR, Western blot, SRB assay, Hoechst-efflux assay, siRNA-mediated gene silencing, kinase inhibitor screening.

full_output.paper_title: Altered larval activation response associated with multidrug resistance in the canine hookworm Ancylostoma caninum.

tbb-iso-1.notes: mutation in codon 167 (F167Y) imparts benzimidazole resistance
tbb-iso-1.evidence_note: The paper explicitly states that the F167Y mutation in the β-tubulin isotype 1 gene imparts benzimidazole resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic characterization of Salmonella isolated from retail chicken and humans with diarrhea in Qingdao, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 79 antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) in Salmonella isolates from retail chicken and humans with diarrhea in Qingdao, China, including aac(6')-Iaa, bla TEM-1B, tet(A), aph(6)-Id, aph(3")-Ib, sul2, floR, qnrS1, bla NDM-1, mcr-1.1, and mcr-9.1. These genes conferred resistance to various antibiotics such as aminoglycosides, beta-lactams, tetracyclines, sulfonamides, chloramphenicol, fluoroquinolones, carbapenems, and colistin.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and in silico analysis using ResFinder database.

full_output.paper_title: Hyperbaric oxygen augments susceptibility to C. difficile infection by impairing gut microbiota ability to stimulate the HIF-1α-IL-22 axis in ILC3.
full_output.key_findings: Hyperbaric oxygen (HBO) increases susceptibility to C. difficile infection (CDI) by altering gut microbiota composition and reducing butyrate production, which impairs HIF-1α-IL-22 signaling in ILC3. Butyrate supplementation restores ILC3 function and reduces CDI severity.
full_output.methodology: Mouse models, 16S rDNA sequencing, qPCR, FITC-dextran assay, and cytokine analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular detection of Shiga toxin and extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Escherichia coli isolates from sheep and goats.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in E. coli isolates from sheep and goats, including bla CTX-M-9, bla CTX-M-25, stx2, mcr-4, floR, mcr-1, tet(A), sulI, tet(O), tet(W), parC, mcr-2, ampC, qnrS, and ermB. These genes confer resistance to various antibiotics such as beta-lactams, colistin, tetracycline, sulfonamides, fluoroquinolones, and macrolides.
full_output.methodology: PCR and phenotypic testing were used to identify AMR genes and resistance profiles in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Resistance mechanism of Escherichia coli strains with different ampicillin resistance levels.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in several genes, including ampC, murE, ftsI, marR, gutQ, rpoC, dcuA, frdD, and amiB, which contribute to ampicillin resistance in E. coli strains. The ampC promoter mutation was found to significantly increase ampC gene expression and ampicillin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genomic and transcriptomic analyses were performed on E. coli strains with varying levels of ampicillin resistance. Whole-genome sequencing and RNA-seq were used to identify mutations and gene expression changes.
full_output.sample_size: Three E. coli strains (non-resistant, 10-fold resistant, and 95-fold resistant) were analyzed.

full_output.paper_title: Diversity and characterization of culturable fungi associated with the marine sea cucumber Holothuria scabra.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various culturable fungi associated with the marine sea cucumber Holothuria scabra, highlighting their potential for producing antimicrobial metabolites. Notably, Aspergillus terreus F10M7, Trichoderma harzianum F31M4, and T. harzianum F31M5 showed potent antimicrobial activity against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria and human pathogenic fungi.
full_output.methodology: The study involved isolation, identification, and characterization of fungi from different sections of H. scabra, including enzymatic activity tests and antimicrobial assays.

full_output.paper_title: Development of 2nd generation aminomethyl spectinomycins that overcome native efflux in Mycobacterium abscessus.

whiB7.validation_method: generation of deletion mutants and analysis of susceptibility

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies tetV as a major efflux pump responsible for spectinomycin resistance in Mycobacterium abscessus and shows that the 2nd generation aminomethyl spectinomycins (eAmSPCs) overcome this resistance by reducing efflux. The transcriptional regulator whiB7 was found to upregulate resistance genes, including tetV.
full_output.methodology: Generation of spontaneous mutants, whole-genome sequencing, MIC testing, and transcriptomic analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of a novel bacteriophage endolysin (LysAB1245) with extended lytic activity against distinct capsular types associated with Acinetobacter baumannii resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes LysAB1245, a novel bacteriophage endolysin with broad lytic activity against multidrug-resistant (MDR) Acinetobacter baumannii isolates with various capsular types.
full_output.methodology: Expression and purification of LysAB1245, antibacterial activity testing, and determination of MIC and MBC.
full_output.sample_size: 19 isolates of MDR A. baumannii and ATCC 19606

full_output.paper_title: The Bradyrhizobium japonicum exporter ExsFGH is involved in efflux of ferric xenosiderophores from the periplasm.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the RND efflux pump genes exsF, exsG, and exsH as critical for the efflux of ferric xenosiderophores from the periplasm in Bradyrhizobium japonicum, highlighting their role in maintaining siderophore homeostasis and contributing to resistance against certain antibiotics like tetracycline.
full_output.methodology: Genetic analysis of suppressor mutants, whole-genome sequencing, and functional assays including iron uptake and antibiotic sensitivity tests.

full_output.paper_title: Intracellular Pseudomonas aeruginosa enhances the pathogenicity of Acanthamoeba in a rat model of keratitis
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Pseudomonas aeruginosa as an intracellular bacterium within Acanthamoeba, which enhances the severity of keratitis in an animal model.
full_output.methodology: The study used molecular techniques, FISH, TEM, and an animal model to investigate the role of intracellular P. aeruginosa in Acanthamoeba keratitis.

full_output.paper_title: Low genetic diversity of Treponema pallidum ssp. pertenue (TPE) isolated from patients' ulcers in Namatanai District of Papua New Guinea: Local human population is infected by three TPE genotypes.

mutations_found.validated_by: sequencing of 23S rRNA genes in TPE isolates

full_output.key_findings: The study identified three TPE genotypes (J E 11, S E 22, and T E 13) with low genetic diversity in the Namatanai District of Papua New Guinea. An A2058G mutation in the 23S rRNA gene was found in three TPE isolates, conferring azithromycin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Multi-locus sequence typing (MLST) of TPE isolates, sequencing of 23S rRNA genes, and analysis of PCR-positive samples.

full_output.paper_title: A preliminary exploration on the mechanism of the carbapenem-resistance transformation of Serratia marcescens in vivo.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the mechanisms of carbapenem resistance in Serratia marcescens, highlighting the role of bla KPC gene acquisition, increased expression of bla KPC, and loss of a porin gene leading to higher expression of bla CTX-M-14.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, qPCR, and MIC testing were used to analyze carbapenem resistance mechanisms in Serratia marcescens.

full_output.paper_title: First report of Acinetobacter pittii acute community-acquired pneumonia in an immunocompetent patient in France following a heat wave.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies two beta-lactamase-encoding chromosomal genes, blaADC-25 and blaOXA-500, in a wild-type Acinetobacter pittii isolate from a community-acquired pneumonia case in France, which are consistent with the observed antibiotic resistance profile.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: The importance of the bacterial spectrum in the clinical diagnostics and management of patients with spontaneous pyogenic spondylodiscitis and isolated spinal epidural empyema: a 20-year cohort study at a single spine center.

MSSA.validation_method: isolated from patients and tested for susceptibility

full_output.key_findings: The study identified various bacterial species including MSSA, MRSA, Streptococcus spp., Enterococcus spp., CoNS, Enterobacterales, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, highlighting their roles in causing spondylodiscitis and isolated spinal epidural empyema.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of 187 patients with spondylodiscitis and isolated spinal epidural empyema, involving microbiological assessments and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Increase in antioxidant capacity associated with the successful subclone of hypervirulent carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae ST11-KL64.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies specific genes within the pK2044-like plasmid of ST11-KL64 hv-CRKP, including g142, g536, ymoA, g417, g280, and g499, which are associated with virulence and metabolic processes. The deletion of a 3 kb region in the plasmid affects methionine metabolism and antioxidant capacity, contributing to the survival of the subclone in macrophages.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, comparative genomics, transcriptomic analysis, and functional assays were used to validate the role of the deleted region in antioxidant capacity and methionine metabolism.

full_output.paper_title: Assessment of Antibiotic Resistance among Clinical Isolates of Enterobacteriaceae in Nepal.
full_output.key_findings: The study found high levels of antibiotic resistance among Enterobacteriaceae isolates in Nepal, with significant resistance to penicillins, cephalosporins, and fluoroquinolones. Multidrug-resistant (MDR) and extensively drug-resistant (XDR) strains were prevalent, particularly among E. coli, C. freundii, and K. pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed clinical isolates of Enterobacteriaceae using the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method to assess antimicrobial susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: Entomotherapy as an alternative treatment for diseases due to Gram-negative bacteria in Burkina Faso.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antibacterial activity of insect extracts against Gram-negative bacteria, highlighting the potential of entomotherapy as an alternative treatment for bacterial infections.
full_output.methodology: Antibacterial activity of insect extracts was tested using the agar diffusion method against various Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.sample_size: Thirteen medicinal insects were collected from three provinces in Burkina Faso.

full_output.paper_title: Novel betulin derivatives as multidrug reversal agents targeting P-glycoprotein.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies betulin derivatives 6g and 6i as effective P-glycoprotein (P-gp) inhibitors, reversing multidrug resistance in leukemia cells by enhancing the intracellular accumulation of doxorubicin.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized synthetic chemistry, cytotoxicity assays, and molecular modeling to evaluate the P-gp inhibitory activity of betulin derivatives.

full_output.paper_title: Heparin-network-mediated long-lasting coatings on intravascular catheters for adaptive antithrombosis and antibacterial infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a heparin-network-mediated coating (HS/DAC) on intravascular catheters that exhibits long-lasting antithrombotic and antibacterial properties, effectively reducing thrombus formation and bacterial infections in both in vitro and in vivo models.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a combination of biochemical analyses, in vitro assays, and in vivo models to evaluate the antithrombotic and antibacterial efficacy of the HS/DAC coating.

full_output.paper_title: Filling knowledge gaps related to AmpC-dependent β-lactam resistance in Enterobacter cloacae.

full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the role of ECL_03254, a putative AmpC-type beta-lactamase, in Enterobacter cloacae. Despite high expression, it did not significantly increase resistance to cephalosporins. The primary AmpC gene ECL_00553 was found to confer resistance to cefoxitin and cefotaxime.
full_output.methodology: Cloning of genes, MIC determination, RT-PCR, and Sanger sequencing were used to validate the resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Phage Paride can kill dormant, antibiotic-tolerant cells of Pseudomonas aeruginosa by direct lytic replication.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies phage Paride as a novel bacteriophage capable of directly lysing deep-dormant, antibiotic-tolerant Pseudomonas aeruginosa cells. Paride's ability to replicate on these cells is dependent on the bacterial stress response pathways involving (p)ppGpp and RpoS.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized deep-dormant cultures of Pseudomonas aeruginosa and conducted phage infection experiments, one-step growth assays, and genetic analysis to investigate Paride's mechanism of action.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified that older age is associated with a higher number of detectably expressed antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) in the lower respiratory tract microbiome of critically ill patients. Specifically, adults showed higher expression of beta-lactam, aminoglycoside, and tetracycline resistance genes compared to children.
full_output.methodology: Metatranscriptomic RNA sequencing was used to analyze the lower respiratory tract microbiome of critically ill patients, focusing on the detection and expression of antimicrobial resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Evolution of extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing ST131 Escherichia coli at a single hospital over 15 years.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies various extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL) genes, including blaCTX-M-15, blaCTX-M-27, blaCTX-M-14, and others, in ST131 Escherichia coli isolates from a single hospital over 15 years. These genes are responsible for resistance to multiple β-lactam antibiotics and are carried on both plasmids and the chromosome. Mutations in genes such as ftsI, arnC, gloB, and fyuA were also found to contribute to resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and BLASTP searches against the ResFinder database were used to identify ESBL genes and mutations in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Dynamics and quantitative contribution of the aminoglycoside 6'-N-acetyltransferase type Ib [AAC(6')-Ib] to amikacin resistance.

aac(6')-Ib.genetic_context: aac(6′)-Ib gene is located within plasmids and chromosomes as part of integrons, transposons, genomic islands, and other genetic structures
aac(6')-Ib.evidence_note: The paper describes the role of AAC(6′)-Ib in conferring resistance to amikacin through acetylation.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the aminoglycoside 6'-N-acetyltransferase type Ib (AAC(6')-Ib) and its role in amikacin resistance, showing that resistance increases linearly with AAC(6')-Ib concentration until a plateau is reached due to protein aggregation.
full_output.methodology: Used a fluorescence-based system to quantify AAC(6')-Ib molecules and CRISPRi to modulate its copy number in E. coli.

full_output.paper_title: Polymyxin B and ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid act synergistically against Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: Polymyxin B and EDTA act synergistically against P. aeruginosa and S. aureus, showing significant synergy in planktonic and biofilm forms, especially against P. aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: Checkerboard assays, MIC/MBC, MBEC, and SEM were used to evaluate synergy and antimicrobial effectiveness.

full_output.paper_title: The metabolic slowdown caused by the deletion of pspA accelerates protein aggregation during stationary phase facilitating antibiotic persistence.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that deletion of the pspA gene increases bacterial dormancy depth and persister formation, which is linked to protein aggregation and reduced antibiotic susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: The study used time-lapse imaging, transcriptome profiling, and ATP measurements to analyze the effects of pspA deletion on bacterial dormancy and antibiotic persistence.

full_output.paper_title: Genome-based assessment of antimicrobial resistance reveals the lineage specificity of resistance and resistance gene profiles in Riemerella anatipestifer from China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple AMR genes and mutations in Riemerella anatipestifer, highlighting the high prevalence of bla OXA-like, tet(X) genes, and specific mutations like gyrA(S83I) and rpoB(H491N).
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify AMR genes and mutations.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in the gut microbiota of weaned piglets, including tet(A), tet(L), tet(X), vat(E), erm(X), mph(A), and TEM-33, which confer resistance to tetracyclines, macrolides, and beta-lactams. Probiotic supplementation with Lactiplantibacillus plantarum P-8 altered the ARG profile in the colonic microbiota, suggesting a potential role in mitigating antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic analysis of gut microbiota from weaned piglets treated with probiotics, antibiotics, or no treatment.

full_output.paper_title: Regional spread of an atypical ESBL-producing Escherichia coli ST131H89 clone among different human and environmental reservoirs in Western Switzerland.

blaTEM-1.validation_method: genomic analysis and detection via NGS

full_output.paper_title: Marinomonas mediterranea synthesizes an R-type bacteriocin.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies MEDPRO2 as a genomic region encoding an R-type bacteriocin in Marinomonas mediterranea, which exhibits antimicrobial activity against other Marinomonas species.
full_output.methodology: Genome analysis, mass spectrometry, and antimicrobial activity assays were used to characterize the R-type bacteriocin.

full_output.paper_title: Polymyxins with Potent Antibacterial Activity against Colistin-Resistant Pathogens: Fine-Tuning Hydrophobicity with Unnatural Amino Acids.
full_output.key_findings: The study explores polymyxin analogues with unnatural amino acids, demonstrating that hydrophobicity correlates with antibacterial activity against colistin-resistant pathogens. Compounds like 5d and 5e showed exceptional activity against resistant strains, highlighting the potential of optimizing hydrophobicity for effective antimicrobial agents.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of polymyxin analogues, determination of antibacterial activity via broth microdilution assays, and analysis of hydrophobicity using RP-HPLC.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that piperacillin/tazobactam MICs of 8 mg/L and ≥16 mg/L were significantly associated with increased in-hospital 30-day mortality in patients with third-generation cephalosporin-resistant Escherichia coli bloodstream infections. However, no specific AMR genes or mutations were characterized in this paper.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective cohort study analyzing the association between piperacillin/tazobactam MICs and mortality in patients with E. coli bloodstream infections.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of community-acquired Clostridioides difficile strains in Israel, 2020-2022.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterized community-acquired Clostridioides difficile strains in Israel, identifying various sequence types (STs) and analyzing their virulence factors and antibiotic susceptibility. No specific AMR genes or mutations were experimentally validated in this study.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, MLST analysis, toxin gene detection, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize the strains.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of In-Vitro Activity of Ceftaroline Against Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus Clinical Isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that none of the MRSA isolates were resistant to ceftaroline, with 91.4% being sensitive and 8.6% showing intermediate susceptibility. The mecA gene was confirmed in MRSA isolates using real-time PCR.
full_output.methodology: The study used Vitek 2 system for species identification, cefoxitin disk diffusion for MRSA detection, E-test for ceftaroline MIC, and real-time PCR for mecA gene confirmation.

full_output.paper_title: Design, Synthesis, and Evaluation of New 1H-Benzo[d]imidazole Based PqsR Inhibitors as Adjuvant Therapy for Pseudomonas aeruginosa Infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies 6f as a potent PqsR antagonist that effectively inhibits the pqs quorum sensing system in P. aeruginosa, reducing the production of virulence factors such as pyocyanin and AQs, and enhancing the efficacy of antibiotics against biofilms.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of 6f and its analogues, in vitro evaluation of their biological activity in P. aeruginosa strains, and determination of their effect on AQ production and pyocyanin levels.

full_output.paper_title: Gut metabolite L-lactate supports Campylobacter jejuni population expansion during acute infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the lctP gene, which encodes an L-lactate transporter, as essential for C. jejuni growth during infection. Mutagenesis of lctP significantly reduced bacterial colonization and growth in the ferret gut.

full_output.paper_title: Biological characterization and genomic analysis of a novel methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus phage, SauPS-28.

These mutations, including I179S, reduce the cost of the bla TEM-116* plasmid, demonstrating an antagonistic interaction between the phage gene and the β-lactamase.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and molecular characterization of extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli isolates from dairy cattle with endometritis in Gansu Province, China.

full_output.paper_title: Concurrent transmission of multiple carbapenemases in a long-term acute-care hospital.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibility and serotype distribution of Streptococcus pneumoniae isolates among children in Suzhou, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study reported the antimicrobial susceptibility and serotype distribution of Streptococcus pneumoniae isolates from children in Suzhou, China, between 2017 and 2018. The most common resistance pattern of non-invasive isolates was macrolides + sulfamethoxazole + clindamycin + tetracycline. The most extensive resistance pattern of invasive isolates was macrolides + β-lactams + sulfamethoxazole + clindamycin + tetracycline. Serotypes 19F, 6B, 23F, 6A, and 19A were identified as predominant in Suzhou. PCV13 serotype coverage was 80.9%.
full_output.methodology: Clinical data of hospitalized children with Streptococcus pneumoniae were collected and analyzed. Serotypes were determined using the Quellung reaction. Antibiotic resistance was tested using the E-test diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Nitric oxide sensor NsrR is the key direct regulator of magnetosome formation and nitrogen metabolism in Magnetospirillum.

full_output.methodology: The study utilized genetic manipulation, qRT-PCR, EMSA, and bioluminescence assays to investigate the role of NsrR Mg in regulating magnetosome formation and nitrogen metabolism.

full_output.paper_title: A whole-cell hypersensitive biosensor for beta-lactams based on the AmpR-AmpC regulatory circuit from the Antarctic Pseudomonas sp. IB20.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a whole-cell biosensor based on the AmpR-AmpC regulatory system from Pseudomonas sp. IB20, which can detect beta-lactam antibiotics with high sensitivity, particularly carbapenems.
full_output.methodology: Genetic modification of E. coli SN0301 with the ampR-ampC system, RT-qPCR for gene expression analysis, and biosensor testing with various beta-lactam antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization and risk assessment of novel SXT/R391 integrative and conjugative elements with multidrug resistance in Proteus mirabilis isolated from China, 2018-2020.

full_output.paper_title: Nosocomial surveillance of multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii: a genomic epidemiological study.

full_output.paper_title: Insights gained from sequencing Australian non-invasive and invasive Streptococcus pyogenes isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified antimicrobial-resistance genes such as tetM, ermA, ermB, mefA, and dfrG in less than 10% of the 318 S. pyogenes isolates analyzed, primarily in non-invasive infections.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial properties and urease suppression ability of Lactobacillus inhibit the development of infectious urinary stones caused by Proteus mirabilis.

full_output.paper_title: Research on Bacterial Diversity and Antibiotic Resistance in the Dairy Farm Environment in a Part of Shandong Province.

full_output.paper_title: Prolonged Antibiotic Use in a Preclinical Model of Gulf War Chronic Multisymptom-Illness Causes Renal Fibrosis-like Pathology via Increased micro-RNA 21-Induced PTEN Inhibition That Is Correlated with Low Host Lachnospiraceae Abundance.

full_output.paper_title: Safety Assessment and Probiotic Potential Comparison of Bifidobacterium longum subsp. infantis BLI-02, Lactobacillus plantarum LPL28, Lactobacillus acidophilus TYCA06, and Lactobacillus paracasei ET-66.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that B. longum subsp. infantis BLI-02, L. plantarum LPL28, L. acidophilus TYCA06, and L. paracasei ET-66 exhibited no antibiotic resistance and mutagenic activity. full_output.methodology: The study assessed antibiotic resistance, mutagenicity, and toxicity of the probiotic strains using MIC tests, Ames test, acute and sub-chronic toxicity tests, and in vitro adherence and bacteriostatic activity assays.

full_output.paper_title: Effects of Silybum marianum L. Seed Extracts on Multi Drug Resistant (MDR) Bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antibacterial effects of Silybum marianum seed extracts against multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria, identifying ethanol extract as the most effective. The extract showed bacteriostatic activity against MDR isolates, including Staphylococcus aureus, Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Escherichia coli.
full_output.methodology: Antibacterial activity was assessed using disc diffusion, MIC determination, and TEM. GC-MS identified bioactive compounds, and ADMET analysis predicted drug-like properties.

full_output.paper_title: Amide/Amino-Based Functional Additives for Lubricants: Structure, Antimicrobial Activity and Wear Resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified two quaternary ammonium compounds (QACs), mono–15 and 15–4–15, which exhibited potent bactericidal activity against both Gram-positive (Staphylococcus aureus) and Gram-negative (Salmonella enteritica) bacteria. These compounds showed effective antibacterial properties when incorporated into vegetable-based greases, demonstrating potential for use in food-grade lubricants.

Tribological and oxidation stability tests were also conducted to assess the impact of the additives on lubricant performance.

full_output.paper_title: Comparison of Antibacterial Activities of Korean Pine (Pinus densiflora) Needle Steam Distillation Extract on Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus Focusing on Membrane Fluidity and Genes Involved in Membrane Lipids and Stress.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the antibacterial activity of Korean pine needle steam distillation extract (SDPNE) against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus, revealing that SDPNE affects membrane fluidity and alters fatty acid composition, leading to reduced bacterial growth. full_output.methodology: The study used paper disk diffusion, optical density measurements, fluorescence polarization, gas chromatography-mass spectrometry, and real-time q-PCR to assess the antibacterial effects and molecular mechanisms of SDPNE.

full_output.paper_title: Metal nanoparticles as inhibitors of enzymes and toxins of multidrug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the challenges posed by multidrug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and explores the potential of metal nanoparticles as inhibitors of its enzymes and toxins. It highlights the mechanisms of resistance in S. aureus, including the presence of resistance genes like mecA, and emphasizes the need for alternative therapies due to the rising prevalence of antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: The paper is a review article discussing the mechanisms of resistance in S. aureus and the potential of metal nanoparticles as therapeutic agents.

full_output.paper_title: Transmission of fluoroquinolones resistance among multidrug-resistant tuberculosis in Shanghai, China: a retrospective population-based genomic epidemiology study.

gyrA.notes: Mutations in gyrA were found in 94.6% of FQ-R strains.

gyrB.notes: Mutations in gyrB were found in 10.5% of FQ-R strains.

rrs.notes: The rrs 1401A > G mutation was more frequent in FQ-R strains.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified that 34.7% of MDR-TB patients in Shanghai had fluoroquinolone resistance (FQ-R), with 33.2% of these cases attributed to transmitted FQ-R strains. Key mutations associated with FQ-R included gyrA and gyrB chromosomal mutations, as well as the rrs 1401A > G mutation.
full_output.methodology: Genomic epidemiology study using whole-genome sequencing and statistical analysis to identify FQ-R mechanisms and transmission patterns.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characteristics, fitness, and virulence of high-risk and non-high-risk clones of carbapenemase-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterized 20 high-risk clones (HiRCs) and 10 non-HiRCs of XDR K. pneumoniae, focusing on factors related to their epidemiological success. While no clear genomic differences in known virulence markers were found, HiRCs were more virulent than non-HiRCs in a Galleria mellonella model.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, cgMLST, and in vitro and in vivo experiments were used to analyze the molecular characteristics, fitness, and virulence of the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Heterotrophic bacteria in drinking water: evaluating antibiotic resistance and the presence of virulence genes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a variety of antibiotic resistance genes in heterotrophic bacteria from drinking water, highlighting the presence of multidrug-resistant strains and the potential health risks associated with these bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify antibiotic resistance and virulence genes in heterotrophic bacteria isolated from drinking water.

full_output.paper_title: Colony phase variation switch modulates antimicrobial tolerance and biofilm formation in Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that the WGA-binding extracellular polysaccharide layer in opaque A. baumannii protects against colistin, suggesting a novel mechanism of antimicrobial tolerance.
full_output.methodology: Microscopy, MIC testing, and genetic manipulation experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Nitric oxide-releasing prodrug for the treatment of complex Mycobacterium abscessus infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates a nitric oxide-releasing prodrug, MD3, for the treatment of Mycobacterium abscessus infections, showing its broad antimycobacterial activity and lack of resistance development.
full_output.methodology: The study used microdilution susceptibility assays, serial passage resistance studies, and in vivo mouse models to assess MD3's antimicrobial activity and resistance profile.

full_output.paper_title: The mechanism of action of auranofin analogs in B. cenocepacia revealed by chemogenomic profiling.

full_output.methodology: In vitro enzyme assays, CRISPRi mutagenesis, BarSeq analysis, and MIC testing.

full_output.paper_title: Canine Staphylococcaceae circulating in a Kenyan animal shelter.

aac(6')-Ie-aph(2'')-Ia.encodes: gentamicin and kanamycin acetyl- and phosphotransferase

full_output.key_findings: The study identified various AMR genes in Staphylococcaceae strains isolated from dogs in a Kenyan animal shelter, including tetracycline, beta-lactam, and aminoglycoside resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, MIC testing, and plasmid analysis were used to characterize AMR genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Human carriage of ESBL/pAmpC-producing Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae in relation to the consumption of raw or undercooked vegetables, fruits, and fresh herbs.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla CTX-M-15 and bla DHA-1 as the most prevalent ESBL/pAmpC genes in ESBL-E/K isolates from the Dutch population, with no specific raw or undercooked vegetables, fruits, or herbs significantly increasing the risk of ESBL-E/K carriage.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and microbiological culture techniques were used to detect and characterize ESBL-E/K isolates from fecal samples.
full_output.sample_size: 537 participants in the first sampling round and 489 in the second.

full_output.paper_title: Single-cell analysis reveals that cryptic prophage protease LfgB protects Escherichia coli during oxidative stress by cleaving antitoxin MqsA.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies LfgB, a protease from cryptic prophage CP4-57, as a critical component in the stress response of Escherichia coli. LfgB degrades the antitoxin MqsA, leading to the activation of the stress response regulator RpoS, thereby enhancing cellular survival under oxidative stress conditions.
full_output.methodology: Single-cell transcriptomics, protease activity assays, and genetic manipulation experiments were employed to analyze the role of LfgB in stress response mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic characterization of Pseudomonas spp. on food: implications for spoilage, antimicrobial resistance and human infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antimicrobial resistance genes in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from food, including aph(3)_IIb, blaOXA, blaPDC, fosA, catB7, crpP, aac(3)_IVa, and aph(4)_Ia, indicating the presence of multidrug-resistant strains capable of causing human infections.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and comparative genomic analysis were used to identify antimicrobial resistance genes and virulence factors in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from food samples.

full_output.paper_title: Method for plasmid-based antibiotic-free fermentation.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a method for plasmid-based antibiotic-free fermentation by utilizing the infA gene under an inducible promoter for plasmid selection and maintenance.
full_output.methodology: Genetic modification of E. coli strains using λ-red recombineering and plasmid-based selection strategies.

full_output.paper_title: Effect of UV pretreatment on the source control of floR during subsequent biotreatment of florfenicol wastewater.
full_output.key_findings: UV pretreatment effectively reduced the relative abundance of floR in both genomic and plasmid DNA during subsequent biotreatment processes, indicating its potential for controlling antibiotic resistance gene proliferation.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative PCR (qPCR) was used to analyze the abundance of floR and intI1 genes in sludge samples.

full_output.paper_title: Within-host genomic evolution of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus in long-term carriers.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the genomic evolution of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) in long-term carriers, identifying a median within-host mutation rate of 4.9 SNPs/genome/year and 2.7 allelic differences/genome/year. It found no significant differences in mutation rates between subgroups, including those from households or with continuous exposure. SNPs occurred randomly across the genome, and no specific genes were identified as hotspots for mutations.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) of 424 isolates from 121 long-term MRSA carriers was performed, followed by comparative analysis using core genome multilocus sequence typing (cgMLST) and single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) analyses.

full_output.paper_title: Increase of respiratory illnesses among children in Beijing, China, during the autumn and winter of 2023.

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that daptomycin does not trigger resistance mediated by the BceAB transporter in Streptococcus pneumoniae, indicating that it can avoid resistance mechanisms involving this transporter.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth microdilution to determine MICs, GFP fusion analysis, and ATPase assays to investigate the interaction between daptomycin and the BceAB transporter.

full_output.paper_title: Klebsiella pneumoniae DedA family proteins have redundant roles in divalent cation homeostasis and resistance to phagocytosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that Klebsiella pneumoniae DedA family proteins YqjA and YghB are involved in divalent cation homeostasis and resistance to phagocytosis. Their deletion leads to sensitivity to alkaline pH, elevated temperatures, and EDTA/SDS, which can be rescued by divalent cations. Additionally, the deletion affects capsule formation and increases susceptibility to phagocytosis.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, mutant construction, and growth assays were conducted to evaluate the role of YqjA and YghB in K. pneumoniae.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance, virulence profile, and genetic analysis of ESBL-producing Escherichia coli isolated from Nile tilapia in fresh markets and supermarkets in Thailand.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of ESBL-producing E. coli in Nile tilapia, with the most prevalent AMR genes being bla TEM, tetA, and qnrS. These genes conferred resistance to ampicillin, tetracycline, and fluoroquinolones, respectively.
full_output.methodology: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) was used to detect AMR genes and virulence factors in E. coli isolates from Nile tilapia samples.

full_output.paper_title: Cassette recombination dynamics within chromosomal integrons are regulated by toxin-antitoxin systems.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that toxin-antitoxin (TA) systems within chromosomal integrons regulate cassette recombination dynamics, with TA cassettes playing a critical role in maintaining the stability of large integron arrays by inducing cell death when cassette loss becomes excessive.
full_output.methodology: Genetic assays, PCR, long-read sequencing, and competitive growth experiments were used to investigate the role of TA systems in regulating cassette recombination dynamics in Vibrio cholerae.

full_output.paper_title: Ecological prevalence, genetic diversity, and multidrug resistance of Salmonella enteritidis recovered from broiler and layer chicken farms.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various AMR genes in Salmonella enteritidis isolates from broiler and layer chicken farms, including blaCTX-M, blaDHA-1, qnrA, qnrB, qnrS, gyrA, erm(B), erm(C), msr(A), tet(A), and tet(B). These genes conferred resistance to multiple antibiotics such as beta-lactams, quinolones, macrolides, and tetracyclines.
full_output.methodology: PCR and electrophoresis were used to identify AMR genes in Salmonella enteritidis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Gonococcal resistance to zoliflodacin could emerge via transformation from commensal Neisseria species. An in-vitro transformation study.
