Several gyrB mutations, including M464R, T472P, D429N, S467N, S467G, K450I, and M29I, were identified as conferring resistance to zoliflodacin.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and transformation experiments were used to identify and validate zoliflodacin resistance mutations in Neisseria species.

full_output.paper_title: Biogenic selenium nanoparticles and selenium/chitosan-Nanoconjugate biosynthesized by Streptomyces parvulus MAR4 with antimicrobial and anticancer potential.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the biosynthesis of selenium nanoparticles (SeNPs) and a selenium/chitosan nanoconjugate by Streptomyces parvulus MAR4, which exhibit antimicrobial and anticancer activities. The nanoconjugate showed the highest antimicrobial activity and significant cytotoxicity against cancer cell lines.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the biosynthesis of SeNPs and nanoconjugates, followed by characterization using UV-visible spectroscopy, XRD, FTIR, TEM, and SEM. Antimicrobial and cytotoxic activities were evaluated using MIC assays and MTT assays.

full_output.paper_title: Influence of age, socioeconomic status, and location on the infant gut resistome across populations.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the infant gut resistome across different populations and found variations in antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) abundance based on age, socioeconomic status, and geographic location. Gram-negative genera such as Escherichia, Enterobacter, Citrobacter, and Klebsiella were found to harbor a rich set of ARGs, including those targeting glycopeptides, fluoroquinolones, sulfonamides, macrolides, and tetracyclines.
full_output.methodology: The study used metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) from 6122 infant stool samples to analyze the resistome using RGI with the CARD database.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic Determinants in MRSA Carriage and Their Association with Decolonization Outcome.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that ciprofloxacin-resistant MRSA lineages were associated with higher eradication failure rates, and identified specific mutations in gyrA, grlA, grlB, and rpoB that conferred resistance to ciprofloxacin and rifampicin.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and phenotypic susceptibility testing were used to identify resistance genes and mutations associated with MRSA decolonization outcomes.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization of extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli isolated from lower respiratory tract samples between 2002 and 2019 in the Central Slovenia region.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla CTX-M, bla TEM, and aac(6')-Ib-cr as the primary resistance genes in ESBL-EC isolates from LRT samples in Central Slovenia. The bla CTX-M group 1 was the most prevalent, followed by bla TEM and aac(6')-Ib-cr.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and bioinformatics analysis were used to characterize resistance genes and phylogenetic groups in ESBL-EC isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Personalising intravenous to oral antibiotic switch decision making through fair interpretable machine learning.
full_output.key_findings: The study develops a machine learning model to predict when patients can switch from intravenous (IV) to oral antibiotic treatment, focusing on clinical parameters and ensuring fairness and interpretability.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a machine learning model trained on clinical data from ICU stays, employing SHAP values for feature selection and genetic algorithms for optimization.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic diversity of β-lactamase producing Pseudomonas aeruginosa in Iran; the impact of global high-risk clones.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various β-lactamase genes, including blaIMP, blaNDM, blaOXA-48, blaVIM, SHV, PER, OXA-1, and TEM, in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from Iran, highlighting the prevalence of carbapenem resistance and the diversity of β-lactamase-producing strains.
full_output.methodology: The study employed multiplex PCR, phenotypic testing, and MLST to characterize β-lactamase genes and assess antimicrobial resistance profiles in P. aeruginosa isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Structure-Activity Relationship Study to Develop Peptide Amphiphiles as Species-Specific Antimicrobials.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 33 peptide amphiphiles (PAs) with broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity against various Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. Key structural parameters influencing activity included zeta potential and logP values, with specific PAs showing high activity against S. aureus, E. coli, P. aeruginosa, and A. baumannii.
full_output.methodology: The study involved designing and synthesizing PAs, evaluating their antimicrobial activity via MIC and MBC assays, and analyzing structure-activity relationships using PCA.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) was the most common antimicrobial-resistant organism (ARO) reported, with an infection prevalence of 0.5 per 100 inpatients. Vancomycin-resistant Enterococci (VRE) had a prevalence of 0.1 infections per 100 inpatients, and extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing organisms had a prevalence of 0.4 per 100 inpatients. No patients were reported to have carbapenemase-producing organisms (CPO) infections.
full_output.methodology: A point prevalence survey was conducted in 55 Canadian hospitals to determine the prevalence of infections caused by selected antimicrobial-resistant organisms (AROs).

full_output.paper_title: Small Molecule Benzothiophene with In Vivo Efficacy in a Mouse Model of Drug-Resistant Enterococcus faecium Infection.

full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis and biological evaluation of benzothiophene derivatives, including MIC assays, mouse liver microsome stability tests, and in vivo efficacy studies in a mouse model of infection.

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the structure and function of microbial membrane transport proteins, including aquaporins and formate/nitrite transporters (FNTs), highlighting their roles in biotechnological applications and potential as drug targets.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews the structural and functional characteristics of membrane transport proteins using experimental and computational approaches.

full_output.paper_title: First global report about the prevalence of multi-drug resistant Haemophilus influenzae: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

full_output.methodology: Systematic review and meta-analysis of studies on MDR H. influenzae prevalence, using PRISMA guidelines and statistical analysis tools.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence, antibiotic resistance and molecular characterization of Staphylococcus aureus in ready-to-eat fruits and vegetables in Shanghai, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antibiotic resistance genes in Staphylococcus aureus isolates from ready-to-eat fruits and vegetables in Shanghai, China, including genes conferring resistance to beta-lactams, fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, lincosamides, and fosfomycin.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing was used to analyze antibiotic resistance genes and virulence factors in S. aureus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Efficacy of delafloxacin alone and in combination with cefotaxime against cefotaxime non-susceptible invasive isolates of Streptococcus pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: Delafloxacin showed higher pneumococcal activity than levofloxacin, with 76.7% susceptibility against cefotaxime non-susceptible invasive isolates of Streptococcus pneumoniae. Synergistic interactions between delafloxacin and cefotaxime were observed in vitro.
full_output.methodology: Minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) were determined using gradient diffusion strips, and synergy was evaluated via the GDS cross method.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that thiomarinol A overcomes intrinsic resistance in Escherichia coli by utilizing a dithiolopyrrolone moiety, enhancing antibiotic accumulation and activity. full_output.methodology: The study used antibiotic susceptibility testing, accumulation assays, and structural activity relationship studies to evaluate the effectiveness of thiomarinol A and its derivatives against E. coli.

full_output.paper_title: Sub-inhibitory antibiotic treatment selects for enhanced metabolic efficiency.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that antibiotics select for enhanced metabolic efficiency in bacterial populations, which can contribute to resistance. This efficiency is reflected in lower K_S values, indicating improved substrate utilization and biomass generation.
full_output.methodology: The study combines mathematical modeling and experimental evolution of E. coli under sub-inhibitory antibiotic concentrations to analyze metabolic efficiency and resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Occurrence and characteristics of extended-spectrum-β-lactamase- and pAmpC-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae isolated from companion animals with urinary tract infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) and plasmid-encoded AmpC (pAmpC) genes in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from companion animals with urinary tract infections, highlighting the prevalence of these resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize ESBL and pAmpC genes in K. pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Accessory genes define species-specific routes to antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Host- plasmid network structure in wastewater is linked to antimicrobial resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Targeted inhibition of the HNF1A/SHH axis by triptolide overcomes paclitaxel resistance in non-small cell lung cancer.

full_output.paper_title: Expression and characterization of the new antimicrobial peptide AP138L-arg26 anti Staphylococcus aureus.

full_output.paper_title: LL-37_Renalexin hybrid peptide exhibits antimicrobial activity at lower MICs than its counterpart single peptides.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the design, production, and purification of a novel hybrid antimicrobial peptide LL-37_Renalexin, which exhibits potent antimicrobial activity against various bacterial clinical isolates at lower minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) compared to its individual counterparts, LL-37 and Renalexin.

full_output.paper_title: Distribution of antibiotic resistance genes and their pathogen hosts in duck farm environments in south-east coastal China.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the heterologous biosynthesis of new antibacterial lanthipeptides named melittapeptins A-C from the myxobacterium Melittangium boletus. These peptides exhibited potent antibacterial activity against the Gram-positive bacterium Micrococcus luteus.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative molecular profiling of multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa identifies novel mutations in regional clinical isolates from South India.

cfr.genetic_context: The cfr gene was first discovered in 2000 in the bacterial species Mammaliicoccus sciuri (previously Staphylococcus sciuri) and was later found on plasmids in isolates from other sources.
cfr.evidence_note: The paper describes the structural basis of Cfr-mediated antimicrobial resistance and mechanisms to evade it.

cfr.notes: Cfr-mediated C8-methylation of A2503 prevents A2062 rotation and forms a symmetrical Hoogsteen base-pair with A2062.
cfr.evidence_note: The paper explicitly states that Cfr is a methylase that modifies the universally conserved ribosomal adenosyl residue A2503 of the 23S rRNA by C-methylation at position 8.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Cfr as a methylase that confers resistance to multiple classes of PTC-targeting antibiotics by modifying A2503 in 23S rRNA, leading to steric clashes and allosteric changes that hinder drug binding.
full_output.methodology: Structural analysis of Cfr-modified ribosomes and microbiological testing of antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluating the efficacy of different antibiotics against Neisseria gonorrhoeae: a pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic analysis using Monte Carlo simulation.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the efficacy of various antibiotics against Neisseria gonorrhoeae using Monte Carlo simulation and pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic analysis, highlighting the declining effectiveness of traditional cephalosporins and the potential of zoliflodacin.
full_output.methodology: The study used Monte Carlo simulation combined with pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic analysis to assess the efficacy of antibiotics against Neisseria gonorrhoeae.

full_output.paper_title: Oligoribonuclease mediates high adaptability of P. aeruginosa through metabolic conversion.
full_output.key_findings: The study reveals that deletion of the oligoribonuclease (orn) gene in P. aeruginosa affects its metabolism, motility, and virulence, leading to increased pathogenicity and biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: Construction of orn deletion strain, TMT quantitative proteomic analysis, bacterial growth and motility tests, virulence factor detection, and biofilm formation assays.

full_output.paper_title: Mycobacterium abscessus extracellular vesicles increase mycobacterial resistance to clarithromycin in vitro.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that extracellular vesicles (EVs) released by clarithromycin (CLR)-treated Mycobacterium abscessus increase the resistance of M. abscessus to CLR. Proteomic analysis revealed that EVs from CLR-treated M. abscessus carried higher levels of 50S ribosomal proteins, which are the target of CLR.
full_output.methodology: Proteomic analysis of M. abscessus cells and EVs, along with experiments assessing the effect of EVs on CLR resistance in vitro.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and antibiotic resistance of Salmonella in organic and non-organic chickens on the Eastern Shore of Maryland, USA.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that Salmonella isolates from both organic and non-organic chickens exhibited resistance to several antibiotics, with tetracycline, minocycline, and nitrofurantoin showing the highest resistance rates. Additionally, the presence of virulence genes invA, pagC, and spvC was detected in most isolates, with spvC being more prevalent in non-organic chicken isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the isolation and identification of Salmonella from chicken carcasses, followed by antimicrobial susceptibility testing and PCR detection of virulence genes.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic analysis of multidrug-resistant Delftia tsuruhatensis isolated from raw bovine milk.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple efflux pump genes and a genus-specific OXA-926-like beta-lactamase in the multidrug-resistant Delftia tsuruhatensis strain MR-6/3H, contributing to resistance against various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and comparative genomics were used to characterize the Delftia tsuruhatensis MR-6/3H strain.

full_output.paper_title: Transcriptome reveals the role of the htpG gene in mediating antibiotic resistance through cell envelope modulation in Vibrio mimicus SCCF01.

mutations_found.validated_by: antibiotic susceptibility testing and transcriptome analysis

htpG.notes: The htpG gene is involved in maintaining cell envelope integrity and resistance to antibiotics targeting the cell wall and membrane.

full_output.key_findings: The htpG gene is involved in maintaining the structural integrity of the cell envelope in Vibrio mimicus, and its deletion leads to increased sensitivity to several antibiotics targeting the cell wall and membrane.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing, transcriptome analysis, and genetic manipulation techniques were used to investigate the role of htpG in antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and antimicrobial resistance profiles of extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli in East Tennessee dairy farms.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Escherichia coli in East Tennessee dairy farms, with high prevalence and multidrug resistance. Key AMR genes included blaCTX-M, blaSHV, and blaTEM, which conferred resistance to beta-lactam antibiotics such as ampicillin and ceftriaxone.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic resistance testing and molecular confirmation using MALDI-TOF MS.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiology and antimicrobial resistance trends of Acinetobacter species in the United Arab Emirates: a retrospective analysis of 12 years of national AMR surveillance data.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a decline in antimicrobial resistance among Acinetobacter species in the UAE over a 12-year period, with notable decreases in resistance to imipenem, meropenem, and amikacin. Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter spp. (CRAB) were associated with higher mortality and longer hospital stays.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of 17,564 Acinetobacter isolates from national AMR surveillance data spanning 2010-2021.

full_output.paper_title: Structure-function-guided design of synthetic peptides with anti-infective activity derived from wasp venom.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes the design and evaluation of synthetic peptides derived from wasp venom, focusing on improving antimicrobial activity against Gram-negative bacteria through structure-function guided modifications. Key findings include the identification of specific amino acid substitutions that enhance antimicrobial potency and reduce toxicity.
full_output.methodology: The research employed structure-function guided design, alanine scanning, and Lys substitutions to modify natural peptides, followed by assessment of antimicrobial activity, cytotoxicity, and mechanism of action.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical use of tigecycline may contribute to the widespread dissemination of carbapenem-resistant hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae strains.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the bla KPC-2 gene as a critical factor in carbapenem resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae, highlighting its role in the dissemination of carbapenem-resistant hypervirulent strains.
full_output.methodology: Construction of isogenic strains, cloning, and MIC testing were used to validate the role of bla KPC-2 in carbapenem resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the efficacy of VesiX, a cetylpyridinium chloride (CPC)-based solution, against uropathogenic bacteria, demonstrating its rapid bactericidal activity and low cytotoxicity towards bladder epithelial cells. It also shows that combining VesiX with gentamicin reduces intracellular UPEC in cultured bladder epithelial cells.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth microdilution assays, time-kill kinetic profiles, cytotoxicity assays, and invasion assays to evaluate the antimicrobial properties of VesiX and its combination with gentamicin.

full_output.paper_title: Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV) LANA prevents KSHV episomes from degradation.
full_output.key_findings: The study reveals that Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV) latency-associated nuclear antigen (LANA) actively prevents viral episomes from degradation by shielding them from the cGAS-STING pathway and autophagy.
full_output.methodology: The study used an inducible protein degradation system (AID) to deplete LANA and analyze the effects on KSHV episome stability, combined with molecular biology techniques such as Western blotting, qPCR, and immunofluorescence.

full_output.paper_title: A comparison of antimicrobial regimen outcomes and antibiogram development in microbial keratitis: a prospective cohort study in Alexandria, Egypt.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the antimicrobial susceptibility profiles of various pathogens causing microbial keratitis, highlighting the effectiveness of specific antibiotics such as vancomycin, moxifloxacin, gentamicin, ceftazidime, natamycin, and voriconazole. It also noted resistance trends in certain bacteria and fungi.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the disc diffusion method according to CLSI guidelines.

full_output.paper_title: Incidence, pathogens and antimicrobial resistance of blood and cerebrospinal fluid isolates from a tertiary neonatal unit in South Africa: A 10 year retrospective review.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a high incidence of blood and cerebrospinal fluid infections in neonates, with a predominance of Gram-negative pathogens, particularly Acinetobacter baumannii and Klebsiella pneumoniae. Carbapenem resistance was prevalent, with 31% of Gram-negative isolates showing resistance, and rates increasing over time. Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) rates decreased from 91% in 2010 to 55% in 2019.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective review of laboratory records of bacterial and fungal isolates from blood and cerebrospinal fluid cultures of neonates admitted to a tertiary hospital in South Africa over a 10-year period.

full_output.paper_title: Larvicidal potential, antimicrobial properties and molecular docking analysis of Egyptian Mint (Mentha rotundifolia) against Culex pipiens L. (Diptera: Culicidae) and Midgut-borne Staphylococcus aureus.
